words.enDefinition: to cover an expense without charging it to someone else

examples.en: The club agreed to absorb the cost of extra envelopes rather than increase the mailing fee.
examples.zh: 社团同意「自行承担额外信封的成本」，不提高邮寄费。

examples.en: The repair team could absorb the cost of replacing one connector under its original quote.
examples.zh: 维修小组可以在原报价下「自行承担更换一个接头的成本」。

collocations: absorb the cost of a replacement
be able to absorb the cost

words.enDefinition: a submission asking for a place in a business accelerator programme

examples.en: Our accelerator application explained what we had learned after six weeks of testing the idea.
examples.zh: 我们的「加速器项目申请」说明了过去六周测试创意的收获。

examples.en: I reviewed the accelerator application before my partner sent it to the programme manager.
examples.zh: 搭档把「加速器项目申请」发给项目经理之前，我又检查了一遍。

words.enDefinition: To confirm that the item or service provided is satisfactory under the agreed requirements.

examples.en: We could accept the work once both groups confirmed the finished banner matched the proof.
examples.zh: 双方确认做好的横幅与校样一致后，我们就可以「确认验收」。

examples.en: The coordinator was ready to accept the work after checking the names on every printed folder.
examples.zh: 协调员核对了每个印制资料夹上的姓名后，准备「确认验收」。

collocations: decide whether to accept the work
be ready to accept the work
accept the work after checking it

words.enDefinition: Requirements that a finished item or piece of work needs to meet before the client accepts it.

examples.en: Our acceptance criteria said the signs needed to be legible from the entrance to the hall.
examples.zh: 我们的「验收标准」要求，从大厅入口能看清这些标牌。

examples.en: The studio checked the finished display boards against the acceptance criteria in the task brief.
examples.zh: 工场按任务书里的「验收标准」检查了做好的展板。

words.enDefinition: A document or entry showing what work was accepted, by whom, and on what date.

examples.en: The acceptance record named the student organiser who had approved the delivery of the finished signs.
examples.zh: 「验收记录」写明了是哪个学生组织者确认了成品标牌交付。

examples.en: We checked the acceptance record to confirm whether both sets of panels had been approved.
examples.zh: 我们查阅了「验收记录」，确认两套展板是否都已通过。

words.enDefinition: A review to check whether submitted work meets the requirements for acceptance.

examples.en: The gallery arranged an acceptance review so both partners could inspect the signs in daylight.
examples.zh: 画廊安排了一次「验收审查」，让两家合作方能在白天检查标牌。

examples.en: The organiser invited two people from the student group to take part in the acceptance review.
examples.zh: 组织者请学生小组的两个人参与「验收审查」。

words.zhGloss: 验收有条件通过，须更正
words.enDefinition: A status saying that approval depends on making the specified corrections.
acceptedZhAnswers: 验收有条件通过，须更正

examples.en: The poster was marked “Accepted subject to corrections” because two sponsor names were still misspelled.
examples.zh: 还有两个赞助方的名字拼错了，所以海报被标为「验收有条件通过，须更正」。

examples.en: We read “Accepted subject to corrections” and checked which room numbers the organiser wanted changed.
examples.zh: 看到「验收有条件通过，须更正」后，我们确认了组织者想改哪些房间号。

collocations: mark something accepted subject to corrections
an outcome of accepted subject to corrections
list items as accepted subject to corrections

words.enDefinition: an arrangement defining who answers for decisions and results

examples.en: We drafted an accountability framework spelling out who would answer for spending at each branch.
examples.zh: 我们起草了一份「问责框架」，明确各家分店的开支由谁负责。

examples.en: The workshop's accountability framework said that managers had to explain major changes to the board.
examples.zh: 工作坊的「问责框架」规定，管理人员得向董事会解释重大变更。

words.enDefinition: A slide naming the people or organisations whose help is being recognised.

examples.en: The students added an acknowledgement slide naming the print shop that supplied their posters.
examples.zh: 学生们加了一张「致谢幻灯片」，写上为他们提供海报的印刷店名称。

examples.en: The acknowledgement slide appeared while the organiser thanked the club's partners at the end.
examples.zh: 活动尾声，组织者向社团合作方道谢时，屏幕上显示了「致谢幻灯片」。

words.enDefinition: a diagram showing how activities reinforce a chosen strategy

examples.en: Our activity system map linked the café's short menu to its quick ordering and preparation steps.
examples.zh: 我们的「活动系统图」把咖啡馆的精简菜单和快速点餐及备餐环节联系起来。

examples.en: The lecturer used an activity system map to show why the mobile repair service travelled light.
examples.zh: 讲师用「活动系统图」说明为什么上门维修服务每次只带少量工具。

words.enDefinition: a model that relies on advertising to fund access

examples.en: The campus newsletter adopted an ad-supported model, keeping subscriptions free for readers throughout the term.
examples.zh: 校园简报采用「广告支持模式」，让读者整个学期都能免费订阅。

examples.en: We discussed an ad-supported model for the free student map in our entrepreneurship seminar.
examples.zh: 创业研讨课上，我们为免费学生地图讨论了「广告支持模式」。

words.enDefinition: An extra product that can be added to the main purchase

examples.en: We offered a spare bookmark as an add-on item for the notebook orders.
examples.zh: 我们为下单笔记本的顾客提供一个备用书签作为「加购商品」。

examples.en: The gift sleeve was an add-on item, so I counted it separately.
examples.zh: 礼品封套是「额外加购的商品」，所以我把它单独计算。

words.enDefinition: Things that make it difficult for people to start and continue using a new method or tool.

examples.en: One of the adoption barriers was that evening volunteers rarely checked the shared inbox.
examples.zh: 「采用新做法的障碍」之一，是晚间值班的志愿者很少查看共用收件箱。

examples.en: We discussed adoption barriers with staff before recommending that both sites use the same booking form.
examples.zh: 我们先和员工谈了「采用新做法的障碍」，才建议两个场点使用同一份预约表。

words.enDefinition: evidence suggesting that people are beginning to use or accept a new product or service

examples.en: We treated repeat bookings from the same society as an adoption signal rather than a guarantee.
examples.zh: 我们把同一个社团多次预约视为「开始采用的迹象」，仍继续观察后续使用。

examples.en: An adoption signal appeared when volunteers began recommending the app without being asked.
examples.zh: 志愿者开始主动推荐应用，出现了「开始采用的迹象」。

words.enDefinition: money earned by displaying or publishing paid advertisements

examples.en: Advertising revenue from two local shops helped cover the printing costs of our campus magazine.
examples.zh: 两家本地商店带来的「广告收入」分担了我们校园杂志的印刷费。

examples.en: The student podcast recorded advertising revenue separately from what it earned by selling printed guides.
examples.zh: 学生播客把「广告收入」和卖纸质指南赚的钱分别记账。

words.enDefinition: a group that offers specialist advice to an organisation

examples.en: The student venture asked its advisory board to review the plan for adding evening appointments.
examples.zh: 学生创业团队请「顾问委员会」审阅增设晚间预约的计划。

examples.en: Our lecturer explained why an advisory board might include a former customer and a local supplier.
examples.zh: 讲师解释了为什么「顾问委员会」可能吸纳一位以前的顾客和一家本地供应商。

words.enDefinition: To make or check that the work addresses what the client considers most important.

examples.en: We reordered the recommendations to align with client priorities before sharing our first draft.
examples.zh: 分享第一稿前，我们调整了建议的顺序，使其「契合客户的优先事项」。

examples.en: Our adviser asked whether both options would align with client priorities for the next semester.
examples.zh: 指导老师问，两种方案是否都「契合客户下学期的优先事项」。

collocations: make sure recommendations align with client priorities
check whether findings align with client priorities
adapt the work to align with client priorities

words.enDefinition: a single stated price covering all required charges

examples.en: The photographer offered an all-in price that covered the session, editing, and delivery of digital files.
examples.zh: 摄影师给出了「全包价」，含拍摄、修图和交付电子文件。

examples.en: We advertised an all-in price for the workshop, including materials and access to the studio.
examples.zh: 我们公布了工作坊的「全包价」，包含材料费和工作室使用费。

collocations: an all-in price for the package

words.enDefinition: Assign a quantity of goods to particular sales locations or orders

examples.en: We needed to allocate stock between the library stall and the craft market.
examples.zh: 我们需要在图书馆摊位和手工市集之间「分配库存货品」。

examples.en: I waited to allocate stock until both student groups had confirmed their orders.
examples.zh: 两个学生小组都确认订单后，我才「分配库存货品」。

words.enDefinition: the fixed amount of time participants are given to prepare for a task

examples.en: We used our allocated prep time to read the case and build a simple chart.
examples.zh: 我们用「分配到的准备时间」阅读案例，做了一张简单的图。

examples.en: The teams had the same allocated prep time regardless of their presentation time that afternoon.
examples.zh: 无论当天下午几点演示，各队「分配到的准备时间」都一样。

collocations: finish within the allocated prep time
make good use of the allocated prep time

words.enDefinition: an early development version used for initial testing, typically before the beta stage

examples.en: The alpha version could save a booking but did not yet send a confirmation message.
examples.zh: 「早期测试版」可以保存预约，但还不能发送确认消息。

examples.en: Our tutor tried the alpha version before we invited anyone outside the project to use it.
examples.zh: 我们邀请项目外的人使用之前，导师试了「早期测试版」。

words.enDefinition: a different location from which work can temporarily continue

examples.en: The arts centre identified a nearby studio as an alternate site for evening classes.
examples.zh: 艺术中心把附近一间工作室定为晚间课程的「备用场所」。

examples.en: The class checked whether the alternate site had enough storage for tools and customer orders.
examples.zh: 同学们查看了「备用场所」是否有足够空间存放工具和顾客订购的物品。

words.enDefinition: a former student of an institution who has founded a company or venture

examples.en: An alumni founder returned to campus to discuss her first year of running a business.
examples.zh: 一位「校友创业者」回到学校，谈自己经营公司的第一年。

examples.en: We met an alumni founder who had started a small studio while completing his degree.
examples.zh: 我们见了一位「校友创业者」，他在读学位时创办了一个小工作室。

words.enDefinition: comments based on individual experiences or stories rather than systematically collected data

examples.en: The survey helped us check whether the anecdotal feedback represented a wider problem with the service.
examples.zh: 问卷帮我们检查，「个别经验反馈」是否指向这项服务中更普遍的问题。

examples.en: We treated the anecdotal feedback as a starting point for another set of interviews with students.
examples.zh: 我们把「个别经验反馈」作为起点，又做了一轮学生访谈。

collocations: combine anecdotal feedback with survey data

words.enDefinition: to add notes, questions or comments directly to the case material while reading

examples.en: I used two colours to annotate the case and mark what the manager did not know.
examples.zh: 我用两种颜色「给案例材料加批注」，标出经理当时还不知道的事。

examples.en: We were asked to annotate the case before comparing recommendations with our small discussion groups.
examples.zh: 老师要求我们先「给案例材料加批注」，然后再在讨论小组里比较建议。

collocations: annotate the case as you read
use comments to annotate the case
ask students to annotate the case

words.enDefinition: subscription-based income expressed as an annual amount

examples.en: Our pitch listed annual recurring revenue from subscriptions and reported equipment sales on a separate slide.
examples.zh: 推介展示列出了订阅带来的「年度经常性收入」，另用一页介绍设备销售。

examples.en: For the exercise, we translated all monthly subscription amounts into annual recurring revenue before comparing teams.
examples.zh: 完成练习时，我们把所有月度订阅金额都换算成「年度经常性收入」，再比较各小组。

words.enDefinition: A small gap kept between appointments to allow for delays

examples.en: We added an appointment buffer so there was time to reset the portrait backdrop.
examples.zh: 我们加了「预约间隔缓冲时间」，有时间整理人像拍摄的背景。

examples.en: Without an appointment buffer, one long repair pushed every later booking back.
examples.zh: 因为没留「预约间隔缓冲时间」，一单修得久，后面的预约全晚了。

words.enDefinition: The latest time by which a person must confirm or approve something for work to continue as planned.

examples.en: We set an approval deadline so the printer would have enough time for both programme covers.
examples.zh: 我们定了「确认批准的最后期限」，好让印刷店有足够时间做两份手册的封面。

examples.en: The designer asked whether the approval deadline applied to the poster or the banner too.
examples.zh: 设计员问「确认批准的最后期限」是只针对海报，还是也适用于横幅。

words.enDefinition: the point at which a decision needs additional approval

examples.en: In our case, the approval threshold determined which purchases had to go to the director.
examples.zh: 我们的案例按「审批门槛」决定哪些采购必须报负责人批准。

examples.en: The branch exceeded the approval threshold when it ordered a second set of display stands.
examples.zh: 分店订购第二套展示架后，采购金额超过了「审批门槛」。

words.enDefinition: Permission to begin printing something once its content and layout have been checked.

examples.en: The organiser gave approval to print after correcting a speaker's name on the programme cover.
examples.zh: 组织者更正了手册封面上一位讲者的姓名后，「同意付印」。

examples.en: The student studio waited for approval to print after replacing the old venue name in the artwork.
examples.zh: 学生工作室把图稿上的旧场地名换掉后，等对方「同意付印」。

words.enDefinition: A preview of printed or designed work that has been checked and accepted for production.

examples.en: The printer kept the approved proof with the job notes for our student society booklet.
examples.zh: 印刷店把「已确认的校样」和学生社团小册子的制作记录放在一起。

examples.en: I compared the finished handout with the approved proof while we counted the boxes at collection.
examples.zh: 取件点数时，我把做好的讲义和「已确认的校样」作了比较。

words.enDefinition: The way work is performed at present, including differences between written steps and actual practice.

examples.en: Our diagram showed the as-is process for booking a repair at the community bicycle workshop.
examples.zh: 这张图展示了社区自行车维修工场的「现行流程」，说明怎样预约维修。

examples.en: The volunteers checked whether the as-is process matched what they did on busy Saturdays.
examples.zh: 志愿者核对了「现行流程」，看看是否符合他们周六忙起来时的实际做法。

collocations: compare findings with the as-is process

words.enDefinition: To request documents or other information that explain the setting and history of a project.

examples.en: We took time to ask for background material about how the cooperative had grown recently.
examples.zh: 我们专门「索要了背景资料」，想了解合作社近期是怎么发展起来的。

examples.en: The student team chose to ask for background material before interviewing the theatre's front desk staff.
examples.zh: 学生团队决定先「索要背景资料」，再采访剧院前台工作人员。

collocations: ask for background material before a visit
ask for background material about the service
ask for background material at kickoff

words.enDefinition: organising a project's assumptions so the team can decide which important uncertainties to test first

examples.en: We used assumption mapping to separate things we knew from things we still needed to test.
examples.zh: 我们通过「假设梳理与排序」，区分已经知道的情况和还需要验证的地方。

examples.en: The assumption mapping session helped the team agree on which question mattered most that week.
examples.zh: 「假设梳理与排序」的环节帮团队确定了当周最关键的问题。

words.enDefinition: A record of the assumptions a project relies on and any updates when they are checked.

examples.en: We updated the assumptions log when the second branch explained how it counted repeat visitors.
examples.zh: 第二个分点解释怎样统计再次来访的访客后，我们更新了「假设记录表」。

examples.en: The assumptions log showed which ideas still needed to be checked against the booking data.
examples.zh: 「假设记录表」显示了哪些想法仍须用预约数据加以核实。

words.enDefinition: To give permission for tasks beyond the original plan to go ahead.

examples.en: The coordinator could authorize extra work after checking that the budget would cover two new signs.
examples.zh: 协调员确认预算够做两块新标牌后，可以「准许开展额外工作」。

examples.en: Our student group asked who could authorize extra work once the original quote had been accepted.
examples.zh: 接受原报价后，我们学生小组问谁能「准许开展额外工作」。

collocations: ask someone to authorize extra work
be able to authorize extra work

words.enDefinition: a period during which a person is free and can be scheduled for work

examples.en: I entered an availability window that started after my Tuesday afternoon lecture.
examples.zh: 我录入的「可排班的时间范围」从周二下午下课后开始。

examples.en: The supervisor looked at each person's availability window before assigning the evening market shifts.
examples.zh: 主管分配晚间集市班次前，查看了每个人的「可排班的时间范围」。

words.enDefinition: the average time the worker takes to handle an interaction, often including related work after it

examples.en: The team tracked average handle time for repair questions at the student enterprise's service desk.
examples.zh: 团队统计了学生企业服务台回答维修问题的「平均处理时长」。

examples.en: Our average handle time fell after the team made the booking records easier to find.
examples.zh: 团队让预约记录更好找之后，「平均处理时长」缩短了。

words.enDefinition: the average monetary value of a completed order

examples.en: Average order value rose after students began buying both the planner and the matching stickers.
examples.zh: 学生开始把计划本和配套贴纸一起买后，「平均客单价」上升了。

examples.en: The class compared average order value for the online stationery shop and its campus stall.
examples.zh: 班上比较了文具网店和校园摊位的「平均客单价」。

collocations: a rise in average order value

words.enDefinition: revenue in a period divided by the number of users

examples.en: The campus app's average revenue per user included revenue across both free and paying accounts.
examples.zh: 这款校园应用的「每位用户平均收入」以整个用户群为基数，包含免费和付费账户。

examples.en: Our average revenue per user fell as more students signed up for the free plan.
examples.zh: 更多学生注册免费方案后，我们的「每位用户平均收入」下降了。

collocations: an increase in average revenue per user

words.enDefinition: total sales revenue divided by the number of units sold

examples.en: Our average selling price rose after students bought more large prints than small ones at the fair.
examples.zh: 集市上，同学们买的大幅印刷品多于小幅印刷品，我们的「平均售价」随之上升。

examples.en: The team used average selling price to compare two months with very different sales volumes.
examples.zh: 团队用「平均售价」比较销售量差异很大的两个月。

collocations: track changes in average selling price

words.enDefinition: a cost that would disappear if an activity stopped

examples.en: Packing supplies were an avoidable cost for the student team if it stopped offering home delivery.
examples.zh: 对学生团队来说，一旦停送上门，包装用品费用就是「可避免成本」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to identify one avoidable cost if the stall stopped opening on Fridays.
examples.zh: 导师让我们找出一项摊位周五停止营业后可以省下的「可避免成本」。

collocations: an avoidable cost of running a service

words.enDefinition: a quick approximate calculation used to check the scale or feasibility of something

examples.en: A back-of-the-envelope calculation suggested we could serve forty people before the room closed that evening.
examples.zh: 「快速粗算」表明，当晚房间关闭前我们能服务四十个人。

examples.en: I did a back-of-the-envelope calculation to check whether the stock would last through the weekend.
examples.zh: 我做了次「快速粗算」，确认库存够不够用到周末结束。

words.enDefinition: A frame used to hold up the background behind a display

examples.en: We hung a plain piece of fabric from the backdrop stand behind our table.
examples.zh: 我们在桌子后面的「背景布支架」上挂了块素布。

examples.en: The backdrop stand fitted behind the table without taking up the next seller’s space.
examples.zh: 「背景布支架」正好放在桌子后面，没有占到旁边摊商的地方。

collocations: hang fabric on a backdrop stand

words.enDefinition: A stiff sheet placed behind a flat item for support

examples.en: We slid a backing board behind each poster before putting it into a sleeve.
examples.zh: 把海报放进封套前，我们在每张后面都垫了块「防弯背板」。

examples.en: The backing board kept the print from bending while I carried it across campus.
examples.zh: 我带着版画穿过校园时，「防弯背板」防止它弯折。

words.enDefinition: A frame that holds a promotional banner upright

examples.en: I moved the banner stand beside the table so customers could see our name.
examples.zh: 我把「横幅展示架」挪到桌边，好让顾客看见我们叫什么。

examples.en: The banner stand folded down small enough to fit in the equipment box.
examples.zh: 「横幅展示架」折起来够小，可以装进设备箱。

words.enDefinition: buyers' ability to demand better prices or other terms

examples.en: The bargaining power of buyers was high because two campus departments placed almost every order.
examples.zh: 两个学校部门下了几乎所有订单，因此「购买方议价能力」很强。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how the bargaining power of buyers might change as more repair outlets opened.
examples.zh: 导师问，更多维修门店开业时，「购买方议价能力」可能会怎样变化。

collocations: assess the bargaining power of buyers
changes in the bargaining power of buyers

words.enDefinition: suppliers' ability to influence prices, terms, or availability

examples.en: The bargaining power of suppliers increased when the fictional café lost its only nearby bakery.
examples.zh: 虚构的咖啡馆失去附近唯一一家供货面包坊后，「供应商议价能力」提高了。

examples.en: The group assessed the bargaining power of suppliers before recommending another source of printing paper.
examples.zh: 小组先评估了「供应商议价能力」，再建议另找一家印刷用纸供应商。

collocations: assess the bargaining power of suppliers
changes in the bargaining power of suppliers

words.enDefinition: something that makes entering a market difficult for newcomers

examples.en: In the case, the expensive printing equipment was a barrier to entry for small newcomers.
examples.zh: 在案例中，昂贵的印刷设备是小型新进入者面临的一项「进入壁垒」。

examples.en: Our class discussed whether scarce workshop space created a barrier to entry for local repair services.
examples.zh: 我们班讨论了工坊场地短缺会不会给本地维修服务形成「进入壁垒」。

words.enDefinition: the initial price before extras or adjustments are added

examples.en: The base price covered a plain canvas bag, with embroidery available for an extra charge.
examples.zh: 「基础价格」包含一个素面帆布袋，刺绣需另付费。

examples.en: Our base price included a basic portrait session and one edited image for each student.
examples.zh: 我们的「基础价格」涵盖一次基本人像拍摄，并为每位同学提供一张修过的照片。

collocations: add fees to the base price

words.enDefinition: A measurement taken before a change so later measurements can be compared with it.

examples.en: We used the average reply time as a baseline measure before the help desk changed its form.
examples.zh: 服务台换表格之前，我们用平均回复时间作为一个「基线指标」。

examples.en: The client asked which baseline measure we would compare with results from the reminder trial.
examples.zh: 客户问，我们会拿哪个「基线指标」来对比提醒试验的结果。

collocations: compare results with a baseline measure

words.enDefinition: a reference scenario whose results are used to compare the results of other scenarios

examples.en: We used the shop's current opening hours as our benchmark scenario for comparing the three alternatives.
examples.zh: 我们把店铺现有营业时间作为「基准对照情景」，用来比较另外三种方案。

examples.en: The benchmark scenario made it clear how many more orders the new proposal could handle.
examples.zh: 「基准对照情景」让人看清新方案能多处理多少订单。

collocations: compare results with a benchmark scenario

words.enDefinition: comments from people a programme or organisation aims to help

examples.en: The student team used beneficiary feedback to change the hours of its free repair workshops.
examples.zh: 学生团队根据「受益者反馈」调整了免费维修工作坊的开放时间。

examples.en: Our lecturer asked what beneficiary feedback suggested about access to the community tool library.
examples.zh: 讲师问，「受益者反馈」反映出社区工具借用中心在服务可及性上有哪些情况。

words.enDefinition: the most favourable plausible set of events or conditions considered in a plan

examples.en: In the best-case scenario, both printers would work and the room would open on time.
examples.zh: 在「最理想的情景」下，两台打印机都能用，房间也会准时开放。

examples.en: We put an estimate for the best-case scenario beside the figure we actually expected.
examples.zh: 我们把「最理想的情景」的估计值列在实际预期的数字旁。

words.enDefinition: someone who tries a pre-release or beta version of a product and helps identify problems

examples.en: A beta tester reported that the booking form did not fit on a smaller phone.
examples.zh: 一位「测试版试用者」报告，预约表在小屏手机上显示不全。

examples.en: I volunteered as a beta tester because I usually borrow equipment before the library opens.
examples.zh: 我报名做「测试版试用者」，因为我经常在图书馆开门前借器材。

words.enDefinition: an hour of work that can be charged to a client

examples.en: The student designer counted the revision call as a billable hour under the project agreement.
examples.zh: 按项目协议，学生设计师把讨论修改的通话计为一小时「可计费工时」。

examples.en: Before submitting my timesheet, I checked whether an hour at the printer's counted as a billable hour.
examples.zh: 交工时表前，我核实了在印刷商那里花的一小时是否属于「可计费工时」。

words.enDefinition: the rate used to charge a client for work

examples.en: The student consultancy wrote its billable rate into the agreement before anyone started the work.
examples.zh: 学生咨询团队在开工前把「对客计费费率」写进了协议。

examples.en: Our billable rate for editing covered the time we spent checking captions as well.
examples.zh: 我们剪辑服务的「对客计费费率」也适用于核对字幕所用的时间。

words.enDefinition: the share of available working time chargeable to clients

examples.en: Billable utilization fell during the week when student designers spent several afternoons training their new members.
examples.zh: 学生设计师花了好几个下午培训新成员，那一周的「可计费工时占比」下降了。

examples.en: We included client work in billable utilization and tracked time spent cleaning equipment separately.
examples.zh: 我们把为客户做的工作算进「可计费工时占比」，另记清洁设备用掉的时间。

words.enDefinition: The designated place where a particular item is kept in storage

examples.en: The bin location on the list told me where to find spare bag handles.
examples.zh: 清单上的「储物格位置」告诉我备用提手放在哪儿。

examples.en: We marked the bin location next to each item in the studio spreadsheet.
examples.zh: 我们在工作室的电子表格里，把「储物格位置」写在每件商品旁边。

words.enDefinition: a constraint that holds with equality at a given feasible solution, using an allowance or meeting a required minimum exactly

examples.en: The case asked whether storage space or staffing hours formed the binding constraint for weekly repairs.
examples.zh: 案例问，对于每周维修量，「紧约束」是存储空间还是员工工时。

examples.en: The staffing limit was a binding constraint because our best plan used every available hour.
examples.zh: 最优方案恰好用完了所有可用工时，所以工时上限是「紧约束」。

words.enDefinition: the person who leads a board and its meetings

examples.en: The board chair gave both branch managers a chance to explain their concerns about the expansion.
examples.zh: 「董事会主席」让两位分店经理都有机会说明他们对扩张的顾虑。

examples.en: In the simulation, the board chair summarised the discussion before asking members for their views.
examples.zh: 在模拟中，「董事会主席」先总结讨论，再请成员发表意见。

words.enDefinition: a smaller group set up by a board for specific work

examples.en: The board committee reviewed the draft budget before the full board discussed the expansion.
examples.zh: 「董事会下设委员会」先审阅预算草案，之后董事会全体成员才讨论扩张。

examples.en: We recommended a board committee to examine the possible effects of moving the repair centre.
examples.zh: 我们建议由一个「董事会下设委员会」研究搬迁维修中心可能带来的影响。

words.enDefinition: the mix of people and expertise on a board

examples.en: The class considered how board composition might affect decisions about opening a rural branch.
examples.zh: 班上讨论了「董事会成员构成」会怎样影响开设乡村分店的决策。

examples.en: Our report assessed board composition by looking at members' experience in education, finance, and retail.
examples.zh: 报告从成员在教育、金融和零售领域的经历出发，评估了「董事会成员构成」。

words.enDefinition: the formal responsibilities and powers assigned to a board

examples.en: The students read the board mandate to see whether the board could approve a new workshop.
examples.zh: 学生查阅了「董事会职责与权限」，想知道董事会能否批准增设工作坊。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether that decision belonged within the board mandate in the fictional case.
examples.zh: 导师问，在虚构案例中，那项决策是否属于「董事会职责与权限」的范围。

words.enDefinition: a group responsible for guiding and overseeing a company

examples.en: In the case, the board of directors reviewed management's plan to open a second branch.
examples.zh: 在案例中，「董事会」审阅了管理层开设第二家分店的计划。

examples.en: The board of directors asked for an update before deciding whether to support the expansion.
examples.zh: 「董事会」在决定是否支持扩张前，要求了解最新情况。

collocations: report to the board of directors
a meeting of the board of directors

words.enDefinition: a board's monitoring of management and major activities

examples.en: The case explored how board oversight could improve reporting at a growing student enterprise.
examples.zh: 案例探讨了「董事会监督」如何改善一家发展中学生企业的报告制度。

examples.en: For our presentation, we used a workshop expansion plan to show what board oversight involved.
examples.zh: 我们在展示中用一个工作坊扩建计划说明「董事会监督」包括什么。

words.enDefinition: a teacher's plan for organising notes and ideas on a board during a lesson

examples.en: The instructor's board plan reserved space for each option and the evidence that supported it.
examples.zh: 导师的「课堂板书规划」给每个方案及其支撑证据都留了位置。

examples.en: I prepared a board plan before leading a short discussion on the case's final decision.
examples.zh: 主持关于案例最终决定的短讨论前，我做了「课堂板书规划」。

words.enDefinition: To reserve a period during which you can work in a studio.

examples.en: We had to book studio time for cutting the panels before the display was assembled.
examples.zh: 展品组装之前我们得「预约工作室使用时段」来裁切面板。

examples.en: Our group decided to book studio time when both designers could check the artwork together.
examples.zh: 我们组决定「预约工作室使用时段」，选两位设计员都能一起核对图稿的时候。

collocations: book studio time for a group

words.enDefinition: A calendar showing reserved and available times for appointments

examples.en: I checked the booking calendar before offering another time for the portrait session.
examples.zh: 我看了「预约日历」，才为人像拍摄另提了一个时间。

examples.en: The booking calendar made it easy to see which afternoons we could still offer.
examples.zh: 从「预约日历」上很容易看出哪些下午还可以约。

collocations: block time on the booking calendar

words.enDefinition: The amount of floor area taken up by a booth

examples.en: We checked the booth footprint before borrowing a second table from the studio.
examples.zh: 从工作室再借一张桌子之前，我们确认了「摊位占地尺寸」。

examples.en: The display needs to stay within the booth footprint marked on the floor.
examples.zh: 陈列用具得放在地板标出的「摊位占地范围」内。

words.enDefinition: A fitted piece placed inside a box to hold its contents

examples.en: I chose a box insert that held the mug and lid separately.
examples.zh: 我挑了一个「包装盒内托」，可以把马克杯和杯盖分开固定。

examples.en: The box insert kept the small ceramic bird in place during transport.
examples.zh: 运输时，「包装盒内托」把陶瓷小鸟固定住了。

words.enDefinition: the probability of a particular outcome given that its chance node has been reached

examples.en: We changed one branch probability after finding better records for the previous month's sales.
examples.zh: 找到上个月更完整的销售记录后，我们调整了一项「分支概率」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to explain the branch probability for lower demand during the summer.
examples.zh: 导师请我们说明夏季需求下降这一项的「分支概率」从何而来。

words.enDefinition: staffing arrangements that keep work going when someone takes a break

examples.en: We planned break coverage so the equipment desk could answer questions throughout the lunch hour.
examples.zh: 我们做好了「休息时的替岗安排」，让器材台在午餐时段一直有人答疑。

examples.en: The shift lead checked break coverage before sending the packing team outside to eat lunch.
examples.zh: 值班组长先确认「休息时的替岗安排」，才让打包人员出去吃午饭。

words.enDefinition: to earn just enough to cover the total costs

examples.en: The student bakery expected to break even if it sold every loaf at the fair.
examples.zh: 学生面包坊预计，只要集市上每条面包都卖出去，就能做到「不盈不亏」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the laundry service could break even during the quiet summer months.
examples.zh: 导师问，洗衣服务在清淡的夏季能不能做到「不盈不亏」。

words.enDefinition: a study of where total revenue equals total cost

examples.en: Our break-even analysis showed how many reusable mugs the stall needed to sell before covering costs.
examples.zh: 我们的「盈亏平衡分析」显示，摊位要卖多少只可重复使用的杯子才能覆盖成本。

examples.en: The lecturer used break-even analysis to compare a permanent workshop with a weekend repair stall.
examples.zh: 讲师用「盈亏平衡分析」比较常设工坊和周末维修摊。

collocations: a break-even analysis for a new product

words.enDefinition: a graph showing where total cost and revenue lines cross

examples.en: The break-even chart showed revenue crossing the total cost line at sixty orders in our example.
examples.zh: 在我们的例子里，「盈亏平衡图」显示收入线在六十单处与总成本线相交。

examples.en: We added a break-even chart to show what higher workshop rent would change in the model.
examples.zh: 我们加了一张「盈亏平衡图」，展示工作坊租金上涨会让模型发生什么变化。

collocations: plot fixed costs on a break-even chart

words.enDefinition: the amount of sales revenue needed to cover total costs

examples.en: Our projected break-even revenue increased when we moved the photography project into a rented studio.
examples.zh: 摄影项目搬进租来的工作室后，我们预计的「盈亏平衡销售额」提高了。

examples.en: We stated break-even revenue in pounds so the judges could compare it with our sales forecast.
examples.zh: 我们用英镑表示「盈亏平衡销售额」，方便评委拿它和销售预测比较。

words.enDefinition: a person responsible for an allocated budget and its use

examples.en: The budget holder checked whether the repair fund could cover an extra set of tools.
examples.zh: 「预算负责人」核实维修经费能不能负担多买一套工具。

examples.en: Our lecturer asked what information the budget holder should see before approving the workshop purchase.
examples.zh: 讲师问，「预算负责人」在批准工作坊的采购前应当看到哪些信息。

words.enDefinition: to make a model that shows how a design is intended to look or be arranged

examples.en: We decided to build a mock-up of the sign so students could comment on its layout.
examples.zh: 我们决定「制作模拟样稿」展示标牌布局，让同学们提意见。

examples.en: I used card from the studio to build a mock-up before the group discussion.
examples.zh: 小组讨论前，我用工作室的卡纸「制作模拟样稿」。

collocations: build a mock-up of a design

words.enDefinition: A presentation of products grouped together as a single purchase

examples.en: The bundle display showed how the small notebook and pen looked together.
examples.zh: 「套装陈列」让来客看到小笔记本和笔搭配起来的效果。

examples.en: We made a separate bundle display for the sets of postcards and stickers.
examples.zh: 我们把明信片加贴纸的套装放在一起，做了个单独的「套装陈列」。

words.enDefinition: setting a single price for several items sold together

examples.en: We used bundle pricing for a sketchbook, pencils, and a ruler sold together at orientation.
examples.zh: 迎新时，我们把速写本、铅笔和尺子一起卖，采用「组合定价」。

examples.en: The pottery team compared bundle pricing for four sessions with charging for each session separately.
examples.zh: 陶艺小组比较了四节课的「组合定价」与按课单独收费。

words.enDefinition: A problem an organisation wants to understand or address as part of its operations.

examples.en: The food cooperative described its business challenge as getting enough volunteers during busy collection hours.
examples.zh: 食品合作社提出了一个「经营难题」，就是怎样在领取高峰时招到足够的志愿者。

examples.en: Our client explained the business challenge before we discussed possible sources of information with staff.
examples.zh: 客户先说明「经营难题」，我们随后和员工讨论可从哪里获取资料。

words.enDefinition: a restriction that limits what a business can realistically decide or do

examples.en: Lack of space became a business constraint once the store started accepting more repair orders.
examples.zh: 店铺开始接更多维修订单后，空间不足成了「业务约束条件」。

examples.en: We treated the long delivery window as a business constraint when assessing the proposed schedule.
examples.zh: 评估拟议日程时，我们把送货时间范围太宽视为「业务约束条件」。

words.enDefinition: ongoing work to prepare for, withstand, and recover from disruption

examples.en: Business continuity management included checking supplier contacts and reviewing what the team learned from each interruption.
examples.zh: 「业务连续性管理」包括核对供应商的联系方式，并回顾团队从每次中断中学到了什么。

examples.en: The class used a campus library to illustrate business continuity management across several service teams.
examples.zh: 班上用校园图书馆举例，说明怎样让多个服务团队共同开展「业务连续性管理」。

words.enDefinition: a plan for keeping critical services running through a disruption

examples.en: The class drafted a business continuity plan for a print shop that might lose its premises.
examples.zh: 同学们为一家可能失去经营场地的打印店起草了「业务连续性计划」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which student services the business continuity plan would cover during a building closure.
examples.zh: 导师问，大楼关闭期间，「业务连续性计划」会涵盖哪些学生服务。

words.enDefinition: individual guidance to help a person plan, start or manage a business

examples.en: The student enterprise centre offered business counselling to people preparing their first market stall.
examples.zh: 学生创业中心给第一次筹备集市摊位的人提供「经营咨询辅导」。

examples.en: I booked business counselling to discuss whether my costs made the idea realistic that term.
examples.zh: 我预约了「经营咨询辅导」，想讨论按当学期的成本算，这个想法是否现实。

words.enDefinition: an assessment of how disruption would affect operations over time

examples.en: We used a business impact analysis to compare the consequences of losing each workshop for a week.
examples.zh: 我们通过「业务影响分析」，比较各工作坊如果停用一周会分别造成什么后果。

examples.en: The business impact analysis showed that leaving the repair desk closed would delay equipment collection.
examples.zh: 「业务影响分析」显示，维修台继续关闭会让器材领取延迟。

collocations: findings from a business impact analysis

words.enDefinition: how a venture creates value and earns money

examples.en: Our bike repair project changed its business model after students asked for home visits.
examples.zh: 有同学提出上门需求后，我们的自行车维修项目调整了「商业模式」。

examples.en: At the showcase, Jia described a business model that relied on renting equipment by the day.
examples.zh: 在展示会上，佳介绍了一种靠按天出租设备赚钱的「商业模式」。

words.enDefinition: a one-page framework for mapping how a venture works

examples.en: Our tutor asked us to complete a Business Model Canvas for the student laundry service.
examples.zh: 导师让我们为学生洗衣服务填写一张「商业模式画布」。

examples.en: The Business Model Canvas helped the team see where its suppliers fit into the plan.
examples.zh: 「商业模式画布」帮助小组看清供应商在计划中扮演的角色。

collocations: fill in a Business Model Canvas

words.enDefinition: whether a venture can sustain itself financially in practice

examples.en: At the showcase, the judges questioned business model viability once the team mentioned subsidized rent.
examples.zh: 展示会上，小组提到租金有补贴后，评委对「商业模式可行性」提出了疑问。

examples.en: Our course project assessed business model viability using separate estimates for term time and summer.
examples.zh: 课程项目分别估计学期内和暑假的情况，以评估「商业模式可行性」。

words.enDefinition: a contest in which teams prepare and present plans for new businesses

examples.en: We entered the business plan competition to get feedback on our idea for local repairs.
examples.zh: 我们参加「商业计划竞赛」，想听听大家对本地维修服务构想的意见。

examples.en: The business plan competition asked teams to explain how they would find their first customers.
examples.zh: 「商业计划竞赛」要求团队解释打算怎么找到首批客户。

words.enDefinition: a business's ability to adapt and recover after difficulties

examples.en: Our lecturer used a supplier closure to illustrate why business resilience mattered to small cafés.
examples.zh: 讲师用一家供应商关门的例子说明，「企业韧性」为什么对小咖啡馆重要。

examples.en: The course case linked business resilience to training several people to handle key tasks.
examples.zh: 课程案例把「企业韧性」与培养多名能承担关键任务的人员联系起来。

words.enDefinition: selling products or services to other businesses

examples.en: In our business-to-business model, local cafés order printed table cards directly from the student team.
examples.zh: 在我们「面向企业客户的」模式下，本地咖啡馆直接向学生团队订购印制桌牌。

examples.en: The business-to-business side of the laundry project worked with two small guesthouses near campus.
examples.zh: 洗衣项目中「面向企业客户的」业务与校园附近的两家小旅馆合作。

words.enDefinition: selling products or services to people for personal use

examples.en: The student team pitched a business-to-consumer service that cleaned trainers for people living on campus.
examples.zh: 学生团队推介了一项「面向个人消费者的」服务，为住校的人清洗运动鞋。

examples.en: Our business-to-consumer model was designed around individual orders for custom phone cases at the market.
examples.zh: 我们「面向个人消费者的」模式以市集上的手机壳个人定制订单为主。

words.enDefinition: time needed for a new customer to contribute enough to recover acquisition costs

examples.en: The student team estimated the CAC payback period using the monthly profit contribution from each subscription.
examples.zh: 学生团队按每份订阅每月带来的利润贡献估算「获客成本回收期」。

examples.en: The CAC payback period became longer when we reduced the monthly price of equipment access.
examples.zh: 调低设备使用月费后，「获客成本回收期」变长了。

words.enDefinition: A group or unit within a university or college that works with you on a project.

examples.en: The library became our campus partner for an exhibition about how students use shared spaces.
examples.zh: 图书馆成为我们的「校内合作方」，一起举办展览，介绍学生如何使用共用空间。

examples.en: We asked our campus partner which rooms could accommodate both demonstrations on the same day.
examples.zh: 我们问「校内合作方」有哪些房间能在同一天容纳两场演示。

words.enDefinition: extra capacity held available so an operation can absorb greater demand or interruptions

examples.en: We kept a capacity buffer in case more students arrived than the workshop bookings suggested.
examples.zh: 我们保留了「备用处理能力」，以防来的人比工作坊预约人数多。

examples.en: A capacity buffer let the repair desk take two urgent jobs without delaying the afternoon orders.
examples.zh: 有了「备用处理能力」，维修台接两件加急活也不耽误下午的订单。

words.enDefinition: the share of available productive capacity actually in use

examples.en: Capacity utilization fell when the student print shop lost several large orders during exam week.
examples.zh: 考试周丢了几笔大单后，学生打印店的「产能利用率」下降了。

examples.en: We measured capacity utilization by comparing booked studio hours with the hours we could offer.
examples.zh: 我们把已预约的工作室时数和可开放的时数作比较，来计算「产能利用率」。

words.enDefinition: To write down the reasons why a particular project choice was made.

examples.en: Our note taker tried to capture decision rationale while the client explained its choice of site.
examples.zh: 客户说明为什么选这个场点时，记录员尽量「记录作出决定的理由」。

examples.en: We use the meeting summary to capture decision rationale so new members can understand earlier choices.
examples.zh: 我们用会议小结「记录作出决定的理由」，让新成员能理解此前的选择。

collocations: make sure to capture decision rationale
capture decision rationale after the meeting
capture decision rationale in the minutes

words.enDefinition: To record views that differ from the main view or proposed conclusion of the group.

examples.en: Our note taker made sure to capture dissenting views about the volunteer training schedule.
examples.zh: 记录员确保把关于志愿者培训安排的「不同意见记录下来」。

examples.en: We wanted to capture dissenting views before reporting which proposed changes the museum staff supported.
examples.zh: 汇报博物馆员工支持哪些拟议改动之前，我们想先「记录不同意见」。

collocations: capture dissenting views in the notes
make sure to capture dissenting views
capture dissenting views during a review

words.zhGloss: 把一项任务留到下一轮
words.enDefinition: to leave a task unfinished and move it into the next working period
acceptedZhAnswers: 把一项任务留到下一轮

examples.en: The shift lead decided to carry over a task that needed the spare keys.
examples.zh: 值班组长决定「把一项任务留到下一轮」，因为这项任务得用备用钥匙。

examples.en: I added a note when I had to carry over a task until Monday morning.
examples.zh: 我不得不「把一项任务留到下一轮」、等周一早上再做，所以加了条备注。

collocations: carry over a task to the next shift
decide to carry over a task
carry over a task if necessary

words.enDefinition: Unsold goods kept for sale at a later event or period

examples.en: Most of the notebooks were carryover stock from last month's student craft fair.
examples.zh: 大部分笔记本都是上个月学生手工市集的「结转库存」。

examples.en: We counted carryover stock before making anything new for the winter market.
examples.zh: 制作冬季市集新品之前，我们先盘点「上一期的结转库存」。

collocations: carryover stock from the previous market

words.enDefinition: a short report or presentation summarising the situation and main issues of a case

examples.en: The case briefing opened with the choice the cafe owner needed to make before winter.
examples.zh: 「案例简报」一开头就介绍了咖啡馆老板入冬前要作的选择。

examples.en: I used our case briefing to explain what figures the class would see on the next slide.
examples.zh: 我用「案例简报」说明大家会在下一页幻灯片看到哪些数据。

words.enDefinition: the order in which events in a case took place

examples.en: I drew a case chronology because the manager's notes discussed earlier events out of order.
examples.zh: 经理的记录没按时间顺序讲早先的事件，我画了「案例事件时间线」。

examples.en: The case chronology showed that the shop changed its hours before the complaints began.
examples.zh: 「案例事件时间线」显示，店铺调整营业时间在先，顾客开始投诉在后。

words.enDefinition: a contest in which teams analyse a business case and present their recommendations to judges

examples.en: Our team entered a case competition held by two local universities in early spring.
examples.zh: 我们团队报名参加了两所当地大学在初春举办的「商业案例竞赛」。

examples.en: The case competition asked students to find a way to keep a repair shop open.
examples.zh: 「商业案例竞赛」要求学生想办法让一家维修店继续经营。

words.enDefinition: a discussion after analysing or presenting a case to reflect on decisions, reasoning and lessons

examples.en: Our case debrief focused on which facts we had missed in the first round of reading.
examples.zh: 我们的「案例讨论复盘」着重看第一遍阅读时漏掉了哪些事实。

examples.en: The case debrief helped us see why both options had looked reasonable at first.
examples.zh: 「案例讨论复盘」让我们看明白，为什么两种方案起初都显得合理。

collocations: take part in a case debrief

words.enDefinition: a short account explaining what happened after the events or decision described in a case

examples.en: The case epilogue revealed how the manager's decision affected the repair business during the next year.
examples.zh: 「案例后记」讲了经理的决定怎样影响维修店下一年的经营。

examples.en: We read the case epilogue only after presenting our own recommendations in the seminar.
examples.zh: 我们在研讨课上陈述了自己的建议，之后才读「案例后记」。

words.enDefinition: an item attached to a case, such as a chart, table or sample document

examples.en: A case exhibit showed how repair demand changed between term time and the summer break.
examples.zh: 一份「案例附录材料」展示了学期内和暑假期间维修需求的变化。

examples.en: The lecturer asked us to refer to a case exhibit when discussing the owner's options.
examples.zh: 讲师请我们在讨论店主的选择时参考一份「案例附录材料」。

words.enDefinition: guiding a case discussion so learners examine evidence, exchange perspectives and reach conclusions

examples.en: We practised case facilitation by taking turns asking quiet group members to share their reasoning.
examples.zh: 我们轮流请比较安静的组员分享理由，以练习「案例讨论引导」。

examples.en: The instructor gave us feedback on case facilitation after we tried leading the evening session.
examples.zh: 我们试着主导晚上的讨论后，导师给了我们关于「案例讨论引导」的反馈。

words.enDefinition: information stated or established in a case that learners can use in their analysis

examples.en: I separated the case facts from my guesses about why the staff had left early.
examples.zh: 我把「案例给出的事实」和自己对员工为什么提前离开的猜测分开了。

examples.en: The professor asked which case facts supported keeping the service open on weekday evenings.
examples.zh: 教授问，有哪些「案例给出的事实」支持工作日晚间继续提供服务。

collocations: base an argument on the case facts

words.enDefinition: the main account in a case that presents its context, events and participants

examples.en: The case narrative described the first month of trading from the owner's point of view.
examples.zh: 「案例叙述」从店主视角讲了开始营业的第一个月。

examples.en: We checked the case narrative to see who knew about the delivery problem that week.
examples.zh: 我们查看「案例叙述」，确认当周哪些人知道送货问题。

collocations: refer back to the case narrative

words.enDefinition: a participant who makes the initial statement in a case discussion before the discussion moves to others

examples.en: As the case opener, I explained which option I would choose if I ran the shop.
examples.zh: 作为「案例讨论开场发言者」，我说明了如果自己开这家店会选哪个方案。

examples.en: The tutor asked a different student to be the case opener for each weekly class.
examples.zh: 每周上课时，导师都会请不同的学生担任「案例讨论开场发言者」。

collocations: prepare to be the case opener

words.enDefinition: a set of readings and evidence distributed for a class, case competition or case exercise

examples.en: The case packet included a description of the shop and two tables of monthly orders.
examples.zh: 「案例材料包」包含店铺介绍和两张月度订单表。

examples.en: We downloaded the case packet before meeting to decide who would analyse the customer figures.
examples.zh: 我们先下载了「案例材料包」，再开会决定谁分析顾客数据。

words.enDefinition: work done before discussing a case, including reading it and developing an initial analysis

examples.en: The tutor allocated forty minutes for case preparation so we could check all three tables.
examples.zh: 导师留了四十分钟做「案例课前准备」，让我们有时间核对三张表。

examples.en: Good case preparation helped me contribute an example before the discussion moved to the figures.
examples.zh: 做好「案例课前准备」后，我能在讨论转到数据之前举出一个例子。

words.enDefinition: a talk that explains a case analysis and any decision or recommendation for the situation

examples.en: Our case presentation led with the decision and used one table to explain the costs.
examples.zh: 我们的「案例陈述」先给出决定，再用一张表解释成本。

examples.en: The instructor asked us to link each recommendation in our case presentation to specific evidence.
examples.zh: 导师请我们把「案例陈述」中的每项建议都和具体证据对应起来。

words.enDefinition: the central person in a case, often the manager whose decision students are asked to consider

examples.en: The case protagonist had only a week to decide what to do with the spare room.
examples.zh: 「案例主角」只有一周时间决定怎么使用空置房间。

examples.en: We tried to see the dispute from the perspective of the case protagonist before voting.
examples.zh: 投票前，我们试着从「案例主角」的角度看待这场争执。

words.enDefinition: the time when competition organisers make the case materials available to teams

examples.en: The organisers postponed the case release time so teams in other time zones could participate.
examples.zh: 组织者推迟了「案例材料公布时间」，让其他时区的团队也能参加。

examples.en: We checked the case release time before booking a room for our preparation session.
examples.zh: 我们预订备赛用房间前，查看了「案例材料公布时间」。

words.enDefinition: an assessment guide stating what parts of a case response are scored and how

examples.en: The case scoring rubric gave extra weight to explaining the consequences of each possible decision.
examples.zh: 「案例评分标准表」给解释各项决策后果这一项设了更高权重。

examples.en: We compared our recommendation with the case scoring rubric before submitting the final slides.
examples.zh: 提交最终的幻灯片之前，我们把建议与「案例评分标准表」作了核对。

words.enDefinition: A person or organisation that supports an activity with money.

examples.en: A cash sponsor offered to cover the printing costs for our student photography exhibition.
examples.zh: 一位「现金赞助方」提出承担学生摄影展的印刷费用。

examples.en: The organiser thanked the cash sponsor after explaining how the money was used for the event.
examples.zh: 组织者说明这笔款项在活动中的用途后，感谢了「现金赞助方」。

words.enDefinition: chiefly British English for counting the cash and checking it against recorded sales at the end of a shift

examples.en: The manager completed the cash-up while I put away the signs beside the counter.
examples.zh: 我收起柜台旁的指示牌时，经理做完了「收班清点并核对现金」。

examples.en: We recorded a small difference during the cash-up and checked the earlier receipts together.
examples.zh: 「收班清点并核对现金」时，我们记下了一笔小差额，一起核对了早先的收据。

words.enDefinition: staff engaged to work as needed, often without a regular schedule

examples.en: We brought in casual staff for the fair because Friday would be especially busy.
examples.zh: 周五展会特别忙，我们为此安排了「按需排班的员工」。

examples.en: The rota listed casual staff separately so the coordinator could confirm their available hours.
examples.zh: 排班表单列了「按需排班的员工」，方便协调员确认他们有空的时段。

words.enDefinition: placing decision-making authority at higher levels of an organisation

examples.en: Centralisation meant the campus outlets needed head office approval for changes to their price lists.
examples.zh: 「集权化」意味着校园各门店修改价目表前都要总部批准。

examples.en: The class discussed whether centralisation would help the branches use a consistent borrowing policy.
examples.zh: 班上讨论了「集权化」能否帮助各分店采用统一的借用政策。

words.enDefinition: to question whether a belief used in an analysis is justified by the available evidence

examples.en: I decided to challenge an assumption about costs after finding the original quotation in the appendix.
examples.zh: 在附录里找到原始报价后，我决定「质疑一项关于成本的假设」。

examples.en: The case discussion gave us a chance to challenge an assumption shared by all three groups.
examples.zh: 案例讨论让我们有机会「质疑一项假设」，三个小组都默认它成立。

collocations: be willing to challenge an assumption

words.enDefinition: a point in a decision tree representing an uncertain event, with branches for possible outcomes

examples.en: The chance node showed two possibilities for demand during the first school holiday of the year.
examples.zh: 「随机事件节点」列出了本年度第一次学校放假时需求可能有的两种情况。

examples.en: We added a chance node after choosing the larger room because attendance was still unknown.
examples.zh: 选择较大的房间后，出席人数还不确定，我们因此加了一个「随机事件节点」。

collocations: assign probabilities at a chance node

words.enDefinition: A document recording an approved adjustment to previously agreed work and any related details.

examples.en: The change order recorded the extra panel and set a new date for the finished signs.
examples.zh: 「已批准的变更单」记下了新增面板，并为完成整套标牌定了新日期。

examples.en: The printer received a change order before replacing the original cover paper with thicker stock.
examples.zh: 印刷店收到「已批准的变更单」后，把原封面纸换成了较厚的纸。

collocations: check the revised schedule on a change order

words.enDefinition: A request to alter a task, requirement, or other detail in work that has been planned.

examples.en: The organiser sent a change request asking us to use the new logo on the signs.
examples.zh: 组织者发来一份「变更申请」，请我们在标牌上用新的标识。

examples.en: The printer reviewed our change request and said the new paper size was available.
examples.zh: 印刷店看了我们的「变更申请」，说可以用新的纸张尺寸。

words.enDefinition: a list of checks or tasks for switching a workstation from one job to another

examples.en: We used a changeover checklist before switching the printer from signs to small price labels.
examples.zh: 把打印机从印指示牌切换为印小价签前，我们用了「切换准备清单」。

examples.en: The changeover checklist reminded me to put away the blocks from the previous printing job.
examples.zh: 「切换准备清单」提醒我收好上一项印刷工作用过的印版。

words.enDefinition: time needed to switch a process, station or machine from one job or product to another

examples.en: We reduced changeover time by keeping both sizes of paper beside the same printer.
examples.zh: 我们把两种尺寸的纸都放在同一台打印机旁，缩短了「切换准备时间」。

examples.en: The changeover time between two different badge sizes was longer than one complete printing cycle.
examples.zh: 两种徽章尺寸的「切换准备时间」比一个完整的打印周期还长。

words.enDefinition: to bill separately for things beyond the basic offering

examples.en: The photography team kept its basic price low and chose to charge for extras such as prints.
examples.zh: 摄影小组控制基础价格，对纸质照片等「附加项目另收费」。

examples.en: We agreed to charge for extras only when a client requested more than two edits.
examples.zh: 我们约定，只有客户要求修改超过两轮时，才对「附加项目另收费」。

collocations: charge for extras such as delivery
decide whether to charge for extras

words.enDefinition: to bill separately each time a session takes place

examples.en: The language tutors decided to charge per session so students could book without a membership.
examples.zh: 语言辅导老师决定「按次收费」，同学们不用入会就能预约。

examples.en: Our music group can charge per session even when the same club books several workshops.
examples.zh: 即使同一个社团预订多场工作坊，我们音乐小组也可「按次收费」。

collocations: charge per session rather than monthly

words.enDefinition: To compare work with its original instructions to see whether the requirements are met.

examples.en: We stopped to check against the brief before sending the finished labels to the venue.
examples.zh: 把做好的标签送到场馆之前，我们先「对照任务说明核查」。

examples.en: The designer asked the volunteers to check against the brief while she counted the finished signs.
examples.zh: 设计员请志愿者「对照任务说明核查」，自己清点做好的标牌。

collocations: check the design against the brief
check against the brief before delivery

words.zhGloss: 检查是否存在抽样偏差
words.enDefinition: To look for ways in which a sample may systematically differ from the group it is intended to represent.
acceptedZhAnswers: 检查是否存在抽样偏差

examples.en: We needed to check for sampling bias because all the volunteers we interviewed worked on weekdays.
examples.zh: 我们采访的志愿者都在工作日值班，所以得「检查是否存在抽样偏差」。

examples.en: The adviser asked us to check for sampling bias before summarising the museum visitors' responses.
examples.zh: 指导老师请我们先「检查是否存在抽样偏差」，再总结博物馆访客的答复。

collocations: check for sampling bias in the responses
take time to check for sampling bias
check for sampling bias before interpreting results

words.enDefinition: Record an arriving shipment after verifying which items it contains

examples.en: I helped check in a delivery while the other students prepared our samples for display.
examples.zh: 其他同学在准备展示样品时，我帮忙「登记了一批到货」。

examples.en: We needed to check in a delivery before adding the new stickers to our stock count.
examples.zh: 把新贴纸加进库存前，我们得先「登记这批到货」。

collocations: check in a delivery from a supplier
check in a delivery at the studio
check in a delivery against the list

words.enDefinition: to mark a task on a list to show it has been completed

examples.en: I waited to check off a task until the printed copies were on the counter.
examples.zh: 纸质副本放到了柜台上，我才「勾选任务为已完成」。

examples.en: The checklist showed when to check off a task such as counting the remaining supplies.
examples.zh: 检查清单说明了清点剩余物资之类的工作何时可以「勾选为已完成」。

collocations: check off a task on the list
remember to check off a task
check off a task after completing it

words.expression: check whether the issue is widespread
words.lemma: check whether the issue is widespread
words.enDefinition: To find out whether a problem occurs in many relevant places or situations.
acceptedEnVariants: check whether the issue is widespread

examples.en: We visited a second branch to check whether the issue is widespread across the charity.
examples.zh: 我们走访了第二个分点，「核查问题在这家慈善机构是否普遍」。

examples.en: The student team agreed to check whether the issue is widespread before recommending a process change.
examples.zh: 学生团队商定先「核查问题是否普遍」，再建议更改流程。

collocations: check whether the issue is widespread across sites
check whether the issue is widespread before responding
ask someone to check whether the issue is widespread

words.enDefinition: arrangements that prevent one person or group from holding unchecked power

examples.en: The students proposed checks and balances so the branch manager could not approve her own expenses.
examples.zh: 学生提出了「制衡机制」，防止分店经理自行批准自己的开支。

examples.en: Our lecturer asked how the checks and balances would work in a small student cooperative.
examples.zh: 讲师问，一个小型学生合作社将怎样运用这套「制衡机制」。

collocations: a system of checks and balances

words.enDefinition: To make clear what categories, terms, or measurements mean in the records used for analysis.

examples.en: We asked staff to clarify the data definitions for a repeat visitor before comparing the totals.
examples.zh: 比对汇总数据前，我们请员工「明确再次来访者的数据口径」。

examples.en: Our team needed to clarify the data definitions because two branches counted collections in different ways.
examples.zh: 两个分点统计取件次数的方式不同，我们团队需要「明确数据口径」。

collocations: clarify the data definitions with staff
take time to clarify the data definitions
clarify the data definitions before reporting

words.enDefinition: a thorough clean of a work area after an activity or shift has finished

examples.en: Our usual clean-down took longer because the last workshop used every table in the room.
examples.zh: 最后一场工作坊用了屋里所有桌子，例行的「营业后的清洁收拾」花了更长时间。

examples.en: We agreed who would do the clean-down before the morning crew arrived to set up.
examples.zh: 我们商定了早班来布置前，由谁负责「营业后的清洁收拾」。

words.enDefinition: to complete work that has accumulated and is still waiting to be processed

examples.en: We needed two quiet afternoons to clear the backlog before accepting new repair orders.
examples.zh: 接新维修订单前，我们得用两个空闲的下午「清理积压事项」。

examples.en: The team stayed an extra hour to clear the backlog of equipment labels that morning.
examples.zh: 那天上午团队多留了一小时，「清理积压的器材标签制作任务」。

words.enDefinition: The client's formal or informal agreement to something before work continues or is accepted.

examples.en: We waited for client approval before adding the new sponsor's name to both banner designs.
examples.zh: 我们先等「委托方确认」，再把新赞助方的名称加到两份横幅设计里。

examples.en: The designer asked for client approval before making the same change on both programme covers.
examples.zh: 设计员先请「委托方确认」，再在两份手册封面作同样的修改。

words.enDefinition: A short document or explanation from the client describing the problem and what it wants the team to do.

examples.en: The client brief explained why the museum wanted to understand delays in school group bookings.
examples.zh: 「客户项目说明」解释了博物馆为什么想查清学校团体预约拖延的原因。

examples.en: We read the client brief before asking the cooperative which changes it had already tried.
examples.zh: 我们先阅读了「客户项目说明」，再问合作社已经尝试过哪些调整。

words.enDefinition: Data supplied by a client for the team to use in its project work.

examples.en: We checked the dates in the client data before comparing weekdays with weekend group bookings.
examples.zh: 我们先核对「客户提供的数据」里的日期，再对比工作日和周末的团体预约。

examples.en: The client data covered only the main venue, so we asked for the second location's totals.
examples.zh: 「客户提供的数据」只涵盖主场馆，所以我们索取了第二个场点的汇总数据。

collocations: check the quality of client data

words.enDefinition: A conversation with the client after a stage or project to review what happened and what to learn from it.

examples.en: Our client debrief covered which data took longest to collect and what helped us work together.
examples.zh: 「与客户的总结交流」谈到了哪些数据最难收集，以及哪些做法帮助了合作。

examples.en: The museum director used the client debrief to explain which recommendations her team would take forward.
examples.zh: 博物馆馆长在「与客户的总结交流」中说明，她的团队会落实哪些建议。

collocations: discuss lessons at the client debrief

words.enDefinition: One scheduled period or cycle in which the client reviews work and sends comments.

examples.en: We scheduled a client feedback round after the first draft of our museum booking report.
examples.zh: 博物馆预约报告出第一稿后，我们安排了「一轮客户反馈」。

examples.en: The client feedback round raised a question about how the group counted late repair collections.
examples.zh: 「这一轮客户反馈」提出了一个问题，是关于我们小组怎样统计延迟领取维修品。

collocations: include a client feedback round in the project

words.enDefinition: A meeting at the start of a project at which the team and client discuss what they will do together.

examples.en: We held the client kickoff at the bicycle workshop to see where repairs were booked.
examples.zh: 我们在自行车维修工场开了「与客户召开的启动会」，现场看看维修预约在哪里办。

examples.en: At the client kickoff we agreed to start by reviewing the last month's booking totals.
examples.zh: 在「与客户召开的启动会」上，我们商定先核对上月的预约总量。

words.enDefinition: A person who passes questions, information, and updates between the client and the project team.

examples.en: The client liaison confirmed which members of staff we could interview about the booking process.
examples.zh: 「客户联络人」确认了我们可以采访哪些员工来了解预约流程。

examples.en: Our studio named a client liaison to collect questions from both sides before each meeting.
examples.zh: 我们工作室指定了一名「客户联络人」，在每次会议前收集双方的问题。

words.enDefinition: An organisation that brings a problem to a student team and works with it on the project.

examples.en: Our client partner showed us how volunteers registered deliveries at the local food cooperative.
examples.zh: 「提出委托的合作机构」向我们演示了当地食品合作社的志愿者怎样登记送来的货物。

examples.en: We asked the client partner whether weekend bookings were recorded separately from weekday reservations.
examples.zh: 我们问「提出委托的合作机构」，周末的预约是否与工作日的预约分开记录。

words.enDefinition: Tasks the client is expected to carry out under a service arrangement.

examples.en: The document listed client responsibilities such as supplying photographs and checking the spelling of names.
examples.zh: 文件列出了「委托方职责」，比如提供照片和核对姓名拼写。

examples.en: We discussed client responsibilities at the first meeting so both teams knew who supplied the artwork.
examples.zh: 初次开会时，我们讨论了「委托方职责」，让双方知道由谁提供图稿。

words.enDefinition: The person on the client's side who coordinates its part of the work with the student team.

examples.en: The client-side lead booked time with volunteers so we could observe their afternoon intake routine.
examples.zh: 「客户方项目负责人」和志愿者约了时间，让我们观察他们下午接收物品的流程。

examples.en: Our client-side lead checked the figures before sharing the findings with the museum director.
examples.zh: 「客户方项目负责人」先核对了数字，再把调查发现发给博物馆馆长。

words.enDefinition: Materials the client provides for someone else to use in carrying out agreed work.

examples.en: The printer checked the client-supplied materials before agreeing to use them for the exhibition signs.
examples.zh: 印刷店先核查了「委托方提供的材料」，再同意用于制作展览标牌。

examples.en: The brief listed photographs and paper samples among the client-supplied materials for the job.
examples.zh: 任务书把照片和纸样列为这项工作中「委托方提供的材料」。

collocations: draw up a list of client-supplied materials

words.zhGloss: 与客户共同开展的工作会
words.enDefinition: A meeting in which the client and project team work together on a particular problem or draft.
acceptedZhAnswers: 与客户共同开展的工作会

examples.en: We used a client working session to lay out the volunteer intake steps on cards.
examples.zh: 我们在「与客户共同开展的工作会」上，把招募志愿者的各个步骤写到卡片上排开。

examples.en: Both branches joined a client working session to rewrite the reminder text together on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 两个分点都参加了周二「与客户共同开展的工作会」，一起改写提醒文案。

collocations: bring a draft to the client working session

words.enDefinition: the recorded time when a worker logs the start of work

examples.en: My clock-in time was five minutes after opening because the tablet took time to start.
examples.zh: 平板启动耽搁了一会儿，我的「上班打卡时间」是开门后五分钟。

examples.en: The supervisor checked my clock-in time after I noticed an error in the timesheet.
examples.zh: 我发现工时表有错后，主管核对了我的「上班打卡时间」。

words.enDefinition: the recorded time when a worker logs the end of work

examples.en: I checked my clock-out time before leaving the student centre after our evening shift.
examples.zh: 晚班结束后，我离开学生中心前查看了自己的「下班打卡时间」。

examples.en: The clock-out time was later than expected because we helped clear the display area.
examples.zh: 我们的「下班打卡时间」比预期晚，因为帮忙收拾了展示区。

words.enDefinition: Stop an order form from accepting any more customer submissions

examples.en: We'll close the order form once we have enough requests for the first print run.
examples.zh: 第一轮印刷攒够订单后，我们就「关闭下单表单」。

examples.en: I forgot to close the order form and found three extra requests the next morning.
examples.zh: 我忘了「关闭下单表单」，第二天早上发现多了三笔订单。

collocations: remember to close the order form
decide when to close the order form
close the order form at noon

words.enDefinition: a beta test limited to a selected group of users

examples.en: The team ran a closed beta with two societies before inviting students from other departments.
examples.zh: 团队先请两个社团试用「封闭测试」，后来才邀请其他系的学生。

examples.en: We made changes after the closed beta showed that several labels were hard to understand.
examples.zh: 「封闭测试」反馈显示好几个标签不好懂，我们据此作了修改。

words.enDefinition: a list of things to complete or verify when closing a business or finishing operations

examples.en: The closing checklist reminded us to record leftover stock and return the storeroom key.
examples.zh: 「收班检查清单」提醒我们记录剩余库存，并归还储藏室钥匙。

examples.en: I finished the closing checklist before leaving the stall with the last two volunteers.
examples.zh: 我完成了「收班检查清单」，和最后两名志愿者一起离开摊位。

words.enDefinition: the workers responsible for finishing operations and closing a workplace at the end of the day

examples.en: The closing crew counted the remaining supplies before stacking the chairs near the storeroom.
examples.zh: 「收班班组」清点完剩余物资，才把椅子叠放在储藏室旁。

examples.en: Our closing crew left a brief note about an order still waiting for collection.
examples.zh: 我们的「收班班组」留了张简短的便条，说明还有一笔订单没人来取。

words.enDefinition: the regular tasks workers carry out to finish operations and close a workplace

examples.en: Our closing duties included packing the display and noting any repairs still waiting for collection.
examples.zh: 我们的「收班工作」包括收起展品，记下仍等着领取的维修件。

examples.en: I finished my closing duties before handing the keys to the supervisor at the entrance.
examples.zh: 我完成「收班工作」后，在入口把钥匙交给了主管。

words.enDefinition: the amount of cash counted in a till when a shift or business day ends

examples.en: I entered the closing till count after the supervisor checked the notes beside the register.
examples.zh: 主管核对完收银机旁的记录后，我录入了「收班现金盘点金额」。

examples.en: The closing till count was lower than expected, so I asked the supervisor to check the receipts.
examples.zh: 「收班现金盘点金额」少于预期，我请主管核对收据。

words.enDefinition: A person or group that shares the work of organising an event with another.

examples.en: The print studio joined as a co-organizer and helped arrange the workshops for new members.
examples.zh: 印刷工场以「联合组织者」身份加入，帮忙为新成员安排工作坊。

examples.en: Each co-organizer checked the final programme before we sent it to the other partners.
examples.zh: 发给其他合作方之前，每个「联合组织者」都检查了最终版活动手册。

collocations: name a co-organizer in the programme

words.enDefinition: One of two or more people or organisations supporting the same event as sponsors.

examples.en: The student newspaper joined as a co-sponsor and helped publicise the exhibition across campus.
examples.zh: 学生报以「联合赞助方」的身份加入，帮助在校园里宣传展览。

examples.en: We listed each co-sponsor separately so visitors could see who contributed to the event.
examples.zh: 我们分别列出了每个「联合赞助方」，让访客知道哪些单位为活动做了贡献。

words.enDefinition: An organisation working with another group to plan or carry out an activity.

examples.en: Each collaborating organization sent someone to the planning meeting for our student design fair.
examples.zh: 每个「参与协作的机构」都派人参加了学生设计市集的筹备会。

examples.en: We asked the collaborating organization to bring photographs for the shared display about the project.
examples.zh: 我们请「参与协作的机构」带些照片，用于共同展示项目。

words.enDefinition: A short document outlining what a joint project is for and what each group will do.

examples.en: The collaboration brief explained which team would design the signs and who would check them.
examples.zh: 「合作任务简报」说明了哪个团队设计标牌，以及由谁检查。

examples.en: We gave the print shop a collaboration brief before discussing how much it could contribute.
examples.zh: 讨论印刷店可以提供多少支持之前，我们先给了他们一份「合作任务简报」。

words.enDefinition: A single order created from items that were requested separately

examples.en: The two roommates asked us to make a combined order for one pickup.
examples.zh: 两个室友请我们把他们的需求「合成一笔订单」，一起取货。

examples.en: Our combined order included postcards for three people in the same house.
examples.zh: 我们的「合并订单」里有同一住处三个人要的明信片。

collocations: a combined order for two people

words.enDefinition: a situation in which a product or service could become a sustainable business

examples.en: The group saw a commercial opportunity when several societies asked about the same repair service.
examples.zh: 几个社团都问到同一种维修服务，小组看到了一个「可商业化的机会」。

examples.en: The adviser asked what made the idea a commercial opportunity beyond the one campus market.
examples.zh: 顾问问，除了这一所学校的市场之外，这个创意为什么还算一个「可商业化的机会」。

words.enDefinition: a sequence of steps by which a research result or new idea can become a market offering

examples.en: The team outlined a commercialisation pathway from a laboratory demonstration to testing with local customers.
examples.zh: 团队列出了一条从实验室演示到和本地客户共同测试的「成果商业化路径」。

examples.en: We discussed which partners could help with the commercialisation pathway after the grant ended.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了资助结束后，哪些伙伴能协助推进「成果商业化路径」。

words.enDefinition: a business model that earns a share of transactions

examples.en: The student booking site used a commission-based model and kept a percentage of every completed booking.
examples.zh: 学生预订网站采用「佣金模式」，从每笔完成的预订中抽取一定比例。

examples.en: We compared a commission-based model with charging each seller an annual fee to use the marketplace.
examples.zh: 我们将「佣金模式」和向每位卖家收取平台年费的做法作了比较。

words.enDefinition: a case designed to be taught alongside another case to give a contrasting or additional perspective

examples.en: The companion case presented the same shop's move from the staff members' point of view.
examples.zh: 「配套案例」从员工视角讲述了同一家店搬迁的事情。

examples.en: We studied the companion case after discussing the original one from the perspective of customers.
examples.zh: 我们从顾客角度讨论了原案例，随后学习了「配套案例」。

collocations: teach a companion case alongside the original

words.enDefinition: an examination of two or more cases to explain similarities and differences in choices or outcomes

examples.en: Our comparative case analysis explored why two similar shops chose quite different opening hours.
examples.zh: 我们的「比较案例分析」探讨，两家相像的店为什么选了差别很大的营业时间。

examples.en: The comparative case analysis helped us separate local constraints from challenges that both businesses faced.
examples.zh: 「比较案例分析」帮我们区分了各地特有的限制和两家都面临的困难。

collocations: findings from a comparative case analysis

words.zhGloss: 把预测值和结果作比较
words.enDefinition: to check how well predicted outcomes match outcomes that are observed or produced
acceptedZhAnswers: 把预测值和结果作比较

examples.en: We stayed after the simulation to compare forecasts with results for both of our shops.
examples.zh: 模拟结束后我们留下来，对两家店都「把预测值和结果作比较」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to compare forecasts with results before explaining why the difference mattered.
examples.zh: 导师请我们先「把预测值和结果作比较」，再解释差异为什么重要。

collocations: compare forecasts with results each week
learn to compare forecasts with results
use a chart to compare forecasts with results

words.enDefinition: to examine how different options are expected to turn out before choosing one

examples.en: We met after class to compare projected outcomes for two possible collection locations on campus.
examples.zh: 我们课后碰头，「比较校园两处自取地点的预测结果」。

examples.en: Our slides compare projected outcomes using the same demand and cost assumptions for both options.
examples.zh: 我们的幻灯片为两个方案采用相同的需求和成本假设，「比较预测结果」。

collocations: compare projected outcomes side by side
use a chart to compare projected outcomes
compare projected outcomes under different assumptions

words.enDefinition: goals that are difficult to achieve together because improving one may mean sacrificing another

examples.en: The club had competing objectives because it wanted to reduce prices and extend opening hours.
examples.zh: 社团想降价，也想延长营业时间，面临「相互冲突的目标」。

examples.en: The class listed competing objectives before deciding how the business should respond to longer queues.
examples.zh: 全班先列了「相互冲突的目标」，再判断商家该怎样应对队伍变长。

words.enDefinition: a document giving participants a contest's task, requirements and key deadlines

examples.en: The competition brief said we could use information from the exhibits and the case narrative.
examples.zh: 「竞赛任务说明」写了我们可以用案例图表附件和正文里的信息。

examples.en: I read the competition brief twice because the slide limit was lower than I expected.
examples.zh: 幻灯片页数上限比我预期低，我把「竞赛任务说明」读了两遍。

words.enDefinition: an ability to create more value or operate more efficiently than rivals

examples.en: The student publisher's access to inexpensive campus printing gave it a competitive advantage over local rivals.
examples.zh: 学生出版社能低价使用校园印刷服务，让它相较本地同行有了「竞争优势」。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether a faster booking system would create a lasting competitive advantage.
examples.zh: 导师问，更快的预约系统会不会带来长期的「竞争优势」。

words.enDefinition: competition among firms already operating in the same industry

examples.en: Competitive rivalry intensified after three nearby repair stalls began offering the same pickup hours.
examples.zh: 附近三个维修摊开始提供相同的自取时间后，「同行竞争」更激烈了。

examples.en: We examined competitive rivalry before discussing whether the campus print shop could charge more.
examples.zh: 在讨论校园打印店能否提价前，我们研究了「同行竞争」。

words.enDefinition: the range of markets or customer groups a company chooses to serve

examples.en: The workshop narrowed its competitive scope when it started repairing only bicycles owned by campus staff.
examples.zh: 工作坊开始只修校园员工的自行车后，缩小了「竞争范围」。

examples.en: Our class compared the competitive scope of a neighbourhood café and a regional catering service.
examples.zh: 我们班比较了社区咖啡馆与区域餐饮服务商的「竞争范围」。

words.enDefinition: a plan for succeeding against rivals in a market

examples.en: The fictional repair firm chose a competitive strategy based on fast service rather than broader coverage.
examples.zh: 虚构的维修企业选择以快速服务为主的「竞争战略」，没有把重点放在扩大覆盖面上。

examples.en: In our report, we compared the competitive strategy of a campus bookshop with two online sellers.
examples.zh: 在报告中，我们把校园书店的「竞争战略」和两家网店的做法作了比较。

words.enDefinition: To finish passing the agreed work, materials, or information to the person taking over.

examples.en: The gallery needed to complete the handover before the student team left for its summer placements.
examples.zh: 画廊得在学生团队去参加暑期实习前「完成交接」。

examples.en: We used the meeting to complete the handover of designs and labels for the exhibition.
examples.zh: 我们利用这次会议「完成交接」，把展览设计稿和标签交了过去。

collocations: agree when to complete the handover

words.enDefinition: The state of loaned goods or equipment at the time they are brought back.

examples.en: The studio recorded the condition on return after our group brought back the display stands.
examples.zh: 我们小组还回展架后，工作室记录了它们「归还时的状况」。

examples.en: Both partners checked the condition on return before putting the borrowed projector back into storage.
examples.zh: 借来的投影仪放回储藏室之前，双方核对了它「归还时的状况」。

words.enDefinition: Verify that the customer accepts a different item in the order

examples.en: I called to confirm a substitution before packing the cream bag instead of the white one.
examples.zh: 我先打电话「确认替换商品」，才把白色包换成米白色的装进去。

examples.en: We needed to confirm a substitution because we only had larger envelopes left.
examples.zh: 只剩较大的信封了，所以我们得先「确认能不能替换」。

collocations: confirm a substitution with the customer
ask someone to confirm a substitution
need to confirm a substitution before packing

words.enDefinition: To check that the people doing the work will be able to see or use the information they need.

examples.en: We needed to confirm access to data before planning which booking patterns to compare.
examples.zh: 我们需要先「确认可以获取数据」，再计划比较哪些预约规律。

examples.en: The project lead asked us to confirm access to data with the museum's research office.
examples.zh: 项目负责人让我们和博物馆研究办公室「确认可以获取数据」。

collocations: confirm access to data with the client
ask someone to confirm access to data
confirm access to data before analysis

words.enDefinition: The date the people involved have agreed and confirmed for a service to take place.

examples.en: The confirmed service date mattered because the photographer needed someone to open the gallery early.
examples.zh: 摄影师需要有人提早打开画廊，所以「已确认的服务日期」很重要。

examples.en: We checked the confirmed service date before telling volunteers when to move the display tables.
examples.zh: 我们先核对了「已确认的服务日期」，再通知志愿者什么时候搬展示桌。

collocations: ask for the confirmed service date
write down the confirmed service date

words.enDefinition: evidence from different sources suggesting conclusions that do not agree with each other

examples.en: We found conflicting evidence about whether bookings fell after the change in collection time.
examples.zh: 关于自取时间更改后预约量是否下降，我们找到了「相互矛盾的证据」。

examples.en: The tutor encouraged us to explain conflicting evidence before arguing for a change in hours.
examples.zh: 导师鼓励我们在主张调整营业时间前，先解释「相互矛盾的证据」。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement where the supplier is paid when goods sell

examples.en: The ceramics club used a consignment model so students kept ownership of pieces until they sold.
examples.zh: 陶艺社采用「寄售模式」，作品卖出之前仍归创作的同学所有。

examples.en: Under the consignment model, the student shop sends us a share only after a bag sells.
examples.zh: 按「寄售模式」，只有帆布袋卖出后，学生商店才会把我们的份额转过来。

words.enDefinition: A defined period of work in which consultants help a client address an agreed problem.

examples.en: Our consulting engagement focused on how the community theatre scheduled its rehearsal rooms after school.
examples.zh: 我们的「咨询项目合作」关注社区剧院怎样安排放学后的排练室。

examples.en: The student team completed a consulting engagement with a museum that wanted shorter booking queues.
examples.zh: 学生团队和一家希望缩短预约队列的博物馆完成了「一次咨询项目合作」。

words.enDefinition: A course in which students learn consulting by working on a real problem with an organisation.

examples.en: I took a consulting practicum that paired our class with a local bicycle repair charity.
examples.zh: 我选了一门「咨询实践课」，我们班和当地一家自行车维修慈善机构对接。

examples.en: The consulting practicum met on Fridays so client teams could join discussions before the weekend.
examples.zh: 「咨询实践课」安排在周五，这样合作单位的团队可以在周末前参加讨论。

words.enDefinition: A written account of the consulting team's question, methods, findings, and recommendations for the client.

examples.en: The consulting report identified two ways the repair charity could track uncollected bicycles more consistently.
examples.zh: 「咨询报告」指出，维修慈善机构有两种方法可以更稳定地跟踪尚未被领走的自行车。

examples.en: We gave the client the consulting report and a short guide to reading the charts.
examples.zh: 我们给客户提供了「咨询报告」，还附上一份图表阅读简要指南。

words.enDefinition: A transfer of goods arranged without meeting the other person directly

examples.en: We arranged a contactless handoff for the bags by using the agreed shelf.
examples.zh: 我们用双方说好的架子放袋子，完成了「无接触交接」。

examples.en: The buyer requested a contactless handoff because nobody would be home until much later.
examples.zh: 买家说要很晚才有人到家，于是提出「无接触交接」。
