collocations: a contactless handoff at the door

words.enDefinition: advice that applies only if a stated condition or event holds

examples.en: We wrote a contingent recommendation that depended on the landlord approving a second storage room.
examples.zh: 我们写了项「取决于条件的建议」，前提是房东同意再开放一间储物室。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to explain when the contingent recommendation should actually be put into effect.
examples.zh: 导师请我们解释「取决于条件的建议」应在什么情况下真正实施。

words.enDefinition: a practice activity that tests how essential work would continue

examples.en: During a continuity exercise, the print team tested serving customers from a different campus building.
examples.zh: 在「业务连续性演练」中，打印团队测试了从校园另一栋楼为顾客提供服务。

examples.en: Our continuity exercise checked how quickly the service desk could contact everyone with a booking.
examples.zh: 我们的「业务连续性演练」检查了服务台能多快联系上所有已经预约的人。

words.enDefinition: income earned by providing what a contract specifies

examples.en: We recorded contract revenue for the posters once the university department accepted the finished work.
examples.zh: 学校相关部门验收成品后，我们把制作海报所得款项记为「合同收入」。

examples.en: The print club listed contract revenue from societies that hired it to make event programmes.
examples.zh: 印刷社团列出了为其他社团制作活动节目单获得的「合同收入」。

words.enDefinition: a factor deliberately held constant to keep its changes from influencing a comparison

examples.en: We kept the shipping charge as a control variable while comparing demand at three different prices.
examples.zh: 我们比较三个价位的需求时，把运费设为「控制变量」，保持不变。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to explain why total staffing hours were a control variable in the simulation.
examples.zh: 导师请我们解释，为什么员工总工时是模拟中的「控制变量」。

words.enDefinition: making a product or change available gradually while monitoring its effects

examples.en: We used a controlled rollout so the busiest societies could keep their old booking process initially.
examples.zh: 我们采用「受控分批推出」，让最忙的社团起初还能沿用旧的预约流程。

examples.en: The controlled rollout expanded after the first two departments reported that their reservations worked normally.
examples.zh: 头两个系反馈预约正常后，「受控分批推出」扩大了范围。

words.enDefinition: a business jointly owned and democratically controlled by its members

examples.en: Our class compared a cooperative enterprise owned by its users with a shop owned by one family.
examples.zh: 我们班把一家由用户共同拥有的「合作社」与一家家族商店作了比较。

examples.en: The case described how members of a cooperative enterprise decided what to do with a surplus.
examples.zh: 案例描述了「合作社」的成员如何决定怎样使用盈余。

words.enDefinition: an organisational strength built through skills that support multiple offerings

examples.en: The case company used its core competence in small-batch printing to serve several very different groups.
examples.zh: 案例公司运用小批量印刷方面的「核心能力」，服务了多个差异很大的群体。

examples.en: Our report asked how the workshop could apply its core competence in repair to another service.
examples.zh: 报告探讨工作坊能否把维修方面的「核心能力」用到另一项服务中。

words.enDefinition: the main thing a venture provides to its customers

examples.en: The stall's core offering was a simple lunch box, with drinks available as extras.
examples.zh: 摊位的「核心产品」是简餐盒，饮品可以另点。

examples.en: Our core offering for the first term was same-day repair for torn backpacks.
examples.zh: 第一学期，我们的「核心服务」是当天修好撕破的背包。

words.enDefinition: the system by which a company is directed and overseen

examples.en: We studied corporate governance through a case about who could question the founder's decisions.
examples.zh: 我们用一个关于谁有权质疑创始人决策的案例学习「公司治理」。

examples.en: The corporate governance module compared the responsibilities of managers, board members, and company owners.
examples.zh: 「公司治理」课比较了经理、董事会成员和公司所有者的职责。

words.enDefinition: choices about the businesses and markets a company operates in

examples.en: Our case examined the corporate strategy behind a publisher's decision to enter the training business.
examples.zh: 我们研究了某出版社决定进入培训行业背后的「公司层战略」。

examples.en: The tutor asked how corporate strategy would change if the retailer sold one of its divisions.
examples.zh: 导师问，如果这家零售商出售一个事业部，「公司层战略」会怎样改变。

words.enDefinition: a model designed primarily around keeping costs low

examples.en: Our assignment described a cost-driven business model built around shared ovens and one standard sandwich.
examples.zh: 我们的作业介绍了一个「成本驱动型商业模式」，以共享烤箱和单一标准三明治为基础。

examples.en: The team presented a cost-driven business model for a campus shuttle with fixed pickup points.
examples.zh: 团队展示了一个采用固定上车点的校园接驳服务「成本驱动型商业模式」。

collocations: a cost-driven business model focused on efficiency

words.enDefinition: an estimate of expenses expected over a future period

examples.en: We updated the cost forecast after the workshop gave us a new quote for evening hire.
examples.zh: 工作室给出新的晚间租用报价后，我们更新了「成本预测」。

examples.en: The judges asked whether the cost forecast included tool maintenance after the first semester.
examples.zh: 评委问，「成本预测」有没有算上第一学期之后的工具维护。

words.enDefinition: competing by achieving lower costs than other firms in an industry

examples.en: The case company pursued cost leadership by offering standard repairs and using the same tools everywhere.
examples.zh: 案例公司通过提供标准化维修并在各处使用相同工具追求「成本领先」。

examples.en: We discussed whether cost leadership was possible for a workshop that bought small quantities of materials.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了采购材料量较少的工作坊能否做到「成本领先」。

words.enDefinition: the money or other benefits lost or spent because action is taken later

examples.en: We weighed the cost of delay against the possibility of receiving better information next week.
examples.zh: 我们在「延迟造成的成本」与下周可能拿到更好信息之间作权衡。

examples.en: The cost of delay rose once the repair desk started turning people away each afternoon.
examples.zh: 维修台开始每天下午都不得不谢绝一些人后，「延迟造成的成本」上升了。

collocations: compare the cost of delay with the benefits

words.enDefinition: the cost associated with handling one order on average

examples.en: Our cost per order increased when we began adding protective packaging to every mug shipment.
examples.zh: 每单马克杯都加上防护包装后，我们的「单笔订单成本」上升了。

examples.en: The student team compared cost per order for pickup at the stall and for home delivery.
examples.zh: 学生团队比较了摊位自取和送货上门的「单笔订单成本」。

words.enDefinition: setting a price by adding a markup to cost

examples.en: For the course exercise, we used cost-plus pricing after calculating the cost of a printed mug.
examples.zh: 课程练习里，我们算出一只印花杯的成本后，采用了「成本加成定价」。

examples.en: The workshop tutor demonstrated cost-plus pricing using the materials and labour needed for a tote bag.
examples.zh: 工作坊导师用制作帆布袋所需的材料和人工，演示了「成本加成定价」。

words.enDefinition: the main costs a venture faces and how they relate

examples.en: The cost structure changed when our team replaced a rented studio with a shared workshop.
examples.zh: 团队改用共享工作坊后，「成本结构」发生了变化。

examples.en: Our lecturer asked us to explain the cost structure of a one-person campus delivery service.
examples.zh: 讲师让我们解释由一人运营的校园配送服务的「成本结构」。

words.enDefinition: the full cost of meeting a customer's needs

examples.en: Our cost to serve rose for customers who asked the team to collect equipment off campus.
examples.zh: 对于要求团队到校外取设备的顾客，我们的「客户服务成本」上升了。

examples.en: The team estimated the cost to serve small clubs that needed help setting up online booking.
examples.zh: 团队估算了帮助小型社团设置在线预订产生的「客户服务成本」。

collocations: the cost to serve a customer segment

words.enDefinition: Count items separately for each code identifying a distinct product version

examples.en: We had to count by SKU because the similar bags had different fabric codes.
examples.zh: 几个包看着差不多，面料代码却不一样，所以我们得「按商品代码盘点」。

examples.en: Let's count by SKU before the fair so we can track colors separately.
examples.zh: 我们在市集前「按商品代码盘点」吧，这样能按颜色分别记录。

collocations: ask everyone to count by SKU

words.enDefinition: A form used to record quantities during a physical count

examples.en: Tariq marked the opened boxes on the count sheet as we counted them.
examples.zh: 我们数到开过的箱子时，塔里克在「盘点记录表」上作了标记。

examples.en: I left the count sheet near the shelf so we could update it together.
examples.zh: 我把「盘点记录表」放在架子旁边，方便我们一起更新。

words.enDefinition: a worker who helps customers or visitors at a counter

examples.en: The counter attendant checked each receipt before handing over a bag from the shelf.
examples.zh: 「柜台服务员」先逐张核对收据，再从货架上取袋子交给顾客。

examples.en: I asked the counter attendant who could help students with a large equipment order.
examples.zh: 我问「柜台服务员」，谁能帮助要订大量器材的学生。

words.enDefinition: to work at a counter for a time so the usual worker can do something else

examples.en: I offered to cover the counter while my coworker collected boxes from the storeroom downstairs.
examples.zh: 同事去楼下储藏室拿箱子时，我主动提出「代为照看柜台」。

examples.en: We asked a trained volunteer to cover the counter until the afternoon cashier came back.
examples.zh: 我们请一名受过培训的志愿者「代为照看柜台」，等下午班收银员回来。

collocations: cover the counter for ten minutes
ask someone to cover the counter
cover the counter during a break

words.enDefinition: one of the people who work together as a crew to carry out a job

examples.en: Each crew member checked one section of the hall after the last visitor had gone.
examples.zh: 最后一位访客离开后，每名「班组成员」检查了大厅的一个区域。

examples.en: I showed a new crew member where we kept the supplies for the next shift.
examples.zh: 我给新来的「班组成员」指出了下一班用的物资放在哪里。

words.enDefinition: Shredded paper folded into crinkles for decoration or cushioning in boxes

examples.en: I used crinkle paper to hold the small gift box in place.
examples.zh: 我用了「皱褶填充纸条」来固定小礼盒。

examples.en: The extra crinkle paper was in a drawer beside our packing table.
examples.zh: 多余的「皱褶填充纸条」放在打包桌旁边的抽屉里。

collocations: fill a box with crinkle paper

words.enDefinition: a value expressing how much one criterion counts in a comparison with other criteria

examples.en: We adjusted the criterion weight for price once the group realised most options were affordable.
examples.zh: 小组发现大多数方案都负担得起，便调整了价格这项「评估标准的权重」。

examples.en: The spreadsheet showed how each criterion weight affected the total score for the room.
examples.zh: 表格显示，各项「评估标准的权重」怎样影响该房间的总分。

words.enDefinition: an activity essential to keeping an organisation able to operate

examples.en: The case identified equipment collection as a critical business function during the move to another building.
examples.zh: 案例把器材领取列为搬到另一栋楼期间的「关键业务职能」。

examples.en: Our group had to justify why taking bookings was a critical business function for the workshop.
examples.zh: 我们小组要说明，对于工作坊来说，接受预约为什么是「关键业务职能」。

words.enDefinition: a resource or service that an important activity relies on

examples.en: Access to the shared kitchen was a critical dependency for the catering project in our case.
examples.zh: 在我们的案例里，能否使用共享厨房是配餐项目的「关键依赖项」。

examples.en: The lecturer asked us to identify a critical dependency outside the repair team's direct control.
examples.zh: 讲师让我们找出一个维修团队无法直接控制的「关键依赖项」。

words.enDefinition: To compare what interviewees said with other accounts or records to see whether they agree.

examples.en: We took time to cross-check interview accounts before describing how each site recorded late collections.
examples.zh: 说明各场点怎样记录迟领之前，我们专门「交叉核对了访谈说法」。

examples.en: Our adviser asked us to cross-check interview accounts with the dates in the volunteer log.
examples.zh: 指导老师请我们结合志愿者日志里的日期「交叉核对访谈说法」。

collocations: cross-check interview accounts before drawing conclusions

words.enDefinition: organising interdependent work between people in different functions

examples.en: Cross-functional coordination helped the design, finance, and packing teams agree on a date for the change.
examples.zh: 通过「跨职能协调」，设计、财务和打包团队商定了变更日期。

examples.en: The lecturer asked how the new reporting arrangements might affect cross-functional coordination during the busy term.
examples.zh: 讲师问，新的汇报安排会怎样影响繁忙学期的「跨职能协调」。

words.enDefinition: exchanging information between people who work at different times in the same operation

examples.en: The team improved cross-shift communication by keeping notes where both crews could read them.
examples.zh: 团队把记录放在两班人都能看到的地方，改进了「跨班次沟通」。

examples.en: We discussed cross-shift communication after the evening crew opened the wrong collection shelf twice.
examples.zh: 晚班两次开错自取货架后，我们讨论了怎么做好「跨班次沟通」。

words.enDefinition: using revenue from one offering to support a different one

examples.en: The student cinema used a cross-subsidy from weekend screenings to keep weekday tickets affordable.
examples.zh: 学生影院用周末放映的收入提供「交叉补贴」，让工作日的票价保持实惠。

examples.en: Our plan used a cross-subsidy so that full-price repairs could support a reduced rate for bursary recipients.
examples.zh: 我们计划用全价维修业务提供「交叉补贴」，让领助学金的同学能享受较低收费。

words.enDefinition: to teach workers to carry out tasks in more than one role or area

examples.en: We wanted to cross-train staff so the stall could stay open if someone was absent.
examples.zh: 我们想「给员工做跨岗位培训」，这样有人缺勤时摊位也能营业。

examples.en: The owner agreed to cross-train staff in order collection and the preparation of stock labels.
examples.zh: 店主同意「给员工做跨岗位培训」，涵盖自取和制作库存标签。

words.enDefinition: A review of how a process, service, or organisation works before any proposed change is made.

examples.en: Our current-state assessment showed how the same request passed through three different desks at the theatre.
examples.zh: 「现状评估」显示，同一项申请在剧院内要经过三个不同的服务台。

examples.en: The current-state assessment included interviews and a review of one month's group booking records.
examples.zh: 「现状评估」包括访谈，以及查阅一个月的团体预约记录。

words.enDefinition: A customer request to change an item for their particular needs

examples.en: A custom request came in for a notebook with two initials on the cover.
examples.zh: 有人提了个「定制需求」，想给笔记本封面印两个姓名首字母。

examples.en: I checked the custom request before choosing which color of thread to use.
examples.zh: 选用哪种颜色的线之前，我核对了「定制需求」。

words.enDefinition: the average cost of gaining one new customer

examples.en: Our tutor asked why customer acquisition cost rose after the student café paid for local advertising.
examples.zh: 学生咖啡馆付费做本地广告后，导师问为什么「获客成本」上升了。

examples.en: The small print shop calculated customer acquisition cost using the expenses linked to finding new buyers.
examples.zh: 小型打印店根据寻找新买家的相关开支计算「获客成本」。

words.enDefinition: learning directly from potential customers to test assumptions about their needs and behaviour

examples.en: We did customer discovery before deciding whether to develop an equipment booking service for students.
examples.zh: 我们先做「客户需求探索」，再决定要不要为学生开发设备预约服务。

examples.en: The entrepreneurship course set aside two weeks for customer discovery in nearby shops and cafés.
examples.zh: 创业课程安排了两周时间，让大家到附近的商店和咖啡馆做「客户需求探索」。

words.enDefinition: a belief to be tested about who might use, buy or benefit from a proposed offering

examples.en: Our customer hypothesis focused on society organisers who already run several events each term.
examples.zh: 我们「关于目标客户的假设」聚焦于每学期已经办好几场活动的社团组织者。

examples.en: The interviews challenged our customer hypothesis about who would pay for a short equipment rental.
examples.zh: 访谈动摇了我们「关于目标客户的假设」，原先以为会付费短租设备的人可能不同。

words.enDefinition: an estimate of the economic value a business expects from a customer over the entire relationship, sometimes based on revenue and sometimes on profit

examples.en: Our team estimated customer lifetime value for students likely to keep using the equipment lending service.
examples.zh: 团队估算了可能继续使用设备借用服务的学生的「客户终身价值」。

examples.en: The tutor said our customer lifetime value estimate assumed members would stay for three academic terms.
examples.zh: 导师说，我们估算「客户终身价值」时假设会员会留下三个学期。

collocations: compare customer lifetime value across groups

words.enDefinition: watching how customers behave to learn what they do in practice

examples.en: Our customer observation showed that people often skipped the instructions printed beside the rental desk.
examples.zh: 「客户行为观察」表明，人们往往不会看租赁服务台旁印着的说明。

examples.en: We used customer observation to learn where visitors stopped while trying to find our stall.
examples.zh: 我们通过「客户行为观察」了解访客找摊位时会在哪些地方停下来。

words.enDefinition: the profit a venture earns from serving a particular customer

examples.en: We checked customer profitability after noticing that some large orders needed repeated visits for alterations.
examples.zh: 发现一些大单得反复上门修改后，我们检查了「客户盈利性」。

examples.en: The tutor explained customer profitability using the revenue and service costs of two typical club accounts.
examples.zh: 导师用两个典型社团客户的收入和服务成本解释了「客户盈利性」。

words.enDefinition: the ways a venture interacts with and supports customers

examples.en: The pottery team put personal help with glazing under customer relationships on its canvas.
examples.zh: 陶艺小组在画布的「客户关系」栏里填了为顾客提供上釉指导。

examples.en: Our advisor asked how customer relationships would change if the booking service became fully automated.
examples.zh: 导师问，如果预订服务完全自动化，「客户关系」会有什么变化。

words.enDefinition: A regular count of a selected part of the inventory

examples.en: We did a cycle count of the notebooks instead of counting every product again.
examples.zh: 我们只对笔记本做了次「循环盘点」，所有商品都重数一遍就免了。

examples.en: The cycle count this week will cover the cards kept in the studio cupboard.
examples.zh: 本周的「循环盘点」会数工作室柜子里的卡片。

words.enDefinition: the elapsed time to complete one repeated unit of work or operation

examples.en: We measured cycle time for printing one badge so we could plan our staffing.
examples.zh: 我们测量了印一枚徽章的「周期时间」，以便安排人手。

examples.en: The cycle time fell after we moved frequently used supplies closer to the table.
examples.zh: 常用物资移到桌边之后，「周期时间」缩短了。

words.enDefinition: the maximum amount of work an operation can handle in a day under given conditions

examples.en: Our daily capacity fell once two repair benches were needed for a different event.
examples.zh: 两张维修台被调去办另一场活动，我们的「日处理能力」下降了。

examples.en: We calculated the daily capacity before setting a limit on bookings for the workshop.
examples.zh: 我们先计算「日处理能力」，再给工作坊设定预约上限。

words.enDefinition: Goods in storage that have been harmed and may be unsellable

examples.en: We put damaged stock in a separate crate so it couldn't be sold accidentally.
examples.zh: 我们把「破损库存」放进另一个周转箱，防止误卖。

examples.en: The ceramics crew checked for damaged stock before folding the tables for the night.
examples.zh: 陶艺组当晚收折叠桌前，先检查有没有「破损库存」。

words.enDefinition: Missing information that limits what can be analysed or concluded from existing records.

examples.en: A data gap made it difficult to compare bookings confirmed before and after the holiday.
examples.zh: 有一处「数据缺口」，因此很难对比假期前后确认的预约。

examples.en: We mentioned the data gap upfront because the museum had no figures for weekend school visits.
examples.zh: 博物馆没有周末学校团体来访的数据，所以我们一开始就指出了「数据缺口」。

words.enDefinition: a weakness in available data that affects what conclusions can reasonably be drawn

examples.en: One data limitation was that the report combined returns from both stores into one total.
examples.zh: 一项「数据局限」是报告把两家门店的退货量合成一个总数。

examples.en: We noted the data limitation beside our estimate so readers could see what was uncertain.
examples.zh: 我们在估计值旁注明了「数据局限」，让读者知道哪里有不确定性。

words.enDefinition: the amount charged for a day of work

examples.en: The student photographer quoted a day rate to cover the tournament from morning until evening.
examples.zh: 学生摄影师为从早到晚拍摄赛事报出了「按日收费标准」。

examples.en: We included the editor's day rate when comparing different ways to produce the short conference video.
examples.zh: 比较会议短片的不同制作方案时，我们把剪辑师的「按日收费标准」算了进去。

words.enDefinition: The person you speak with about ordinary questions or scheduling at the partner organisation.

examples.en: Sara was our day-to-day contact at the gallery while we reviewed its visitor booking process.
examples.zh: 我们审查画廊访客预约流程期间，萨拉是我们在画廊的「日常联络人」。

examples.en: We sent small scheduling questions to our day-to-day contact instead of waiting for the review meeting.
examples.zh: 遇到小的日程问题，我们发给「日常联络人」，不用等到评审会再问。

words.enDefinition: Goods that have remained unsold and are unlikely to sell

examples.en: The old event shirts became dead stock once that year's design was replaced.
examples.zh: 活动 T 恤的旧款被当年新设计替换后，就成了「积压滞销库存」。

examples.en: I found two boxes of dead stock while clearing the studio for next term.
examples.zh: 我在收拾工作室准备下学期用时，发现了两箱「积压滞销库存」。

words.enDefinition: shifting decision-making authority away from the centre to local units

examples.en: Decentralisation gave each workshop more freedom to decide which equipment it should repair first.
examples.zh: 「分权化」让各工作坊能更自主地决定先修哪些设备。

examples.en: In the case, decentralisation helped branch managers respond to problems without waiting for head office.
examples.zh: 案例中的「分权化」让分店经理不必等总部就能应对问题。

words.enDefinition: a teaching case that asks learners to recommend a choice facing a person or organisation

examples.en: The decision case ended before the manager chose whether to open a second repair booth.
examples.zh: 「决策型案例」在经理决定是否开第二个维修摊位之前结束。

examples.en: In the decision case, we had to choose between relocating the shop and staying near campus.
examples.zh: 在这个「决策型案例」中，我们得在搬店和留在校园附近之间作选择。

words.enDefinition: a planned point at which progress and evidence are reviewed before a later decision is taken

examples.en: We scheduled a decision checkpoint after the first ten orders in the autumn trial.
examples.zh: 我们把秋季试点完成头十笔订单的时点设为「决策检查点」。

examples.en: The next decision checkpoint gave us time to compare feedback from both collection locations.
examples.zh: 下一次「决策检查点」让我们有时间比较两处自取点的反馈。

words.enDefinition: the factors or standards used to judge and compare possible choices

examples.en: Our decision criteria included setup cost, staff time and how easily students could reach the stall.
examples.zh: 我们的「决策标准」包括布置成本、工时和学生到摊位的便利程度。

examples.en: The group agreed on decision criteria before reading any of the detailed proposals from suppliers.
examples.zh: 小组在阅读供应商的详细方案之前先商定了「决策标准」。

words.enDefinition: the latest time by which a choice must be made

examples.en: The decision deadline was Friday because the owner had to reply to the landlord that afternoon.
examples.zh: 「决策截止时间」是周五，因为店主得在当天下午给房东答复。

examples.en: We moved the decision deadline after the supplier agreed to hold the quote for another week.
examples.zh: 供应商同意把报价再保留一周，我们相应调整了「决策截止时间」。

words.enDefinition: a situation requiring a choice between options with substantial or conflicting drawbacks

examples.en: The decision dilemma was whether to lower prices or keep enough income to staff the counter.
examples.zh: 团队面临的「决策两难」是降价，还是保住给柜台配备员工所需的收入。

examples.en: Our tutor asked us to explain the decision dilemma before suggesting an answer to the case.
examples.zh: 导师请我们先说明「决策两难」体现在哪里，再为案例提出解决办法。

words.enDefinition: a value entered in a simulation to represent a choice controlled by the participant

examples.en: We entered the new price as a decision input before running the simulation a second time.
examples.zh: 第二次运行模拟前，我们把新价格作为「决策输入项」填了进去。

examples.en: We entered the number of workers assigned to repairs as a decision input for Saturday.
examples.zh: 我们把周六安排去维修的人数作为「决策输入项」填了进去。

words.enDefinition: a person or group with authority to choose what action to take

examples.en: The brief said the decision maker was the founder, even though the manager had prepared the figures.
examples.zh: 简报写明「决策者」是创始人，尽管数据是经理准备的。

examples.en: Our group asked whether the decision maker could change the opening hours without consulting the board.
examples.zh: 我们小组问，「决策者」能不能在不征求董事会意见的情况下调整营业时间。

words.enDefinition: a table that records how each option rates against each criterion, with weights when needed

examples.en: Our decision matrix compared three venues by cost, equipment, location and available opening hours.
examples.zh: 我们用「决策矩阵」比较三个场地的成本、设备、地点和可开放时段。

examples.en: The decision matrix made it clear why the cheapest room had not scored highest.
examples.zh: 「决策矩阵」说明了为什么最便宜的房间得分并非最高。

words.enDefinition: a concise document recording a decision, its rationale and relevant next steps

examples.en: The manager circulated a decision memo after choosing to keep the current collection point.
examples.zh: 经理决定保留现有自取点后，传阅了一份「决策备忘录」。

examples.en: Our decision memo explained why the business had selected a smaller space near the library.
examples.zh: 我们的「决策备忘录」说明了企业为什么选图书馆附近较小的场地。

collocations: record a choice in a decision memo

words.enDefinition: a point in a decision tree where a decision maker chooses among actions

examples.en: We marked the decision node where the owner could renew the lease or move elsewhere.
examples.zh: 我们标出了「决策节点」，店主要在这里选择续租还是搬去别处。

examples.en: Before adding the costs, I checked whether we had labelled the correct decision node.
examples.zh: 加上成本之前，我核对了有没有把正确的「决策节点」标出来。

words.enDefinition: the result a decision is intended to achieve

examples.en: Our main decision objective was to reduce the waiting time without increasing the team's weekly costs.
examples.zh: 我们主要的「决策目标」是在不增加团队每周成本的情况下缩短等待时间。

examples.en: The group changed its decision objective after learning that the shop already had enough customers.
examples.zh: 得知店铺已有足够多的顾客后，小组更改了「决策目标」。

words.enDefinition: a result that follows a decision, sometimes depending on events outside the decision maker's control

examples.en: We could not know the decision outcome until students tried the new pickup hours.
examples.zh: 要等学生试过新的自取时段，我们才知道「决策结果」。

examples.en: The case compared each possible decision outcome with what the manager had originally hoped to achieve.
examples.zh: 案例把每一种可能的「决策结果」与经理原先希望达到的结果作了比较。

words.enDefinition: a moment or stage when someone must choose which action to take next

examples.en: The case reached a decision point when the landlord offered a different unit for the workshop.
examples.zh: 房东为工作室提供另一个铺位时，案例到了「决策时点」。

examples.en: We stopped reading at the decision point and wrote down our preferred course of action.
examples.zh: 我们读到「决策时点」就停下来，记下了自己倾向的做法。

words.enDefinition: the reasoning that explains why a particular choice was made

examples.en: The decision rationale explained why student access mattered more than the lowest possible rent.
examples.zh: 「决策理由」说明了为什么方便学生到达比把租金压到最低更重要。

examples.en: The lecturer asked whether the decision rationale still held if the evening classes moved online.
examples.zh: 讲师问，如果晚课改到线上，「决策理由」是否依然成立。

words.enDefinition: The authority different people or groups have to make particular project decisions.

examples.en: The project charter clarified decision rights for changing the questions we planned to ask volunteers.
examples.zh: 项目章程明确了有哪些人有权改志愿者访谈问题，也就是这方面的「决策权限」。

examples.en: We discussed decision rights after two managers gave different advice about testing the new form.
examples.zh: 两位经理对测试新表格给出不同意见后，我们讨论了「决策权限」。

collocations: record decision rights in the charter

words.enDefinition: a level or condition at which the preferred choice or recommended action changes

examples.en: The team chose a decision threshold of fifty bookings before paying for the larger room.
examples.zh: 团队把五十笔预约设为「决策阈值」，达到后才付费租用较大的房间。

examples.en: We compared the forecast with our decision threshold before recommending whether to keep the evening service.
examples.zh: 在建议是否保留晚间服务前，我们把预测值和「决策阈值」作了比较。

words.enDefinition: a branching diagram showing choices, uncertain events and possible outcomes

examples.en: We drew a decision tree to compare what could happen if the club ordered early.
examples.zh: 我们画了「决策树」，比较社团提前下单后可能出现的不同结果。

examples.en: The decision tree showed two possible outcomes after the manager chose the larger space.
examples.zh: 「决策树」标出了经理选择较大场地后可能出现的两种结果。

words.enDefinition: a choice made when relevant conditions or possible outcomes are not fully known

examples.en: The case illustrated a decision under uncertainty because no one could predict demand after the holiday.
examples.zh: 这是个「不确定条件下的决策」案例，因为没人能预测假期后的需求。

examples.en: We modelled the decision under uncertainty using two plausible levels of customer demand for the next term.
examples.zh: 我们采用下学期两种可能的需求水平，模拟了「不确定条件下的决策」。

words.enDefinition: A place set aside for the supplies or equipment of one group or project.

examples.en: The workshop offered dedicated storage for our large boards between the two exhibition dates.
examples.zh: 两场展览之间，工场为我们的大展板提供了「专用存放空间」。

examples.en: Our team requested dedicated storage so unfinished signs would stay separate from the other group's tools.
examples.zh: 我们团队申请「专用存放空间」，好把没做完的标牌和另一组的工具分开放。

words.enDefinition: to explain why a recommended choice is sound when others question it

examples.en: I had to defend a recommendation the team made despite some uncertainty about customer demand.
examples.zh: 尽管顾客需求还不确定，我得「为团队的建议说明理由」。

examples.en: The judges asked our group to defend a recommendation using the figures in the case packet.
examples.zh: 评审请我们小组用案例材料包里的数据「为这项建议说明理由」。

collocations: be prepared to defend a recommendation
use evidence to defend a recommendation

words.enDefinition: the removal of one or more levels of management

examples.en: The case company considered delayering after finding that routine requests passed through three levels of approval.
examples.zh: 案例公司发现日常申请要经过三级审批，于是考虑「减少管理层级」。

examples.en: Our group discussed whether delayering would put too much responsibility on the remaining branch managers.
examples.zh: 我们小组讨论了「减少管理层级」会不会让留下的分店经理承担过多责任。

words.enDefinition: power officially passed to another person or unit to act

examples.en: The branch lead used delegated authority to approve the replacement of a broken display table.
examples.zh: 分店负责人用「下放的权限」批准更换坏掉的展示桌。

examples.en: We reviewed delegated authority after both departments assumed they could sign off on the purchase.
examples.zh: 两个部门都认为自己能批准采购后，我们重新核对了「下放的权限」。

words.enDefinition: To provide the promised work or materials in the way and at the time agreed.

examples.en: The student studio confirmed it could still deliver as agreed after replacing one of the materials.
examples.zh: 换了一种材料后，学生工作室确认仍可以「按约定交付」。

examples.en: We asked whether the team could deliver as agreed despite the change of venue on Friday.
examples.zh: 虽然周五换了场地，我们还是询问团队是否能「按约定交付」。

collocations: be ready to deliver as agreed
make sure we can deliver as agreed

words.enDefinition: To hand over parts of agreed work at separate times as successive stages are completed.

examples.en: The printer agreed to deliver in stages so we could check the programmes before the banners.
examples.zh: 印刷店同意「分阶段交付」，这样我们能先验手册，再验横幅。

examples.en: We decided to deliver in stages because the floor plans were ready before the display labels.
examples.zh: 因为平面图比展品标签先准备好，我们决定「分阶段交付」。

words.enDefinition: The date by which a particular agreed item or piece of work needs to be provided.

examples.en: The deliverable due date was Friday because the programmes went to print the following Monday.
examples.zh: 「交付截止日」是周五，因为手册下周一就要送印。

examples.en: Our coordinator checked the deliverable due date before arranging the club's final review of the artwork.
examples.zh: 我们的协调员先确认了「交付截止日」，再安排社团最终审核图稿。

words.enDefinition: A list of the items, documents, or other results a team is expected to provide.

examples.en: We agreed on a deliverables list before asking the student studio for a design quote.
examples.zh: 请学生工作室为设计报价前，我们商定了「交付物清单」。

examples.en: The gallery checked the deliverables list to see whether social media graphics were included too.
examples.zh: 画廊查了「交付物清单」，看看是否也包含社交媒体用图。

words.enDefinition: The file type, physical form, or other format in which agreed work will be provided.

examples.en: We agreed on the delivery format before the photographer edited the images for our catalogue.
examples.zh: 摄影师为我们的目录修图之前，我们先商定了「交付格式」。

examples.en: The brief described the delivery format for both the digital posters and the printed handouts.
examples.zh: 任务书说明了电子海报和纸质讲义各自的「交付格式」。

words.enDefinition: A trip during which someone delivers goods to several customers

examples.en: We finished the delivery round before heading back to campus for our lecture.
examples.zh: 我们跑完「一轮送货行程」，就回学校上课了。

examples.en: I added a stop to the delivery round when the other seller called.
examples.zh: 另一名摊商打来电话时，我给「这轮送货行程」加了一站。

words.enDefinition: The amount by which a delivery falls short of the order

examples.en: We tracked the delivery shortfall after only half our thank-you cards arrived on Monday.
examples.zh: 周一只收到一半感谢卡后，我们记下了「少交付的数量」。

examples.en: The supplier offered to make up the delivery shortfall before Saturday's student market.
examples.zh: 供应商说会在周六学生市集之前「把少交的货」补齐。

words.enDefinition: an event at which teams demonstrate their ventures or products to an invited audience

examples.en: We prepared three working examples for demo day at the end of the accelerator programme.
examples.zh: 加速器项目结束时有「创业项目展示日」，我们为此准备了三个能运行的演示案例。

examples.en: The audience asked about testing after our team showed the prototype on demo day.
examples.zh: 我们团队在「创业项目展示日」拿出原型后，观众问了测试情况。

words.enDefinition: An item kept out to show customers how a product works

examples.en: We brought one demo unit so visitors could try the folding book stand.
examples.zh: 我们带了一个「演示用样品」，让来逛的人试用折叠书架。

examples.en: The demo unit let people hear what the little wooden speaker sounded like.
examples.zh: 顾客可以用「演示用样品」试听小木音箱的声音。

collocations: keep a demo unit on the table

words.enDefinition: a short recording showing how a product, service or prototype works

examples.en: We filmed a demo video so the panel could review our prototype after the presentation.
examples.zh: 我们录了「演示视频」，评审组在介绍结束后可以回看我们的原型。

examples.en: The demo video followed a student from making a booking to collecting the borrowed equipment.
examples.zh: 「演示视频」跟拍了一名学生从预约到领取借用器材的过程。

words.enDefinition: grouping jobs into departments by shared characteristics or responsibilities

examples.en: We discussed departmentalisation by product after reading a case about a campus equipment supplier.
examples.zh: 读过校园设备供应商的案例后，我们讨论了按产品进行「部门划分」。

examples.en: The lecturer asked whether departmentalisation by location would help the fictional retailer serve local customers.
examples.zh: 讲师问，按地点做「部门划分」能不能让虚构的零售商更好地服务当地顾客。

words.enDefinition: A document explaining what a design should achieve and listing its key requirements and constraints.

examples.en: The design brief asked for a poster that could be read from across the entrance hall.
examples.zh: 「设计任务书」要求海报从入口大厅对面也能看清。

examples.en: We asked the gallery to check the design brief before our team drafted the new signs.
examples.zh: 我们团队开始画新标牌草稿之前，请画廊核对了「设计任务书」。

words.enDefinition: a user or organisation that works closely with a team to shape a product during development

examples.en: The library became a design partner and helped us test the checkout screen with students.
examples.zh: 图书馆成为「设计合作伙伴」，帮我们和学生一起测试借用界面。

examples.en: As a design partner, the cycling club offered regular feedback on each version of the repair kit.
examples.zh: 骑行社作为「设计合作伙伴」，定期对每一版维修套件提出意见。

words.enDefinition: An observation supported by evidence from an investigation into how or why a problem occurs.

examples.en: The report listed a diagnostic finding about replies that staff drafted without ever sending them.
examples.zh: 报告列出一项「问题诊断所得的发现」，有些回复工作人员写了却一直没发。

examples.en: We shared a diagnostic finding about room changes before recommending a new reminder process.
examples.zh: 建议更改提醒流程前，我们分享了一项关于换房间的「问题诊断所得的发现」。

words.enDefinition: The period when a team analyses evidence to explain what is causing the problem.

examples.en: The diagnostic phase showed that most missed appointments came from a gap in the reminder process.
examples.zh: 「问题诊断阶段」发现，大多数爽约是预约提醒流程有缺漏造成的。

examples.en: We used the diagnostic phase to determine why theatre requests were answered faster at one site.
examples.zh: 我们在「问题诊断阶段」查明，为什么剧院有一个场点处理申请更快。

collocations: conduct interviews during the diagnostic phase

words.enDefinition: a competitive approach centred on distinct features or benefits

examples.en: The café chose a differentiation strategy based on reliable delivery to buildings outside the main campus.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆选择「差异化战略」，特色是可靠地把餐食送到主校区以外的楼宇。

examples.en: Our instructor asked which parts of the service supported the company's differentiation strategy in the case.
examples.zh: 授课老师问，案例中服务的哪些环节支撑了公司的「差异化战略」。

words.enDefinition: selling directly to shoppers without an independent retailer

examples.en: The student label chose a direct-to-consumer approach and sold its tote bags through its own website.
examples.zh: 学生品牌采用「直接面向消费者的」做法，通过自家网站卖帆布袋。

examples.en: Our direct-to-consumer sales brought the pottery team into regular contact with buyers at weekend markets.
examples.zh: 我们「直接面向消费者的」销售方式让陶艺小组经常在周末市集接触买家。

words.enDefinition: information that counts against a claim or assumption instead of supporting it

examples.en: We looked for disconfirming evidence before accepting the owner's explanation for the fall in sales.
examples.zh: 相信店主对销量下降的解释前，我们先找了「反驳该解释的证据」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether any disconfirming evidence appeared in the tables attached to the case.
examples.zh: 导师问，案例附表里有没有「反驳假设的证据」。

words.enDefinition: a conversation aimed at learning about someone's current problems, needs and behaviour

examples.en: In the discovery interview, I asked how the organiser currently lent equipment to new members.
examples.zh: 在「需求探索访谈」中，我问组织者，现在是怎么把器材借给新成员的。

examples.en: We changed our next discovery interview after realising we had been talking too much ourselves.
examples.zh: 我们发现自己说得太多，就调整了下一次「需求探索访谈」的做法。

collocations: record notes from a discovery interview

words.enDefinition: The early stage of a project in which the team learns about the organisation and the problem.

examples.en: During the discovery phase we read the charity's guides and learned how it allocated appointments.
examples.zh: 「初步了解阶段」，我们读了慈善机构的指南，了解了他们怎样分配预约。

examples.en: The discovery phase took longer because both theatre sites had different ways of recording cancellations.
examples.zh: 两个剧院场点记录取消预约的方式不同，「初步了解阶段」因此花了更长时间。

words.enDefinition: A stand that holds a sign or picture upright for viewing

examples.en: A small display easel held the club's poster at the front of the stall.
examples.zh: 一架小「陈列画架」在摊位前支着社团的海报。

examples.en: I brought a display easel to show the larger of my two prints.
examples.zh: 我带了一个「陈列画架」，展示我两幅版画中较大的那幅。

collocations: prop something up on a display easel

words.enDefinition: A hook used to hang items where shoppers can see them

examples.en: I hung the key chains from a display hook beside the handwritten sign.
examples.zh: 我把钥匙扣挂在手写招牌旁的「商品陈列挂钩」上。

examples.en: The earrings were light enough to share a single display hook on the board.
examples.zh: 耳环够轻，可以几副一起挂在板上的同一个「陈列挂钩」上。

collocations: hang an item on a display hook

words.enDefinition: Goods kept in the selling area to be seen by customers

examples.en: We moved the display stock inside when rain started blowing across the tables.
examples.zh: 雨开始随风扫到桌上时，我们就把「陈列中的货」搬进了室内。

examples.en: The last two journals we sold came from the display stock on the shelf.
examples.zh: 我们卖掉的最后两本手账是从架上的「陈列商品」里拿的。

words.enDefinition: A shallow container used to arrange products so customers can see them

examples.en: We kept the little badges in a display tray next to the mirror.
examples.zh: 我们把小徽章放在镜子旁边的「商品陈列托盘」里。

examples.en: I switched to a divided display tray so the colors would stay separate.
examples.zh: 我换了一个带隔格的「陈列托盘」，免得不同颜色的货混在一起。

collocations: arrange items in a display tray

words.enDefinition: an arrangement with separate units for products, regions, or customer groups

examples.en: The case company moved to a divisional structure when it began serving two very different regions.
examples.zh: 开始服务两个差异很大的地区后，案例公司改用了「事业部制结构」。

examples.en: We drew a divisional structure with one division for repairs and another for equipment hire.
examples.zh: 我们画了一个「事业部制结构」，一部负责维修，另一部负责设备出租。

words.enDefinition: Tools or equipment given to a group for it to keep and use.

examples.en: The student workshop received donated equipment when a print shop cleared out its old studio.
examples.zh: 一家印刷店清理旧工作室时，给了学生工场一批「获赠设备」。

examples.en: The organiser checked the donated equipment against the list before adding it to the shared studio.
examples.zh: 组织者先把「获赠设备」与清单核对，再把设备放进共用工作室。

words.enDefinition: Supplies or raw materials given freely to support a project or activity.

examples.en: The student studio used donated materials to make signs for the community repair event.
examples.zh: 学生工作室用「捐赠的材料」制作社区维修活动的指示牌。

examples.en: We sorted the donated materials before deciding what to use for the workshop demonstrations.
examples.zh: 我们先整理了「捐赠的材料」，再决定工作坊演示用哪些。

collocations: credit the source of donated materials

words.enDefinition: Professional work or practical help provided free of charge as a contribution.

examples.en: The event team listed donated services such as photography and basic editing in its final report.
examples.zh: 活动团队在最终报告中列出了摄影和简单剪辑等「获赠的服务」。

examples.en: We budgeted for printing separately because the donated services only covered the design work.
examples.zh: 我们单独给印刷留了预算，因为「获赠的服务」只包括设计。

words.enDefinition: a secondary reporting relationship, usually with less direct authority

examples.en: The case used dotted-line reporting so a regional lead could advise staff outside her direct team.
examples.zh: 案例采用「虚线汇报关系」，让地区负责人能够指导直属团队以外的员工。

examples.en: Our tutor showed dotted-line reporting between the designer and the project manager on the chart.
examples.zh: 导师在图上标出了设计师和项目经理之间的「虚线汇报关系」。

words.enDefinition: a plausible outcome worse than the main forecast

examples.en: In our downside scenario, fewer societies rented speakers and several large bookings moved to next term.
examples.zh: 我们的「不利情景」是假设租音箱的社团变少，几笔大单还推迟到下学期。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether we had included a downside scenario for a semester with weak demand.
examples.zh: 导师问，我们有没有纳入一个学期需求低迷的「不利情景」。

words.enDefinition: a record of periods when equipment or an operation could not be used as planned

examples.en: The downtime log showed how long the label printer was unavailable during the morning shift.
examples.zh: 「停工记录」显示，标签打印机在早班期间有多久不能用。

examples.en: Our supervisor checked the downtime log before deciding which equipment needed attention this week.
examples.zh: 主管先查看「停工记录」，再决定本周哪些设备需要处理。

words.enDefinition: An order prepared but not yet finalised as a customer purchase

examples.en: I saved a draft order while the customer decided which notebook cover they wanted.
examples.zh: 顾客还在选要哪个笔记本封面，我就先保存了「订单草稿」。

examples.en: The draft order was still open when we got the correct spelling of her name.
examples.zh: 收到她名字的正确拼写时，「订单草稿」还没定稿。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement in which someone reports to two managers

examples.en: Under dual reporting, the analyst reported to the finance manager and the campus project director.
examples.zh: 实行「双重汇报」时，分析员要向财务经理和校园项目负责人汇报。

examples.en: The case company tried dual reporting after several teams began sharing the same design staff.
examples.zh: 几个团队开始共用同一批设计人员后，案例公司尝试了「双重汇报」。

words.enDefinition: Entering the same information more than once, or an extra record created in that way.

examples.en: We found a duplicate entry when the museum recorded one school group under two booking dates.
examples.zh: 博物馆把同一个学校团体登记在两个预约日期下，我们发现了这条「重复录入」的记录。

examples.en: The new form reduced duplicate entry by letting both desks refer to the same record.
examples.zh: 新表格让两个服务台共用同一条记录，减少了「重复录入」。

words.enDefinition: a manager responsible for overseeing a business or location during a particular period

examples.en: The duty manager moved two employees to the entrance when the queue reached the stairs.
examples.zh: 队伍排到了楼梯口，「值班经理」便调了两名员工到入口。

examples.en: We contacted the duty manager before changing the opening time on the noticeboard outside.
examples.zh: 我们先联系了「值班经理」，才修改室外公告栏上的开门时间。

words.enDefinition: a schedule listing who is assigned to particular duties or times

examples.en: I checked the duty roster to find out who was looking after the display that afternoon.
examples.zh: 我看了「值班表」，查当天下午谁负责展示台。

examples.en: The new duty roster put a second person on collection during the lunch break.
examples.zh: 新「值班表」在午餐时段增加了一名负责取货的人。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement allowing selected users or the public to try a product before its general release

examples.en: I joined the early access programme so I could use the tool for our club's events.
examples.zh: 我参加了「提前体验计划」，这样就能在社团活动中用这个工具。

examples.en: The group started an early access programme to collect feedback before the next public release.
examples.zh: 小组启动了「提前体验计划」，准备在下一次公开发布前收集意见。

words.enDefinition: someone who starts using a new product or service before most people do

examples.en: An early adopter used our equipment booking service every week and suggested several changes.
examples.zh: 一位「早期采用者」每周都用设备预约服务，还提了好几项修改建议。

examples.en: We asked an early adopter why she had tried the service before her friends did.
examples.zh: 我们问一位「早期采用者」，她为什么比朋友更早试用这项服务。

words.enDefinition: Information showing who started using a change and how it was used soon after introduction.

examples.en: The early adoption data showed more weekend volunteers used the booking form than we expected.
examples.zh: 「初期使用数据」显示，用预约表的周末志愿者比我们预计的多。

examples.en: We checked early adoption data before asking why one site kept using the old booking list.
examples.zh: 询问为什么有一个场点还在用旧预约名单前，我们看了「初期使用数据」。

collocations: share early adoption data with the team

words.enDefinition: how many of the people who try a new product keep using it after their first use

examples.en: We tracked early user retention by checking who made another booking during the following month.
examples.zh: 我们查看接下来一个月谁又预约了，以跟踪「早期用户留存」。

examples.en: The mentor asked about early user retention because the first week had many one-time users.
examples.zh: 第一周很多人只用过一次，所以顾问询问了「早期用户留存」情况。

words.enDefinition: lower average costs achieved as output expands

examples.en: Our student print shop gained economies of scale by spreading setup costs over more notebooks.
examples.zh: 学生打印店把开印成本分摊到更多笔记本上，获得了「规模经济」效应。

examples.en: The tutor asked why economies of scale might be harder to achieve for individual music lessons.
examples.zh: 导师问，为什么一对一音乐课可能更难实现「规模经济」。

words.enDefinition: Original project files that someone can open in the appropriate software and modify.

examples.en: The designer included editable source files so the club could update names for future events.
examples.zh: 设计员附上了「可编辑的源文件」，这样社团能为以后的活动更新名字。

examples.en: We asked for editable source files when the gallery wanted to translate the signs later.
examples.zh: 画廊打算日后翻译标牌时，我们请对方提供「可编辑的源文件」。

words.enDefinition: Early findings that are becoming clear as an investigation continues.

examples.en: Our emerging findings suggested that the hardest step was finding a free room after school.
examples.zh: 我们「逐渐显现的调查结果」表明，最难的是放学后找到一间空房。

examples.en: The client asked about emerging findings after we finished visiting its second collection site.
examples.zh: 我们走访完第二个领取点之后，客户问起「逐渐显现的调查结果」。

collocations: share emerging findings with the client

words.enDefinition: a final summary that connects the main ideas, findings or viewpoints in a lesson

examples.en: The tutor's end-of-class synthesis connected our pricing debate to the shop's limited working hours.
examples.zh: 导师的「课堂结尾综合归纳」把我们对定价的讨论与店铺营业时间有限联系起来。

examples.en: I wrote down the end-of-class synthesis because it helped me understand why the recommendations differed.
examples.zh: 我记下了「课堂结尾的综合归纳」，因为它帮我理解了各项建议为何不同。

collocations: take notes on an end-of-class synthesis

words.enDefinition: a report prepared at the end of a shift that summarises what happened or remains unfinished

examples.en: The end-of-shift report listed the orders we had completed and one repair still in progress.
examples.zh: 「班末报告」列出了我们完成的订单，还有一件仍在维修的物品。

examples.en: I checked the end-of-shift report before contacting the customer who had left a bag behind.
examples.zh: 联系落下包的顾客之前，我查了「班末报告」。

words.enDefinition: the person who actually uses a product or service, who may be different from its purchaser

examples.en: We tested the kit with an end user after speaking to the person who orders supplies.
examples.zh: 和订购耗材的人谈过之后，我们请一位「最终使用者」测试了套件。

examples.en: The end user needed to read the instructions while keeping both hands on the equipment.
examples.zh: 「最终使用者」需要在双手都放在器材上的时候读说明。

words.enDefinition: The person who leads and coordinates the consulting team's work with a particular client.

examples.en: The engagement lead assigned someone to count bookings and someone else to arrange the visit.
examples.zh: 「咨询项目牵头人」安排一人统计预约，另一人协调参观。

examples.en: Each engagement lead reported to the instructor after the first client meeting of the term.
examples.zh: 学期的第一次客户会议结束后，每位「咨询项目牵头人」都向老师作了汇报。

collocations: ask the engagement lead to coordinate

words.enDefinition: an experienced entrepreneur affiliated with an institution to advise or work with its ventures

examples.en: The entrepreneur-in-residence held a drop-in session for teams preparing their first customer interviews that month.
examples.zh: 当月，「驻校创业导师」为准备首次客户访谈的团队办了一场无需预约的答疑。

examples.en: I asked the entrepreneur-in-residence how she had found customers when starting her first company.
examples.zh: 我问「驻校创业导师」，她开第一家公司时是怎么找到客户的。

words.enDefinition: the team member who leads the exploration of a project's potential as a business

examples.en: The entrepreneurial lead organised interviews with local businesses that could use the team's design.
examples.zh: 「创业转化负责人」安排了访谈，对象是可能使用该团队设计的本地企业。

examples.en: Our entrepreneurial lead reported what customers told us during the training programme each Friday.
examples.zh: 每到周五培训时，我们的「创业转化负责人」都会汇报从客户那里听到的情况。

words.enDefinition: a way of thinking that looks for opportunities and tests practical ways to act on them

examples.en: The tutor described an entrepreneurial mindset as looking for gaps and learning through small experiments.
examples.zh: 导师把「创业者思维」解释为发现缺口，并通过小实验学习。

examples.en: The project helped students practise an entrepreneurial mindset without asking them to start a company.
examples.zh: 项目让学生练习运用「创业者思维」，无需真的开公司。

words.enDefinition: a course on entrepreneurship that a student can choose as part of a programme

examples.en: My entrepreneurship elective asked us to talk to potential customers before designing a detailed solution.
examples.zh: 「创业选修课」要求我们先找潜在客户聊一聊，再详细设计解决办法。

examples.en: She took an entrepreneurship elective in her final year to learn how to test ideas.
examples.zh: 她最后一年修了「创业选修课」，学习怎样测试创意。

words.enDefinition: an organised series of activities that teaches people about developing and starting a venture

examples.en: The entrepreneurship programme gave students a chance to test ideas without immediately starting a company.
examples.zh: 「创业培养项目」给了学生测试创意的机会，可以不用马上开公司。

examples.en: I joined an entrepreneurship programme that met in the business school one evening a week.
examples.zh: 我参加了一个「创业培养项目」，每周有一晚在商学院上课。

words.enDefinition: An introductory session explaining what equipment is available and how it is used in a workspace.

examples.en: The studio offered an equipment orientation for student teams preparing to use the shared workspace.
examples.zh: 工作室向即将使用共用空间的学生团队提供了「设备使用介绍」。

examples.en: Our equipment orientation included a tour of the tools the display teams could reserve later.
examples.zh: 「设备使用介绍」包括带我们看一遍展示团队之后可以预约的工具。

collocations: offer equipment orientation to new users

words.enDefinition: A booking to use particular equipment at an agreed date or time.

examples.en: I made an equipment reservation for the large trimmer we needed to finish the posters.
examples.zh: 我做了「设备预约」，订了完成海报所需的大裁纸机。

examples.en: The studio coordinator confirmed our equipment reservation before telling us when to collect the kit.
examples.zh: 工作室协调员确认了我们的「设备预约」，再告诉我们什么时候去领器材。

words.enDefinition: A record showing who used equipment and when or how it was used.

examples.en: The studio checked its equipment use log to see which team used the projector last.
examples.zh: 工作室查了「设备使用记录」，看看最后用了投影仪的是哪个团队。

examples.en: I added our workshop time to the equipment use log before leaving the shared studio.
examples.zh: 离开共用工作室前，我把我们使用设备的时间填进了「设备使用记录」。

collocations: fill in the equipment use log

words.enDefinition: To record how something works or performs before making a change so later results have a reference.

examples.en: We used the last month's attendance totals to establish a baseline before testing the reminder text.
examples.zh: 我们用上月到场总人数「建立比较基线」，再测试提醒文案。

examples.en: The team needed to establish a baseline for wait times before suggesting any changes to reception.
examples.zh: 团队需要先为等待时间「建立比较基线」，再对接待流程提出调整建议。

collocations: establish a baseline before the trial
use existing data to establish a baseline
help the client establish a baseline

words.enDefinition: The expected amount of time needed to complete a job once the necessary materials are available.

examples.en: The student printer gave us an estimated turnaround after seeing the size of the display boards.
examples.zh: 学生运营的印刷店看到展板大小后，告诉了我们「预计完成所需时间」。

examples.en: The estimated turnaround changed because two of the files needed larger images before printing.
examples.zh: 其中两个文件要换成尺寸更大的图片才能印刷，所以「预计完成所需时间」变了。

words.enDefinition: Support such as money, goods, or services provided by a sponsor for a particular event.

examples.en: The ceramics club sought event sponsorship to cover the cost of printing its exhibition programme.
examples.zh: 陶艺社寻求「活动赞助」，用于支付展览手册的印刷费用。

examples.en: Event sponsorship helped the student organisers run a second workshop after the first one filled.
examples.zh: 首场工作坊满员后，「活动赞助」帮学生组织者加开了一场。

words.enDefinition: a recommendation grounded in relevant evidence rather than opinion alone

examples.en: Our tutor wanted an evidence-based recommendation that addressed the shortage of staff during the evening.
examples.zh: 导师希望给出一项「有证据支持的建议」，解决晚间人手不足的问题。

examples.en: We wrote an evidence-based recommendation after comparing seasonal sales and speaking to workers at both locations.
examples.zh: 我们比较了季节销售情况，还与两处员工交谈，之后写了一项「有证据支持的建议」。

words.enDefinition: A record that lets someone trace an observation or claim back to its supporting material.

examples.en: We kept an evidence trail so the client could trace each queue estimate to its source.
examples.zh: 我们保留了「可追溯的证据记录」，这样客户能查到每项排队估算的来源。

examples.en: The adviser checked our evidence trail before asking how many bookings we had excluded.
examples.zh: 指导老师查阅了「可追溯的证据记录」，再问我们排除了多少项预约。

collocations: check the evidence trail for a finding

words.enDefinition: the way an organisation handles cases that fall outside its normal procedure

examples.en: The supervisor taught exception handling for orders with missing names during our first training session.
examples.zh: 首次培训时，主管以缺少姓名的订单为例，讲解了「例外情况处理」。

examples.en: We reviewed exception handling after discovering that several visiting societies had no local contact number.
examples.zh: 发现几个来访社团没有本地联系电话后，我们重新检查了「例外情况处理」流程。

words.enDefinition: Use of the space by one group alone for an agreed period.

examples.en: We booked exclusive use of the space while two student groups recorded a joint performance.
examples.zh: 两个学生小组录制联演节目时，我们订了「单独使用该场地」的时段。

examples.en: The event organiser asked about exclusive use of the space during the launch on Friday.
examples.zh: 活动组织者问，周五发布会期间能否「单独使用该场地」。

collocations: book exclusive use of the space
ask about exclusive use of the space
pay for exclusive use of the space

words.zhGloss: 面向管理层的简明成果汇报
words.enDefinition: A short summary of findings or progress prepared for senior leaders who need to make decisions.
acceptedZhAnswers: 面向管理层的简明成果汇报

examples.en: The student team prepared an executive readout explaining the effect of the museum's current booking delays.
examples.zh: 学生团队准备了一份「面向管理层的简明成果汇报」，说明博物馆目前预约拖延带来的影响。

examples.en: The executive readout focused on the decision the charity's board needed to make that month.
examples.zh: 「面向管理层的简明成果汇报」聚焦慈善机构董事会当月需要作出的决定。

words.enDefinition: A senior person in an organisation who backs a project and helps it get attention and resources.

examples.en: The executive sponsor introduced us to the people who ran the museum's group booking service.
examples.zh: 「项目的高层支持者」把我们介绍给负责博物馆团体预约服务的人。

examples.en: Our executive sponsor attended the midpoint review and asked the department to share anonymised totals.
examples.zh: 我们的「项目高层支持者」参加了中期评审，请该部门共享匿名化的汇总数据。

words.enDefinition: a note explaining details, definitions or limitations in a chart or other exhibit

examples.en: The exhibit note explained that the table counted bookings rather than completed repair jobs.
examples.zh: 「附表或附图的注释」说明，表里统计的是预约数量，只凭这张表看不出修了多少件。

examples.en: I checked the exhibit note before comparing sales figures from the two different locations.
examples.zh: 比较两个地点的销售额之前，我读了「附表或附图的注释」。

words.enDefinition: A service carried out more quickly than the provider's ordinary process.

examples.en: We asked about expedited service when the organiser needed the new signs by Friday morning.
examples.zh: 组织者周五上午就要用新标牌，我们问了「加急服务」的事。

examples.en: The studio could offer expedited service for the labels after another small job was postponed.
examples.zh: 另一项小工作推迟后，工作室能为这批标签提供「加急服务」。

collocations: ask whether expedited service is available

words.zhGloss: 与指导老师的进度沟通
words.enDefinition: A brief meeting with a faculty adviser to discuss how the student project is going.
acceptedZhAnswers: 与指导老师的进度沟通

examples.en: We raised the missing weekend records at our faculty check-in before choosing a different comparison.
examples.zh: 我们在「与指导老师的进度沟通」中提到周末记录缺失，之后选了另一种比较方法。

examples.en: Our faculty check-in covered the client meeting and which findings were ready to share.
examples.zh: 「与指导老师的进度沟通」谈到了客户会议，以及哪些发现已经可以分享。

collocations: raise a concern at the faculty check-in

words.enDefinition: An effort to deliver an order that did not result in delivery

examples.en: I recorded a failed delivery attempt and asked the buyer to suggest another time.
examples.zh: 我登记了「一次投递未成功」的情况，请买家另提个时间。

examples.en: We brought the framed print back after a failed delivery attempt at the dorm.
examples.zh: 在宿舍「试送一次没送成」后，我们把带框版画带了回来。

collocations: reschedule after a failed delivery attempt

words.enDefinition: an experiment that did not produce the intended outcome or could not be completed as intended

examples.en: The team treated its failed experiment as evidence that the pickup process still needed work.
examples.zh: 团队把「失败的实验」视为一个信号，说明领取流程还有待改进。

examples.en: We wrote about the failed experiment in our report and explained why people had stopped halfway.
examples.zh: 我们在报告里写了这次「失败的实验」，也解释了为什么大家做到一半就停了。

words.enDefinition: a recommendation for what to do if the preferred choice becomes impossible or unsuitable

examples.en: Our fallback recommendation was to share the existing counter instead of renting the larger space.
examples.zh: 「备用建议」是共用现有柜台，不租那个更大的场地。

examples.en: I added a fallback recommendation because the store had not yet secured funding for repairs.
examples.zh: 店铺的维修经费还没落实，所以我补了一项「备用建议」。

words.enDefinition: a firm that enters shortly after a pioneer and learns from it

examples.en: The second printing service entered as a fast follower and added pickup hours students had requested.
examples.zh: 第二家打印服务商作为「快速跟随者」入场，增加了学生要求的取货时段。

examples.en: In the simulation, a fast follower could use what the first firm had learned about demand.
examples.zh: 模拟训练中，「快速跟随者」可以利用第一家企业对需求的了解。

words.enDefinition: a choice that can realistically be carried out with the available resources and time

examples.en: When the room closed earlier than expected, our only feasible option was to meet at noon.
examples.zh: 房间提前关闭后，我们唯一的「可行选项」是中午开会。

examples.en: The professor asked us to provide a feasible option within the shop's staffing and budget limits.
examples.zh: 教授请我们在店铺的人手与预算限制内提供一个「可行选项」。

words.enDefinition: comments about how well a particular part of a product works or meets users' needs

examples.en: We collected feature feedback on the calendar rather than asking students to review the whole service.
examples.zh: 我们收集了关于日历的「对具体功能的反馈」，而没有让学生评价整个服务。

examples.en: The feature feedback helped us decide where to put the button for changing a pickup time.
examples.zh: 「对具体功能的反馈」帮我们决定了修改领取时间的按钮放在哪儿。

words.enDefinition: A repeating process in which people make a change, gather responses, and improve it again.

examples.en: The team built a feedback loop so staff could report problems after each reminder test.
examples.zh: 团队建立了「反馈循环」，让员工每次测试提醒后都能反映问题。

examples.en: A short feedback loop helped us correct the directions before the second set of visitors arrived.
examples.zh: 在第二批访客来之前，一个简短的「反馈循环」帮我们纠正了指引。

collocations: use a feedback loop to improve a process

words.enDefinition: a test conducted in the place or conditions where a product or service is intended for use

examples.en: We ran a field trial by letting students try the equipment station during two evening classes.
examples.zh: 我们让学生在两场晚课期间试用器材站，做了「实际环境试验」。

examples.en: The field trial showed that the printed sign was hard to see from the footpath.
examples.zh: 「实际环境试验」表明，从步道上很难看清印出来的标牌。

words.enDefinition: The finished version of the graphic design prepared for use or production.

examples.en: The gallery received the final artwork for the banner two days before the exhibition opened.
examples.zh: 展览开幕前两天，画廊收到了横幅的「最终图稿」。

examples.en: We checked the final artwork to make sure the sponsor's name matched the lettering on the poster.
examples.zh: 我们核对了「最终图稿」，确保赞助方名称和海报上的写法一致。

words.enDefinition: A presentation at the end of a project where the team shares its findings and recommendations with the client.

examples.en: Our final client presentation explained why the museum's weekend visitors needed different reminders from school groups.
examples.zh: 我们的「面向客户的最终汇报」解释了，为什么博物馆周末访客需要的提醒和学校团体不同。

examples.en: The student team rehearsed the final client presentation before showing the theatre director both booking alternatives.
examples.zh: 学生团队先排练了「面向客户的最终汇报」，再给剧院负责人看两种预约替代方案。

words.enDefinition: the last assigned period in a schedule for giving a presentation

examples.en: Our final presentation slot was just before the judges left the room to compare scores.
examples.zh: 「最后一场展示时段」是我们的，讲完后评审就离场去核对分数。

examples.en: The organisers gave the final presentation slot to the team whose train had arrived late.
examples.zh: 组织者把「最后一场展示时段」让给了火车晚点的那一队。

words.enDefinition: information obtained directly through observation, experience or contact with the source

examples.en: We collected first-hand evidence by watching students try to check out equipment during the lunch break.
examples.zh: 我们观察学生午休时如何借设备，收集了「第一手证据」。

examples.en: The panel asked for first-hand evidence that people would use the service outside the main campus.
examples.zh: 评审组请我们提供「第一手证据」，说明主校区以外也有人会用这项服务。

words.enDefinition: a benefit gained by entering a market before competitors

examples.en: The case company gained a first-mover advantage by signing venue agreements before rival services opened.
examples.zh: 案例公司赶在竞争对手开业前签下场地协议，取得了「先发优势」。

examples.en: Our class asked whether the app's first-mover advantage would last once similar services appeared locally.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了本地出现类似服务后，这款应用的「先发优势」还能维持多久。

words.enDefinition: A mirror shoppers can use to see how clothing fits

examples.en: We set a fitting mirror behind the rail so people could try on jackets.
examples.zh: 我们在衣架后面放了面「试穿镜」，方便顾客试夹克。

examples.en: The fitting mirror was taller than our usual one and barely fitted in the car.
examples.zh: 这面「试穿镜」比平时用的要高，差一点就塞不进车里。

words.enDefinition: a project with a price agreed for the whole job

examples.en: The society chose a fixed-price project so it knew what the poster redesign would cost.
examples.zh: 社团选择了「固定价项目」，这样海报重新设计要花多少钱就有数了。

examples.en: Our fixed-price project covered two rounds of edits, with further revisions billed separately if requested.
examples.zh: 我们的「固定价项目」涵盖两轮修改，如需更多修改则另收费。

words.enDefinition: a schedule in which the assigned working hours or days stay the same on a regular basis

examples.en: My fixed schedule gave me the same two afternoons each week at the repair stand.
examples.zh: 我的「固定排班」是每周同样两个下午在维修摊工作。

examples.en: The owner offered a fixed schedule so I could plan my course commitments in advance.
examples.zh: 店主给我安排了「固定排班」，这样我可以提前安排课程事务。

words.enDefinition: to mark a particular matter as needing further attention or action later

examples.en: If a booking still looked uncertain, we had to flag it for follow-up before closing.
examples.zh: 如果预约还有疑问，我们得在关门前「将这件事标记待跟进」。

examples.en: I couldn't match the form to an order, so I had to flag it for follow-up.
examples.zh: 我找不到与那张表对应的订单，只好「将这件事标记待跟进」。

collocations: flag it for follow-up by the next shift
flag it for follow-up before closing

words.enDefinition: charging one fixed amount for a defined service

examples.en: The student laundry shop chose flat-rate pricing for every bag within the same weight limit.
examples.zh: 学生洗衣店采用「统一费率定价」，未超过同一重量上限的每袋衣物收费相同。

examples.en: We explained that flat-rate pricing covered any repair on the repair stall's list.
examples.zh: 我们解释说，维修摊清单上的所有项目都采用「统一费率定价」。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement with relatively few levels of management

examples.en: The small publisher kept a flat structure so editors could speak directly with the director.
examples.zh: 小出版社保留了「扁平组织结构」，编辑可以直接和负责人交流。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether a flat structure would still work when the team doubled in size.
examples.zh: 导师问，团队人数翻倍后，「扁平组织结构」能否继续运作。

words.enDefinition: workers assigned wherever they are needed rather than to a single fixed station

examples.en: The floating staff helped with packing until more customers arrived at the pickup desk.
examples.zh: 「机动人员」先帮忙打包，等到自取台顾客多了再过去帮忙。

examples.en: We kept two floating staff free to help wherever the queue began to grow.
examples.zh: 我们留了两名「机动人员」，哪边排队的人开始多了就去哪边帮忙。

words.enDefinition: a person who oversees workers and service activity in the main working or customer area

examples.en: The floor supervisor moved the waiting area after the queue began blocking the main entrance.
examples.zh: 队伍开始挡住正门后，「现场主管」把等候区挪了位置。

examples.en: A floor supervisor checked that each new worker knew which station they were covering.
examples.zh: 一名「现场主管」确认每个新员工都知道自己负责哪个工位。

words.enDefinition: competing by serving a narrow part of a market

examples.en: The case firm adopted a focus strategy by serving campus cycling clubs instead of all riders.
examples.zh: 案例企业采用「聚焦战略」，专做校园骑行社团的生意。

examples.en: The students asked whether a focus strategy made sense for a print shop near two art schools.
examples.zh: 学生问，打印店开在两所艺术院校附近，适不适合采用「聚焦战略」。

words.enDefinition: the officially established roles and relationships used to organise work

examples.en: In the formal structure, the project leads report directly to the director of the student enterprise.
examples.zh: 按「正式组织结构」，项目负责人直接向学生企业的负责人汇报。

examples.en: The case described a formal structure that gave local offices responsibility for their own purchases.
examples.zh: 案例中的「正式组织结构」允许当地办事处自行负责采购。

words.enDefinition: the extent to which written rules govern how work is done

examples.en: Formalisation increased when the cooperative began writing down rules that had previously been agreed verbally.
examples.zh: 合作社开始把原先口头商定的规则写下来后，「组织正式化」程度提高了。

examples.en: The class discussed how much formalisation would help a small design studio work more consistently.
examples.zh: 班上讨论，小型设计工作室做到何种程度的「组织正式化」有助于统一做法。

words.enDefinition: an agreement setting out how business founders will work together and share rights and responsibilities

examples.en: We discussed the founder agreement with an adviser before deciding how to allocate responsibilities.
examples.zh: 在决定怎么分工前，我们和顾问讨论了「创始人协议」。

examples.en: Their founder agreement described how decisions would be made if one student left the project.
examples.zh: 他们的「创始人协议」说明了如果有学生离开项目，团队该如何作出决定。

words.enDefinition: a group of founders taking part in the same programme during the same period

examples.en: Our founder cohort met every Wednesday to compare progress on interviews and early product tests.
examples.zh: 我们这个「同期创业者小组」每周三碰头，交流访谈和早期产品测试的进展。

examples.en: The new founder cohort included teams from the engineering school and the arts faculty.
examples.zh: 新的「同期创业者小组」有来自工程学院和艺术系的团队。

words.enDefinition: a short presentation in which a founder explains a venture and seeks interest or support

examples.en: The founder pitch started with a real problem the team had observed at several campus events.
examples.zh: 那场「创业者项目推介」开头讲了团队在几场校园活动中观察到的一个真实问题。

examples.en: I practised my founder pitch with two classmates who had never heard of the project.
examples.zh: 我找两个没听过这个项目的同学练习「创业者项目推介」。

collocations: give feedback on a founder pitch

words.enDefinition: an account of what led a founder to start a business and how it developed

examples.en: Her founder story explained how borrowing art equipment as a student led to the venture.
examples.zh: 她的「创业者经历」讲了在校时借用艺术器材的体验如何促成这次创业。

examples.en: The coach asked us to connect our founder story to the problem we had observed.
examples.zh: 教练请我们把「创业者经历」和已经观察到的问题联系起来。

collocations: include a founder story in a pitch

words.enDefinition: the original group of people who start and develop a venture

examples.en: The founding team met after class to agree on the first version of its service.
examples.zh: 「创始团队」课后开会，商定了第一版服务的内容。

examples.en: Two art students and a computer science student made up the founding team that term.
examples.zh: 当学期的「创始团队」由两名艺术专业学生和一名计算机专业学生组成。

words.enDefinition: a model in which operators pay to use a business system and brand

examples.en: In class, we compared a franchise model with a student chain that operated every shop itself.
examples.zh: 课上，我们比较了「特许经营模式」和由学生连锁品牌自己运营所有门店的做法。

examples.en: The team described a franchise model where local operators used the same sandwich stall name and menu.
examples.zh: 小组介绍了一种「特许经营模式」，当地经营者使用统一的三明治摊位名称和菜单。

words.zhGloss: 基础免费增值收费模式
words.enDefinition: a model with a free offering and optional paid upgrades
acceptedZhAnswers: 基础免费增值收费模式

examples.en: The student app used a freemium model with free schedules and paid exports for clubs.
examples.zh: 学生应用采用「基础免费、增值收费的模式」，日程表免费，社团需要导出时再付费。

examples.en: We sketched a freemium model where basic practice quizzes were free and detailed explanations cost extra.
examples.zh: 我们设计了「基础免费、增值收费的模式」，基础练习测验免费，详细讲解另外收费。

collocations: a freemium model with paid upgrades

words.enDefinition: The view of people who deal directly with customers, service users, or daily operations.

examples.en: The frontline perspective helped us see why the old form was still useful at busy times.
examples.zh: 「一线人员的视角」帮我们理解，为什么旧表格在繁忙时段还有用。

examples.en: We interviewed volunteer receptionists to include a frontline perspective in the museum's booking project.
examples.zh: 我们访谈了前台志愿者，把「一线人员的视角」纳入博物馆预约项目。

words.enDefinition: Prepare the requested goods and get them to the customer

examples.en: We couldn't fulfil an order for twenty mugs with only twelve in the cupboard.
examples.zh: 柜子里只有十二个马克杯，没法「履行那笔要二十个杯子的订单」。

examples.en: I could fulfil an order from our remaining stock without making another print run.
examples.zh: 我用剩余库存就能「完成一笔订单」，不用再印一批。

collocations: be able to fulfil an order

words.enDefinition: the total of direct expenses and allocated indirect costs

examples.en: Our fully loaded cost for the workshop included materials, tutor time, and a share of the rent.
examples.zh: 工作坊「含间接费用的总成本」包括材料、导师工时和分摊的租金。

examples.en: The team calculated the fully loaded cost of each lesson before presenting the model to classmates.
examples.zh: 团队算出每一节课「含间接费用的总成本」后，才向同学展示商业模型。

collocations: estimate the fully loaded cost per hour

words.enDefinition: having all the workers needed or planned for a shift, team or location

examples.en: The desk was fully staffed by noon, just as the first group of visitors arrived.
examples.zh: 到中午，服务台「人员配齐」，正赶上第一批来访者到场。

examples.en: We expect the evening stall to be fully staffed once the new volunteers finish training.
examples.zh: 我们预计新志愿者培训结束后，晚间摊位就能「人员配齐」。

collocations: make sure the desk is fully staffed

words.enDefinition: a manager responsible for a specialist department or area

examples.en: The functional manager approved training for designers assigned to several different campus projects that term.
examples.zh: 该「职能部门经理」批准了本学期派往不同校园项目的设计师的培训。

examples.en: I drew the functional manager above the finance team in our organisational design exercise.
examples.zh: 在组织设计练习里，我把「职能部门经理」画在财务团队上方。

words.enDefinition: an early model that performs one or more of the intended practical functions

examples.en: Our functional prototype recorded returns even though its display showed only a few basic options.
examples.zh: 我们的「功能原型」虽只显示几个基本选项，却已经能记录归还。

examples.en: The team tested a functional prototype that could process real orders during the workshop trial.
examples.zh: 在工作坊试用环节，团队测试了一个能处理真实订单的「功能原型」。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement that groups people by their work specialism

examples.en: The fictional publisher used a functional structure with separate editorial, finance, and production teams.
examples.zh: 虚构的这家出版社采用「职能型结构」，分别设有编辑、财务和制作团队。

examples.en: Our tutor asked when a functional structure might make it harder for departments to cooperate.
examples.zh: 导师问，在哪些情况下，「职能型结构」可能让部门之间更难合作。

collocations: organise teams in a functional structure

words.enDefinition: A proposed sequence of activities showing how work would be done after changes are made.

examples.en: The future-state workflow showed how one shared form could replace the two separate booking lists.
examples.zh: 「拟议的新工作流程」展示了怎样用一张共用表格替代两份独立预约名单。

examples.en: The theatre staff reviewed our future-state workflow to see who would send the new reminders.
examples.zh: 剧院工作人员审查了「拟议的新工作流程」，看看由谁发送新的提醒。

words.enDefinition: a business unit responsible for a particular area

examples.en: Each geographic division could adapt its repair service to local travel distances and working hours.
examples.zh: 各「地区事业部」可以根据当地交通距离和营业时间调整维修服务。

examples.en: The lecturer asked why the company might create a geographic division for its northern branches.
examples.zh: 讲师问，公司为什么可能为北部的分支设立一个「地区事业部」。

collocations: delegate decisions to a geographic division

words.enDefinition: To return to the planned timetable after a delay or interruption.

examples.en: We shortened two interviews to get back on schedule after the museum closed early on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 博物馆周二提前关门后，我们缩短了两场访谈，好「赶上原计划」。

examples.en: The team could get back on schedule once the client gave us the missing figures.
examples.zh: 客户给了缺失的数据后，团队就可以「恢复按计划推进」。

collocations: help the team get back on schedule
try to get back on schedule
work together to get back on schedule

words.enDefinition: A small card carrying a personal message included with a gift

examples.en: I tucked the gift message card into the bag before sticking the label on.
examples.zh: 贴标签前，我把「礼品留言卡」塞进了袋子。

examples.en: The gift message card went with the blue mug, according to the order details.
examples.zh: 按订单详情，「礼品留言卡」应和蓝色马克杯放在一起。

words.enDefinition: a decision on whether to proceed with a project, release or planned activity

examples.en: We made the go/no-go decision after reviewing what had happened during the two campus trials.
examples.zh: 看过两次校园试点的结果，我们作了「继续或停止的决定」。

examples.en: The advisor postponed our go/no-go decision until the last team had reported its findings.
examples.zh: 顾问把「继续或停止的决定」推迟到最后一支团队汇报结果之后。

words.enDefinition: an assessment of how well an organisation is directed and overseen

examples.en: The fictional cooperative began a governance review after members asked for clearer rules about decisions.
examples.zh: 成员希望把决策规则说得更清楚，这家虚构的合作社于是启动了「治理审查」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked us to show what information a governance review would need from each branch.
examples.zh: 导师让我们说明，「治理审查」需要从各分店收集哪些信息。

collocations: the findings of a governance review

words.enDefinition: the arrangement of bodies and roles that direct and oversee an organisation

examples.en: The students drew the governance structure of a cooperative with a board elected by members.
examples.zh: 学生画出了一个由成员选举董事会的合作社的「治理结构」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how the governance structure would change if workers had seats on the board.
examples.zh: 导师问，如果员工能在董事会中占有席位，「治理结构」会发生什么变化。

words.enDefinition: A metal grid used to hang merchandise or attach display hooks

examples.en: We used a gridwall panel to hang the prints above the bags.
examples.zh: 我们用「陈列网格板」把版画挂在包的上方。

examples.en: I carried the gridwall panel into the hall before fetching the hooks.
examples.zh: 我先把「陈列网格板」搬进大厅，再去拿挂钩。

collocations: hang prints on a gridwall panel

words.enDefinition: the work a team hands in after analysing a case together

examples.en: Our group case submission included a chart explaining how we had compared the three locations.
examples.zh: 我们的「小组提交的案例作业」里有一张图，说明我们如何比较这三个地点。

examples.en: I checked the group case submission to make sure everyone had added their references.
examples.zh: 我检查了「小组提交的案例作业」，确保每个人都加上了自己的参考资料。

collocations: hand in the group case submission

words.enDefinition: Information or responsibility that goes missing when work is passed between people, teams, or steps.

examples.en: The staff described a handoff gap between confirming a booking and preparing the workshop room.
examples.zh: 员工指出，从确认预约到布置工作坊房间，中间存在一个「交接环节的缺口」。

examples.en: We checked the two logs to find the handoff gap that left visitors without confirmations.
examples.zh: 我们核对了两份日志，查找导致访客没收到确认的「交接环节的缺口」。

words.enDefinition: The transfer of a process, responsibilities, or materials to the team that will run them day to day.

examples.en: The handoff to operations included explaining who would update the repair queue at closing time.
examples.zh: 「移交给运营团队」时，我们解释了每天关门由谁更新维修队列。

examples.en: The museum asked us to include two short demonstrations in the handoff to operations next week.
examples.zh: 博物馆请我们在下周「移交给运营团队」时，安排两场简短演示。

collocations: prepare for the handoff to operations

words.enDefinition: a message or record confirming that someone has received a handover and its relevant information

examples.en: The coordinator waited for a handover acknowledgement before leaving the repair desk for the evening.
examples.zh: 协调员等收到「交接收悉确认」，才在晚上离开维修台。

examples.en: I sent a handover acknowledgement after finding both keys and the notes for tomorrow's stall.
examples.zh: 我找到两把钥匙和明天摊位用的记录后，发出了「交接收悉确认」。

words.enDefinition: A bundle of final files, notes, or other materials passed to the person taking over a project.

examples.en: The handover package included the approved artwork and the addresses of the displays across campus.
examples.zh: 「交接资料包」里有已确认的图稿和校园各处展示点的地址。

examples.en: Our volunteers checked the handover package before giving the gallery keys to the next group.
examples.zh: 志愿者把画廊钥匙交给下一组之前，检查了「交接资料包」。

words.enDefinition: a planned limit on the number of positions or workers that can be supported

examples.en: The student enterprise set a headcount budget before deciding how many extra people to hire.
examples.zh: 学生企业先定了「人员编制预算」，再决定多招多少人。

examples.en: We checked whether the headcount budget allowed another weekend position for the summer term.
examples.zh: 我们查了「人员编制预算」能否在夏季学期再安排一个周末岗位。

words.enDefinition: a detailed model that resembles the intended product in appearance, interaction or behaviour

examples.en: We built a high-fidelity prototype after students could complete the main task on the mock-up.
examples.zh: 同学们能在样稿上完成主要任务后，我们做了「高保真原型」。

examples.en: The high-fidelity prototype looked like the finished service but did not handle real bookings yet.
examples.zh: 「高保真原型」看起来像最终的服务，但还处理不了真实预约。

words.zhGloss: 需要大量人工沟通的服务
words.enDefinition: a service involving substantial personal attention and direct interaction
acceptedZhAnswers: 需要大量人工沟通的服务

examples.en: Our high-touch service pairs each new language learner with a tutor for a planning call.
examples.zh: 我们的「需要大量人工沟通的服务」会为每位新学员安排辅导老师，先打电话商量学习计划。

examples.en: The tailoring team explained why its high-touch service required extra time for individual fittings.
