examples.zh: 裁缝服务小组解释了为什么他们的「需要大量人工沟通的服务」需要为每次单独试衣留更多时间。

words.enDefinition: Pause an order until an issue is resolved or information arrives

examples.en: We had to hold an order because the customer hadn't picked a thread color.
examples.zh: 顾客还没选线的颜色，所以我们得「暂缓处理一笔订单」。

examples.en: I asked the stall to hold an order until we could confirm the new quantity.
examples.zh: 我请摊位那边「暂缓处理一笔订单」，等我们确认新的数量。

collocations: ask us to hold an order
hold an order until the details are confirmed

words.enDefinition: combining businesses at the same stage of production or distribution

examples.en: We discussed horizontal integration after the fictional campus bookshop agreed to combine with another book retailer.
examples.zh: 虚构的校园书店同意与另一家图书零售商合并后，我们讨论了「横向一体化」。

examples.en: The case showed horizontal integration when two local moving services began operating under the same company.
examples.zh: 案例中，两家本地搬家服务商开始由同一家公司经营，体现了「横向一体化」。

words.enDefinition: A partner that provides a location or takes responsibility for welcoming participants and running an activity.

examples.en: The hosting partner showed us where to put the display tables before the market opened.
examples.zh: 市集开放前，「协作承办方」领我们去看了展示桌的位置。

examples.en: Our hosting partner arranged a small room for visiting artists to prepare their materials.
examples.zh: 「协作承办方」安排了一个小房间，给来访的艺术家准备材料用。

words.enDefinition: checking a set of ideas to decide which ones deserve further investigation

examples.en: We used idea screening to set aside projects that needed equipment we could not borrow.
examples.zh: 经过「创意初筛」，我们暂时放下了那些需要用到无法借到的器材的项目。

examples.en: After idea screening, our group took two options to the mentor for a longer discussion.
examples.zh: 「创意初筛」后，我们小组带着两个方案去找导师详谈。

words.enDefinition: time when a worker or piece of equipment is available but is not doing its intended work

examples.en: We recorded idle time while the team waited for the materials to reach the workshop.
examples.zh: 团队等材料送到工作室时，我们记录了「闲置时间」。

examples.en: The printer's idle time fell after we put all the label requests in one place.
examples.zh: 标签打印需求集中到一起以后，打印机的「闲置时间」减少了。

words.enDefinition: the first action to take now that a decision or event has occurred

examples.en: Our immediate next step was to ask the library whether it could provide another table.
examples.zh: 我们「眼下的下一步」是问图书馆能不能再提供一张桌子。

examples.en: The case presenter ended by explaining the immediate next step before discussing longer plans.
examples.zh: 案例演讲人在结尾先说明「眼下的下一步」，再谈长远计划。

collocations: agree on the immediate next step

words.enDefinition: systematic assessment of the changes an activity helps produce

examples.en: The lecturer used impact measurement to examine whether affordable repairs helped students keep using their bicycles.
examples.zh: 讲师用「影响评估」考察实惠的维修有没有帮助学生继续使用原来的自行车。

examples.en: Our class discussed impact measurement before choosing indicators for the community equipment library.
examples.zh: 我们班先讨论了「影响评估」，然后为社区器材借用中心选择指标。

words.enDefinition: communicating evidence about changes an organisation helps bring about

examples.en: The venture improved its impact reporting by sharing data on who used the repair workshops.
examples.zh: 该项目分享了哪些人使用维修工作坊的数据，改进了「影响报告」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether impact reporting should include the things that had not improved yet.
examples.zh: 导师问，「影响报告」是否应该涵盖那些尚未改善的方面。

words.enDefinition: A later check on whether agreed changes have been put into practice and how they are working.

examples.en: We scheduled an implementation follow-up after the charity had used the appointment reminder for a month.
examples.zh: 慈善机构预约提醒用满一个月后，我们安排了「实施情况跟进」。

examples.en: The implementation follow-up helped the museum see why one site still used the earlier form.
examples.zh: 「实施情况跟进」帮博物馆知道了，为什么有一个场点仍用旧表格。

collocations: review results at an implementation follow-up

words.zhGloss: 单项改动的实施负责人
words.enDefinition: The person or team accountable for putting one agreed change or recommendation into practice.
acceptedZhAnswers: 单项改动的实施负责人

examples.en: The client named an implementation owner for each change when we handed over the project report.
examples.zh: 我们交付项目报告时，客户为每项改动都指定了「单项改动的实施负责人」。

examples.en: Our implementation owner checked whether both branches had added the revised reminder to their booking forms.
examples.zh: 我们的「单项改动的实施负责人」核对了两个分点有没有把新版提醒加进预约表。

words.enDefinition: A plan describing the steps, timing, and responsibilities for putting a recommendation into practice.

examples.en: Our implementation plan assigned the theatre supervisor to check the first week's new booking records.
examples.zh: 我们的「实施计划」安排剧院主管核对头一周的新预约记录。

examples.en: The client wanted an implementation plan before asking two branches to change their confirmation messages.
examples.zh: 请两个分点更改确认消息之前，客户想先有一份「实施计划」。

words.enDefinition: a possible problem that could hinder a plan while it is being put into effect

examples.en: One implementation risk was that staff would not have time to learn the new booking process.
examples.zh: 一项「实施风险」是员工可能没时间学习新的预约流程。

examples.en: The manager asked us to identify an implementation risk that the schedule could help reduce.
examples.zh: 经理请我们找出可通过调整时间安排来降低的一项「实施风险」。

words.enDefinition: An overview showing the main stages and order of work for carrying out a recommendation.

examples.en: The implementation roadmap showed a small trial before the form was introduced across both branches.
examples.zh: 「实施路线图」安排先小范围试用，再在两个分点都启用表格。

examples.en: We added a progress review between the two stages on the client's implementation roadmap.
examples.zh: 我们在客户的「实施路线图」上加了一次进度评审，放在两个阶段之间。

collocations: plot stages on an implementation roadmap

words.enDefinition: the order in which the steps required to put a plan into effect take place

examples.en: Our implementation sequence put staff training before any announcement about the new collection hours.
examples.zh: 我们的「实施顺序」把员工培训排在发布新的自取时间通知之前。

examples.en: The group revised the implementation sequence after learning that the shelves would arrive next month.
examples.zh: 小组得知货架要下个月到，修改了「实施顺序」。

words.enDefinition: making a product within the venture with its own people or facilities

examples.en: In-house production let the team change the notebook covers without waiting for an outside printer.
examples.zh: 「自行生产」让小组能更换笔记本封面，无需等外部印刷商。

examples.en: Our in-house production moved into the university workshop after the craft market became a regular event.
examples.zh: 手作市集变成定期活动后，我们把「自行生产」搬到了学校工坊。

words.zhGloss: 实物或服务形式的资助
words.enDefinition: A specific contribution made in goods, services, or facilities instead of money.
acceptedZhAnswers: 实物或服务形式的资助

examples.en: We recorded the donated picture frames as an in-kind contribution to our student art show.
examples.zh: 我们把获赠的相框记为学生艺术展的「实物资助」。

examples.en: The event summary listed printing as an in-kind contribution from the shop across the road.
examples.zh: 活动小结把马路对面商店提供的印刷服务列为一笔「非现金资助」。

words.enDefinition: A person or organisation that donates goods or services in place of money.

examples.en: The neighbourhood café was an in-kind donor for the club's first student art show.
examples.zh: 街坊咖啡馆是社团首场学生艺术展的「非现金捐赠方」。

examples.en: We contacted the in-kind donor to confirm how many blank sketchbooks would be available.
examples.zh: 我们联系了「非现金捐赠方」，确认能提供多少本空白素描本。

words.enDefinition: Sponsorship provided as goods or services, such as equipment, materials, or use of a space.

examples.en: A local printer offered in-kind sponsorship by producing programmes for the student film festival.
examples.zh: 本地一家印刷店提供「非现金赞助」，为学生电影节印制手册。

examples.en: The club listed the loan of display boards as in-kind sponsorship for its spring exhibition.
examples.zh: 社团把借用展板列为春季展览的「非现金赞助」。

words.enDefinition: Goods expected to arrive but not yet received or recorded on hand

examples.en: We cleared a shelf for incoming stock before the new mugs arrived Friday.
examples.zh: 周五新马克杯送到前，我们腾出了一个架子放「待入库的货」。

examples.en: The incoming stock includes three packs of bags we need for next week.
examples.zh: 「待入库货品」里有我们下周要用的三包袋子。

words.enDefinition: To use the client's comments to revise or improve what the project team has prepared.

examples.en: We took a day to incorporate client feedback before sending the museum our updated recommendations.
examples.zh: 把更新的建议发给博物馆之前，我们花一天时间「把客户反馈纳入修改」。

examples.en: The students amended the diagram to incorporate client feedback about who confirmed the weekend bookings.
examples.zh: 学生们调整了图表，「把客户关于谁确认周末预约的反馈纳入修改」。

collocations: incorporate client feedback into the report
take time to incorporate client feedback
revise the draft to incorporate client feedback

words.enDefinition: extra profit attributable to a specific change in activity

examples.en: We estimated incremental profit from opening the stall on Fridays after accounting for extra labour.
examples.zh: 把额外人工算进去后，我们估算了周五出摊能带来的「增量利润」。

examples.en: The team found little incremental profit from delivery once it included the cost of packaging.
examples.zh: 团队发现，把包装成本算进去后，配送带来的「增量利润」很少。

words.enDefinition: a group admitted to an incubator at a particular time, or the period of admission

examples.en: The autumn incubator intake included three teams working on services for students living off campus.
examples.zh: 秋季「孵化器招收批次」有三支团队在做面向校外住宿学生的服务。

examples.en: We postponed our application until the next incubator intake to make time for interviews.
examples.zh: 我们把申请推迟到下一个「孵化器招收批次」，好腾出时间做访谈。

collocations: apply for the next incubator intake

words.enDefinition: the work of examining a case and reaching a reasoned view independently of other participants

examples.en: My independent case analysis helped me see two plausible ways to use the spare room.
examples.zh: 通过「独立案例分析」，我看到了空房间的两种可行用途。

examples.en: I began my independent case analysis before anyone shared their views in the small group.
examples.zh: 小组里还没人说自己的看法前，我就开始了「独立案例分析」。

words.enDefinition: a board member without ties likely to undermine independent judgment

examples.en: In our case, an independent director questioned the proposed purchase from a business owned by a founder.
examples.zh: 案例中，一位「独立董事」质疑向创始人名下的企业采购的提案。

examples.en: We discussed why the fictional company wanted an independent director with experience in community lending.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了这家虚构公司为什么希望聘请有社区借贷经验的「独立董事」。

words.enDefinition: a written account of a case analysis completed by one student

examples.en: My individual case write-up explained why I had ruled out the cheaper of the two premises.
examples.zh: 我的「个人案例分析报告」解释了为什么排除两个铺位中较便宜的那个。

examples.en: The tutor asked for an individual case write-up before we presented our group conclusions.
examples.zh: 导师要求我们在陈述小组结论之前提交「个人案例分析报告」。

words.enDefinition: the unofficial relationships through which people share information and work together

examples.en: The informal organisation included people from different departments who helped one another with common problems.
examples.zh: 「非正式组织关系」把来自不同部门、会互相帮着解决常见问题的人连在一起。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how the informal organisation affected decisions in a small campus publishing team.
examples.zh: 导师问，「非正式组织关系」怎样影响一个小型校园出版团队的决策。

collocations: the role of the informal organisation

words.enDefinition: the facts or evidence that someone could access when making a past decision

examples.en: We read only the information available at the time before choosing what to recommend to the shop.
examples.zh: 为店铺选建议方案前，我们只看了「当时能掌握的信息」。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether the decision was reasonable given the information available at the time.
examples.zh: 导师问，考虑到「当时能掌握的信息」，那个决定是否合理。

collocations: based on the information available at the time
review the information available at the time
act on the information available at the time

words.enDefinition: a limit caused by relevant information being unavailable, incomplete or difficult to obtain in time

examples.en: The information constraint meant the team could compare only the prices it had already received.
examples.zh: 受「信息受限条件」影响，团队只能比较已经收到的报价。

examples.en: We discussed the information constraint before recommending that the owner delay signing the agreement until Friday.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「信息受限条件」，然后建议店主把签约推迟到周五。

words.enDefinition: a difference between information currently available and information needed to understand or decide something

examples.en: Our biggest information gap was who could approve a trial of the later pickup hours.
examples.zh: 我们最大的「信息缺口」是，不知道谁有权批准试行晚一点的取货时段。

examples.en: The professor asked how we would close the information gap before the manager had to decide.
examples.zh: 教授问，我们会怎样在经理必须作出决定前填补「信息缺口」。

words.enDefinition: A list of documents, figures, or other information the team asks the client to provide.

examples.en: We sent an information request list before asking staff to compare their two booking forms.
examples.zh: 请员工比较两个预约表之前，我们发了一份「所需资料清单」。

examples.en: The client reviewed our information request list and offered totals for all four visitor entrances.
examples.zh: 客户看了我们的「所需资料清单」，愿意提供全部四个访客入口的汇总数据。

words.enDefinition: money awarded to help develop or test a new product, process or idea

examples.en: The students used an innovation grant to pay for the materials needed for their test.
examples.zh: 同学们用「创新项目资助」支付了测试所需的材料费用。

examples.en: Our tutor read the innovation grant application and suggested making the experiment more specific.
examples.zh: 导师看了「创新项目资助」申请，建议把实验写得更具体。

collocations: fund a pilot with an innovation grant

words.enDefinition: a space or programme where people collaborate and experiment with new ideas and solutions

examples.en: The innovation lab hosted a workshop on designing better signs for the campus buildings.
examples.zh: 「创新实验室」办了一个工作坊，讨论如何给校园建筑设计更好用的标识。

examples.en: We met in the innovation lab to sketch different versions of the booking screen.
examples.zh: 我们在「创新实验室」碰头，画了几个不同版本的预约界面。

words.enDefinition: a model that allows users to interact with simulated features or controls

examples.en: The interactive prototype let students select a pickup time and see a sample confirmation screen.
examples.zh: 学生可以在「可交互原型」上选领取时间，并看到示例确认页面。

examples.en: We shared the interactive prototype so classmates could try the buttons before the studio session.
examples.zh: 我们分享了「可交互原型」，让同学在工作室课开始前试用里面的按钮。

words.enDefinition: A document, sample, or other output provided before the whole project is complete.

examples.en: The marked floor plan was an interim deliverable before the student studio built the panels.
examples.zh: 学生工作室做展板前，带标记的平面图是一项「阶段交付物」。

examples.en: We reviewed an interim deliverable so the organisers could confirm the size of the signs.
examples.zh: 我们先审查了一项「阶段交付物」，让组织者确认标牌的大小。

words.enDefinition: A person inside an organisation who actively builds support for a proposed project or change.

examples.en: The museum's education coordinator became an internal champion for simplifying the school group booking process.
examples.zh: 博物馆的教育协调员成了「组织内部推动者」，支持简化学校团体预约流程。

examples.en: We asked an internal champion to explain the proposed change at the client team's weekly meeting.
examples.zh: 我们请一位「组织内部推动者」在客户团队的周会上说明拟议改动。

words.enDefinition: An interviewee's agreement to take part or to allow a particular use of the interview.

examples.en: The student team recorded interview consent before taking notes on how volunteers greeted new visitors.
examples.zh: 学生团队先记录「受访者同意」，才记下志愿者怎样接待新访客。

examples.en: Our adviser checked that we had interview consent before we quoted anyone in the draft.
examples.zh: 在草稿中引用受访者的话之前，指导老师先核对我们是否已取得「受访者同意」。

words.enDefinition: a planned list of topics or questions that helps someone conduct an interview

examples.en: I brought an interview guide but asked a few extra questions about borrowing equipment after dark.
examples.zh: 我带了「访谈提纲」，还加问了几个关于天黑以后借用器材的问题。

examples.en: Our interview guide started with questions about the student's usual journey home from evening classes.
examples.zh: 我们的「访谈提纲」先问学生平时上完晚课是怎么回家的。

words.enDefinition: a concise account of the main points learned in an interview

examples.en: I wrote an interview summary while the student's description of the borrowing process was still fresh.
examples.zh: 那位学生对借用流程的描述我还记得很清楚，就写了份「访谈摘要」。

examples.en: The interview summary noted that the participant had tried three different ways to find the service.
examples.zh: 「访谈摘要」记下了参与者曾试过三种方式查找这项服务。

words.zhGloss: 访谈中反复出现的主题
words.enDefinition: Topics or patterns that emerge from what people say across a set of interviews.
acceptedZhAnswers: 访谈中反复出现的主题

examples.en: The main interview themes were unclear instructions and a lack of reminders for evening appointments.
examples.zh: 「访谈中反复出现的主题」主要是指引不清楚，以及晚间预约缺少提醒。

examples.en: We shared the interview themes with our adviser before choosing which examples to include.
examples.zh: 选定要写进去的例子之前，我们把「访谈中反复出现的主题」发给了指导老师。

words.enDefinition: offering a temporary initial rate when something is first marketed

examples.en: The bicycle storage project used introductory pricing during its first month on campus to attract customers.
examples.zh: 自行车寄存项目入驻校园的第一个月采用「入市初期优惠定价」来吸引顾客。

examples.en: Our handout marked the end date for introductory pricing beside the studio's later standard rate.
examples.zh: 宣传单在工作室日后正常收费的旁边标出了「入市初期优惠定价」的截止日期。

words.enDefinition: to demonstrate that evidence contradicts a hypothesis under the tested conditions

examples.en: One unexpected result was not enough to invalidate a hypothesis about regular equipment use.
examples.zh: 一次出乎意料的结果不足以「证伪关于器材常规使用的假设」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked what kind of test could invalidate a hypothesis about weekly student demand.
examples.zh: 导师问，哪种测试能「证伪关于学生每周需求的假设」。

collocations: enough evidence to invalidate a hypothesis
use data to invalidate a hypothesis

words.enDefinition: a trial restricted to selected people or organisations invited by its organisers

examples.en: We ran an invite-only pilot with three clubs that frequently used the same campus spaces.
examples.zh: 我们和三个经常用同一批校园场地的社团做了「仅限受邀者的试点」。

examples.en: The invite-only pilot helped us resolve scheduling problems before opening the service to other groups.
examples.zh: 「仅限受邀者的试点」帮我们解决了时间安排问题，之后才向其他小组开放服务。

words.enDefinition: a choice that cannot be undone or can be undone only with great difficulty

examples.en: Selling the second repair bench was an irreversible decision for our small team that term.
examples.zh: 当学期对我们这个小团队来说，卖掉第二张维修台是「难以撤回的决定」。

examples.en: The tutor asked what evidence we would need before making an irreversible decision about the shop.
examples.zh: 导师问，在对店铺作出「难以撤回的决定」前，我们需要哪些证据。

words.enDefinition: a quick reference that helps a worker carry out a particular task while doing it

examples.en: The new cashier kept a small job aid beside the register to check uncommon payment options.
examples.zh: 新收银员把一份小小的「岗位操作提示」放在收银机旁，用来查看不常见的支付选项。

examples.en: I drew a simple job aid showing where to put equipment ready for pickup.
examples.zh: 我画了一张简单的「岗位操作提示」，标明可以领取的设备该放哪里。

words.enDefinition: A short description of what needs to be done for a particular assignment or piece of work.

examples.en: The studio gave us a job brief for making new labels for the shared shelves.
examples.zh: 工作室给了我们一份「工作任务简要说明」，要求为共用架子做新标签。

examples.en: The job brief said who would check the finished folders before the student fair opened.
examples.zh: 「工作任务简要说明」写明了学生市集开放之前由谁检查做好的资料夹。

words.enDefinition: A slip containing the instructions for a specific piece of work

examples.en: I attached a job ticket to the tote that needed a longer strap.
examples.zh: 我把一张「作业工单」贴在需要加长背带的托特包上。

examples.en: The job ticket listed which part of the jacket the student wanted mended.
examples.zh: 「作业工单」写了那位同学想补夹克的哪个部位。

words.enDefinition: Used to name the people or groups that did the work of organising an activity together.

examples.en: The poster said the market was jointly organized by the studio and the student union.
examples.zh: 海报写着，市集「由工作室和学生会联合组织」。

examples.en: The exhibition was jointly organized by the film society and a studio near the station.
examples.zh: 展览「由电影社和车站附近的一家工作室联合组织」。

collocations: an event jointly organized by students

words.enDefinition: questions a panel asks participants to understand or test the reasoning behind their entry

examples.en: The judges' questions focused on the risks that we had mentioned in our final slide.
examples.zh: 「评审提问」主要围绕我们在最后一页幻灯片上提到的风险。

examples.en: We took turns answering the judges' questions so each person could explain their own analysis.
examples.zh: 我们轮流回答「评审提问」，让每个人都能解释自己做的分析。

words.enDefinition: a group responsible for reviewing and scoring entries or performances in a competition

examples.en: The judging panel included a local shop owner and two lecturers from the business school.
examples.zh: 「评审团」有一位本地店主和两名商学院讲师。

examples.en: We gave the judging panel a short explanation of how we had estimated repair demand.
examples.zh: 我们向「评审团」简要介绍了维修需求的估算方法。

words.enDefinition: to maintain the same prices over a period

examples.en: The campus café found a new supplier and managed to keep prices steady through the semester.
examples.zh: 校园咖啡馆找到了新供应商，整个学期都设法「保持价格稳定」。

examples.en: We planned to keep prices steady until the next batch of notebooks arrived in April.
examples.zh: 我们计划在四月下一批笔记本到货之前「保持价格稳定」。

collocations: keep prices steady for a month

words.zhGloss: 把同一订单的货放一起
words.enDefinition: Keep all the items from one customer purchase in one place
acceptedZhAnswers: 把同一订单的货放一起

examples.en: We used a tray to keep the order together until the envelopes were labelled.
examples.zh: 信封贴好标签之前，我们先用托盘「把同一笔订单的货放在一起」。

examples.en: Can you keep the order together while I check whether the extra mug has arrived?
examples.zh: 我去看看多加的马克杯到了没有，你能先「把这笔订单的货放在一起」吗？

collocations: use a basket to keep the order together
remember to keep the order together
need to keep the order together

words.enDefinition: the main actions a venture must carry out

examples.en: When we listed key activities, collecting and cleaning the rental mugs came before product design.
examples.zh: 列「关键业务活动」时，我们把回收和清洗租用杯子排在了产品设计之前。

examples.en: Our advisor asked which key activities the student team could realistically handle during exam week.
examples.zh: 导师问学生团队，考试周实际上还能做哪些「关键业务活动」。

words.enDefinition: the outside relationships that help a venture operate

examples.en: On the canvas, we listed the campus print shop and the library under key partnerships.
examples.zh: 我们在画布的「关键合作关系」栏里填写了校内打印店和图书馆。

examples.en: The mentor asked which key partnerships mattered once we started taking orders across town.
examples.zh: 导师问我们，开始接城里各处的订单后，哪些「关键合作关系」会很重要。

words.enDefinition: reliance on one person for essential knowledge or work

examples.en: The class case showed key-person dependency because only the founder knew how to contact suppliers.
examples.zh: 在课堂案例中，只有创始人知道如何联系供应商，体现了「关键人员依赖」。

examples.en: We discussed how the workshop could reduce key-person dependency before the student manager graduated.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了工作坊怎样在学生经理毕业前减少「关键人员依赖」。

words.enDefinition: the assets a venture relies on to operate

examples.en: The repair team listed its workbench and tool library as key resources for the service.
examples.zh: 维修小组把工作台和设备借用中心列为开展服务的「关键资源」。

examples.en: Losing access to the university kitchen would remove one of our key resources for catering.
examples.zh: 要是不能再用学校厨房，我们的配餐项目就会失去一项「关键资源」。

words.enDefinition: A list of topics to discuss at the first meeting of a project.

examples.en: We shared the kickoff agenda with the theatre manager before visiting the rehearsal rooms on Monday.
examples.zh: 周一去看排练室之前，我们把「启动会议程」发给了剧院经理。

examples.en: The kickoff agenda included time to confirm what the cooperative hoped to learn about volunteer scheduling.
examples.zh: 「启动会议程」安排了时间，确认合作社想从志愿者排班方面了解什么。

collocations: add an item to the kickoff agenda

words.enDefinition: Sharing the information and practical understanding needed for others to continue work after a project.

examples.en: We planned knowledge transfer so the charity could update its volunteer briefing without asking our team.
examples.zh: 我们规划了「知识移交」，让慈善机构以后自己就能更新志愿者工作说明。

examples.en: The last workshop focused on knowledge transfer to the people who would maintain the booking form.
examples.zh: 最后一次工作坊的重点，是向今后维护预约表的人做「知识移交」。

words.enDefinition: charging for selected items individually instead of as a bundle

examples.en: At the design studio, à la carte pricing allowed clubs to buy only the services they needed.
examples.zh: 设计工作室采用「单项定价」，社团只需购买自己需要的服务。

examples.en: The editing team kept à la carte pricing for optional captions, translations, and extra revisions.
examples.zh: 剪辑小组继续对可选字幕、翻译和额外修改采用「单项定价」。

collocations: an à la carte pricing menu

words.enDefinition: Attach an identifying tag to every bag so orders stay separate

examples.en: Please label each bag with the order number before you put it on the shelf.
examples.zh: 请先「逐袋贴好标签」写上订单号，再把袋子放到架子上。

examples.en: We had to label each bag because three different people ordered the same mug.
examples.zh: 有三个人订了同款马克杯，所以我们得「逐袋贴标签」。

collocations: label each bag with a name

words.enDefinition: the amount of work time needed for each produced unit

examples.en: The team tracked labor hours per unit while making its first batch of reusable notebook covers.
examples.zh: 团队制作首批可反复使用的笔记本封套时，记录了「单位人工工时」。

examples.en: We used labor hours per unit to compare hand assembly with jobs done in the workshop.
examples.zh: 我们用「单位人工工时」比较手工组装和在工作坊完成的工序。

collocations: record average labor hours per unit

words.enDefinition: a shift during the later part of an operation's daily or regular working hours

examples.en: I chose the late shift at the book stall because my course ended after lunch.
examples.zh: 我的课午饭后才结束，所以选了书摊的「晚班」。

examples.en: I worked the late shift, so I collected the loan forms before the hall closed.
examples.zh: 我上「晚班」，就在大厅关闭之前收齐了借用表。

words.enDefinition: a list of tasks or conditions to check before opening or releasing a product or service

examples.en: The launch checklist asked who could answer student questions during the first week of operation.
examples.zh: 「发布前检查清单」里有一项，要确认服务运行首周谁来回答学生提问。

examples.en: We added another payment test to the launch checklist after practising with fake orders.
examples.zh: 用模拟订单练习后，我们在「发布前检查清单」上又加了一个支付测试项。

words.enDefinition: how well a product, team and its supporting arrangements are prepared for a launch

examples.en: We reviewed launch readiness after volunteers tried to handle several bookings in a single hour.
examples.zh: 志愿者试着在一小时内处理几个预约后，我们评估了「发布准备程度」。

examples.en: The mentor asked what evidence of launch readiness the student team could show that afternoon.
examples.zh: 顾问问，学生团队当天下午能拿出什么证据来说明「发布准备程度」。

words.enDefinition: The principal person or group coordinating the organisation of an event or activity.

examples.en: The lead organizer confirmed who would open the venue and where speakers should leave their bags.
examples.zh: 「牵头组织者」确认了谁来开场馆门，以及演讲者可以把包放在哪里。

examples.en: Our club acted as lead organizer for the exhibition with support from two local studios.
examples.zh: 当地两家工作室提供支持，我们社团担任展览的「牵头组织者」。

collocations: the lead organizer for an event

words.enDefinition: The sponsor with the principal supporting role among several sponsors for an event or project.

examples.en: The craft shop became our lead sponsor after offering materials for all four student workshops.
examples.zh: 这家手工艺品店提出为四场学生工作坊提供材料，成为我们的「主要赞助方」。

examples.en: The lead sponsor was invited to meet the student organisers before the showcase opened.
examples.zh: 展演开场前，「主要赞助方」受邀和学生组织者见面。

words.enDefinition: a user who faces emerging needs ahead of most others and stands to benefit substantially from a solution

examples.en: One lead user had already built a shared spreadsheet to solve the scheduling problem herself.
examples.zh: 一位「领先用户」已经自己建了张共享表格来解决排班问题。

examples.en: We asked a lead user whether other equipment managers were beginning to face similar problems.
examples.zh: 我们问一位「领先用户」，其他器材管理员是不是也开始遇到类似问题。

words.enDefinition: a report describing what a team learned while testing its ideas and assumptions

examples.en: Our learning report focused on what changed after we talked to three different equipment managers.
examples.zh: 我们的「试验学习总结」重点记录，与三位器材管理员交谈后，认识有哪些变化。

examples.en: The mentor asked to see our learning report before approving another round of interviews next week.
examples.zh: 导师想先看我们的「试验学习总结」，再批准下周开展新一轮访谈。

words.enDefinition: Understanding gained from reflecting on what worked and what went wrong during a project.

examples.en: We wrote down lessons learned about doing site visits before asking volunteers to complete surveys.
examples.zh: 我们记下了「总结出的经验教训」，比如怎样在请志愿者做问卷前开展现场走访。

examples.en: The adviser shared our lessons learned with the next class before its first client meeting.
examples.zh: 指导老师在下一届学生首次见客户前，分享了我们「总结出的经验教训」。

collocations: apply lessons learned to another project

words.enDefinition: a model that charges others for permission to use something

examples.en: The illustration students proposed a licensing model for cafés that wanted to print their designs on mugs.
examples.zh: 插画专业的同学为想在杯子上印图案的咖啡馆提出了「授权经营模式」。

examples.en: Our licensing model gave campus clubs permission to reuse the graphics in their own brochures.
examples.zh: 我们的「授权经营模式」允许校内社团在自家的宣传册中使用这些图案。

words.enDefinition: Restricted to the particular event being discussed rather than other events or later uses.

examples.en: The designer said use of the artwork was limited to this event when we asked about reprinting.
examples.zh: 我们问能否重印时，设计员说图稿「仅限用于本次活动」。

examples.en: The offer of free equipment was limited to this event because the university needed it back.
examples.zh: 因为学校需要收回设备，免费出借的器材「仅限用于本次活动」。

collocations: use is limited to this event
access is limited to this event
a licence limited to this event

words.enDefinition: formal power to direct the work of people who report to you

examples.en: The branch manager had line authority over employees assigned to the shop in our case.
examples.zh: 在我们的案例里，分店经理对分配到店里的员工拥有「直线职权」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked who held line authority after the company split its main repair team.
examples.zh: 导师问，公司拆分主维修团队后，由谁行使「直线职权」。

words.enDefinition: the published price before any negotiated or promotional adjustment

examples.en: The student print shop showed a list price for each poster size on its order form.
examples.zh: 学生打印店在订单表上列出了各尺寸海报的「标价」。

examples.en: We kept the list price unchanged and showed the club discount on a separate line.
examples.zh: 我们保持「标价」不变，另起一行列出社团折扣。

words.enDefinition: freedom for a local unit to make its own decisions

examples.en: Greater local autonomy let each branch set opening hours that suited its neighbourhood and staff.
examples.zh: 更大的「下属单位自主权」让每家分店能自行设定适合附近居民和员工的营业时间。

examples.en: The class case asked how much local autonomy the central office should give its stores.
examples.zh: 课堂案例问，总部应该给各家门店多少「下属单位自主权」。

collocations: a high degree of local autonomy

words.enDefinition: A business in the surrounding area that works with a group on a shared project.

examples.en: The club invited a local business partner to show students how it prints small runs.
examples.zh: 社团邀请「本地商家合作方」向学生展示怎样小批量印刷。

examples.en: Our local business partner lent two display stands for the exhibition at the student centre.
examples.zh: 「本地商家合作方」借了两个展架给学生中心的展览用。

collocations: work with a local business partner

words.enDefinition: A planned path for delivering orders to addresses in a nearby area

examples.en: Our local delivery route ends near campus, so I can drop off the largest box last.
examples.zh: 我们的「本地送货路线」终点在学校附近，所以我可以最后送最大的箱子。

examples.en: We grouped three stops on the local delivery route because the customers lived on one road.
examples.zh: 三位顾客住在同一条路上，我们就在「本地送货路线」上把这三站排在一起。

collocations: combine stops on a local delivery route

words.enDefinition: A recommendation intended to be carried out over a longer period or to have lasting effects.

examples.en: Our longer-term recommendation was to combine both sites' booking records after the museum replaced its software.
examples.zh: 我们「着眼长期的建议」是，博物馆换软件后把两处场点的预约记录合在一起。

examples.en: The team described weekly volunteer training as a longer-term recommendation because it needed sustained staffing.
examples.zh: 团队把每周志愿者培训列为「着眼长期的建议」，因为需要持续安排人手。

words.enDefinition: a simple early model that shows the main ideas without looking or working like a finished product

examples.en: We used a low-fidelity prototype on paper to test the order of the booking steps.
examples.zh: 我们用纸做了一个「低保真原型」，测试预约步骤的顺序。

examples.en: The tutor encouraged us to improve the low-fidelity prototype before spending time on visual details.
examples.zh: 导师鼓励我们先改好「低保真原型」，再花时间打磨视觉细节。

words.enDefinition: A notification that the quantity of an item is running low

examples.en: The low-stock alert went off when we had three green mugs left to sell.
examples.zh: 还剩三个绿马克杯可卖时，系统发出了「库存不足提醒」。

examples.en: I set a low-stock alert for envelopes before we scheduled another print market.
examples.zh: 安排下一场版画市集前，我给信封设了个「库存不足提醒」。

collocations: a low-stock alert for each variant

words.enDefinition: an estimate intended to show the low end of what a quantity could plausibly be

examples.en: Our lower-bound estimate included only bookings that had already been confirmed by each group.
examples.zh: 「下界估计」只纳入各小组已经确认的预约。

examples.en: The lower-bound estimate suggested we still needed two workers even if no walk-ins arrived.
examples.zh: 「下界估计」表明，即使没有现场来访者，也需要两名员工。

words.enDefinition: Produce items in groups instead of making each one separately

examples.en: The canvas bags are easy to make in batches because they all use the same pattern.
examples.zh: 帆布包用的都是同样的纸样，所以很容易「分批制作」。

examples.en: We chose items to make in batches on the afternoons when the studio was quiet.
examples.zh: 我们选了一些可以在工作室清静的下午「分批制作」的商品。

collocations: choose items to make in batches

words.enDefinition: a choice between producing something internally and buying it externally

examples.en: The student café faced a make-or-buy decision when demand for its bread doubled in March.
examples.zh: 三月份面包需求翻倍后，学生咖啡馆面临「自制还是外购的决策」。

examples.en: We wrote a short report on the make-or-buy decision for the reusable boxes at our stall.
examples.zh: 我们写了份简短报告，讨论摊位的可重复使用餐盒该「自制还是外购」。

words.enDefinition: To add enough detail about what to do, who does it, and how, so someone can act on a recommendation.

examples.en: We added a suggested owner and timing to make the recommendation actionable for the charity.
examples.zh: 我们加上了建议负责人和时间安排，好让慈善机构的团队「实际执行这项建议」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to make the recommendation actionable by describing what staff would do first.
examples.zh: 老师请我们写清楚员工首先会做什么，「让建议可以实际执行」。

collocations: try to make the recommendation actionable
add steps to make the recommendation actionable
include a test to make the recommendation actionable

words.enDefinition: Make goods in advance to keep them available for future orders

examples.en: For our plain notebooks, we make to stock so buyers can collect them immediately.
examples.zh: 素面笔记本是我们「提前按库存备货做的」，买家随时能取。

examples.en: We decided to make to stock for the two designs that always sell quickly.
examples.zh: 有两个款一直卖得很快，我们决定「提前做出来备货」。

collocations: make to stock for regular sales

words.enDefinition: the executive board that manages a company in a two-tier governance system

examples.en: The management board presented its proposal for a new repair centre to the supervisory board.
examples.zh: 「管理委员会」向监督董事会提交了增设维修中心的提案。

examples.en: In class, we discussed which day-to-day decisions belonged to the fictional retailer's management board.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们讨论了这家虚构零售商的「管理委员会」负责哪些日常决策。

collocations: a meeting of the management board

words.enDefinition: freedom for managers to make judgments within agreed limits

examples.en: In our case, the shop's weekend opening hours were left to management discretion.
examples.zh: 在案例中，商店周末的营业时间由「管理层自主裁量权」决定。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how management discretion might help the team respond to an unusually busy week.
examples.zh: 导师问，「管理层自主裁量权」怎样帮助团队应对格外忙碌的一周。

words.enDefinition: a learning exercise that models an organisation so participants can test decisions and observe results

examples.en: We used a management simulation to see how reducing staff hours affected our ability to serve customers.
examples.zh: 我们通过「经营管理模拟」观察，缩短员工工时会怎样影响接待顾客的能力。

examples.en: The management simulation showed the effect of several teams changing their prices during the same period.
examples.zh: 「经营管理模拟」展示了多个团队在同一时期调整价格所产生的影响。

collocations: take part in a management simulation

words.enDefinition: a difficult problem that requires someone in a management role to set priorities or take action

examples.en: The managerial challenge was how to keep both services running with only one experienced worker.
examples.zh: 「管理难题」在于，只有一名有经验的员工，如何同时维持两项服务。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which managerial challenge had the greatest effect on the business that year.
examples.zh: 导师问，哪项「管理难题」对那年企业的影响最大。

words.enDefinition: A manual task that lets people get work done despite a problem with the usual process.

examples.en: The repair shop used a manual workaround when the order form could not track borrowed tools.
examples.zh: 订单表无法跟踪借出的工具时，维修店用了「手动替代办法」。

examples.en: We documented the manual workaround because new volunteers were copying the same list every morning.
examples.zh: 新志愿者每天早晨都要抄一遍相同的名单，我们记录了这个「手动替代办法」。

words.enDefinition: Record that the prepared goods have been collected by the customer

examples.en: Choose "Mark as collected" after the buyer takes both bags from the counter.
examples.zh: 买家从柜台拿走两袋货后，选择「标记为已取货」。

examples.en: I forgot to click "Mark as collected" after the last pickup on Friday.
examples.zh: 周五最后一单取走后，我忘了点「标记为已取货」。

collocations: mark as collected in the system

words.enDefinition: In British English, a spot assigned to a market seller

examples.en: We booked a market pitch near the entrance for our screen printed bags.
examples.zh: 我们在入口附近订了一个「市集摊位」，卖我们丝网印制的包。

examples.en: Our market pitch was beside the stairs, so we used a narrow table.
examples.zh: 我们的「市集摊位」在楼梯边，所以用了张窄桌子。

words.enDefinition: To correspond in relevant details to the sample that has already been agreed or accepted.

examples.en: The colour needed to match the approved sample before the gallery would accept the boards.
examples.zh: 颜色需要「与已确认的样品一致」，画廊才会接收这些展板。

examples.en: We checked whether the stand bases would match the approved sample after the material changed.
examples.zh: 材料改了之后，我们核查展架底座是否仍「与已确认的样品一致」。

collocations: match the approved sample in colour
make sure the items match the approved sample
check that the product will match the approved sample

words.enDefinition: The quantity or value of materials available to a person or group as part of an arrangement.

examples.en: Our materials allowance covered paper for the workshop and cardboard for a single display board.
examples.zh: 我们的「材料使用额度」包括工作坊用纸和制作一块展板的纸板。

examples.en: We split the materials allowance between two groups after checking how many posters each needed.
examples.zh: 我们先确认每组需要多少海报，再在两组之间分配「材料使用额度」。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement with intersecting lines of responsibility, such as departments and projects

examples.en: In the matrix structure, the designer reported to both the design manager and the project lead.
examples.zh: 在「矩阵式结构」下，设计师同时向设计经理和项目负责人汇报。

examples.en: The class compared a matrix structure with separate departments that rarely shared people across projects.
examples.zh: 班上比较了「矩阵式结构」和部门独立运作、很少跨项目调人的安排。

words.enDefinition: the longest interruption a service can withstand without unacceptable harm

examples.en: The students estimated maximum tolerable downtime for a service that stores equipment for evening collection.
examples.zh: 学生估算了一个为晚间自取保管器材的服务的「最大可容忍停运时间」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why maximum tolerable downtime was shorter for returns than for new bookings.
examples.zh: 导师问，为什么归还业务的「最大可容忍停运时间」要比新预约业务更短。

words.enDefinition: To count or estimate how many people have started using a new service, tool, or process.

examples.en: We used the booking totals to measure uptake after the gallery introduced the new request form.
examples.zh: 画廊启用新申请表后，我们用预约汇总数据来「衡量实际采用情况」。

examples.en: The repair charity planned to measure uptake without collecting any additional personal details from volunteers.
examples.zh: 维修慈善机构计划「衡量实际采用情况」，无需再收集志愿者的个人信息。

collocations: measure uptake of the new form

words.enDefinition: a tightly controlled arrangement with specialised roles and formal rules

examples.en: The fictional warehouse used a mechanistic structure with clearly prescribed duties and several approval levels.
examples.zh: 虚构的这家仓库采用「机械式组织结构」，职责有明确规定，审批分好几级。

examples.en: In the exercise, a mechanistic structure made it easy to see who could approve each change.
examples.zh: 练习中，「机械式组织结构」让每项变更由谁批准变得很清楚。

words.enDefinition: joint ownership of an organisation by the people who belong to it

examples.en: The case described how member ownership gave students a shared stake in the equipment business.
examples.zh: 案例描述了「成员共同所有」如何使学生在设备经营项目中拥有共同权益。

examples.en: Our lecturer compared member ownership with a model that let outside investors hold the entire business.
examples.zh: 讲师将「成员共同所有」与让外部投资者持有整个企业的模式作了比较。

collocations: a model based on member ownership

words.enDefinition: the process of pairing participants with suitable mentors based on their needs and experience

examples.en: The programme opened mentor matching after asking each team what kind of help it needed.
examples.zh: 项目先问各团队需要哪类帮助，随后启动「导师匹配」。

examples.en: I filled in a mentor matching form before meeting an adviser from the design industry.
examples.zh: 我先填了「导师匹配」表，后来见到了一位来自设计行业的顾问。

words.enDefinition: a grant that provides a small amount of money for a specific project or activity

examples.en: A microgrant covered the first set of materials for our student-run repair stall that month.
examples.zh: 当月，一笔「小额资助」支付了学生经营的维修摊所需的第一批材料。

examples.en: The programme awarded a microgrant after the team explained how it planned to test the idea.
examples.zh: 团队讲清怎样测试创意之后，项目方发放了一笔「小额资助」。

words.enDefinition: a brief conversation during a shift to see how work is progressing and what help is needed

examples.en: We held a mid-shift check-in after lunch to see which orders could be finished that day.
examples.zh: 午饭后我们做了次「班中碰头会」，看看哪些订单当天能做完。

examples.en: The mid-shift check-in let us move someone to the service desk before the queue grew.
examples.zh: 「班中碰头会」让我们在排队的人变多前调了一人去服务台。

words.enDefinition: A presentation near the middle of a project sharing what the team has learned so far.

examples.en: The midpoint presentation included staff feedback on the theatre's two ways of confirming rehearsal bookings.
examples.zh: 「中期项目汇报」包括员工对剧院两种排练预约确认方式的反馈。

examples.en: We gave a midpoint presentation to show where museum visitors were getting stuck when booking.
examples.zh: 我们做了「中期项目汇报」，说明博物馆访客在预约时卡在哪一步。

collocations: include a finding in the midpoint presentation

words.enDefinition: A review around the middle of a project to discuss progress, early findings, and remaining work.

examples.en: The midpoint review helped us decide which problems deserved more attention before the next site visit.
examples.zh: 「中期项目评审」帮我们确定，下次实地走访前哪些问题值得进一步关注。

examples.en: Our client asked to invite the volunteer coordinator to the midpoint review on Friday.
examples.zh: 客户提出邀请志愿者协调员参加周五的「中期项目评审」。

collocations: discuss findings at a midpoint review

words.enDefinition: a meeting or assessment that checks progress at a planned point in a project

examples.en: At the milestone review, we presented test results from the library and the student centre.
examples.zh: 在「阶段成果评审」中，我们展示了图书馆和学生中心的测试结果。

examples.en: The milestone review identified two tasks the team needed to finish before inviting more users.
examples.zh: 「阶段成果评审」确定了邀请更多用户前团队得完成的两项任务。

words.enDefinition: the shortest amount of work time a client is billed for

examples.en: Our student consultancy listed minimum billable time on the quote for each remote support session.
examples.zh: 学生咨询团队在每次远程支持的报价上都列出了「最低计费时长」。

examples.en: The designer explained that minimum billable time covered preparation even when a call ended early.
examples.zh: 设计师解释，即便电话提前结束，「最低计费时长」也涵盖了准备工作。

collocations: a minimum billable time of one hour

words.enDefinition: the smallest amount billed even for a minor job

examples.en: The bike stall applied a minimum charge when a repair took less than ten minutes.
examples.zh: 维修不到十分钟时，自行车摊按「最低收费」收钱。

examples.en: We put the minimum charge on the notice so customers knew what a small job would cost.
examples.zh: 我们把「最低收费」写进告示，让顾客知道小活儿要花多少钱。

words.enDefinition: the smallest number of people required to carry out a specified operation or task

examples.en: We agreed the minimum crew size for opening the studio would be two people.
examples.zh: 我们商定，开放工作室的「最低班组人数」是两人。

examples.en: The supervisor checked the minimum crew size before approving the quietest shift of the week.
examples.zh: 主管批准一周最清闲的班次前，核对了「最低班组人数」。

words.enDefinition: the least amount of service an organisation aims to maintain

examples.en: Our case defined a minimum service level of one staffed desk during the move to temporary rooms.
examples.zh: 案例规定，搬到临时场地期间，「最低服务水平」是保留一个有人值守的服务台。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to explain how the project would meet its minimum service level.
examples.zh: 导师让我们解释，该项目怎样达到「最低服务水平」。

words.enDefinition: a basic usable version of a product built with enough features to test important assumptions with real users

examples.en: Our minimum viable product accepted reservations for just one collection point near the student centre.
examples.zh: 我们的「最小可行产品」只能预约学生中心附近的一个领取点。

examples.en: We released a minimum viable product to see whether people would use the service repeatedly.
examples.zh: 我们发布了「最小可行产品」，想看看大家会不会反复使用这项服务。

words.enDefinition: a comparison that suggests an inaccurate conclusion because important differences are ignored or hidden

examples.en: Comparing total visits gave a misleading comparison because one shop was open twice as long.
examples.zh: 比较到访总量是「会引起误解的比较」，因为其中一家店开门时间是另一家的两倍。

examples.en: The lecturer asked us to correct a misleading comparison in the first table of our report.
examples.zh: 讲师请我们改正报告第一张表里一处「会引起误解的比较」。

words.enDefinition: An instance of choosing an incorrect item to fill an order

examples.en: We spotted a mispick when a green mug turned up in the bag.
examples.zh: 我们发现袋里有个绿马克杯，就知道「拣错货」了。

examples.en: I recorded the mispick before swapping the large shirt for a medium.
examples.zh: 我先登记了这次「拣货错误」，再把大号 T 恤换成中号。

words.enDefinition: a missing record because a worker did not register the start of a shift

examples.en: I reported a missed clock-in when the supervisor noticed a blank entry on the schedule.
examples.zh: 主管注意到那栏记录是空的，我报了「漏打上班卡」。

examples.en: The team lead explained how to correct a missed clock-in during our first training shift.
examples.zh: 值班组长在我们首班培训时解释了怎么补「漏打上班卡」。

words.enDefinition: a missing record because a worker did not register the end of a shift

examples.en: I reported a missed clock-out after noticing that my Thursday shift had no end time.
examples.zh: 我发现周四那个班没记录结束时间，报了「漏打下班卡」。

examples.en: The supervisor corrected my missed clock-out after checking when the last customer had left.
examples.zh: 主管核实了最后一位顾客离开的时间，然后补录了我「漏打的下班卡」。

collocations: an entry for a missed clock-out

words.enDefinition: a gradual move away from an organisation's stated purpose

examples.en: Members worried about mission drift as the cooperative began serving fewer students on tight budgets.
examples.zh: 得到合作社服务的经济拮据学生越来越少，成员开始担心出现「使命偏离」。

examples.en: The lecturer asked whether taking private bookings might lead to mission drift in the community workshop.
examples.zh: 讲师问，接受私人预约会不会使社区工作坊出现「使命偏离」。

words.enDefinition: a short statement explaining an organisation's central purpose

examples.en: The team revised its mission statement after members disagreed about who the bookshop should serve.
examples.zh: 成员对书店该服务谁意见不一，团队随后修改了「使命宣言」。

examples.en: In class, we compared the workshop's mission statement with the projects it actually funded.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们将工作坊的「使命宣言」与它实际资助的项目作了比较。

words.enDefinition: To keep checking how a new process is being introduced and what happens during that period.

examples.en: The charity asked two supervisors to monitor the rollout and report where volunteers needed more help.
examples.zh: 慈善机构请两位主管「跟踪推广实施进度」，并报告哪些方面的志愿者还需要帮助。

examples.en: We gave the client a simple chart to monitor the rollout of its new reminder process.
examples.zh: 我们给了客户一张简单的图表，用来「跟踪新提醒流程的推广实施进度」。

collocations: ask someone to monitor the rollout
use a dashboard to monitor the rollout

words.enDefinition: subscription-based income expressed as a monthly amount

examples.en: We used monthly recurring revenue to compare the subscription project before and after the summer break.
examples.zh: 我们用「月度经常性收入」比较订阅项目在暑假前后的情况。

examples.en: Jia divided the prepaid annual fee by twelve when calculating monthly recurring revenue for the class.
examples.zh: 佳在为课程计算「月度经常性收入」时，把预付年费除以了十二。

words.enDefinition: to designate the person who will coordinate implementation overall across the people and tasks involved

examples.en: The museum agreed to name an implementation lead before it tested the new group booking form.
examples.zh: 博物馆同意，在测试新的团体预约表前先「指定落实负责人」。

examples.en: We asked the charity to name an implementation lead to coordinate the work across both sites.
examples.zh: 我们请慈善机构「指定落实负责人」，协调两个场点的实施工作。

collocations: ask the client to name an implementation lead
agree to name an implementation lead
prepare to name an implementation lead

words.enDefinition: an organisation coordinated through linked units or partner organisations

examples.en: The textbook case described a network organisation linking a design studio to several independent makers.
examples.zh: 教材案例介绍了一家「网络型组织」，把设计工作室和几家独立制造商连在一起。

examples.en: We discussed how a network organisation might coordinate work when each partner had different schedules.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了每个合作伙伴时间安排不同时，「网络型组织」怎样协调工作。

words.enDefinition: a question worded without suggesting a preferred answer or implying a judgement

examples.en: The mentor asked us to start with a neutral question about how people currently book equipment.
examples.zh: 导师请我们先「中立提问」，问大家现在是怎么预约设备的。

examples.en: A neutral question gave the student room to describe what had happened in her own words.
examples.zh: 「中立提问」让那位学生能用自己的话叙述经过。

collocations: rewrite something as a neutral question

words.enDefinition: A notice clarifying that naming or recognising an organisation does not mean recommending it or its products.

examples.en: The programme said No endorsement implied beside the list of businesses that supplied the materials.
examples.zh: 手册在材料供应商名单旁注明「不代表支持或认可」。

examples.en: Our group discussed what No endorsement implied meant before approving the acknowledgement page for printing.
examples.zh: 批准印制致谢页前，我们小组讨论了「不代表支持或认可」是什么意思。

collocations: a note saying no endorsement implied
read the no endorsement implied note

words.enDefinition: a board member who does not run daily operations

examples.en: A non-executive director asked the manager how the new equipment would improve the repair service.
examples.zh: 一位「非执行董事」问经理，新设备会怎样改善维修服务。

examples.en: The lecturer asked us to compare the managing director's work with that of a non-executive director.
examples.zh: 讲师请我们比较总经理和「非执行董事」的工作。

collocations: a non-executive director on the board

words.enDefinition: a constraint that is not reached exactly at the given feasible solution and has some unused allowance

examples.en: The budget was a nonbinding constraint because our chosen plan cost less than the limit.
examples.zh: 我们选的方案花费低于上限，因此预算是「非紧约束」。

examples.en: I marked the available desks as a nonbinding constraint because several were left unused.
examples.zh: 还有几张桌子没用，我将可用桌数标为「非紧约束」。

collocations: a nonbinding constraint at the solution
show why a constraint is nonbinding

words.enDefinition: a result measured in terms other than money, such as time, quality or customer experience

examples.en: Waiting time was a nonfinancial outcome we considered when comparing plans for the repair shop.
examples.zh: 等候时长是比较维修店方案时，我们考虑的一项「非财务结果」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to mention one nonfinancial outcome alongside the forecast change in revenue.
examples.zh: 导师请我们在预测收入变化之外，再提到一项「非财务结果」。

words.enDefinition: A visit made specifically to see how an activity or process is carried out in practice.

examples.en: We arranged an observation visit to see how the repair charity recorded appointments during opening hours.
examples.zh: 我们安排了「现场走访观察」，了解维修慈善机构在开放时段怎样登记预约。

examples.en: The observation visit showed us how many people arrived without a confirmed time that afternoon.
examples.zh: 「现场走访观察」让我们看到，当天下午有多少人没确认预约时间就来了。

collocations: take notes during an observation visit

words.enDefinition: charging a different rate during less busy times

examples.en: The studio tried off-peak pricing to attract pottery groups on quiet weekday mornings.
examples.zh: 工作室试用了「非高峰时段定价」，吸引陶艺小组在较空闲的工作日上午来。

examples.en: Our team compared off-peak pricing for morning rentals with the rate charged after classes.
examples.zh: 团队把早间租用的「非高峰时段定价」与下课后的收费作了比较。

words.enDefinition: a work shift scheduled for a period when demand is comparatively low

examples.en: I took an off-peak shift on Wednesday to learn how to count the stock.
examples.zh: 我周三上了一个「非高峰班次」，学习怎么清点库存。

examples.en: The new volunteer chose an off-peak shift because it was easier to ask questions then.
examples.zh: 新志愿者选了「非高峰班次」，那时比较方便提问。

words.enDefinition: to ask whether another worker wants to take a shift assigned to you

examples.en: I chose to offer a shift to a coworker after the tutor moved our seminar.
examples.zh: 导师调整研讨课时间后，我选择向同事「提出转让一个班次」。

examples.en: The scheduling app lets workers offer a shift even when they do not need one back.
examples.zh: 排班应用允许员工「提出转让一个班次」，即使不需要别人换一个班给自己。

collocations: offer a shift to a colleague
learn how to offer a shift

words.enDefinition: workers who are available to respond or come in if called during an agreed period

examples.en: The coordinator arranged for on-call staff to handle deliveries arriving after the afternoon shift.
examples.zh: 协调员安排了「随时待命的员工」，处理下午班结束后到的送货。

examples.en: The on-call staff were contacted only when the queue could no longer be managed safely.
examples.zh: 排队的人多到难以维持秩序时，团队才联系了「随时待命的员工」。

collocations: make sure on-call staff are available

words.enDefinition: the supervisor responsible for a workplace or activity during the current shift

examples.en: The on-duty supervisor helped a new cashier check the register before the first sale.
examples.zh: 第一笔销售前，「在岗主管」帮新收银员检查了收银机。

examples.en: I left a message for the on-duty supervisor about the spare keys in the office.
examples.zh: 我给「在岗主管」留了条消息，说备用钥匙放在办公室。

words.enDefinition: instruction or guided practice provided during a person's assigned work hours

examples.en: I received on-shift training at the repair stall when orders were slow on Tuesday morning.
examples.zh: 周二上午订单少，我在维修摊参加了「当班培训」。

examples.en: The supervisor scheduled on-shift training for new staff before the last week of the term.
examples.zh: 主管在学期最后一周前给新员工安排了「当班培训」。

words.enDefinition: a voting rule giving each member an equal vote

examples.en: The student cooperative used one member, one vote when deciding whether to open a second workshop.
examples.zh: 学生合作社决定是否增开一个工作坊时，采用「一人一票」规则。

examples.en: Our tutor contrasted one member, one vote with voting rights tied to the number of shares.
examples.zh: 导师把「一人一票」和按持股数量分配表决权的做法作了比较。

collocations: a one member, one vote rule
the principle of one member, one vote

words.enDefinition: a very brief presentation that explains a proposal, product or venture in about a minute

examples.en: The tutor asked for a one-minute pitch before we prepared the full presentation for Friday.
examples.zh: 为周五准备完整演示前，导师让我们先做个「一分钟推介」。

examples.en: My one-minute pitch explained who used the service, what it did and why it mattered.
examples.zh: 我的「一分钟推介」说明了谁用这项服务、它能做什么，以及为什么有用。

words.enDefinition: a sale with no scheduled follow-up charges

examples.en: We treated each printed planner as a one-time sale, even if buyers came back later.
examples.zh: 我们把每本纸质计划本都视为「一次性销售」，即使买家之后可能再来。

examples.en: The illustrator chose a one-time sale for each download rather than charging a monthly fee.
examples.zh: 插画师决定每次下载按「一次性销售」收费，不按月收钱。

collocations: a one-time sale of a product
earn revenue from a one-time sale

words.enDefinition: a beta test open to a wider public so more people can try the product and provide feedback

examples.en: During our open beta, students at any nearby university could try the interactive campus map.
examples.zh: 在「公开测试」期间，本地各高校的学生都能试用这张互动校园地图。

examples.en: The help page explained that search might still be unreliable during the open beta.
examples.zh: 帮助页面说明，「公开测试」期间搜索功能可能还不稳定。

words.enDefinition: an interview that encourages participants to respond in their own words rather than choosing fixed answers

examples.en: We chose an open-ended interview because we did not yet know which problems were most important.
examples.zh: 我们选了「开放式访谈」，因为还不知道哪些问题最重要。

examples.en: The open-ended interview revealed a problem that none of our survey questions had mentioned.
examples.zh: 「开放式访谈」揭示了一个我们在问卷里没有提到的问题。

words.enDefinition: An order that still needs work before it can be closed

examples.en: There was one open order left for a tote bag with longer handles.
examples.zh: 还剩一笔「待处理订单」，要的是带长提手的手提包。

examples.en: I checked every open order before promising the remaining stock to walk-ups.
examples.zh: 答应把剩下的货卖给现场顾客之前，我检查了每笔「待处理订单」。

words.enDefinition: Questions or issues that still need discussion, information, or a decision.

examples.en: We listed open points from the meeting before asking the client who could answer them.
examples.zh: 我们列出了会议中「尚未解决的事项」，再问客户谁能回答。

examples.en: The project coordinator noted the open points so everyone knew what to check before Friday.
examples.zh: 项目协调员记下了「尚未解决的事项」，让大家知道周五前还要查什么。

words.enDefinition: a scheduled shift that does not yet have a worker assigned to it

examples.en: I requested an open shift after my Friday seminar was moved to the following week.
examples.zh: 周五研讨课改到下周后，我申请了一个「待认领班次」。

examples.en: The coordinator added an open shift when the market announced that it would stay open later.
examples.zh: 集市宣布延长开放时间后，协调员添加了一个「待认领班次」。

words.enDefinition: a list of things to check or complete before opening a workplace

examples.en: The opening checklist included checking that no orders from the previous day were still on the shelf.
examples.zh: 「开店检查清单」要求检查货架上是否还有前一天的订单。

examples.en: We updated the opening checklist after the new display needed a separate power supply.
examples.zh: 新展示台需要单独接电，我们更新了「开店检查清单」。

words.enDefinition: a question directed to a particular student without advance notice at the start of a case discussion

examples.en: The lecturer used an opening cold call to ask which option the shop should choose.
examples.zh: 讲师用一次「开场点名提问」问那家店该选哪个方案。

examples.en: I prepared my recommendation in case I got the opening cold call in our seminar.
examples.zh: 我准备好了自己的建议，以防研讨课「开场点名提问」叫到我。

collocations: start with an opening cold call
prepare for the opening cold call

words.enDefinition: the workers responsible for getting a workplace ready at the start of the day

examples.en: The opening crew checked the displays and put the signs out before the market opened.
examples.zh: 「开店班组」先检查陈列并把指示牌放到外面，然后集市才开放。

examples.en: I asked to join the opening crew because my lectures did not start until noon.
examples.zh: 我的课中午才开始，所以我申请加入「开店班组」。

words.enDefinition: the regular tasks workers carry out before a workplace opens for the day

examples.en: My opening duties included filling the display and checking which orders were ready for collection.
examples.zh: 我的「开店准备工作」包括补好展台上的货，确认哪些订单可以自取。

examples.en: We split the opening duties between three people so the counter could open on time.
examples.zh: 我们三个人分担了「开店准备工作」，柜台便能准时营业。

words.enDefinition: to run a venture while its costs exceed revenue

examples.en: The campus café could operate at a loss during exam week because very few students visited.
examples.zh: 考试周过来的人很少，校园咖啡馆可能会「亏损运营」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how long the project could operate at a loss before needing more support.
examples.zh: 导师问，项目可以「亏损运营」多久才需要更多支持。

collocations: continue to operate at a loss
operate at a loss for a month

words.enDefinition: an assumption about how an activity will run, such as hours, capacity or staff availability

examples.en: One operating assumption was that two people could pack all the orders before the store closed.
examples.zh: 一项「运营假设」是，两个人能在关店前打包完所有订单。

examples.en: The owner challenged our operating assumption about how long the counter would stay open on Fridays.
examples.zh: 店主质疑了我们关于周五柜台营业时长的「运营假设」。

words.enDefinition: how people and processes are organized to run a venture

examples.en: Our operating model moved repairs to a shared workshop and kept collections at the stall.
examples.zh: 我们的「运营模式」调整为在共享工作坊维修，在摊位收取待修物品。

examples.en: The judges asked what the operating model looked like when both founders had morning classes.
examples.zh: 评委问，两位创办人上午都有课时，项目采用怎样的「运营模式」。

words.enDefinition: A practical guide that tells people how to do recurring work and handle common situations.

examples.en: The students wrote an operating playbook for handling bookings when two theatre rooms were requested together.
examples.zh: 学生们编写了「日常操作手册」，说明有人同时预约剧院的两个房间时该怎么处理。

examples.en: We added examples to the operating playbook so new volunteers could practise before their first shift.
examples.zh: 我们在「日常操作手册」中加了实例，让新志愿者首次值班前能练习。

collocations: use an operating playbook to train staff

words.enDefinition: the ability to keep essential work going when people, schedules or conditions change unexpectedly

examples.en: Keeping spare tools nearby helped maintain operational continuity during the busy university fair.
examples.zh: 校园展会期间，店里在近处备了一套工具，以维持「运营连续性」。

examples.en: The new roster helped maintain operational continuity while two supervisors attended training on different days.
examples.zh: 两名主管分不同日子参加培训，新排班表帮助维持了「运营连续性」。

words.enDefinition: the process of noticing a situation that could support a useful new business or service

examples.en: For our lesson on opportunity recognition, we observed how students waited for evening buses.
examples.zh: 为学习「商业机会识别」，我们观察了学生晚上怎么等公交车。

examples.en: The founder described opportunity recognition as listening for problems people encounter repeatedly on campus.
examples.zh: 那位创业者说，「商业机会识别」就是留意人们在校园里反复遇到的问题。

words.enDefinition: A change made to the details of an existing order

examples.en: I wrote down the order amendment so we would pack the smaller print.
examples.zh: 我记下了这次「订单修改」，这样我们就会装较小的那幅版画。

examples.en: We confirmed the order amendment before adding a second notebook to her bag.
examples.zh: 我们先确认了「订单修改」，才往她的袋子里多放了一本笔记本。

words.enDefinition: The latest time when orders are accepted for a particular batch

examples.en: Our order cutoff is Thursday at noon for anyone collecting prints on Friday.
examples.zh: 想周五来取版画的话，我们的「截单时间」是周四中午。

examples.en: I set the order cutoff early enough to pack everything before my evening class.
examples.zh: 我把「截单时间」设得够早，这样上晚课前能打包好所有东西。

words.enDefinition: The process of preparing an order and getting it to the customer

examples.en: We handled order fulfilment ourselves, from sorting the stock to handing over each bag.
examples.zh: 从整理库存到把一个个袋子交给顾客，整个「订单履约」过程都由我们自己负责。

examples.en: The group moved order fulfilment to the studio so orders could be packed indoors.
examples.zh: 小组把「订单履约」移到工作室，这样可以在室内打包。

words.enDefinition: The process of receiving and recording new orders for work

examples.en: We moved order intake to a shared form after losing two paper notes.
examples.zh: 弄丢两张纸条之后，我们改用共享表单「接收和登记订单」。

examples.en: Amira handled order intake while I checked how many bags we could still make.
examples.zh: 阿米拉负责「接单登记」，我去查我们还能做多少个包。

words.enDefinition: A record of the orders a seller has received

examples.en: The order log showed which notebooks still needed a name on the cover.
examples.zh: 「订单登记表」上写着哪些笔记本的封面还需要加名字。

examples.en: I entered the phone order in our order log after speaking to the customer.
examples.zh: 与顾客通完话后，我把这笔电话订单录入了「订单登记表」。

words.enDefinition: an estimate aimed at finding the approximate scale, such as tens, hundreds or thousands

examples.en: We needed an order-of-magnitude estimate of how many shelves a campus-wide service might use.
examples.zh: 我们需要对覆盖全校的服务所需货架数做一个「数量级估算」。

examples.en: An order-of-magnitude estimate was enough to show that one small room could not hold the stock.
examples.zh: 做个「数量级估算」就足以看出，一间小屋装不下这些库存。

words.enDefinition: Selecting the correct items from stored stock for specific orders

examples.en: We did order picking in the cupboard before anyone started sealing the envelopes.
examples.zh: 大家开始封信封前，我们先从柜子里「按单拣货」。

examples.en: Our color labels made order picking easier when the team packed after class.
examples.zh: 小组下课后打包时，色标让「按单拣货」更容易。

words.enDefinition: The sequence of orders waiting to be handled or completed

examples.en: One person watched the order queue while the rest of us packed boxes.
examples.zh: 一个人盯着「待处理订单队列」，其他人都在打包。

examples.en: The order queue filled up with bag orders after the club posted our photos.
examples.zh: 社团发了我们的照片后，「待处理订单队列」里一下子挤满了买包的订单。

words.enDefinition: The time needed to complete an order after receiving it

examples.en: We shortened order turnaround by keeping extra handles ready to sew onto bags.
examples.zh: 我们多备了些能直接缝到包上的提手，缩短了「订单周转时间」。

examples.en: I estimated the order turnaround before agreeing to make another set of mugs.
examples.zh: 答应再做一套马克杯之前，我先估算了「订单周转时间」。

words.enDefinition: a flexible arrangement with adaptable roles and less central control

examples.en: The design team adopted an organic structure so members could shift roles quickly during the project.
examples.zh: 设计团队采用「有机式组织结构」，成员可以在项目期间迅速改变分工。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how an organic structure might help a business respond quickly to unexpected requests.
examples.zh: 导师问，「有机式组织结构」如何帮助企业迅速应对计划外的请求。

collocations: switch to a more organic structure

words.enDefinition: a diagram of roles and reporting relationships in an organisation

examples.en: The tutor asked us to update the organisational chart after the two departments were combined.
examples.zh: 两个部门合并后，导师让我们更新「组织结构图」。

examples.en: I checked the organisational chart to see where the university print service sat within the department.
examples.zh: 我查看了「组织结构图」，想知道学校的打印业务在这个部门中归哪一级管理。

words.enDefinition: shared beliefs and habits that shape how an organisation works

examples.en: The guest speaker described an organisational culture where staff were comfortable admitting small mistakes.
examples.zh: 客座讲者描述了一种让员工可以坦然承认小错误的「组织文化」。

examples.en: Our report examined how organisational culture influenced the way the workshop welcomed new members.
examples.zh: 报告分析了「组织文化」怎样影响工作坊接纳新成员的方式。

words.enDefinition: the process of arranging roles and relationships across an organisation

examples.en: Our lecturer introduced organisational design with a case about a repair business that had just doubled in size.
examples.zh: 讲师用一家规模刚翻倍的维修企业作为案例，介绍「组织设计」。

examples.en: The class compared approaches to organisational design before deciding how to group the library service teams.
examples.zh: 同学们先比较了不同的「组织设计」做法，再决定怎样给图书馆服务团队分组。

words.enDefinition: a purposeful change to an existing arrangement of roles or units

examples.en: The fictional retailer began an organisational redesign after opening separate stores for repairs and rentals.
examples.zh: 虚构的零售商为维修和租赁分别开店后，开始「组织重构」。

examples.en: Our group linked the organisational redesign to problems that appeared when the first branch opened.
examples.zh: 我们小组把「组织重构」与第一家分店开业时出现的问题联系起来。

words.enDefinition: a group that works in isolation from other groups

examples.en: The inventory team became an organisational silo because it rarely shared changes with the repair desk.
examples.zh: 库存团队很少把变更情况告诉维修台，成了一个「组织孤岛」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked what made the finance office an organisational silo in the class case.
examples.zh: 导师问，课堂案例里的财务处为什么会成为「组织孤岛」。

words.enDefinition: the arrangement of roles and authority within an organisation

examples.en: The organisational structure showed which teams reported directly to the manager of the arts centre.
examples.zh: 该「组织结构」显示哪些团队直接向艺术中心经理汇报。

examples.en: Our case report described how the organisational structure changed when the second branch opened.
examples.zh: 我们的案例报告介绍了第二家分店开业后，「组织结构」有什么变化。

words.enDefinition: Detailed requirements for what the finished work should be like, such as size, format, or quality.

examples.en: The output specifications gave different dimensions for the lobby signs and the small table signs.
examples.zh: 「成品规格要求」为大堂标牌和桌面小牌给出了不同尺寸。

examples.en: Our team asked for the output specifications before editing the photographs for the exhibition wall.
examples.zh: 团队在为展墙修照片之前，请对方提供了「成品规格要求」。

words.enDefinition: Not included in the tasks or services originally agreed for a project.

examples.en: Transporting the display boards was outside the scope of the work agreed with the studio.
examples.zh: 运送展板「不在与工作室约定的工作范围内」。

examples.en: The organiser asked whether redesigning the invitations would be outside the scope of the printing job.
examples.zh: 组织者问，重新设计请柬是否「不在印刷工作的约定范围内」。

words.enDefinition: Requested changes that still need to be completed before work is ready.

examples.en: The designer shared a list of outstanding revisions before our group met at the studio.
examples.zh: 我们小组到工作室碰面前，设计员分享了一份「尚未完成的修改」清单。

examples.en: We finished the outstanding revisions after the venue confirmed the correct entrance for the event.
examples.zh: 场地方确认了活动的正确入口后，我们完成了「尚未完成的修改」。

words.enDefinition: work shifts that share a period when workers from both are on duty

examples.en: We used overlapping shifts so the morning crew could explain the work to the afternoon team.
examples.zh: 我们安排了「有重叠时段的班次」，让早班能向下午班说明手头工作。

examples.en: The schedule included overlapping shifts while the shop stayed open during the student fair.
examples.zh: 学生展会期间店面继续营业，排班表安排了「有重叠时段的班次」。

collocations: use overlapping shifts for a handover

words.enDefinition: having more workers available than the amount of work reasonably requires

examples.en: The stall seemed overstaffed on Friday because most students left after their last lecture.
examples.zh: 周五大多数学生上完最后一堂课就走了，摊位看起来「人员配备过多」。

examples.en: We try to avoid being overstaffed in the morning when deliveries have not yet arrived.
examples.zh: 早上货物还没送到，我们尽量避免「人员配备过多」。

words.enDefinition: A supply of goods in excess of what is needed

examples.en: The green notebooks became overstock after we ordered too many in spring.
examples.zh: 春天绿皮笔记本订得太多，后来就「库存过剩」了。

examples.en: The library helped us clear our overstock by buying the extra blank journals.
examples.zh: 图书馆买下了多余的空白手账本，帮我们清掉了「过剩库存」。

words.enDefinition: a person who owns a business and takes part in running its daily operations

examples.en: As the owner-operator, Leila set the schedule and worked the counter on busy afternoons.
examples.zh: 莉拉是「亲自经营的业主」，她排班，也在客流大的下午照看柜台。

examples.en: I asked the owner-operator how she balanced repairs and sales with her afternoon classes.
examples.zh: 我问那位「亲自经营的业主」，她如何兼顾维修、销售和下午的课。

words.enDefinition: Take apart a stall and put its equipment away after trading

examples.en: We waited for the last pickup before we began to pack down the stall.
examples.zh: 等最后一位顾客取完货，我们才开始「收摊收设备」。

examples.en: Could you help me pack down the stall once the other sellers clear the aisle?
examples.zh: 等其他摊商把过道清出来，你能帮我「收摊撤掉设备」吗？

collocations: start to pack down the stall
pack down the stall at closing time

words.enDefinition: Put items into different packages instead of packing them together

examples.en: Please pack separately when two people have paid for items in the same set.
examples.zh: 同一套商品由两个人分别付款时，请「分开打包」。

examples.en: We can pack separately if the tall cups don't fit beside the small bowls.
examples.zh: 高一点的杯子如果放不进小碗旁边，我们可以「分开打包」。

words.enDefinition: A check that the contents of a package match an order

examples.en: The final packing check caught a white bag in an order for navy.
examples.zh: 最后一次「打包核对」发现，有人把要藏蓝色的订单装成了白包。

examples.en: We added a packing check after two notebook orders got mixed up last week.
examples.zh: 上周两笔笔记本订单弄混了，我们加了一道「打包核对」。

words.enDefinition: A place set up with supplies for packing orders or parcels

examples.en: We set up a packing station with tape and boxes behind the stall.
examples.zh: 我们在摊位后设了一个「打包装货工位」，备好胶带和盒子。

examples.en: I left the tissue paper at the packing station before going to class.
examples.zh: 去上课前，我把包装薄纸留在了「打包装货工位」。

words.enDefinition: a model made from paper to test a design or sequence before implementing it

examples.en: The paper prototype had separate cards for the pages students would see on their phones.
examples.zh: 「纸质原型」每页用一张单独的卡片，模拟学生在手机上会看到的内容。

examples.en: We changed the order of the cards in the paper prototype after watching three people try it.
examples.zh: 看过三个人试用后，我们调换了「纸质原型」中卡片的顺序。

words.enDefinition: To set an issue aside for later so the current discussion or work can continue.

examples.en: We agreed to park an issue about summer opening hours until the manager could join.
examples.zh: 我们商定先「暂时搁置一个问题」，就是夏季开放时间，等经理能参加再谈。

examples.en: The team decided to park an issue raised by the second branch until the data arrived.
examples.zh: 团队决定，数据到之前先「暂时搁置第二个分点提出的问题」。

collocations: decide to park an issue until the review
park an issue for later discussion

words.enDefinition: A delivery containing only part of what was ordered

examples.en: We got a partial delivery of blank journals before opening our end of term booth.
examples.zh: 学期末摆摊前，我们订的空白手账本「只送到了一部分」。

examples.en: Our supplier offered a partial delivery on Tuesday and the rest the following week.
examples.zh: 供货商提出周二「先交付部分货物」，剩下的下一周再送。

words.enDefinition: Having some ordered items supplied while others are still outstanding

examples.en: I marked the order partially fulfilled because the customer took only the prints.
examples.zh: 顾客只拿走了版画，所以我把订单标成「已部分履约」。

examples.en: The mug order remained partially fulfilled until we delivered the last two boxes.
examples.zh: 最后两箱还没交付前，马克杯订单一直显示「已部分履约」。

words.enDefinition: a fixed payment that supports someone taking part in a programme, placement or study

examples.en: The participant stipend helped cover my travel to the entrepreneurship programme during the spring term.
examples.zh: 春季学期，「参与津贴」帮我负担了参加创业培养项目的交通费。

examples.en: The application explained how and when students would receive their participant stipend after joining.
examples.zh: 申请材料说明了学生加入后如何、何时领取「参与津贴」。

words.enDefinition: an approach that involves affected people in guiding an organisation

examples.en: The campus food project tried participatory governance by inviting members to help set its priorities.
examples.zh: 校园餐饮项目尝试「参与式治理」，请成员参与确定先做哪些事。

examples.en: Our class debated whether participatory governance could work when half the members lived off campus.
examples.zh: 班上讨论了一半成员住在校外时，「参与式治理」是否行得通。

words.enDefinition: The person responsible for coordinating work between the groups in a partnership.

examples.en: Our partnership lead checked which group was bringing equipment for each afternoon workshop session.
examples.zh: 「合作负责人」核对了每天下午的工作坊分别由哪个小组带设备。

examples.en: The student centre named a partnership lead to coordinate our work with the print studio.
examples.zh: 学生中心指定了一名「合作负责人」，协调我们与印刷工场的工作。

words.enDefinition: A document or presentation suggesting how two groups could work together and what each would contribute.

examples.en: Our partnership proposal suggested that the student group manage the exhibition and the studio lend equipment.
examples.zh: 我们的「合作提案」建议由学生小组管理展览，工作室出借设备。

examples.en: The gallery asked us to explain our roles more clearly in the partnership proposal.
examples.zh: 画廊请我们在「合作提案」中更清楚地说明各自的角色。

words.enDefinition: to make another party pay an increased expense

examples.en: When paper became more expensive, the print team decided to pass on the cost to customers.
examples.zh: 纸价上涨后，打印小组决定把这笔成本「转嫁」给顾客。

examples.en: The student stall chose not to pass on the cost of compostable cups during the trial.
examples.zh: 试行期间，学生摊位决定不把可堆肥杯子的成本「转嫁」给顾客。

collocations: pass on the cost to customers
pass on the cost of delivery

words.zhGloss: 按自己能负担的金额支付
words.enDefinition: an arrangement allowing customers to pay according to their means
acceptedZhAnswers: 按自己能负担的金额支付

examples.en: We put “Pay what you can” on the sign for our student-run repair afternoon.
examples.zh: 学生组织的下午维修活动上，我们在牌子上写了「按自己能负担的金额支付」。

examples.en: The theatre group tried a pay what you can policy for its first performance of the term.
examples.zh: 剧团在本学期首场演出试用了「按自己能负担的金额支付」的办法。

words.enDefinition: a person or organization that pays for an offering

examples.en: For our note-sharing service, the department was the paying customer and the students used it.
examples.zh: 我们的笔记共享服务中，系里是「付费客户」，使用者是学生。

examples.en: The student bakery got its first paying customer at the residence hall's open day.
examples.zh: 学生面包坊在宿舍开放日迎来了第一位「付费客户」。

collocations: convert a trial user into a paying customer

words.enDefinition: a time during which demand for a product or service is especially high

examples.en: The lunch hour was our peak-demand period because most students finished class at noon.
examples.zh: 午餐时间是我们的「需求高峰时段」，因为大多数学生中午才下课。

examples.en: We stocked the counter before the peak-demand period began at the end of lectures.
examples.zh: 课程结束后就是「需求高峰时段」，我们提前给柜台补好了货。

words.enDefinition: Having a closure that sticks after a protective strip is removed

examples.en: I bought peel-and-seal envelopes so we wouldn't need tape for each order.
examples.zh: 我买了「揭纸即粘的」信封，这样每笔订单就不用另贴胶带。

examples.en: The peel-and-seal bags worked well for the smallest cards on our table.
examples.zh: 「揭纸即粘的」袋子很适合装我们桌上最小的卡片。

words.enDefinition: another founder at a similar stage or in the same community

examples.en: I asked a peer founder how she scheduled interviews around classes and part-time work.
examples.zh: 我问一位「创业同辈」，她是怎么在上课和做兼职之余安排访谈的。

examples.en: A peer founder shared how his team had found a room for weekly testing.
examples.zh: 一位「创业同辈」分享了他们团队如何找到每周做测试的场地。

collocations: get advice from a peer founder

words.enDefinition: pricing based on the number of users given access

examples.en: For the booking software, per-seat pricing meant a society paid for each committee member with access.
examples.zh: 这款预订软件采用「按席位定价」，社团要为每个取得访问权限的委员付费。

examples.en: The team compared per-seat pricing with a single licence covering the whole student newspaper staff.
examples.zh: 团队将「按席位定价」与整家学生报社的员工共用一份授权的做法作比较。

words.enDefinition: A person's or organisation's consent to use the artwork in the way discussed.

examples.en: The club asked for permission to use the artwork in the programme for next year's exhibition.
examples.zh: 社团询问能否取得「使用图稿的许可」，用在明年展览的手册里。

examples.en: We confirmed permission to use the artwork on the banner before placing the print order.
examples.zh: 我们先确认取得了「使用图稿的许可」，才下单印横幅。

collocations: ask for permission to use the artwork
receive permission to use the artwork
confirm permission to use the artwork

words.enDefinition: A form field where customers enter details for a customised item

examples.en: The personalisation field tells us which name to print on the bag.
examples.zh: 「个性化定制输入栏」告诉我们应该在包上印哪个名字。

examples.en: I left the personalisation field optional for people who wanted plain labels.
examples.zh: 我把「个性化定制输入栏」设成选填，方便只要普通标签的顾客。

words.enDefinition: the gradual return of operations in a planned order
