examples.en: The case proposed a phased resumption that reopened equipment returns before the new bookings desk.
examples.zh: 案例提出「分阶段恢复」，先恢复器材归还，再恢复接受新预约的柜台。

examples.en: We debated whether phased resumption would help the campus print shop handle its backlog safely.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「分阶段恢复」能否帮助学校打印店稳妥处理积压工作。

words.enDefinition: A count of the actual items present at a location

examples.en: We did a physical count before loading the prints and found two extra copies.
examples.zh: 装版画前我们做了次「实物盘点」，发现多了两张。

examples.en: The physical count included mugs we planned to put aside for Saturday's pickups.
examples.zh: 「实物盘点」把我们打算留给周六取货的那些马克杯也数进去了。

collocations: verify stock with a physical count

words.enDefinition: Select items from storage and package them for individual orders

examples.en: We can pick and pack all the print orders before our afternoon lab.
examples.zh: 我们能在下午的实验课前，把所有版画订单「拣好货并打包」。

examples.en: I offered to pick and pack while the maker finished painting the last bowl.
examples.zh: 制作同学在给最后一个碗上色，我提出帮忙「拣货并打包」。

words.enDefinition: a readily accessible shelf or slot from which workers routinely pick stock to fill orders

examples.en: I kept the front bin as a pick face for the smallest cards.
examples.zh: 我用前面的那格作为小卡片的「前置拣货位」。

examples.en: We filled the pick face from boxes in the back before pickup opened.
examples.zh: 开放取货前，我们从后面的箱子里拿货，补满了「前置拣货位」。

words.enDefinition: A document listing what to collect from storage for an order

examples.en: The pick ticket told me to take one notebook from the upper shelf.
examples.zh: 「拣货单」上写着从上层架子拿一本笔记本。

examples.en: I attached the pick ticket to the basket while I looked for matching cards.
examples.zh: 我把「拣货单」夹在篮子上，然后去找配套的卡片。

words.enDefinition: to agree to work an additional shift that was not on your schedule

examples.en: I offered to pick up a shift between my lecture and the evening rehearsal.
examples.zh: 我提出在课后到晚间排练之间「接下一个额外班次」。

examples.en: My classmate could pick up a shift after checking that exams had not been moved.
examples.zh: 我的同学确认考试时间没改，可以「接下一个额外班次」。

collocations: offer to pick up a shift
ask to pick up a shift
pick up a shift at short notice

words.enDefinition: A record of orders expected to be collected in person

examples.en: The pickup list showed which orders belonged at the table near the entrance.
examples.zh: 「取货订单清单」标出了哪些订单该放在入口旁的桌子上。

examples.en: I checked the pickup list before carrying the last three packages to campus.
examples.zh: 把最后三个包裹带到学校前，我核对了「取货订单清单」。

collocations: cross names off the pickup list

words.enDefinition: An item the seller offers for collection instead of delivery

examples.en: The framed print was a pickup-only item because I didn't have suitable packaging.
examples.zh: 我没有合适的包装，所以那幅带框的版画是「仅限自取的商品」。

examples.en: I listed each ceramic lamp as a pickup-only item for our market weekend.
examples.zh: 我把每盏陶瓷灯都标为市集周末「仅限自取的商品」。

collocations: mark something as a pickup-only item
a pickup-only item at the fair

words.enDefinition: A message reminding a customer to collect an order already prepared

examples.en: I sent a pickup reminder before leaving the stall for my afternoon lecture.
examples.zh: 离开摊位去上下午的课之前，我发了条「取货提醒」。

examples.en: The pickup reminder included a photo of the library door nearest our table.
examples.zh: 「取货提醒」附了一张离摊位最近的图书馆入口照片。

words.enDefinition: the group of people or organisations selected to take part in a limited trial

examples.en: The first pilot cohort included students from three departments who often borrowed the same equipment.
examples.zh: 第一批「试点参与群体」来自三个系，他们经常借用同样的器材。

examples.en: Our pilot cohort gave feedback after trying the service for two weeks during term time.
examples.zh: 学期内试用两周后，我们的「试点参与群体」给出了反馈。

collocations: follow up with the pilot cohort

words.enDefinition: a customer who uses a product or service in a limited trial before wider availability

examples.en: Our first pilot customer agreed to try the repaired bicycle service for one term.
examples.zh: 我们的首位「试点客户」同意试用翻修自行车服务一个学期。

examples.en: A pilot customer sent us comments after using the booking page for several campus events.
examples.zh: 一位「试点客户」用预约页面办过几场校园活动后，给我们发来了意见。

words.enDefinition: the start of a limited live trial before a product or service is offered more widely

examples.en: The pilot launch gave volunteers a chance to use the new process with real bookings.
examples.zh: 「试点启动」后，志愿者有机会把新流程用到真实预约上。

examples.en: We scheduled the pilot launch for a week when the usual equipment desk could help.
examples.zh: 我们选了常规器材服务台能帮忙的一周作为「试点启动」时间。

words.enDefinition: An assessment of a small trial to decide whether to continue, change, or stop what was tested.

examples.en: The pilot review showed that the new form saved time on weekday bookings at one site.
examples.zh: 「试行后的评审」显示，新表格节省了一个场点工作日的预约处理时间。

examples.en: We brought records from both weeks to the pilot review so the staff could compare them.
examples.zh: 我们把两周的记录都带到「试行后的评审」上，供员工比较。

collocations: discuss results at the pilot review

words.enDefinition: To try a proposed process with a small group or at one location before wider use.

examples.en: The repair charity decided to pilot the new process on Saturdays when more volunteers were present.
examples.zh: 维修慈善机构决定在志愿者较多的周六「小范围试行新流程」。

examples.en: We asked the museum to pilot the new process with one school group before wider use.
examples.zh: 我们请博物馆先找一个学校团体「小范围试行新流程」，再扩大使用范围。

collocations: choose where to pilot the new process
agree to pilot the new process
pilot the new process at one site

words.enDefinition: the specific funding, partnership or other support a presenter requests from a pitch audience

examples.en: Our pitch ask was for space to run weekend tests with two student societies.
examples.zh: 我们「推介结尾的具体请求」是借用场地，周末和两个学生社团一起做测试。

examples.en: The mentor helped us make the pitch ask specific enough for the judges to act on.
examples.zh: 导师帮我们把「推介结尾的具体请求」说得更明确，方便评审提供帮助。

words.enDefinition: a collection of slides used to explain and promote a business proposal or venture

examples.en: Our pitch deck used one slide to explain how students currently borrow equipment from clubs.
examples.zh: 我们的「创业推介幻灯片」用了一页说明学生目前怎么向社团借用器材。

examples.en: I shortened the pitch deck after realising we had only five minutes to present.
examples.zh: 发现介绍时间只有五分钟后，我删减了「创业推介幻灯片」。

words.enDefinition: the aspects judges consider when assessing a pitch, such as evidence, feasibility or clarity

examples.en: We read the pitch judging criteria to see whether the panel expected evidence from potential customers.
examples.zh: 我们看了「推介评审标准」，想知道评审是否要求提供来自潜在客户的证据。

examples.en: The organisers explained the pitch judging criteria before anyone submitted their slides for the final round.
examples.zh: 最终一轮提交幻灯片之前，组织者解释了「推介评审标准」。

words.enDefinition: the first part of a pitch, where the presenter introduces the main situation or attracts interest

examples.en: We changed our pitch opening to start with a story from the campus equipment desk.
examples.zh: 我们改了「推介开场」，从校园器材服务台的一段经历讲起。

examples.en: The pitch opening described a familiar problem before we showed the design on screen.
examples.zh: 「推介开场」先讲了大家熟悉的一个问题，然后才在屏幕上展示设计。

words.enDefinition: a question period during or after a pitch when the audience can ask the team for details

examples.en: During the pitch Q&A, a judge asked why our first tests involved only one sports club.
examples.zh: 在「推介问答」中，一位评审问首轮测试为什么只找了一个体育社团。

examples.en: We rehearsed the pitch Q&A with classmates who had not seen the slide deck yet.
examples.zh: 我们找了还没看过幻灯片的同学，陪我们演练「推介问答」。

collocations: answer questions in the pitch Q&A

words.enDefinition: a practice session before giving a pitch to its intended audience

examples.en: Our pitch rehearsal showed that the live demonstration took longer than we had planned.
examples.zh: 「推介演练」发现，现场演示比我们计划的用时更长。

examples.en: Two other founders attended our pitch rehearsal and questioned how we would reach more customers.
examples.zh: 另外两位创业者参加了我们的「推介演练」，问我们怎么接触到更多客户。

collocations: give feedback at a pitch rehearsal

words.enDefinition: a session in which participants learn and practise how to present a venture succinctly

examples.en: The pitch workshop helped us explain what our service did without reading from the slide.
examples.zh: 「项目推介工作坊」帮我们练习不用照着幻灯片念，也能说清服务的用途。

examples.en: I brought a rough outline to the pitch workshop and tested it with another founder.
examples.zh: 我带了一份粗略提纲来参加「项目推介工作坊」，讲给另一位创业者听了听。

words.enDefinition: to substantially change the direction of a venture idea in response to what the team learns

examples.en: We decided to pivot the business after students asked for evening pickups rather than deliveries.
examples.zh: 学生提出想在晚上自取，我们决定「调整创业方向」。

examples.en: The mentor asked whether we could pivot the business without rebuilding the whole booking system.
examples.zh: 导师问，能不能在不用重做整套预约系统的情况下「调整创业方向」。

collocations: be ready to pivot the business

words.enDefinition: a charge for using an online platform or its services

examples.en: The tutoring website kept a small platform fee whenever a student booked a group lesson.
examples.zh: 每次有学生预订团体课时，家教网站会留下一小笔「平台服务费」。

examples.en: Our team counted the platform fee before estimating how much each craft seller would receive.
examples.zh: 团队估算每位手工艺卖家能拿到多少钱时，先把「平台服务费」算了进去。

words.enDefinition: a framework for analysing five sources of competitive pressure in an industry

examples.en: We applied Porter's Five Forces to compare conditions in local bicycle repair and equipment hire.
examples.zh: 我们运用「波特五力模型」比较本地自行车维修和设备租赁行业的情况。

examples.en: The lecturer used Porter's Five Forces to explain why competition is more than rivalry between shops.
examples.zh: 讲师用「波特五力模型」说明为什么门店间的较量只是竞争的一部分。

collocations: analyse an industry with Porter's Five Forces

words.enDefinition: an assessment after a decision that examines its implementation, results or quality of reasoning

examples.en: The post-decision review found that more students used the later pickup time than we had expected.
examples.zh: 「决策后复盘」发现，晚一点来自取的学生比我们预想的多。

examples.en: In our post-decision review, we compared the original demand forecast with the actual bookings.
examples.zh: 在「决策后复盘」中，我们把原先的需求预测与真实预约数作了比较。

collocations: discuss findings from a post-decision review

words.enDefinition: a discussion after a pitch to review what happened and what could be improved

examples.en: In our post-pitch debrief, we noticed that the audience misunderstood the same example twice.
examples.zh: 在「推介后的复盘」里，我们发现观众两次都误解了同一个例子。

examples.en: Our post-pitch debrief helped us choose which feedback to use before applying to another programme.
examples.zh: 「推介后的复盘」帮我们决定，申请另一个项目前该采用哪些反馈。

collocations: take notes at a post-pitch debrief

words.enDefinition: a person or organisation that might buy a product or service in the future

examples.en: I spoke to a potential customer who manages equipment for several student sports teams.
examples.zh: 我和一位「潜在客户」聊过，他管理着几支学生运动队的器材。

examples.en: A potential customer asked whether our repair service would be available over the winter break.
examples.zh: 一位「潜在客户」问，我们寒假期间有没有维修服务。

words.enDefinition: how realistic it is to carry out a proposal under actual conditions

examples.en: We checked practical feasibility by asking who could staff the repair desk at seven.
examples.zh: 我们问了谁能七点去维修台值班，以验证「实际可行性」。

examples.en: The tutor wanted us to discuss practical feasibility as well as the strength of the idea.
examples.zh: 导师希望我们除了说创意的优点，也讨论「实际可行性」。

words.enDefinition: a programme that helps very early teams test an idea and prepare for further development

examples.en: The pre-accelerator accepted teams that were still deciding which problem they wanted to solve.
examples.zh: 这个「预加速创业项目」也接收还在确定要解决什么问题的团队。

examples.en: We joined a pre-accelerator to check our assumptions before applying to the main programme.
examples.zh: 我们加入了「预加速创业项目」，先核实假设，再申请正式项目。

words.enDefinition: notes made before a class about a case's facts, uncertainties and possible decisions

examples.en: My pre-class case notes included two questions about the shop's supply costs in winter.
examples.zh: 我的「课前案例笔记」里有两个关于那家店冬季供货成本的问题。

examples.en: We compared pre-class case notes over lunch before joining the rest of the tutorial group.
examples.zh: 加入其他辅导课同学前，我们午饭时对比了彼此的「课前案例笔记」。

words.enDefinition: A review conducted before handing over agreed work or goods to catch remaining problems.

examples.en: We arranged a pre-delivery review to check the display labels before handing them to the gallery.
examples.zh: 我们安排了「交付前检查」，把展品标签交给画廊之前先核对一遍。

examples.en: The pre-delivery review revealed that one sponsor's name was missing from the rear banner.
examples.zh: 「交付前检查」发现后面的横幅漏掉了一家赞助方的名字。

words.enDefinition: A sample made before the main run to show how the finished goods are expected to look or work.

examples.en: The student team checked a pre-production sample before ordering enough canvas bags for the fair.
examples.zh: 学生团队在订购市集所需数量的帆布袋之前，检查了「生产前样品」。

examples.en: The workshop brought a pre-production sample so we could test whether the stand fit our table.
examples.zh: 工场带来一个「生产前样品」，好让我们试试展架能不能放到桌上。

words.enDefinition: Early suggestions for action that may change after more work or feedback.

examples.en: We shared preliminary recommendations about the reminder process while volunteers were still testing the wording.
examples.zh: 志愿者还在试用提示语时，我们分享了关于提醒流程的「初步建议」。

examples.en: The theatre manager reviewed our preliminary recommendations before we estimated the effort each would require.
examples.zh: 剧院经理先看了我们的「初步建议」，我们随后估算每条建议需要多少投入。

words.enDefinition: an exercise that starts by imagining a project has already failed and works backwards to identify possible causes

examples.en: We ran a premortem by assuming the evening pickup trial had already failed and asking why.
examples.zh: 我们做了「项目失败预演」，先假设晚间取货试点已经失败，再找原因。

examples.en: The premortem identified late deliveries as a risk the team had not discussed before.
examples.zh: 「项目失败预演」找出了一项团队此前没讨论过的风险，即送货延迟。

collocations: discuss the findings from a premortem

words.enDefinition: a set of products or services paid for in advance

examples.en: The student tutor sold a prepaid package of four conversation lessons at the start of term.
examples.zh: 开学时，学生辅导老师出售含四节口语课的「预付套餐」。

examples.en: We compared a prepaid package with single bookings for the campus pottery studio's open sessions.
examples.zh: 我们比较了校园陶艺工作室开放时段的「预付套餐」和单次预约。

words.enDefinition: a condition that must be met before a plan can be put into action

examples.en: A second collection table was a prerequisite for implementation of the new pickup process.
examples.zh: 设第二张自取桌是启用新取货流程的「实施前提」。

examples.en: The case identified staff training as a prerequisite for implementation before the shop advertised longer hours.
examples.zh: 案例把员工培训列为店铺宣传延长营业时间的「实施前提」。

collocations: state the main prerequisite for implementation

words.zhGloss: 以呈献名义署名的赞助方
words.enDefinition: A sponsor prominently credited as presenting an event in some of its publicity.
acceptedZhAnswers: 以呈献名义署名的赞助方
以呈献方名义署名的赞助商

examples.en: The presenting sponsor was credited directly under the festival title on the programme cover.
examples.zh: 活动手册把「以呈献名义署名的赞助方」列在节庆名称正下方。

examples.en: We asked the presenting sponsor to approve how its name appeared beside the exhibition title.
examples.zh: 我们请「以呈献名义署名的赞助方」确认其名称在展览标题旁怎么展示。

words.enDefinition: to set the amount due according to an item's weight

examples.en: At the campus refill stall, we price by weight because shoppers bring containers of different sizes.
examples.zh: 在校园补充装摊位，我们「按重量定价」，因为顾客带来的容器大小各异。

examples.en: The food cooperative chose to price by weight for loose apples supplied by a local farm.
examples.zh: 食品合作社决定对本地农场供应的散装苹果「按重量定价」。

collocations: price by weight rather than quantity
price by weight for loose produce

words.enDefinition: A small sign showing the price of a displayed item

examples.en: I put a price card beside each stack so customers could browse quietly.
examples.zh: 我在每摞商品旁都放了张「标价卡」，让顾客可以安静地选购。

examples.en: We printed a new price card when we added the larger sketchbooks to the table.
examples.zh: 我们把大号素描本也摆上桌时，印了一张新的「标价卡」。

words.enDefinition: the minimum price allowed under a rule or pricing policy

examples.en: The student design team set a price floor for custom posters to cover printing and basic labour.
examples.zh: 学生设计团队为定制海报设定了「最低定价线」，用来覆盖印刷费和基本人工成本。

examples.en: During the simulation, the bakery could not sell below the price floor in its group agreement.
examples.zh: 在模拟项目中，面包坊的售价不能低于小组协议规定的「最低定价线」。

words.enDefinition: A handheld device that prints and applies small price labels

examples.en: We borrowed a price gun to label the notebooks before taking them to campus.
examples.zh: 我们借了把「打价标签枪」，给笔记本贴好价格再带去学校。

examples.en: One person used the price gun while another stacked the cards by design.
examples.zh: 一个人用「打价标签枪」贴标价，另一个人按图案把卡片叠好。

words.enDefinition: an agreement to hold a price for a stated period

examples.en: The printer offered a price lock for the student paper's next three monthly issues.
examples.zh: 印刷商给学生报接下来的三期月刊提供了「锁价安排」。

examples.en: We added a price lock to the quote so the club had time to approve it.
examples.zh: 我们在报价里加了「锁价安排」，让社团留有审批时间。

words.enDefinition: a stated price for supplying specific work or goods

examples.en: I sent the society a price quote for printing fifty programmes before it booked the hall.
examples.zh: 社团预订大厅前，我发去了印制五十份节目单的「报价」。

examples.en: The team received a price quote from the printer that included delivery to the student centre.
examples.zh: 团队收到了印刷商的「报价」，其中包括送到学生活动中心的费用。

words.enDefinition: how strongly customers react to a change in price

examples.en: The team saw higher price sensitivity for ordinary printing than for same-day graduation photos.
examples.zh: 团队发现，普通打印顾客的「价格敏感度」高于当天交付的毕业照顾客。

examples.en: Our lecturer asked whether price sensitivity might change when students compared the two workshop options.
examples.zh: 讲师问，同学们比较两个工作坊方案时，「价格敏感度」会不会发生变化。

words.expression: price yourself out of the market
words.lemma: price yourself out of the market
words.enDefinition: to charge so much that buyers choose other options
acceptedEnVariants: price yourself out of the market

examples.en: The tutor asked how you could price yourself out of the market with an expensive repair service.
examples.zh: 导师问，维修服务收费太高，怎么会让你「定价过高而失去市场」。

examples.en: In the exercise, you could price yourself out of the market even if your materials were excellent.
examples.zh: 在练习情境中，即使材料很好，也可能「因定价过高而失去市场」。

collocations: risk pricing yourself out of the market
price yourself out of the local market
avoid pricing yourself out of the market

words.enDefinition: the basis used to calculate what a customer pays

examples.en: Our team used hours booked as the pricing metric for the shared workshop space.
examples.zh: 团队以预订小时数作为共享工作坊场地的「定价计量单位」。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether number of projects was a fair pricing metric for the student app.
examples.zh: 导师问，用项目数作学生应用的「定价计量单位」是否公平。

words.enDefinition: A preview used to check the appearance and content of a piece before printing it.

examples.en: I found a typo in the print proof and sent it back to the designer.
examples.zh: 我在「印刷校样」里发现一个错字，就把它发回给设计员。

examples.en: The print proof showed how the map would look at the actual size of the handout.
examples.zh: 「印刷校样」显示了地图按讲义的实际尺寸印出来会是什么样。

words.enDefinition: A file prepared in the format and quality needed for printing without further adjustments.

examples.en: The photographer sent a print-ready file for the display board after checking the printer's requirements.
examples.zh: 摄影师确认印刷店的要求后，发来了展板的「可直接印刷的文件」。

examples.en: Our student studio could not start the job until we had received a print-ready file.
examples.zh: 直到收到「可直接印刷的文件」，我们的学生工作室才能开工。

words.enDefinition: Recommendations ordered by importance, urgency, feasibility, or another agreed basis.

examples.en: Our prioritised recommendations put clearer visitor instructions ahead of redesigning the entire booking system.
examples.zh: 我们「按优先级排列的建议」把写清访客指引排在彻底重做预约系统之前。

examples.en: The director reviewed the prioritised recommendations and asked which one would help the volunteers first.
examples.zh: 负责人看了「按优先级排列的建议」，问哪一项能最快给志愿者带来帮助。

words.enDefinition: the way a team defines and describes a problem before working on solutions

examples.en: Changing the problem framing helped us see that students needed timely information, not another booking form.
examples.zh: 调整「界定问题的方式」让我们明白，学生需要的是及时的信息，另做一张预约表解决不了问题。

examples.en: The workshop on problem framing asked us to describe who was affected and under what circumstances.
examples.zh: 「界定问题的方式」工作坊让我们说清楚谁受到影响，以及在什么情况下受影响。

collocations: test different approaches to problem framing

words.zhGloss: 关于问题的待验证假设
words.enDefinition: a proposed explanation of what problem particular people face or why it matters to them
acceptedZhAnswers: 关于问题的待验证假设

examples.en: Our problem hypothesis was that commuters missed repairs because the workshop closed before their classes ended.
examples.zh: 我们「关于问题的待验证假设」是：维修间在下课前就关门，通勤学生来不及过去。

examples.en: We tested the problem hypothesis by asking students to describe their last attempts to borrow equipment.
examples.zh: 我们请学生描述上一次借设备的经历，以检验「关于问题的待验证假设」。

words.enDefinition: a slide in a pitch that shows the problem or unmet need a venture intends to address

examples.en: The problem slide showed how much time students spent finding a place to borrow tools.
examples.zh: 「问题说明页」展示了学生找地方借工具要花多少时间。

examples.en: We cut the problem slide down to one example from our interviews with society organisers.
examples.zh: 我们删减了「问题说明页」，只留了一个访谈社团组织者得到的例子。

words.enDefinition: the match between a real customer problem and a proposed solution that addresses it

examples.en: We focused on problem-solution fit by checking whether the repair service solved a recurring problem.
examples.zh: 我们重点看「问题与方案匹配」，检查维修服务能否解决一个反复出现的问题。

examples.en: Our tutor asked for stronger evidence of problem-solution fit before we built an expensive prototype.
examples.zh: 导师要求先拿出更扎实的「问题与方案匹配」证据，再做成本高的原型。

words.enDefinition: a problem important or frequent enough to justify spending time and resources on it

examples.en: Our adviser asked what evidence showed this was a problem worth solving for commuter students.
examples.zh: 顾问问，什么证据能说明对通勤学生来说这是个「值得解决的问题」。

examples.en: We found a problem worth solving after hearing the same concern in five separate interviews.
examples.zh: 五次单独访谈里都有人提到同一项顾虑，我们发现这是个「值得解决的问题」。

collocations: decide whether it's a problem worth solving

words.enDefinition: the person responsible for maintaining and updating an established procedure

examples.en: The procedure owner updated the collection instructions after the shop moved to another building.
examples.zh: 店面搬到另一栋楼后，「流程负责人」更新了取货说明。

examples.en: We asked the procedure owner whether the same checklist applied to the weekend stall.
examples.zh: 我们问「流程负责人」，周末摊位是不是也用这份检查清单。

words.enDefinition: the stage that limits how quickly work can pass through an entire process

examples.en: Packing became a process bottleneck when three stalls sent orders to one worker at once.
examples.zh: 三个摊位同时把订单交给一名员工，打包成了「流程瓶颈」。

examples.en: We looked for a process bottleneck after noticing a long wait between checkout and pickup.
examples.zh: 发现结账后到取货前要等很久，我们开始找「流程瓶颈」。

words.enDefinition: a visual representation of the steps, decisions and handoffs involved in completing a process

examples.en: The process map showed where a customer order passed from the counter to packing.
examples.zh: 「流程图」标出了顾客订单从柜台转到打包环节的位置。

examples.en: We updated the process map after moving the final inspection to the collection desk.
examples.zh: 我们把最后检查挪到自取台后，更新了「流程图」。

words.zhGloss: 流程中让人受阻的环节
words.enDefinition: A part of a process that regularly causes frustration, delay, or extra work for people.
acceptedZhAnswers: 流程中让人受阻的环节

examples.en: We identified a process pain point where people had to repeat their requests to two desks.
examples.zh: 我们找到了「流程中让人受阻的环节」，人们得把同一个请求对两个服务台说两遍。

examples.en: The charity confirmed that missing names at collection were a process pain point for volunteers.
examples.zh: 慈善机构确认，领物名单漏人是志愿者「在流程中感到受阻的环节」。

words.enDefinition: A difference in how the same activity is performed in different cases, shifts, or locations.

examples.en: We found process variation when one branch took deposits and another branch only recorded names.
examples.zh: 一个分点收押金，另一个只登记姓名，我们发现了「流程做法的差异」。

examples.en: The team looked for process variation before interpreting the totals from different days of the week.
examples.zh: 团队先检查是否存在「流程做法的差异」，再解读一周里不同日期的汇总数据。

words.enDefinition: a business unit responsible for a product or related group of products

examples.en: The case company gave each product division responsibility for its own product development and service.
examples.zh: 案例公司让每个「产品事业部」负责自己的产品开发和服务。

examples.en: Our group imagined a product division that made reusable packaging for cafés near university campuses.
examples.zh: 我们小组构想了一个给大学附近的咖啡馆制作可重复使用包装的「产品事业部」。

words.enDefinition: a situation in which a product meets the needs of a market strongly enough to attract sustained demand

examples.en: Selling a few kits at one campus event did not establish product-market fit for us.
examples.zh: 在一次校园活动上只卖出了几套，这还不能说明已经做到「产品与市场匹配」。

examples.en: The mentor asked us to investigate product-market fit with customers beyond the student society.
examples.zh: 导师请我们到学生社团以外找客户，调查「产品与市场匹配」的情况。

words.enDefinition: a guided explanation showing the main features or steps involved in using a product

examples.en: Our product walkthrough started with the same booking question students had raised in the survey.
examples.zh: 我们的「产品使用演示」从学生在问卷里提到的那个预约问题讲起。

examples.en: The judges followed the product walkthrough on their own screens during the final presentation session.
examples.zh: 最终展示环节，评审各自在屏幕上跟着看了「产品使用演示」。

words.enDefinition: A partner that helps make, assemble, or produce the materials or finished work for a project.

examples.en: Our production partner cut the display boards after we agreed on the finished dimensions.
examples.zh: 我们商定成品尺寸后，「制作合作方」裁切了展板。

examples.en: We chose a production partner that could print the large photographs without trimming their borders.
examples.zh: 我们选了一家「制作合作方」，能印大照片而且不会裁掉边缘。

words.enDefinition: A period reserved for making a certain item or batch

examples.en: We reserved a production slot for the custom bags before borrowing the sewing machine.
examples.zh: 借缝纫机之前，我们先为定制包「预留了制作时段」。

examples.en: There was one production slot left before the studio closed for the holiday.
examples.zh: 工作室放假前还剩一个「制作时段」可预留。

words.enDefinition: a unit responsible for both the revenues and costs it generates

examples.en: In our simulation, each branch operated as a profit centre and reported its own results.
examples.zh: 在模拟中，每家分店作为「利润中心」运营，并汇报各自的盈亏。

examples.en: The lecturer asked whether the café could be treated as a profit centre within the university.
examples.zh: 讲师问，咖啡馆能不能被看作学校内部的一个「利润中心」。

collocations: treat a department as a profit centre

words.enDefinition: The change shown when current results are compared with the original measurement.

examples.en: We tracked progress against baseline by comparing the new reply times with the first week's results.
examples.zh: 我们把新的回复用时与第一周的结果相比，跟踪「相对于基线的进展」。

examples.en: The chart showed progress against baseline after the theatre staff adopted a single booking list.
examples.zh: 剧院员工改用一份预约名单后，图表展示了「相对于基线的进展」。

words.enDefinition: A planned point at which the team checks its progress before continuing with more work.

examples.en: Our progress checkpoint came after the site visits and before we started testing new ideas.
examples.zh: 我们的「进度检查节点」安排在现场走访后、开始测试新想法前。

examples.en: We used a progress checkpoint to check whether the museum had provided all the booking totals.
examples.zh: 我们利用一次「进度检查节点」，确认博物馆是否提供了全部预约汇总数据。

collocations: review work at a progress checkpoint

words.enDefinition: an organisation in which most work is arranged around projects

examples.en: The case described a project-based organisation that assembled a different team for each new exhibition.
examples.zh: 案例介绍了一个「项目制组织」，每场新展览都会另组一支团队。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how staff developed their careers inside a small project-based organisation without fixed departments.
examples.zh: 导师问，在没有固定部门的小型「项目制组织」里，员工怎样发展自己的职业。

words.enDefinition: The regular pattern of meetings, updates, or reviews that keeps project work moving.

examples.en: We agreed on a project cadence with short calls during weeks when the theatre was busy.
examples.zh: 我们商定了「项目沟通与推进节奏」，剧院忙的那几周只做简短通话。

examples.en: The project cadence changed when the client asked to review findings every other Friday.
examples.zh: 客户提出每隔一周的周五看一次调查发现，「项目沟通与推进节奏」也就调整了。

words.enDefinition: A document recording a project's purpose, roles, boundaries, and how the team plans to work.

examples.en: The project charter named the student coordinator and explained when the client would review progress.
examples.zh: 「项目章程」列明了学生协调员，并说明客户会在什么时候审查进度。

examples.en: We revised the project charter after learning that only two branches could join the study.
examples.zh: 得知只有两个分点能参与这项研究后，我们修改了「项目章程」。

words.enDefinition: The final stage of a project when the team records remaining responsibilities and formally wraps up.

examples.en: During project closeout we checked that the museum had the editable files and the final report.
examples.zh: 「项目收尾」时，我们确认博物馆已经拿到了可编辑文件和最终报告。

examples.en: The client reviewed remaining actions at project closeout before introducing the permanent volunteer coordinator.
examples.zh: 在介绍今后长期负责的志愿者协调员之前，客户在「项目收尾」时查看了剩下要做的事。

words.enDefinition: A request to obtain particular data needed for a project.

examples.en: The project data request asked for daily counts of visitors without including anyone's contact details.
examples.zh: 「项目数据申请」要求提供每天的访客人数，无须提供任何人的联系方式。

examples.en: Our client lead clarified the project data request before sending it to the records team.
examples.zh: 客户方负责人把「项目数据申请」说明清楚后，发给了记录管理团队。

collocations: follow up on a project data request

words.enDefinition: A task, event, or input that another part of the project needs before it can proceed.

examples.en: Access to the booking records was a project dependency for comparing the two locations fairly.
examples.zh: 要公平比较两个地点，拿到预约记录是一个「项目依赖条件」。

examples.en: The client agreed to help with one project dependency by introducing us to the volunteer coordinator.
examples.zh: 客户同意帮忙落实一个「项目依赖条件」，把我们介绍给志愿者协调员。

words.enDefinition: An important planned point that marks completion of a stage of a project.

examples.en: We reached a project milestone when both clubs approved the final layouts for the exhibition.
examples.zh: 两个社团都认可展览的最终版式时，我们达到了一个「项目里程碑」。

examples.en: Our studio marked the first sample as a project milestone on the exhibition preparation calendar.
examples.zh: 我们工作室在展览筹备日历上把首件样品标为一个「项目里程碑」。

words.enDefinition: A clear description of what a particular project is intended to achieve.

examples.en: Our main project objective was to reduce the number of unanswered booking requests at the theatre.
examples.zh: 我们的主要「项目目标」是减少剧院未获回复的预约申请。

examples.en: The client asked whether interviewing both teams would help us achieve the project objective.
examples.zh: 客户问，采访两个团队能否帮助我们实现「项目目标」。

collocations: check work against a project objective

words.enDefinition: The process of assigning projects to teams according to factors such as skill, interests, and availability.

examples.en: The course coordinator finished project team matching before putting students in touch with their clients.
examples.zh: 课程协调员完成「项目与团队匹配」后，让学生与各自的客户取得联系。

examples.en: Project team matching took longer when several groups asked to study the same museum service.
examples.zh: 几个小组都想研究博物馆的同一项服务，「项目与团队匹配」耗时更久。

words.enDefinition: A plan setting out the tasks, timing, and assigned responsibilities for a project.

examples.en: The project work plan placed staff interviews before the review of weekend booking patterns.
examples.zh: 「项目工作计划」把员工访谈安排在分析周末预约规律之前。

examples.en: We updated the project work plan after the cooperative offered access to a second collection site.
examples.zh: 合作社同意让我们去第二个领取点之后，我们更新了「项目工作计划」。

collocations: review a project work plan with the client

words.enDefinition: a small test or demonstration showing that an idea is technically or practically feasible

examples.en: We made a proof of concept to show that the sensor could report when a shelf was empty.
examples.zh: 我们做了「概念验证」，演示传感器可以在货架空了时发出报告。

examples.en: The proof of concept worked in one room before we tried it across the building.
examples.zh: 「概念验证」先在一个房间里成功，接着我们才在整栋楼试用。

words.enDefinition: a specific fact, figure or example used to support a broader claim

examples.en: We used the second library's signup as a proof point that the service could expand.
examples.zh: 我们用第二家图书馆的加入作为「佐证」，表明服务规模还可以扩大。

examples.en: A useful proof point came from records showing repeat orders over three months of testing.
examples.zh: 一项有用的「佐证」来自记录，三个月的测试期间有人重复下单。

words.enDefinition: A person or organisation that may agree to sponsor a project but has not yet committed.

examples.en: We showed a prospective sponsor photographs of last year's exhibition before describing our new plans.
examples.zh: 介绍新计划前，我们给「潜在赞助方」看了去年展览的照片。

examples.en: The studio invited a prospective sponsor to visit while students were preparing the display boards.
examples.zh: 学生们准备展板时，工作室邀请一位「潜在赞助方」来参观。

collocations: send materials to a prospective sponsor

words.enDefinition: A thin cover used to protect an item from damage

examples.en: I slid the finished cards into a protective sleeve before labelling the order.
examples.zh: 给订单贴标签之前，我把做好的卡片装进了「防护封套」。

examples.en: The artist sold every print in a protective sleeve to protect its surface.
examples.zh: 画手给每幅出售的版画都加了「防护封套」，保护它的表面。

collocations: slip something into a protective sleeve

words.enDefinition: an early model of a product made so that a team can explore or test its design

examples.en: Our prototype showed how students could reserve a bicycle without visiting the repair stand first.
examples.zh: 我们的「原型」展示了学生怎样不用先去维修摊就能预约自行车。

examples.en: The team built a prototype with borrowed materials before ordering the parts it needed.
examples.zh: 团队先用借来的材料做了一个「原型」，后来才订购需要的零件。

words.enDefinition: a cycle of revising and retesting a prototype in response to what a team learns

examples.en: Our next prototype iteration focused on making the printed instructions easier to read at a distance.
examples.zh: 下一轮「原型迭代」着重让纸质说明离远一点也能看清。

examples.en: The prototype iteration took two days because the team already knew which steps needed changing.
examples.zh: 这一轮「原型迭代」用了两天，因为团队已知道哪些步骤需要改。

words.enDefinition: trying out an early model to see how it works and what might need to change

examples.en: During prototype testing, we saw several students try to return equipment before finding the confirmation screen.
examples.zh: 在「原型测试」中，我们看到几名学生没找到确认页面，就先尝试归还器材。

examples.en: We planned prototype testing for a quiet afternoon when the equipment desk was less busy.
examples.zh: 我们把「原型测试」安排在一个清闲的下午，那时器材服务台人比较少。

words.enDefinition: To make a room, building, or other space available for an organised event.

examples.en: The gallery agreed to provide the venue while the student club arranged speakers and volunteers.
examples.zh: 画廊同意「提供活动场地」，学生社团负责邀请讲者和组织志愿者。

examples.en: A local workshop offered to provide the venue for the first open day in spring.
examples.zh: 当地的一家工作室愿意为春季第一个开放日「提供活动场地」。

collocations: provide the venue for a workshop

words.enDefinition: To bring or supply the materials needed for your work yourself.

examples.en: The workshop notice said to provide your own materials for making signs at the studio.
examples.zh: 工作坊通知写明，在工作室做标牌需要「自行准备材料」。

examples.en: The organiser said to provide your own materials if you wanted to make a second display.
examples.zh: 组织者说，如果想做第二件展品，就要「自行准备材料」。

collocations: need to provide your own materials
agree to provide your own materials
ask whether to provide your own materials

words.enDefinition: A conclusion based on information available so far that may change with more evidence.

examples.en: Our provisional conclusion changed when the cooperatives showed us how they counted rejected donations.
examples.zh: 几家合作社说明怎样统计未接收的捐赠物品后，我们的「暂定结论」改变了。

examples.en: We described the result as a provisional conclusion because only one site had been visited.
examples.zh: 因为只走访了一个场点，我们把这个结果写成「暂定结论」。

words.enDefinition: the point when a business, product or service becomes openly available to its intended public

examples.en: We organised the public launch after the service had been tested with several student societies.
examples.zh: 服务和几个学生社团一起测试过后，我们才组织「正式公开推出」。

examples.en: The public launch included a demonstration for anyone passing through the university's central courtyard.
examples.zh: 「正式公开推出」时有一场演示，经过学校中心庭院的人都可以看。

words.enDefinition: to make the worker schedule available to the people who need to see it

examples.en: We agreed to publish the rota on Fridays so everyone could plan around weekend classes.
examples.zh: 我们商定每周五「发布轮班表」，让大家能腾出时间上周末的课。

examples.en: The manager waited to publish the rota until the fair's opening hours were confirmed.
examples.zh: 经理等展会开放时间确认后才「发布轮班表」。

collocations: publish the rota for next week
be ready to publish the rota

words.zhGloss: 把某人从一项任务上调开
words.enDefinition: to remove a person from a task, often so they can work on something more urgent
acceptedZhAnswers: 把某人从一项任务上调开

examples.en: We had to pull someone off a task to help with the checkout queue.
examples.zh: 我们得「把某人从一项任务上调开」，去帮忙处理结账队伍。

examples.en: The lead checked whether she could pull someone off a task without delaying the repair orders.
examples.zh: 负责人先确认，是否能「把某人从一项任务上调开」而不耽误维修订单。

collocations: pull someone off a task temporarily
decide to pull someone off a task
pull someone off a task to help elsewhere

words.expression: put yourself in the manager's shoes
words.lemma: put yourself in the manager's shoes
words.enDefinition: to imagine the manager's situation, responsibilities and available information when judging a decision
acceptedEnVariants: put yourself in the manager's shoes

examples.en: Try to put yourself in the manager's shoes before judging her decision to cut evening hours.
examples.zh: 评判她缩减晚间营业时间的决定前，试着「站在经理的立场考虑」。

examples.en: Our lecturer said to put yourself in the manager's shoes when comparing the two proposed budgets.
examples.zh: 讲师说，对比两份预算方案时要「站在经理的立场考虑」。

collocations: try to put yourself in the manager's shoes
ask students to put themselves in the manager's shoes
put yourself in the manager's shoes for a moment

words.enDefinition: The number of items that actually arrived in a delivery

examples.en: The quantity received was lower than expected, so we counted the envelopes again.
examples.zh: 「实际收货数量」比预期少，我们又数了一遍信封。

examples.en: I recorded the quantity received beside each fabric color in the studio notebook.
examples.zh: 我在工作室的本子上，记下了每种颜色的面料「实际收到多少」。

collocations: check the quantity received against the order

words.enDefinition: the rule an operation uses to decide which waiting person or job is served next

examples.en: We changed the queue discipline so booked repairs were handled before walk-in requests.
examples.zh: 我们调整了「排队处理规则」，让预约维修先于现场申请处理。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how the queue discipline would deal with people who had already booked.
examples.zh: 导师问，「排队处理规则」会怎么处理那些已经预约的人。

words.enDefinition: A sign showing where people should stand while waiting in line

examples.en: We moved the queue marker away from the entrance after the first rush.
examples.zh: 第一波人潮散了之后，我们把「排队位置标记」从入口旁移开了。

examples.en: A small queue marker kept the pickup line separate from people browsing the stall.
examples.zh: 一个小小的「排队位置标记」把取货队伍和正在逛摊位的人分开了。

words.enDefinition: A useful improvement that can be achieved quickly and with relatively little effort.

examples.en: A clearer confirmation message was a quick win because the staff could update it immediately.
examples.zh: 写清楚确认消息是「短期就能见效的改进」，因为员工马上就能更新。

examples.en: We identified one quick win before discussing changes that would need a longer trial period.
examples.zh: 讨论需要较长时间试行的改动前，我们找出了一项「短期就能见效的改进」。

words.enDefinition: To bring a possible problem that could affect the project to the team's or client's attention.

examples.en: I decided to raise a project risk when the museum rescheduled our only volunteer interview.
examples.zh: 博物馆改了唯一一场志愿者访谈的时间，我决定「提出一项项目风险」。

examples.en: Our team had to raise a project risk after learning the records were stored on paper.
examples.zh: 得知记录只存在纸上之后，我们团队不得不「提出一项项目风险」。

collocations: raise a project risk at a review
raise a project risk with the client

words.enDefinition: a published schedule of standard rates for different services

examples.en: The student photographer's rate card showed separate fees for studio sessions and outdoor group portraits.
examples.zh: 学生摄影师的「收费价目表」分别列出了摄影棚拍摄和户外合影的费用。

examples.en: We updated the rate card when the campus radio station began offering shorter advertising slots.
examples.zh: 校园广播站开始提供时长更短的广告时段后，我们更新了「收费价目表」。

words.enDefinition: a check that people, equipment or supplies are prepared before work begins

examples.en: We completed a readiness check before letting the first group into the equipment workshop.
examples.zh: 我们做完了「就绪确认」，才让第一组进器材工作坊。

examples.en: The shift lead held a readiness check while the afternoon crew set out new labels.
examples.zh: 下午班摆出新标签时，值班组长做了「就绪确认」。

words.enDefinition: Finished items that can be sold without further production work

examples.en: We brought some ready-made stock for shoppers who did not want to place orders.
examples.zh: 我们带了些「已做好的现货」，给不想提前下单的顾客。

examples.en: I kept ready-made stock separate from bags that still needed names sewn onto them.
examples.zh: 我把「已做好的现货」和还需要缝名字的包分开放。

collocations: offer ready-made stock alongside custom orders

words.enDefinition: a quick check that a result makes sense in relation to what is already known

examples.en: I did a reasonableness check by comparing the total with actual sales from last year.
examples.zh: 我把总数与去年实际销售数据比较，做了「合理性检查」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked for a reasonableness check before we cited the figure in our recommendation.
examples.zh: 导师要求我们在建议里引用该数字前做一次「合理性检查」。

words.enDefinition: to transfer an already assigned task to a different person or team

examples.en: We had to reassign a task when the worker responsible for labelling left early.
examples.zh: 负责贴标签的员工早退了，我们得「重新指派任务」。

examples.en: The supervisor chose to reassign a task that was holding up work at the counter.
examples.zh: 主管选择「重新指派任务」，调整那项耽搁柜台工作的任务。

collocations: reassign a task to another worker

words.enDefinition: to advise which step or series of steps a person or organisation should take

examples.en: The assignment asked us to recommend a course of action before the store's lease expired.
examples.zh: 作业要求我们在店铺租约到期之前「建议一套行动方案」。

examples.en: We had to recommend a course of action even though the demand forecast was incomplete.
examples.zh: 虽然需求预测并不完整，我们还是得「建议一套行动方案」。

collocations: recommend a course of action to management
ask someone to recommend a course of action
use the evidence to recommend a course of action

words.enDefinition: a short document that proposes a decision and explains the reasons and expected effects

examples.en: The recommendation memo asked the owner to test evening pickup before moving the whole store.
examples.zh: 「建议备忘录」请店主先试行晚间自取，再考虑全店搬迁。

examples.en: I rewrote our recommendation memo to put the suggested action before the detailed calculations.
examples.zh: 我重写了「建议备忘录」，把建议采取的行动放在详细计算之前。

words.enDefinition: The reasons and evidence that explain why a particular course of action is recommended.

examples.en: Our recommendation rationale explained why one shared form would work better than two separate lists.
examples.zh: 我们写清了「提出建议的依据」，说明一张共用表比两份单独的名单更好用。

examples.en: The client asked for the recommendation rationale before presenting the proposal to its volunteer committee.
examples.zh: 在把方案提交给志愿者委员会之前，客户请我们提供「建议的依据」。

words.enDefinition: A discussion or assessment of proposed actions before the client decides which to take forward.

examples.en: The client scheduled a recommendation review with staff who would have to change their booking routine.
examples.zh: 客户安排了「建议评审」，请需要更改预约日常流程的员工参加。

examples.en: We brought examples of both changes to the recommendation review so the museum could compare them.
examples.zh: 我们把两种改动的实例都带到「建议评审」上，让博物馆加以比较。

collocations: discuss priorities at the recommendation review

words.enDefinition: A small set of recommendations kept for further consideration from a larger set of possibilities.

examples.en: We prepared a recommendation shortlist after the client ruled out moving to a new booking system.
examples.zh: 客户排除了更换预约系统的方案后，我们整理出一份「筛选后的建议清单」。

examples.en: The recommendation shortlist included a new reminder card and a simpler cancellation process.
examples.zh: 「筛选后的建议清单」包括改用新的提醒卡，以及简化取消预约的流程。

words.zhGloss: 建议接下来采取的措施
words.enDefinition: Actions the project team advises the client to take after considering the findings.
acceptedZhAnswers: 建议接下来采取的措施

examples.en: Our recommended next steps included testing the clearer reminder language with two groups of visitors.
examples.zh: 我们「建议接下来采取的措施」包括，让两组访客试用更清楚的提醒用语。

examples.en: The client read the recommended next steps before asking which changes could start this term.
examples.zh: 客户看了「建议接下来采取的措施」后，问哪些调整本学期就可以开始。

words.enDefinition: the choice put forward as best suited to the situation after considering the alternatives

examples.en: The recommended option kept the shop near campus while moving only the collection point.
examples.zh: 「推荐方案」让店铺留在校园附近，只搬自取点。

examples.en: We tested whether the recommended option still made sense when the delivery cost increased.
examples.zh: 我们检验了当送货成本上升时，「推荐方案」是否依旧合理。

collocations: compare the recommended option with alternatives

words.enDefinition: Count the items in one storage bin again to verify the tally

examples.en: I had to recount a bin when the tally showed one too many notebooks.
examples.zh: 划记表上多了一本笔记本，我只好「把那格货重数一遍」。

examples.en: Could someone recount a bin while I compare the mug totals with the order sheet?
examples.zh: 我核对马克杯总数和订单表时，能请人「重数一格货品」吗？

collocations: ask someone to recount a bin
recount a bin after an error

words.enDefinition: the point in time to which data must be recoverable after disruption

examples.en: Our recovery point objective allowed for losing no more than two hours of booking records.
examples.zh: 我们的「恢复点目标」最多允许丢失两小时的预约记录。

examples.en: The lecturer used a day's lost order records to explain what a recovery point objective describes.
examples.zh: 讲师以丢失一天的订单记录为例，解释了「恢复点目标」表示什么。

collocations: a recovery point objective for booking data

words.enDefinition: an activity identified as especially important to restore early

examples.en: The group named equipment returns as the first recovery priority for the campus loan desk.
examples.zh: 我们把器材归还列为校园借用服务台首要的「恢复优先项」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether collecting existing orders should be a recovery priority before accepting new ones.
examples.zh: 导师问，在接新订单之前，完成现有订单的取货是否该列为「恢复优先项」。

words.enDefinition: the target length of time after a disruption within which a service or function should be restored

examples.en: The case set a recovery time objective of one afternoon for the campus bookings service.
examples.zh: 案例把校园预约服务的「恢复时间目标」定在一个下午之内。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether a longer recovery time objective would be acceptable for the newsletter.
examples.zh: 导师问，对简报业务来说，更长的「恢复时间目标」是否可以接受。

words.enDefinition: to find and invite suitable people to take part in interviews

examples.en: We used the commuter students' newsletter to recruit interview participants from outside our own course.
examples.zh: 我们通过通勤学生通讯「招募访谈参与者」，也接触到其他专业的同学。

examples.en: Our adviser explained how to recruit interview participants without only relying on friends from class.
examples.zh: 顾问解释了怎样「招募访谈参与者」，不用只靠班里的熟人。

collocations: recruit interview participants through a notice

words.enDefinition: income expected to repeat from ongoing customer agreements

examples.en: The student club's tool library earned recurring revenue through monthly fees for access to equipment.
examples.zh: 学生社团的工具借用中心靠按月收取使用费获得「经常性收入」。

examples.en: The mentors asked whether recurring revenue could cover rent when the team paused one-off sales.
examples.zh: 导师问，团队暂停零星销售时，能否用「经常性收入」支付租金。

words.enDefinition: Change an order's delivery destination after the original destination was arranged

examples.en: We had to redirect a delivery to the campus hall when the studio closed early.
examples.zh: 工作室提前关了，我们不得不把「配送地址改到」校园大厅。

examples.en: I asked if we could redirect a delivery after the buyer switched accommodation.
examples.zh: 买家换住处后，我问能不能「把货改送到另一个地址」。

words.enDefinition: cash placed in a till at the start of a shift so workers can give change

examples.en: We checked the register float before opening the stall to customers on Saturday morning.
examples.zh: 周六上午摊位开门接待顾客前，我们核了「收银找零备用金」。

examples.en: The closing report showed how much register float the next shift would receive for change.
examples.zh: 收班报告写了下一班会收到多少「收银找零备用金」。

words.enDefinition: to use excess income to support future work

examples.en: The cooperative chose to reinvest the surplus in tools that members could borrow from the workshop.
examples.zh: 合作社选择「将盈余再投入」，购置成员可以从工作坊借用的工具。

examples.en: The course case asked how the venture could reinvest the surplus while keeping repairs affordable.
examples.zh: 课程案例问，项目怎样在维持维修价格实惠的同时「将盈余再投入」。

collocations: reinvest the surplus in the community

words.enDefinition: expansion into businesses that share resources or capabilities with existing operations

examples.en: The print shop pursued related diversification by adding small design jobs for its existing customers.
examples.zh: 打印店开始为现有顾客接小型设计业务，走的是「相关多元化」路线。

examples.en: In our case, related diversification let the bicycle workshop use the same skills for equipment rentals.
examples.zh: 在我们的案例中，「相关多元化」让自行车工作坊可以把原有技能用到器材租赁上。

words.enDefinition: Make goods available again after they were set aside for someone

examples.en: We agreed to release reserved stock after getting confirmation that the buyer had cancelled.
examples.zh: 我们确认买家已取消订单后，同意「解除这批货的库存预留」。

examples.en: I didn't want to release reserved stock before the club confirmed its final quantities.
examples.zh: 社团还没确认最终要多少，我不想先「把预留的货放回可售库存」。

collocations: decide when to release reserved stock

words.enDefinition: a person assigned to take over another worker's duties for a short period

examples.en: A relief worker ran the counter while the usual cashier trained two new volunteers.
examples.zh: 原来的收银员去培训两名新志愿者时，一名「替班人员」接管了柜台。

examples.en: The relief worker checked the handover notes before serving the first customer of the evening.
examples.zh: 「替班人员」先看了交接记录，再接待晚上的第一位顾客。

words.enDefinition: money earned by letting others use an asset for payment

examples.en: The student society reported rental income from renting out its portable speakers over the summer.
examples.zh: 学生社团上报了暑期出租便携音箱获得的「租赁收入」。

examples.en: Our projected rental income fell when the library started lending the same equipment for free.
examples.zh: 图书馆开始免费出借相同设备后，我们预计的「租赁收入」下降了。

words.enDefinition: The stock quantity that signals it is time to reorder

examples.en: We reached the reorder point for blank cards sooner than expected this month.
examples.zh: 这个月空白卡片的库存比预想中更早降到了「需要补货的数量」。

examples.en: I raised the reorder point for tote bags before the start of term.
examples.zh: 开学前，我提高了手提袋的「补货触发库存量」。

words.enDefinition: sales made to customers who come back again

examples.en: The repair stall got repeat business from students who returned with a second bike.
examples.zh: 有同学带着第二辆自行车回来维修，修车摊做成了「回头生意」。

examples.en: Our café depended on repeat business from students who came by between the same two classes.
examples.zh: 我们的咖啡馆靠同学们每次在固定两节课之间光顾的「回头生意」维持。

words.enDefinition: using the same product or service on more than one occasion

examples.en: We looked for repeat use after the excitement of the initial demonstration had died down.
examples.zh: 首场演示的新鲜劲过去后，我们观察有没有人「重复使用」。

examples.en: The booking records showed repeat use by several clubs rather than visits by new users.
examples.zh: 预约记录显示，有几个社团在「重复使用」，而没有新用户到访。

words.enDefinition: a way of working that can be followed again under similar conditions

examples.en: We wanted a repeatable process that worked even when a different volunteer opened the stall.
examples.zh: 我们想要一套「可重复执行的流程」，换一个志愿者开摊也能照做。

examples.en: The trainer turned the preparation notes into a repeatable process for the whole team.
examples.zh: 培训员把准备记录整理成整个班组都能使用的「可重复执行的流程」。

words.enDefinition: Put more stock on display when the existing supply runs low

examples.en: Can you replenish the shelf with the small sketchbooks before the morning crowd arrives?
examples.zh: 上午顾客多起来之前，你能拿些小素描本「给货架补货」吗？

examples.en: We needed to replenish the shelf twice because the larger prints sold faster than expected.
examples.zh: 大幅版画卖得比想象中快，我们不得不「给货架补了两次货」。

words.enDefinition: to replace used supplies and restore the amount needed at a work station

examples.en: We stopped to replenish the station with labels after processing the last group of returns.
examples.zh: 处理完上一批退回的物品，我们停下来「给工位补齐标签」。

examples.en: The duty manager asked where to find more supplies to replenish the station before lunch.
examples.zh: 值班经理问午饭前去哪儿找更多物资，好「给工位补齐物资」。

words.enDefinition: To state what the project cannot establish because of limits in data, time, or methods.

examples.en: Our adviser asked us to report limitations because the data covered only the museum's busiest month.
examples.zh: 数据只涵盖博物馆最忙的一个月，指导老师请我们「说明分析的局限」。

examples.en: We chose to report limitations before discussing how the results might apply to other galleries.
examples.zh: 讨论结果能否用于其他画廊之前，我们先「说明分析的局限」。

collocations: report limitations in the final presentation
report limitations of a small sample

words.enDefinition: To ask someone to fix a particular mistake in work they have already produced.

examples.en: We had to request a correction when one of the artist names was spelled incorrectly.
examples.zh: 有位艺术家的名字拼错了，我们只好「请求更正」。

examples.en: The gallery agreed we could request a correction before the studio printed the remaining copies.
examples.zh: 画廊同意，在工场印刷剩下的份数之前，我们可以「请求更正」。

collocations: request a correction to the text
request a correction to a name
ask how to request a correction

words.enDefinition: To ask someone doing a job to also carry out a task beyond the original plan.

examples.en: We needed to request additional work when the gallery asked for more labels on opening day.
examples.zh: 画廊开幕当天又需要一些标签，我们得「提出额外工作请求」。

examples.en: The organiser explained how to request additional work after approving the original list of tasks.
examples.zh: 组织者解释了批准原任务清单后，如何「提出额外工作请求」。

collocations: request additional work from the supplier

words.enDefinition: To ask someone to provide data that is needed but not included in what they already shared.

examples.en: We chose to request missing data for December before drawing conclusions about the winter bookings.
examples.zh: 我们决定先「索取缺失的十二月数据」，再对冬季预约下结论。

examples.en: The student team asked which office to contact to request missing data about group visits.
examples.zh: 学生团队问，应该联系哪个办公室来「索取缺失的数据」，这些数据和团体来访有关。

collocations: request missing data from a client
request missing data for a period
decide whether to request missing data

words.enDefinition: decisions set aside for approval by a specified person or group

examples.en: Our case placed the sale of a branch on the list of reserved matters for the board.
examples.zh: 案例把出售分店列为董事会的「保留审批事项」。

examples.en: The students checked whether buying a second workshop was one of the board's reserved matters.
examples.zh: 学生查看了购置第二个工作坊是否属于董事会的「保留审批事项」。

collocations: draw up a list of reserved matters

words.enDefinition: Individual items set aside for a customer or a specific order

examples.en: I kept the reserved units in a separate box beside the packing table.
examples.zh: 我把这些「已预留的货」放在打包桌旁边的另一个箱子里。

examples.en: There were four reserved units for people who had ordered the larger mugs.
examples.zh: 已订大号马克杯的人有「四件预留的货」。

collocations: mark reserved units in the spreadsheet

words.zhGloss: 把工位恢复到就绪状态
words.enDefinition: to put equipment and materials back in place so a station is ready for its next use
acceptedZhAnswers: 把工位恢复到就绪状态

examples.en: I stayed to reset the station after the final customer collected a repaired light.
examples.zh: 最后一位顾客取走修好的灯后，我留下来「把工位恢复到就绪状态」。

examples.en: Our team had to reset the station before using the table for a different workshop.
examples.zh: 桌子用于另一场工作坊之前，我们团队得「把工位恢复到就绪状态」。

collocations: reset the station after each job

words.enDefinition: risk that remains after actions have been taken to reduce it

examples.en: The residual risk was that a visitor might still walk into the old collection room.
examples.zh: 「剩余风险」是有人仍可能走进旧自取室。

examples.en: Our report described the residual risk even after signs had been placed at both entrances.
examples.zh: 即使两个入口都放了指示牌，报告仍说明了「剩余风险」。

words.enDefinition: a view of strategy that looks to firm resources for advantage

examples.en: We used the resource-based view to explain the workshop's advantage in repairing unusual equipment quickly.
examples.zh: 我们用「资源基础观」解释这家工作坊为何擅长快速维修少见的设备。

examples.en: The resource-based view helped us discuss how the company's accumulated skills differed from those of rivals.
examples.zh: 「资源基础观」帮我们探讨公司的技能积累与竞争对手有什么不同。

collocations: the resource-based view of the firm

words.enDefinition: a choice in which using limited resources for one need leaves less for another

examples.en: The resource trade-off was between spending the weekend on training and extending the stall's hours.
examples.zh: 「资源分配取舍」在于用周末做培训，还是延长摊位的营业时间。

examples.en: We explained the resource trade-off when comparing two different ways to strengthen the collection service.
examples.zh: 比较两种改进取货服务的做法时，我们解释了其中的「资源分配取舍」。

words.enDefinition: a table that identifies what role each person or group has for a set of tasks

examples.en: The responsibility matrix showed who should approve repairs and who should contact each customer.
examples.zh: 「职责分配矩阵」标明了谁批准维修、谁联系各位顾客。

examples.en: We drew a simple responsibility matrix after two teams both tried to order new materials.
examples.zh: 两支团队都想订购新材料后，我们画了一份简单的「职责分配矩阵」。

words.enDefinition: a fee paid to secure continued access to a professional's services

examples.en: The design student received a retainer fee to stay available for the café's menu updates.
examples.zh: 设计专业的学生收取「预聘费」，以便在咖啡馆需要更新菜单时提供服务。

examples.en: The agreement set a regular retainer fee for the tutor's availability during the semester.
examples.zh: 协议规定按期支付「预聘费」，以便这位辅导老师在本学期提供服务。

words.enDefinition: To bring borrowed tools or other equipment back by the agreed time.

examples.en: We promised to return equipment on time so the next student team could start its session.
examples.zh: 我们答应「按时归还设备」，好让下一组学生开始活动。

examples.en: The reminders helped both teams return equipment on time after the afternoon workshop ended.
examples.zh: 下午工作坊结束后，提醒让两个团队记得「按时归还设备」。

collocations: agree to return equipment on time
remember to return equipment on time
help teams return equipment on time

words.enDefinition: the cost incurred in receiving and processing returned items

examples.en: Each opened art kit added a returns handling cost because someone had to check every item.
examples.zh: 每退回一套已拆封的美术工具，就会产生「退货处理成本」，因为得有人逐件检查。

examples.en: We included a returns handling cost for sorting and repacking the notebooks that came back.
examples.zh: 我们把整理和重新包装退回的笔记本所需的「退货处理成本」算了进去。

collocations: the returns handling cost per item

words.enDefinition: the extent to which income depends on a few sources

examples.en: Our mentor noticed high revenue concentration because one residence hall paid for nearly all the repairs.
examples.zh: 导师注意到我们的「收入集中度」很高，几乎所有维修收入都来自同一栋宿舍楼。

examples.en: The team measured revenue concentration before one large client decided whether to renew its contract.
examples.zh: 一位大客户还在考虑是否续约时，团队测算了「收入集中度」。

words.enDefinition: a factor that strongly affects how much money is earned

examples.en: The number of sessions booked was the main revenue driver for our student tutoring service.
examples.zh: 课时预订量是我们学生家教服务的主要「创收关键因素」。

examples.en: The lecturer asked which revenue driver mattered most for a repair stall with only one workbench.
examples.zh: 讲师问，维修摊只有一张工作台时，哪个「创收关键因素」影响最大。

words.enDefinition: income lost through missed charges or process errors

examples.en: The tool library found revenue leakage when some paid accessories never appeared on customers' bills.
examples.zh: 工具借用中心发现，一些收费配件没有上账单，造成了「收入流失」。

examples.en: Our team spotted revenue leakage after comparing the stall's actual orders with its end-of-day receipts.
examples.zh: 把实际订单和日终收款记录一对照，小组发现了「收入流失」。

words.enDefinition: the relative shares of income from different sources

examples.en: Our revenue mix shifted toward paid repairs after the student shop stopped selling spare parts.
examples.zh: 学生商店不再卖零件后，我们的「收入构成」开始侧重付费维修。

examples.en: The team used a pie chart to show the revenue mix from leases, repairs, and lessons.
examples.zh: 团队用饼图展示租赁、维修和课程三项业务的「收入构成」。

collocations: a shift in the revenue mix

words.enDefinition: how a venture plans to earn money from customers

examples.en: The design students compared two options for their revenue model: paid downloads and monthly access.
examples.zh: 设计专业的同学比较了两种「营收模式」：付费下载和按月付费使用。

examples.en: Our revenue model changed once clubs asked to pay for the whole semester in advance.
examples.zh: 有社团提出想预付一整个学期的费用后，我们调整了「营收模式」。

collocations: switch to a new revenue model

words.enDefinition: projected annual revenue if a recent pace continues

examples.en: The lecturer warned that a busy graduation month could inflate the photographer's revenue run rate.
examples.zh: 讲师提醒，毕业季某个月特别忙，可能让摄影师的「营收年化估算值」偏高。

examples.en: We calculated a revenue run rate using April's sales and labeled the number as an estimate.
examples.zh: 我们用四月份的销售额计算「营收年化估算值」，并注明这一数字是估算值。

collocations: base the revenue run rate on recent sales

words.enDefinition: the amount by which revenue falls below expectations

examples.en: We faced a revenue shortfall when half of the booked workshops were cancelled during exams.
examples.zh: 考试期间，约好的一半工作坊取消了，我们出现了「营收缺口」。

examples.en: The team tracked the revenue shortfall against its original forecast for the first six weeks.
examples.zh: 团队参照原先的预测，记录了头六周的「营收缺口」。

words.enDefinition: a distinct way a venture earns money

examples.en: A repair workshop could become a second revenue stream alongside our refurbished bicycle sales.
examples.zh: 开办维修工作坊可以成为我们的第二个「收入来源」，和翻新自行车销售并行。

examples.en: During the showcase, the judges asked which revenue stream would continue over the summer break.
examples.zh: 展示期间，评委问哪个「收入来源」在暑假仍能持续。

words.enDefinition: a choice that can be changed or undone later without disproportionate cost or harm

examples.en: Changing the collection sign was a reversible decision, so we tried the new wording first.
examples.zh: 换自取标牌是「可撤回的决定」，所以我们先试了新版文字。

examples.en: We preferred a reversible decision while we still had little evidence about evening demand.
examples.zh: 晚间需求的证据还很少，我们更愿意作「可撤回的决定」。

words.enDefinition: An agreed length of time in which someone examines work before responding or accepting it.

examples.en: The review period gave both student groups time to check the changes before approving the designs.
examples.zh: 「审查期」给了两个学生小组时间，让大家在批准设计前检查修改内容。

examples.en: We asked whether the review period ended before the studio closed for the summer break.
examples.zh: 我们问「审查期」是否在工作室放暑假前结束。

words.enDefinition: an event, result or condition that prompts a planned decision or arrangement to be reviewed

examples.en: A fall in bookings for two weeks was our review trigger for the new opening hours.
examples.zh: 预约量若连续两周下降，就满足重新评估新营业时间的「触发复核的条件」。

examples.en: The group chose a review trigger so managers would know when to look at the decision again.
examples.zh: 小组选了一个「触发复核的条件」，让经理知道什么时候要重新审视这项决定。

words.enDefinition: To examine consequences of a change that the team did not originally intend or predict.

examples.en: The museum agreed to review unintended effects after one group had trouble with the new form.
examples.zh: 有个团体用新表格时遇到了麻烦，博物馆同意「检查非预期影响」。

examples.en: We asked the charity to review unintended effects before trying the new appointment process across branches.
examples.zh: 我们请慈善机构先「检查非预期影响」，再到各分点试用新的预约流程。

collocations: take time to review unintended effects
review unintended effects after a trial

words.enDefinition: to change a working belief after receiving new information or evidence

examples.en: We had to revise an assumption about demand after speaking to students on two other campuses.
examples.zh: 和另外两个校区的学生聊过后，我们得「修正假设」，重新判断需求。

examples.en: One interview encouraged us to revise an assumption rather than restart the whole project that week.
examples.zh: 一次访谈让我们选择「修正假设」，不必当周把整个项目推倒重来。

collocations: use feedback to revise an assumption

words.enDefinition: A new version of a proof that reflects changes to an earlier preview.

examples.en: The printer sent a revised proof after we added the second speaker's name to the cover.
examples.zh: 我们把第二位讲者的名字加到封面后，印刷店发来了「修订后的校样」。

examples.en: The revised proof showed the new room number in the space beneath the small map.
examples.zh: 「修订后的校样」在小地图下方的位置显示了新房间号。

words.enDefinition: The maximum number of revisions or rounds of changes allowed for a piece of work.

examples.en: The designer suggested a revision limit so the poster would be ready before the exhibition.
examples.zh: 为了在展览前做好海报，设计员建议定一个「修改次数上限」。

examples.en: We reached the revision limit after sending separate comments on the colours and the layout.
examples.zh: 颜色和版式的意见我们分开提，之后就达到了「修改次数上限」。

words.enDefinition: The parts of a draft or recommendation that should be improved first.

examples.en: Our revision priorities included clearer diagrams and fewer technical terms in the report for volunteers.
examples.zh: 我们的「优先修改的事项」包括把图画清楚，以及减少志愿者版报告里的术语。

examples.en: The client confirmed the revision priorities after reading comments from both teams at the theatre.
examples.zh: 客户看了剧院两个团队的意见后，确认了「优先修改的事项」。

collocations: confirm revision priorities with the client

words.enDefinition: A note stating which revisions or how many rounds of changes are included in the service.

examples.en: We checked the line marked “Revisions included” before sending our draft poster to the designer.
examples.zh: 我们先看了标为「包含的修改次数」的一栏，再把海报草稿发给设计员。

examples.en: The quote showed “Revisions included” under the description of the student society's design package.
examples.zh: 学生社团的设计方案说明下，报价单列出了「包含的修改次数」。

collocations: check revisions included in the quote
list revisions included in the package

words.enDefinition: to consider a previous choice again in light of more information or changed conditions

examples.en: We agreed to revisit the decision after students had used the new counter for a month.
examples.zh: 我们同意，让学生使用新柜台一个月后，再「重新审视决定」。

examples.en: The manager had to revisit the decision when the printer failed again during the fair.
examples.zh: 打印机在展会期间再次出故障，经理不得不「重新审视决定」。

collocations: have reason to revisit the decision

words.enDefinition: A repeated return to an earlier step because work has to be corrected or done again.

examples.en: We found a rework loop when incomplete booking forms were returned to the desk each afternoon.
examples.zh: 每天下午总有没填全的预约表被退回服务台，我们发现了一个「反复返工的循环」。

examples.en: The client marked a rework loop where staff had to correct the same record repeatedly.
examples.zh: 客户标出一个「反复返工的循环」，员工得一再更正同一条记录。

collocations: find the cause of a rework loop

words.enDefinition: a group responsible for reviewing risks and how they are managed

examples.en: The fictional company's risk committee considered what would happen if its main supplier stopped trading.
examples.zh: 这家虚构公司的「风险委员会」考虑了如果主要供应商停止营业会怎么样。

examples.en: The risk committee asked management how quickly it could reopen the campus shop after a closure.
examples.zh: 「风险委员会」问管理层，校园商店停业后能多快重开。

words.enDefinition: A plan for reducing the chance or likely effect of problems that could affect a project.

examples.en: Our risk mitigation plan identified another site to visit if the repair workshop had to close.
examples.zh: 我们的「降低项目风险的计划」列出了另一个可走访的场点，以防维修工场不得不关闭。

examples.en: We reviewed the risk mitigation plan when our main contact took a week off suddenly.
examples.zh: 主要联系人突然请了一周假，我们重新查看了「降低项目风险的计划」。

words.enDefinition: an action intended to reduce the chance or severity of a potential problem

examples.en: As a risk mitigation step, we booked a spare room in case the library closed.
examples.zh: 作为一项「降低风险的措施」，我们订了间备用房间，以防图书馆关闭。

examples.en: The adviser asked which risk mitigation step would help if the evening volunteer became unavailable.
examples.zh: 顾问问，如果晚间志愿者来不了，哪一项「降低风险的措施」能帮上忙。

words.enDefinition: A record listing project risks and often how the team plans to monitor or handle them.

examples.en: The risk register listed possible delays if neither branch could provide its records before Friday.
examples.zh: 「项目风险登记表」列出了若两个分点周五前都无法提供记录，可能出现的延误。

examples.en: We checked the risk register before discussing which parts of the project might run late.
examples.zh: 讨论项目哪些部分可能延误之前，我们先看了「项目风险登记表」。

collocations: add an item to the risk register

words.enDefinition: an untested belief with the greatest potential to undermine a project if it is wrong

examples.en: Our riskiest assumption was that people would borrow the kits without help from a member of staff.
examples.zh: 我们「风险最高的假设」是，无需工作人员协助，人们也会来借套件。

examples.en: The mentor urged us to test our riskiest assumption before we bought any equipment for the service.
examples.zh: 导师建议，我们在为服务购买设备之前，先验证「风险最高的假设」。

words.enDefinition: How ready an organisation is to introduce a change to all the people or locations involved.

examples.en: The client assessed rollout readiness after testing the instructions with two new volunteer groups.
examples.zh: 客户在两个新志愿者小组中测试了指引后，评估了「推广实施的准备程度」。

examples.en: Our team checked rollout readiness by asking which branches had already trained their reception staff.
examples.zh: 我们询问哪些分点已培训前台员工，以此检查「推广实施的准备程度」。

words.enDefinition: a change to the order, timing or assignment of scheduled work shifts

examples.en: The manager sent a rota change after the student market extended its evening hours.
examples.zh: 学生集市延长晚间开放时间后，经理发出了「轮班表变更」。

examples.en: I confirmed the rota change with the coworker opening the counter the next morning.
examples.zh: 我和第二天上午负责开柜台的同事确认了「轮班表变更」。

collocations: notify staff about a rota change

words.enDefinition: a schedule in which workers or teams regularly change their assigned shifts or duties

examples.en: The rotating schedule gave each worker a chance to do the more popular morning shift.
examples.zh: 「轮换排班」给每名员工机会轮到更受欢迎的早班。

examples.en: We switched to a rotating schedule after several people had classes on alternate Fridays.
examples.zh: 几个人隔周周五要上课，我们改用了「轮换排班」。

words.enDefinition: an approximate figure calculated from incomplete information or without a detailed method

examples.en: We made a rough estimate of the storage area needed before surveying the whole building.
examples.zh: 勘察整栋楼之前，我们对需要多大储存区做了「粗略估算」。

examples.en: The rough estimate helped us decide whether the larger venue was worth examining in more detail.
examples.zh: 「粗略估算」帮我们判断，值不值得再仔细看看那个较大的场地。

words.enDefinition: One cycle of collecting comments and making a set of changes based on them.

examples.en: We combined everyone's comments for one round of revisions before checking the poster again on Friday.
examples.zh: 我们汇总所有人的意见，进行「一轮修改」，周五再核对海报。

examples.en: After the first round of revisions, the team agreed to keep the original cover image.
examples.zh: 「第一轮修改」结束后，团队同意保留原来的封面图片。

words.enDefinition: An order that needs to be completed sooner than normal

examples.en: We accepted one rush order for the club that needed badges by Thursday.
examples.zh: 那个社团周四之前就要拿到徽章，我们接了一笔他们的「加急订单」。

examples.en: I could take the rush order because all the notebooks already had covers.
examples.zh: 所有笔记本都已经有封面了，所以我能接这笔「加急订单」。

words.enDefinition: the proportions in which different products or services are sold

examples.en: Our sales mix shifted toward smaller notebooks because they could be carried easily around campus.
examples.zh: 小号笔记本在校园里好带，我们的「销量构成」因此更偏向这一规格。

examples.en: The model showed that a change in sales mix could raise profits without increasing total orders.
examples.zh: 模型显示，即使总订单量不变，「销量构成」的变化也可能提高利润。

collocations: a shift in the sales mix

words.enDefinition: the time range in which an order can be collected on the same day it is placed

examples.en: The bakery posted a same-day pickup window for orders placed before its noon cutoff.
examples.zh: 烘焙店为中午截单前下的订单发布了「当天自取时段」。

examples.en: I chose the same-day pickup window so I could collect the prints after class.
examples.zh: 我选了「当天自取时段」，这样下课就能拿版画。

words.enDefinition: Agreement that a sample meets expectations so work on the rest can continue.

examples.en: We waited for sample approval before asking the workshop to cut the remaining display panels.
examples.zh: 我们等「样品确认」后，才请工场裁切剩下的展板。

examples.en: The coordinator recorded sample approval once both partners had checked the shape and colour.
examples.zh: 两家合作方核对形状和颜色后，协调员记录了「样品确认」的结果。

words.enDefinition: Items set aside to show customers before they decide to buy

examples.en: We brought sample stock so buyers could feel each fabric before placing an order.
examples.zh: 我们带了「备好的样品」，这样买家下单前能摸摸各种面料。

examples.en: Keep the sample stock on this side so nobody includes it in today's sales count.
examples.zh: 把「样品库存」放这边，别让人把它也计入今天的销量。

collocations: bring sample stock to a market

words.enDefinition: A small piece of material shown to demonstrate its color or texture

examples.en: I showed a sample swatch of the canvas before she ordered a tote.
examples.zh: 她订手提袋之前，我给她看了「一小块帆布样品」。

examples.en: The maker attached a sample swatch to each card on the color board.
examples.zh: 制作人给色板上的每张卡片都贴了「一小块样布」。

words.enDefinition: comparing outcomes under different plausible sets of assumptions

examples.en: We used scenario analysis to compare a busy summer market with a term of unusually low turnout.
examples.zh: 我们用「情景分析」比较了客流旺盛的夏季市集与客流异常低迷的学期。

examples.en: In our scenario analysis, each case used a different combination of rent, staffing, and order volume.
examples.zh: 在我们的「情景分析」中，每个情景都采用不同的租金、人员配置和订单量组合。

words.enDefinition: an examination of several possible situations to see how their results differ

examples.en: Our scenario comparison showed that the same choice worked whether demand increased slowly or quickly.
examples.zh: 「情景对比」表明，无论需求增长快还是慢，同一选择都能行得通。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to add a scenario comparison to our slides before recommending any option.
examples.zh: 导师请我们在推荐方案前，把「情景对比」放进幻灯片。

words.enDefinition: a value or setting used to define conditions in a scenario, often set by the person building the model

examples.en: The tutor asked why we used winter demand as the main scenario input for the exercise.
examples.zh: 导师问，我们为什么把冬季需求作为这道题的主要「情景分析输入项」。

examples.en: We set lower Saturday demand as a scenario input while keeping the team's chosen price unchanged.
examples.zh: 我们把较低的周六需求量设为「情景分析输入项」，团队选的价格原样保留。

words.enDefinition: a written account of how the conditions and assumptions in a scenario fit together

examples.en: Our scenario narrative explained why orders would increase shortly before the campus festival began.
examples.zh: 我们的「情景文字描述」解释了为什么校园节庆开始前不久订单会增加。

examples.en: The tutor asked for a scenario narrative alongside the table of estimated visitor numbers.
examples.zh: 导师请我们在预估访客人数的表格旁附上「情景文字描述」。

collocations: support assumptions with a scenario narrative

words.enDefinition: a rest period whose start or approximate timing is planned on a work schedule

examples.en: I took my scheduled break after the second cashier arrived to work at the counter.
examples.zh: 第二名收银员到柜台上岗后，我按「排定的休息时段」休息。

examples.en: The scheduled break moved by fifteen minutes when the workshop finished later than we expected.
examples.zh: 工作坊比预期结束得晚，「排定的休息时段」也挪了十五分钟。

words.enDefinition: time that a worker is expected to work according to the schedule

examples.en: I checked my scheduled hours before agreeing to help with another stall during the fair.
examples.zh: 在答应展会期间去另一个摊位帮忙前，我查看了自己的「排定工时」。

examples.en: The schedule showed fewer scheduled hours once the shop reduced its opening times after exams.
examples.zh: 考试后店面缩短了开放时间，排班表上的「排定工时」也少了。

collocations: compare scheduled hours with actual hours

words.enDefinition: A change to what tasks or results are included in the work originally agreed.

examples.en: Adding a second display board counted as a scope change in our agreement with the studio.
examples.zh: 按照我们与工作室的协议，多做一块展板算作「工作范围变更」。

examples.en: The team agreed on the scope change before moving the printing date to the following week.
examples.zh: 团队先商定了「工作范围变更」，再把印刷日期挪到下一周。

words.enDefinition: The gradual addition of extra tasks or requirements beyond what a project originally included.

examples.en: The student studio noticed scope creep when the poster job began to include new window signs.
examples.zh: 做海报的工作开始包括制作新橱窗标牌时，学生工作室注意到「工作范围逐渐扩大」。

examples.en: We recorded new tasks separately to see whether scope creep was affecting the exhibition deadline.
examples.zh: 我们把新任务分开记录，好判断「工作范围逐渐扩大」是否影响了展览的最后期限。

words.enDefinition: the limits on decisions and actions a person may take

examples.en: The case report described the scope of authority for the manager of the campus bookshop.
examples.zh: 案例报告说明了校园书店经理的「权限范围」。

examples.en: We asked whether changing the opening hours fell within the assistant's scope of authority.
examples.zh: 我们问，调整营业时间是否属于助理的「权限范围」。

collocations: act within the scope of authority

words.enDefinition: The tasks, services, or results that a team or supplier is expected to provide.

examples.en: The scope of work covered designing the signs and preparing the files for printing.
examples.zh: 「工作范围」包括设计标牌和准备印刷文件。

examples.en: We checked whether transporting the stands fell within the scope of work for the workshop.
examples.zh: 我们确认了运输展架是否属于工场的「工作范围」。

words.enDefinition: to remove an option from consideration because it fails a basic requirement

examples.en: We used the budget limit to screen out an alternative that required a second lease.
examples.zh: 我们用预算限制「筛掉一个备选方案」，因为它还需要第二份租约。

examples.en: A short preliminary check helped us screen out an alternative before spending time on calculations.
examples.zh: 短暂的初步核查让我们在花时间计算前「筛掉一个备选方案」。

collocations: use criteria to screen out an alternative
decide to screen out an alternative

words.enDefinition: income that arrives mainly at particular times of year

examples.en: The graduation photographer relied on seasonal revenue because most bookings came in May and June.
examples.zh: 毕业照摄影师主要靠「季节性收入」，因为大多数预约集中在五月和六月。

examples.en: We showed seasonal revenue separately when estimating how much the campus stall would earn each month.
examples.zh: 我们估算校园摊位每月能赚多少时，把「季节性收入」单独列了出来。

words.enDefinition: a consequence that follows from an earlier consequence rather than directly from the original action

examples.en: Shorter queues freed up the entrance, and a second-order effect was easier access for nearby shops.
examples.zh: 队伍缩短后不再堵着入口，「间接后续影响」是附近店铺更容易进出了。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to identify a second-order effect before recommending that the shop lower prices.
examples.zh: 导师请我们先找出一个「间接后续影响」，再建议那家店降价。

words.enDefinition: To ask the client for information or views to help the team decide what to do.
