examples.en: We paused to seek client input before deciding which branch should test the new volunteer form.
examples.zh: 我们先停下来「征求客户意见」，再决定由哪个分点试用新的志愿者表格。

examples.en: The student team agreed to seek client input on what should be included in the workshop.
examples.zh: 学生团队商定「征求客户意见」，了解工作坊应该包括哪些内容。

collocations: seek client input on the options
take time to seek client input

words.enDefinition: a group of people who evaluate applicants and decide who is chosen

examples.en: The selection panel asked how our service would work after the semester ended in June.
examples.zh: 「遴选评审组」问，六月学期结束后，我们的服务会怎么运行。

examples.en: We presented our prototype to a selection panel that included two former student founders.
examples.zh: 我们向「遴选评审组」展示了原型，评审中有两位曾在校创业的人。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement where customers complete routine steps on their own

examples.en: Our self-service model lets students book a storage locker online and collect the key themselves.
examples.zh: 我们的「自助服务模式」允许同学们在线预订储物柜，并自行领钥匙。

examples.en: The mentor asked whether a self-service model would still work for students who needed help measuring.
examples.zh: 导师问，需要人帮忙测量的同学能不能使用「自助服务模式」。

words.enDefinition: Sell all of the goods that are still available

examples.en: We hope to sell through the remaining stock before the studio closes for the summer.
examples.zh: 我们希望工作室暑期关闭前「卖完剩余存货」。

examples.en: The club needed to sell through the remaining stock before opening orders for this year's design.
examples.zh: 社团得先「卖完剩余存货」，才能开放今年新设计的订购。

collocations: aim to sell through the remaining stock
try to sell through the remaining stock
sell through the remaining stock by June

words.enDefinition: Goods that are currently in suitable condition and available for sale

examples.en: We took cracked mugs out of sellable inventory before counting the remaining stock.
examples.zh: 数剩余存货之前，我们把有裂纹的马克杯从「可售库存」中剔除了。

examples.en: I checked sellable inventory before telling the club how many bags they could buy.
examples.zh: 告诉社团他们能买多少袋子之前，我查了「可售库存」。

words.enDefinition: To share a document or other material for people to read before a meeting.

examples.en: We agreed to send a pre-read showing the two booking processes before the review meeting.
examples.zh: 我们商定在评审会前「发送会前预读材料」，展示两种预约流程。

examples.en: Could you send a pre-read to the museum manager so she can check the terminology?
examples.zh: 你能给博物馆经理「发送会前预读材料」吗？这样她可以核对术语。

collocations: send a pre-read before the review
send a pre-read to the client
ask someone to send a pre-read

words.zhGloss: 检查调查发现是否合理
words.enDefinition: To see whether findings seem reasonable given the wider context or what people already know.
acceptedZhAnswers: 检查调查发现是否合理

examples.en: We asked staff to sense-check the findings before showing them to the cooperative's volunteer committee.
examples.zh: 把结果给合作社志愿者委员会看之前，我们请工作人员「检查调查发现是否合理」。

examples.en: The adviser offered to sense-check the findings against what the team had seen at both entrances.
examples.zh: 指导老师提出结合团队在两个入口看到的情况，「检查调查发现是否合理」。

collocations: sense-check the findings before sharing them

words.enDefinition: testing how model results change when assumptions are varied

examples.en: Our sensitivity analysis showed how the profit estimate changed as the price of paper increased.
examples.zh: 我们的「敏感性分析」显示，随着纸价上涨，利润估计值会如何变化。

examples.en: The team used sensitivity analysis to find which cost assumptions mattered most for the repair project.
examples.zh: 团队用「敏感性分析」找出哪些成本假设对维修项目影响最大。

words.enDefinition: a table showing how a calculated result changes across different input values

examples.en: The sensitivity table showed operating costs at three different levels of demand for the service.
examples.zh: 「敏感性分析表」列出了三种服务需求量下的运营成本。

examples.en: We used a sensitivity table to see which changes in rent would alter our recommendation.
examples.zh: 我们用「敏感性分析表」检查，租金发生哪些变化会影响建议。

collocations: compare values in a sensitivity table

words.zhGloss: 对假设变化的敏感程度
words.enDefinition: how much a result changes when a particular assumption changes
acceptedZhAnswers: 对假设变化的敏感程度

examples.en: We tested sensitivity to an assumption about opening hours by trying three different closing times.
examples.zh: 我们代入三种关门时间，检验结果「对营业时间假设变化的敏感程度」。

examples.en: The tutor asked which estimate had the greatest sensitivity to an assumption about delivery times.
examples.zh: 导师问，哪个估计值「对送货时间假设变化最敏感」。

words.enDefinition: Given an individual price estimate outside the original package or quote.

examples.en: Additional banners were separately quoted after the studio reviewed our new list of display areas.
examples.zh: 工作室看了新展示区名单后，为新增横幅「单独报价」。

examples.en: The email explained that mounting the prints would be separately quoted once we chose a size.
examples.zh: 邮件说明，等我们选好尺寸，会对装裱印刷品「单独报价」。

collocations: check which items are separately quoted

words.enDefinition: assigning related tasks to different people to keep work independently checked

examples.en: In the case, separation of duties meant one person bought materials and another checked the delivery.
examples.zh: 案例中的「职责分离」是让一人采购材料、另一人验收送货。

examples.en: We discussed separation of duties when designing the checkout process for the campus equipment shop.
examples.zh: 为校园设备店设计结账流程时，我们讨论了「职责分离」。

collocations: a policy on separation of duties

words.enDefinition: a situation where owners and those controlling management are different people

examples.en: Our lecturer used a family business with hired managers to illustrate the separation of ownership and control.
examples.zh: 讲师用聘请职业经理人的家族企业来说明「所有权与控制权分离」。

examples.en: The class discussed how the separation of ownership and control changed who made expansion decisions.
examples.zh: 班上讨论了「所有权与控制权分离」如何改变扩张决策的归属。

collocations: illustrate the separation of ownership and control
consequences of the separation of ownership and control
discuss the separation of ownership and control

words.enDefinition: an optional extra offered alongside the main service

examples.en: On the booking form, express pickup appeared as a service add-on for the laundry project.
examples.zh: 洗衣项目预约表上，快速取衣列在「附加服务」一栏。

examples.en: The student photographer offered a printed album as a service add-on after each portrait session.
examples.zh: 每次人像拍摄结束后，学生摄影师会提供印制相册这项「附加服务」。

words.enDefinition: income earned by performing services for customers

examples.en: We entered the money from tailoring under service revenue and listed fabric sales separately.
examples.zh: 我们把裁缝活赚的钱计入「服务收入」，另列布料销售收入。

examples.en: The repair team estimated service revenue by counting completed jobs during the first term.
examples.zh: 维修小组根据第一学期完成的订单数量估算「服务收入」。

words.enDefinition: A timetable of when parts of an agreed service will be carried out.

examples.en: The service schedule showed when the studio would bring the stands and collect them after closing.
examples.zh: 「服务安排表」写明了工作室何时送来展架，以及闭馆后何时取回。

examples.en: Our coordinator updated the service schedule after the gallery moved the opening to Saturday.
examples.zh: 画廊把开幕改到周六后，我们的协调员更新了「服务安排表」。

words.enDefinition: A period booked or offered for a service to happen

examples.en: I offered a later service slot when the student couldn't bring the jacket before lunch.
examples.zh: 那位同学午饭前送不来夹克，我就给了晚一点的「服务预约时段」。

examples.en: We left one service slot free for a club member who needed a repair.
examples.zh: 我们留了一个「服务预约时段」，给有东西需要修的社团成员。

words.enDefinition: A document setting out what service a provider will perform and what the client and provider agree to do.

examples.en: The student design team reviewed the services agreement before taking on the exhibition signage job.
examples.zh: 学生设计团队接下展览标牌的活之前，看了「服务协议」。

examples.en: Our services agreement described the setup work the studio would carry out on Friday.
examples.zh: 我们的「服务协议」说明了工作室周五要做哪些布置工作。

collocations: include something in the services agreement

words.enDefinition: to decide how much to charge for something

examples.en: The team met after class to set a price for each handmade notebook on the stall.
examples.zh: 团队课后碰头，为摊位上的每本手工笔记本「确定售价」。

examples.en: Our mentor asked how we would set a price for repairs that took very different amounts of time.
examples.zh: 导师问，维修耗时差别很大时，我们怎样「确定售价」。

collocations: set a price for a product
set a price that covers costs

words.enDefinition: to state when you are generally free to accept assigned shifts or duties

examples.en: The app asks you to set your availability before the supervisor prepares next month's schedule.
examples.zh: 主管排下个月的班之前，应用会请你「设置可上班时间」。

examples.en: You can set your availability to start after class on the days you normally work.
examples.zh: 在平常上班的日子，你可以「设置可上班时间」为放学后开始。

collocations: set your availability in the app
ask how to set your availability

words.enDefinition: Putting furniture or equipment in place before an event and taking it down when it is over.

examples.en: The service quote included setup and breakdown for the two display areas near the entrance.
examples.zh: 服务报价包括入口附近两个展示区的「布置和撤场」。

examples.en: Our team planned for setup and breakdown while the venue confirmed when the doors would open.
examples.zh: 场地方确认开放时间时，我们团队安排「布置和撤场」。

collocations: allow time for setup and breakdown

words.enDefinition: a one-off charge for getting a service ready to use

examples.en: The booking service charged a setup fee to create each club's account and import its schedule.
examples.zh: 预订服务收取一笔「开通费」，用于为各社团创建账户并导入日程。

examples.en: We waived the setup fee for the first club because its treasurer uploaded the data herself.
examples.zh: 第一个社团的财务负责人自己上传了数据，我们就免了它的「开通费」。

words.enDefinition: A note indicating that putting equipment or materials in place is part of the service.

examples.en: We chose the option with setup included because volunteers could not get in before noon.
examples.zh: 因为志愿者中午前进不去，我们选了「含现场布置」的方案。

examples.en: The quote said “Setup included” next to the line for the rented display stands.
examples.zh: 报价单在租用展架这一项旁标明「含现场布置」。

collocations: ask whether setup included is an option

words.enDefinition: time needed to prepare equipment or a working area before a task can begin

examples.en: We allowed extra setup time because our display tables had to be brought from another hall.
examples.zh: 展示桌需要从另一座厅搬来，我们多留了些「准备时间」。

examples.en: The new racks shortened setup time before each afternoon collection at the repair desk.
examples.zh: 维修台每天下午开放取货前，新货架缩短了「准备时间」。

words.enDefinition: To watch a staff member at work for a period in order to understand their routine.

examples.en: We asked to shadow a staff member while they handled repair appointments at the front desk.
examples.zh: 我们请求「跟随一名员工观察工作」，看对方怎么在前台处理维修预约。

examples.en: A student consultant went to shadow a staff member on the museum's busiest weekday.
examples.zh: 博物馆一周中最忙的工作日，一名学生咨询顾问去了现场「跟随员工观察工作」。

collocations: arrange to shadow a staff member
shadow a staff member for an hour
ask to shadow a staff member

words.enDefinition: To divide the duty of looking after an activity or task with another person or group.

examples.en: The two clubs agreed to share responsibility for arranging the display boards before the exhibition.
examples.zh: 两家社团同意「共同负责」在展览前布置展板。

examples.en: Our studio and the student centre share responsibility for checking returns after each weekend event.
examples.zh: 我们的工作室和学生中心「共同负责」核对每次周末活动后的归还物品。

collocations: agree to share responsibility for the equipment

words.enDefinition: support functions provided centrally for several parts of an organisation

examples.en: The case company used shared services to handle payroll for all three of its branches.
examples.zh: 案例公司通过「共享服务」处理三个分店的薪资。

examples.en: Our group asked whether shared services would free local managers to concentrate on their customers.
examples.zh: 我们小组想知道，「共享服务」能不能让当地经理腾出精力专注服务顾客。

words.enDefinition: A place where several people or groups keep their supplies or equipment.

examples.en: Each group labelled its boxes before putting them in the shared storage area for the fair.
examples.zh: 各组给自己的箱子贴上标签，才放进市集的「共用存放区」。

examples.en: We checked the shared storage area before ordering another set of stands for the exhibition.
examples.zh: 给展览另订一套展架前，我们先查了「共用存放区」。

collocations: label items in a shared storage area

words.enDefinition: A workspace used by different artists, makers, or groups for their own work or joint projects.

examples.en: The student design group used a shared studio to finish its signs for the market.
examples.zh: 学生设计小组在「共用工作室」里做完了市集标牌。

examples.en: We keep unfinished display panels in the shared studio while both groups prepare their exhibitions.
examples.zh: 两个小组各自准备展览时，我们把没完成的展板放在「共用工作室」。

collocations: book space in a shared studio

words.enDefinition: A table or surface used by more than one person or group to build or prepare things.

examples.en: I left the shared workbench clear so the next group could lay out its prints.
examples.zh: 我把「共用工作台」清空，让下一组可以摊开印刷品。

examples.en: We booked a shared workbench for assembling folders and checking display labels on Thursday.
examples.zh: 我们预订了「共用工作台」，周四用来装资料夹和检查展品标签。

words.enDefinition: Space on shelves available for holding or displaying goods

examples.en: We ran out of shelf space once we unpacked the new greeting cards.
examples.zh: 新到的贺卡一拆包，我们的「货架陈列空间」就不够了。

examples.en: The bowls take up more shelf space than the coasters we sold last term.
examples.zh: 碗比上学期卖的杯垫占用的「货架陈列空间」更多。

words.enDefinition: A small sign attached to a shelf to highlight nearby products

examples.en: I added a shelf talker explaining why the larger notebook had thicker paper.
examples.zh: 我加了一张「货架宣传卡」，解释大号笔记本为什么用了较厚的纸。

examples.en: The shelf talker helped shoppers notice the new design on the bottom shelf.
examples.zh: 「货架宣传卡」让顾客注意到最下层架子上的新品。

collocations: a shelf talker for a new product

words.enDefinition: a short meeting before a shift to explain assignments, priorities and important changes

examples.en: The shift briefing covered new collection times before the first group of customers arrived.
examples.zh: 第一批顾客到来之前，「班前简报」讲了新的取货时间。

examples.en: Our shift briefing moved outside because the stall was still locked when everyone arrived.
examples.zh: 大家到齐时摊位还锁着，我们便把「班前简报」挪到外面开。

words.enDefinition: arrangements to ensure that enough workers are available for a shift

examples.en: The coordinator confirmed shift coverage before inviting more customers to the afternoon sale on campus.
examples.zh: 协调员先确认「班次人员保障」，再邀请更多顾客参加校园下午的售卖活动。

examples.en: We needed shift coverage when the usual worker took time off for a class trip.
examples.zh: 平时值这个班的人请假参加班级出游，我们需要做好「班次人员保障」。

words.enDefinition: the scheduled time when a work shift is due to end

examples.en: I checked the shift end time before offering to help at the walled garden that evening.
examples.zh: 我先查看了「班次结束时间」，才提出当晚去围墙花园帮忙。

examples.en: The manager moved our shift end time after the last equipment collection was cancelled.
examples.zh: 最后一次设备领取取消后，经理调整了我们的「班次结束时间」。

words.enDefinition: a person who coordinates workers and tasks during a particular shift

examples.en: The shift lead assigned one person to the counter and another to the collection shelf.
examples.zh: 「值班组长」安排一人管柜台，另一人管自取货架。

examples.en: I asked the shift lead which jobs still needed doing before the evening handover.
examples.zh: 我问「值班组长」，晚班交接前还有什么工作要做。

words.enDefinition: a record of tasks, changes or incidents during a work shift

examples.en: The shift log showed that two orders had been moved to the evening collection shelf.
examples.zh: 「班次工作记录」显示，有两笔订单已经挪到了晚间自取货架。

examples.en: I entered the new opening time in the shift log before leaving for my seminar.
examples.zh: 我在去研讨课前，把新的开门时间填进了「班次工作记录」。

collocations: make an entry in the shift log

words.enDefinition: the scheduled time when a work shift begins

examples.en: My shift start time changed because the repair stall was opening an hour earlier.
examples.zh: 维修摊提前一小时开门，我的「班次开始时间」也改了。

examples.en: We confirmed each person's shift start time before the student market opened that weekend.
examples.zh: 那个周末的学生集市开放前，我们确认了每个人的「班次开始时间」。

words.enDefinition: a request for another worker to exchange an assigned shift with you

examples.en: The manager reviewed my shift trade request after both workers agreed to the new times.
examples.zh: 我们俩都同意新的时间后，经理审核了我的「换班请求」。

examples.en: I cancelled the shift trade request after my class was postponed until the next week.
examples.zh: 我的课推迟到下周，所以取消了「换班请求」。

collocations: respond to a shift trade request

words.enDefinition: an absence reported so close to a scheduled shift that there is little time to adjust

examples.en: We dealt with a short-notice absence by moving someone to the front desk for lunch.
examples.zh: 有人「临时缺勤」，我们调了一人午餐时段去前台顶岗。

examples.en: The rota showed who to call if a short-notice absence left the stall without cover.
examples.zh: 排班表写了如果有人「临时缺勤」、摊位没人顶班，该给谁打电话。

words.enDefinition: An instance of collecting fewer units than an order requires

examples.en: I reported a short pick when the last carton only held two mugs.
examples.zh: 最后一箱只有两个马克杯，我上报了「拣货数量不足」的情况。

examples.en: The team recorded a short pick after they couldn't find the final postcard pack.
examples.zh: 小组没找到最后一包明信片，于是登记了「拣货数量不足」。

words.enDefinition: operating with fewer workers than are needed to handle the work comfortably

examples.en: The stall was short-staffed after two workers discovered they had exams on the same afternoon.
examples.zh: 两名员工发现当天下午都有考试，摊位那一班便「人手不足」。

examples.en: We stayed open while short-staffed, but we stopped taking repair bookings for the evening.
examples.zh: 「人手不足」时我们继续营业，不过暂停接晚间维修预约。

words.enDefinition: formal confirmation that someone is ready to perform an assigned task without direct supervision

examples.en: The student received sign-off to work independently after completing two shifts with an experienced partner.
examples.zh: 和一位有经验的搭档完成两个班次后，这名学生获得「独立上岗批准」。

examples.en: I asked when workers could get sign-off to work independently at the new equipment desk.
examples.zh: 我问，新器材台的员工什么时候能获得「独立上岗批准」。

words.enDefinition: an assumption introduced to make an analysis manageable by leaving out some complexity

examples.en: For our first estimate, we made a simplifying assumption that each booking took the same time.
examples.zh: 第一次估算时，我们作了个「简化假设」，设定每笔预约处理用时相同。

examples.en: I stated the simplifying assumption beneath the chart so readers could judge its effect.
examples.zh: 我在图下写明了「简化假设」，让读者判断它的影响。

words.enDefinition: a display grouping important data, controls or results for participants in a simulation

examples.en: We checked the simulation dashboard to see whether the delayed orders had reached the collection point.
examples.zh: 我们看了「模拟演练仪表板」，确认延误的订单有没有到自取点。

examples.en: The simulation dashboard showed each team's inventory and number of orders for the current round.
examples.zh: 「模拟演练仪表板」显示当前这轮各队的库存和订单量。

words.enDefinition: a discussion after a simulation to examine decisions, results and lessons

examples.en: The simulation debrief asked us to explain why we had made the first price change.
examples.zh: 在「模拟演练复盘」中，我们需要解释为什么作出第一次价格调整。

examples.en: Our team used the simulation debrief to compare its approach with the two other groups.
examples.zh: 团队借「模拟演练复盘」把自己的办法与另外两组的做法作了对比。

collocations: take notes during a simulation debrief

words.enDefinition: an outcome produced by a simulation after running it with particular decisions or settings

examples.en: The simulation result showed lower revenue than we expected for the shop's longer opening hours.
examples.zh: 「模拟结果」显示，店铺延长营业时间后的收入低于我们预期。

examples.en: One simulation result changed when we adjusted only the number of people assigned to packing.
examples.zh: 只调整打包人手后，就有一项「模拟结果」变了。

collocations: compare a simulation result with a forecast

words.enDefinition: a stage of a simulation in which participants make decisions and receive updated results

examples.en: In the first simulation round, we changed prices but kept the same number of workers.
examples.zh: 在第一轮「模拟」中，我们调了价格，员工人数保持原样。

examples.en: The next simulation round began after all teams had reviewed their results from the previous week.
examples.zh: 各队看完前一周的成绩后，下一轮「模拟」开始了。

words.enDefinition: One designated person or team through whom all messages or requests about an arrangement are handled.

examples.en: The printer named a single point of contact for both our design questions and artwork approvals.
examples.zh: 印刷店指定了「统一对接人」，处理我们的设计问题和图稿确认。

examples.en: Our coordinator was the single point of contact so updates did not get lost between groups.
examples.zh: 为避免进展信息在小组间漏传，我们的协调员担任「统一对接人」。

collocations: designate a single point of contact
act as a single point of contact
provide a single point of contact

words.enDefinition: a component whose failure can stop the operation that relies on it

examples.en: The class identified one shared label printer as a single point of failure for the dispatch desk.
examples.zh: 同学们发现，发货台只靠一台共用标签打印机，存在「单点故障隐患」。

examples.en: Having only one person trained to update the bookings created a single point of failure.
examples.zh: 只有一人受过更新预约的培训，造成了「单点故障隐患」。

collocations: identify a single point of failure
remove a single point of failure
avoid creating a single point of failure

words.enDefinition: A guided walk through a location to see where work happens and how areas or steps connect.

examples.en: A site walkthrough helped us understand why some customers never saw the collection signs.
examples.zh: 一次「现场走查」让我们明白，有些客户为什么始终没看到取货指示。

examples.en: We completed the site walkthrough before asking about the second entrance on the floor plan.
examples.zh: 我们完成「现场走查」后，才问平面图上的第二个入口。

collocations: take notes during the site walkthrough

words.enDefinition: The range of sizes carried for one style of product

examples.en: We brought a full size run of the club shirts to the first market.
examples.zh: 我们第一次出摊带齐了社团 T 恤的「一整套尺码」。

examples.en: After lunch, only the navy sweatshirt still had a full size run available.
examples.zh: 午饭后，只有藏蓝色卫衣还「尺码齐全」。

words.enDefinition: setting different prices along a scale based on the customer's circumstances, such as income

examples.en: The student tutoring group used sliding-scale pricing so participants could choose the rate that fit their income.
examples.zh: 学生辅导小组采用「按情况分档计价」，参与者可以按自己的收入选择相应价位。

examples.en: We explained sliding-scale pricing on the booking page and listed the available rates side by side.
examples.zh: 我们在预订页面说明了「按情况分档计价」，并把相应价位并排列出。

words.enDefinition: a conversation in a small group to compare case interpretations or possible decisions

examples.en: During the small-group case discussion, we found that our two recommendations used the same evidence.
examples.zh: 「小组案例讨论」中，我们发现两份不同的建议用了同样的证据。

examples.en: The small-group case discussion ended with one question that we took to the whole class.
examples.zh: 「小组案例讨论」结束时，我们留了一个问题交给全班讨论。

collocations: prepare for a small-group case discussion

words.enDefinition: the sector of organisations such as cooperatives, mutuals and social enterprises that pursue social or member benefits through economic activity

examples.en: The lecturer introduced the social economy through examples of cooperatives and community businesses near campus.
examples.zh: 讲师用校园附近的合作社和社区企业举例，介绍「社会经济部门」。

examples.en: Our group discussed how the social economy could support rural communities with few local services.
examples.zh: 我们小组讨论了「社会经济部门」怎样支持当地服务较少的乡村社区。

words.enDefinition: a trading organisation whose main aim is social or environmental benefit

examples.en: The class studied a social enterprise that sold repaired bicycles and provided training to local volunteers.
examples.zh: 我们研究了一家「社会企业」，它出售翻新自行车，也为当地志愿者提供培训。

examples.en: Our report asked how the social enterprise would keep its workshops affordable over the summer.
examples.zh: 我们的报告探讨，这家「社会企业」怎样让暑期工作坊保持实惠。

words.enDefinition: starting and developing ventures to address social or environmental problems

examples.en: The social entrepreneurship elective explored how student teams could build businesses around local needs.
examples.zh: 「社会创业」选修课探讨学生团队如何围绕本地需求创办企业。

examples.en: Our social entrepreneurship project compared two ways to provide affordable access to shared tools.
examples.zh: 我们的「社会创业」项目比较了两种让人们以实惠价格使用共享工具的做法。

words.enDefinition: a central purpose to benefit a community or address a problem

examples.en: The repair service's social mission was to make used equipment accessible to more local students.
examples.zh: 维修服务的「社会使命」是让更多本地学生用上二手器材。

examples.en: Potential funding partners asked how the proposed expansion would support the venture's social mission.
examples.zh: 潜在资助方问，拟议的扩张会怎样支持该项目的「社会使命」。

collocations: stay true to the social mission

words.enDefinition: a limited or lightly publicised opening before a more widely announced launch

examples.en: During the soft launch, we kept the new stall open for just two afternoons.
examples.zh: 「低调试运营」期间，我们的新摊位只开了两个下午。

examples.en: The team changed its opening hours after the soft launch attracted students later than expected.
examples.zh: 「低调试运营」时，学生来的时间比预期晚，团队随后调整了开放时间。

words.enDefinition: a proposed idea about how a particular design or service could address an identified need

examples.en: Our solution hypothesis was that evening pickup would help students who missed the afternoon service.
examples.zh: 我们「关于解决方案的假设」是，晚间领取可以帮助赶不上下午服务的学生。

examples.en: We tested the solution hypothesis using a simple reservation form and one staffed pickup evening.
examples.zh: 我们用一张简单的预约表和一次有人员值守的晚间领取，检验了「关于解决方案的假设」。

words.enDefinition: a slide in a pitch that presents the proposed product or service as a solution

examples.en: Our solution slide illustrated how a booking appears to both the library and the student.
examples.zh: 「解决方案页」图示了同一条预约在图书馆和学生端分别是什么样。

examples.en: The team added a drawing to the solution slide so the process was easier to follow.
examples.zh: 团队在「解决方案页」加了一幅图，让流程更容易看懂。

words.enDefinition: something that makes the value, timing or outcome of another thing difficult to predict

examples.en: The date of the equipment delivery was our biggest source of uncertainty for the weekend market.
examples.zh: 器材送到的日期，是我们办周末集市时最大的一项「不确定性的来源」。

examples.en: We identified another source of uncertainty when the landlord declined to confirm the rent in advance.
examples.zh: 房东不肯提前确认租金时，我们找到了另一项「不确定性的来源」。

words.enDefinition: An agreement about how two or more users will use the same workspace.

examples.en: Our space-sharing arrangement gave each team its own table while keeping the shelves available to everyone.
examples.zh: 按「场地共用安排」，每组有自己的桌子，架子则所有人都能用。

examples.en: The gallery reviewed its space-sharing arrangement after a third student group asked to use the studio.
examples.zh: 第三个学生小组申请使用工作室后，画廊重新看了「场地共用安排」。

words.enDefinition: the number of people who report directly to a manager

examples.en: The lecturer calculated the span of control for a manager who supervised eight team leads.
examples.zh: 讲师计算了直接管理八名组长的经理的「管理幅度」。

examples.en: The case compared the span of control in a small shop with that in its main warehouse.
examples.zh: 案例比较了一家小店和它的主仓库的「管理幅度」。

collocations: review a manager's span of control

words.enDefinition: Extra bags or wrapping kept in case more are needed

examples.en: We brought spare packaging because the larger tote bags didn't fit the small sleeves.
examples.zh: 大号托特包装不进小封套，所以我们带了「备用包装材料」。

examples.en: I used our spare packaging when the corner of the first envelope split.
examples.zh: 第一个信封的角破了，我就用了「备用包装材料」。

words.enDefinition: A document listing detailed requirements or characteristics such as sizes, materials, or formats.

examples.en: The specification sheet listed the exact size of the boards needed for the outdoor display.
examples.zh: 「规格表」列出了户外展品所需展板的确切尺寸。

examples.en: The studio asked for a specification sheet before selecting the right cover stock for our catalogue.
examples.zh: 在给目录选合适的封面用纸之前，工作室请我们提供一份「规格表」。

words.enDefinition: Divide goods between separate places where they are stored or sold

examples.en: We decided to split stock between locations because our club was selling on two campuses.
examples.zh: 社团要在两个校区卖东西，所以我们决定「把库存分放两处」。

examples.en: Can we split stock between locations without leaving the downtown stall short of sketchbooks?
examples.zh: 我们能「把库存分放两处」，同时确保市中心的摊位有够用的素描本吗？

collocations: agree to split stock between locations
plan to split stock between locations
split stock between locations for the weekend

words.enDefinition: To pay separate shares of the costs of booking and using an event space.

examples.en: The two student groups agreed to split the venue costs before advertising the weekend market.
examples.zh: 宣传周末市集前，两个学生小组同意「分摊场地费用」。

examples.en: We asked how to split the venue costs when one partner needed an extra room.
examples.zh: 有一家合作方需要额外一间房，我们问该怎样「分摊场地费用」。

collocations: agree to split the venue costs
decide how to split the venue costs

words.enDefinition: the proportion of stock that becomes unusable or unsellable through deterioration

examples.en: The café recorded a higher spoilage rate for fresh berries than for packaged dry snacks.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆记录到新鲜浆果的「损耗率」高于包装干零食。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how a higher spoilage rate would change the cost of each box sold.
examples.zh: 导师问，较高的「损耗率」会怎样影响每卖出一盒的成本。

collocations: track changes in the spoilage rate

words.enDefinition: Features the sponsor is offered in return for support, such as recognition on event materials.

examples.en: The proposal described sponsor benefits including a logo on the cover of our exhibition programme.
examples.zh: 提案列出了「赞助方可获得的回报」，包括在展览手册封面放置赞助方标识。

examples.en: We agreed on sponsor benefits before the café committed to providing drinks for our workshop.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆承诺为工作坊提供饮品之前，我们先谈定了「赞助方可获得的回报」。

words.enDefinition: A promise made by a sponsor to provide specified support for an activity.

examples.en: The sponsor commitment covered printing the programmes for both days of the student film festival.
examples.zh: 「赞助方承诺」包括为学生电影节两天的活动印制手册。

examples.en: Our treasurer recorded the sponsor commitment after the shop told us how many signs it could print.
examples.zh: 商店告诉我们可以印多少块标牌后，财务负责人记录了「赞助方承诺」。

collocations: confirm a sponsor commitment in writing

words.enDefinition: A line of text naming the person or organisation that sponsored an event or project.

examples.en: Please add the sponsor credit line below the title before the programmes go to print.
examples.zh: 手册送印之前，请在标题下方加上「赞助方署名行」。

examples.en: I checked the sponsor credit line against the bakery's official name on its website.
examples.zh: 我核对了「赞助方署名行」，看看和面包店官网上的正式名称是否一致。

words.zhGloss: 赞助方标识的位置安排
words.enDefinition: The planned location of a sponsor's logo on a sign, printed item, or other material.
acceptedZhAnswers: 赞助方标识的位置安排

examples.en: The designer checked sponsor logo placement before sending the poster draft to the student organisers.
examples.zh: 设计师把海报草稿发给学生组织者之前，确认了「赞助方标识的位置安排」。

examples.en: The draft agreement included a diagram showing sponsor logo placement on the welcome banner.
examples.zh: 协议草案附了一张图，展示欢迎横幅上「赞助方标识的位置安排」。

words.enDefinition: Public acknowledgement of a sponsor's contribution to an event or project.

examples.en: The designer set aside the last page for sponsor recognition in our student film programme.
examples.zh: 设计师留出学生电影节手册的最后一页，用于「公开鸣谢赞助方」。

examples.en: We chose a short announcement for sponsor recognition at the start of the exhibition.
examples.zh: 我们决定在展览开场时简短广播，「公开鸣谢赞助方」。

collocations: review sponsor recognition in the programme

words.enDefinition: Signs that display the names or logos of an event's sponsors.

examples.en: The venue manager checked the sponsor signage before we opened the student market to visitors.
examples.zh: 学生市集对访客开放前，场地方检查了「展示赞助方的标牌」。

examples.en: We agreed to put sponsor signage near the welcome table where visitors could see it.
examples.zh: 我们同意把「展示赞助方的标牌」放在迎宾台附近，让访客能看见。

collocations: set aside space for sponsor signage

words.enDefinition: A table set aside at an event for a sponsor's representatives, materials, or display.

examples.en: The organiser reserved a sponsor table near reception so the bakery could display its samples.
examples.zh: 组织者在接待处附近预留了「赞助方展示桌」，方便面包店摆放样品。

examples.en: I checked the sponsor table had enough space for the leaflets and photo display.
examples.zh: 我确认了「赞助方展示桌」有足够空间摆传单和照片展品。

words.enDefinition: A message or record confirming that a sponsor has agreed to provide the proposed support.

examples.en: We received sponsorship confirmation just before the catalogue went to the student printer that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，目录送去学生运营的印刷店前，我们收到了「赞助确认」。

examples.en: The sponsorship confirmation listed the equipment the business had agreed to lend for the exhibition.
examples.zh: 「赞助确认」列出了商家同意借给展览的设备。

words.enDefinition: The person named to handle enquiries and details about an event's sponsorship.

examples.en: The poster listed a sponsorship contact for businesses interested in lending equipment to the organisers.
examples.zh: 海报列出了「赞助对接人」，方便有兴趣借出设备的商家联系组织者。

examples.en: I emailed the sponsorship contact to confirm when the books would arrive at the venue.
examples.zh: 我给「赞助对接人」发了邮件，确认书什么时候送到场地。

words.enDefinition: A message inviting a person or organisation to support a particular project as a sponsor.

examples.en: The club sent a sponsorship invitation to the company that supplied its old display stands.
examples.zh: 社团给以前提供展架的公司发了份「赞助邀请」。

examples.en: The café responded to our sponsorship invitation and asked which event needed the drinks.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆回复了我们的「赞助邀请」，问哪场活动需要饮品。

words.enDefinition: A bundle of contribution options or benefits offered to a potential sponsor.

examples.en: Our club prepared a sponsorship package for local shops interested in supporting the student market.
examples.zh: 社团为有意支持学生市集的本地商店准备了一份「赞助方案」。

examples.en: The bakery reviewed the sponsorship package and asked whether its name would appear on signs.
examples.zh: 面包店看了「赞助方案」，问标牌上会不会出现店名。

words.enDefinition: A document or presentation proposing how a sponsor could support a project and what it would receive.

examples.en: Our sponsorship proposal explained who would visit the exhibition and what the printer could contribute.
examples.zh: 我们的「赞助提案」说明了展览的观众是谁，以及印刷店可以提供哪些支持。

examples.en: The café manager asked to see the sponsorship proposal before discussing the event with us.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆经理希望先看「赞助提案」，再和我们讨论活动。

words.enDefinition: An agreement to continue sponsorship beyond the original event, period, or arrangement.

examples.en: The club discussed sponsorship renewal after the bakery helped with two successful student events.
examples.zh: 面包店支持的两场学生活动都办得很成功，社团之后讨论了「续订赞助安排」。

examples.en: The business asked about sponsorship renewal before agreeing to supply materials for the next semester.
examples.zh: 商家先问了「续订赞助安排」的事，再同意为下学期提供材料。

words.enDefinition: A level of sponsorship associated with an expected contribution and a set of benefits.

examples.en: The brochure described a sponsorship tier for small shops that could donate materials or equipment.
examples.zh: 宣传册介绍了一个面向小商店的「赞助级别」，这些商店可以捐赠材料或设备。

examples.en: Each sponsorship tier had a different offer for how partners would be named on signs.
examples.zh: 每个「赞助级别」对如何在标牌上为合作方署名有不同安排。

words.enDefinition: a check of selected examples or a check made at an unannounced time

examples.en: The supervisor did a spot check on five labels from the afternoon batch of orders.
examples.zh: 主管「抽查」了下午这批订单的五张标签。

examples.en: A spot check revealed that two items had been placed on the wrong collection shelf.
examples.zh: 一次「抽查」发现，两件物品被放到了错误的自取架上。

words.enDefinition: authority to advise or support managers in a specialised area

examples.en: The central finance team exercised staff authority by advising each branch on its annual budget.
examples.zh: 中央财务团队行使「参谋职权」，就各分店的年度预算提供建议。

examples.en: The course case gave the training office staff authority to recommend changes to branch procedures.
examples.zh: 课程案例赋予培训处「参谋职权」，可以建议分店调整操作流程。

words.enDefinition: a door or access point intended for workers rather than customers or visitors

examples.en: The staff entrance was open when I arrived to help prepare for the morning market.
examples.zh: 我来帮忙筹备早市时，「员工入口」已经开了。

examples.en: We told the volunteers to meet by the staff entrance before their first shift.
examples.zh: 我们让志愿者第一班上岗前在「员工入口」集合。

words.enDefinition: the share of available staff time spent on the work an organisation counts as productive

examples.en: We measured staff utilisation during the fair to see whether the repair bench needed another worker.
examples.zh: 展会期间我们统计了「人员工时利用率」，看看维修台是否需要再加一名员工。

examples.en: The student enterprise reviewed staff utilisation before changing the hours at its two service desks.
examples.zh: 学生企业在改动两处服务台的工作时间之前，查看了「人员工时利用率」。

words.enDefinition: an estimate of how many workers will be needed in future periods

examples.en: Our staffing forecast used last year's visitor counts for each afternoon of the student fair.
examples.zh: 我们的「人员需求预测」参考了去年学生展会每天下午的来访人数。

examples.en: The coordinator updated the staffing forecast when a large club booked the evening slot.
examples.zh: 一个大型社团订了晚间时段后，协调员更新了「人员需求预测」。

words.enDefinition: a time or role for which there are fewer workers available than needed

examples.en: The rota revealed a staffing gap just before the evening concert was due to begin.
examples.zh: 排班表显示，晚间音乐会即将开场时会出现「人员缺口」。

examples.en: We covered the staffing gap by moving one worker from packing to the counter.
examples.zh: 我们把一名员工从打包岗位调到柜台，补上了「人员缺口」。

words.enDefinition: the number of staff working or available in an organisation or during a particular period

examples.en: The manager increased the staffing level when the campus fair moved to the larger hall.
examples.zh: 校园展会移到更大的大厅后，经理调高了「人员配备水平」。

examples.en: We maintained the same staffing level even when half the stalls closed for lunch.
examples.zh: 即使一半摊位午餐时暂停营业，我们仍维持同样的「人员配备水平」。

words.enDefinition: a plan for how many workers a business needs, with what skills and at which times

examples.en: The staffing plan put an experienced worker on the stall for each busy lunch period.
examples.zh: 「人员配置计划」在每个繁忙的午餐时段都安排了一名有经验的员工值摊。

examples.en: Our team revised the staffing plan after learning when the evening classes would finish.
examples.zh: 知道晚课几点结束后，我们团队修改了「人员配置计划」。

words.enDefinition: Place prepared orders where they can be collected easily

examples.en: We stage orders for pickup near the front so the queue moves more quickly.
examples.zh: 我们「把订单备放在前面的取货处」，队伍就能走得快些。

examples.en: I stayed to stage orders for pickup before the afternoon customers arrived at the studio.
examples.zh: 我留下来「把订单备放在取货处」，好赶在下午的顾客到工作室前做完。

collocations: stage orders for pickup by time
stage orders for pickup near the door
stage orders for pickup before the fair

words.enDefinition: breaks taken by different workers at different times to maintain coverage

examples.en: The team took staggered breaks so the collection desk could remain open through lunch.
examples.zh: 团队采用「错开安排的休息时间」，让自取台在午餐时段继续开放。

examples.en: Our supervisor added staggered breaks to the schedule for the busiest day of the fair.
examples.zh: 主管给展会最忙的那天加了「错开安排的休息时间」。

words.enDefinition: start times deliberately spread out rather than scheduled for everyone at the same moment

examples.en: With staggered start times, we had enough workers when the campus gates opened at noon.
examples.zh: 用了「错峰上班时间」，校园大门中午开放时，我们的人手够用。

examples.en: We introduced staggered start times after finding that early deliveries needed only one worker.
examples.zh: 发现早间送货只要一名员工处理后，我们引入了「错峰上班时间」。

words.enDefinition: the needs, priorities or concerns of people affected by a decision or project

examples.en: We compared stakeholder interests after reading how the relocation would affect staff, students and suppliers.
examples.zh: 我们了解搬迁对员工、学生和供应商的影响后，比较了「各利益相关方的诉求」。

examples.en: The professor asked which stakeholder interests had received too little attention in the first proposal.
examples.zh: 教授问，首份方案对哪些「利益相关方的诉求」考虑得不够。

words.enDefinition: A planned conversation with someone affected by the project or able to inform its decisions.

examples.en: A stakeholder interview with a volunteer coordinator helped us understand how spare shifts were assigned.
examples.zh: 我们与志愿者协调员做了一次「利益相关方访谈」，了解了临时空班的分配方式。

examples.en: We changed the questions for our next stakeholder interview after visiting the museum entrance.
examples.zh: 走访博物馆入口后，我们改了下一场「利益相关方访谈」的问题。

words.enDefinition: Arrangements that put the project team in touch with people affected by or influential in the work.

examples.en: The client arranged stakeholder introductions before we visited the two community centres on Friday.
examples.zh: 周五我们到两个社区中心走访前，客户安排了「利益相关方引荐」。

examples.en: We asked for stakeholder introductions so we could hear from both volunteers and bookers.
examples.zh: 我们请求安排「利益相关方引荐」，以便听听志愿者和预约者两方的看法。

words.enDefinition: A diagram of the people and groups affected by a project or able to influence it.

examples.en: Our stakeholder map included volunteers who ran the desk and visitors who made group bookings.
examples.zh: 我们的「利益相关方关系图」包括在服务台值班的志愿者和办理团体预约的访客。

examples.en: The faculty adviser checked our stakeholder map and asked who else could approve a trial.
examples.zh: 指导老师看了我们的「利益相关方关系图」，并问还有谁能批准试行。

collocations: show relationships on a stakeholder map

words.enDefinition: arrangements for representing affected groups in decisions

examples.en: The cooperative strengthened stakeholder representation by adding seats for workshop users and local residents.
examples.zh: 合作社增设了工作坊用户和附近居民的席位，加强了「利益相关方代表机制」。

examples.en: The case prompted a discussion about stakeholder representation on the board of a student enterprise.
examples.zh: 案例引发了对学生企业董事会「利益相关方代表机制」的讨论。

words.enDefinition: The arrangement of items and equipment within a market stall

examples.en: We sketched the stall layout before deciding which shelves to bring to campus.
examples.zh: 决定带哪些架子来学校之前，我们画了张「摊位布局」草图。

examples.en: The new stall layout leaves enough space for people to browse the prints.
examples.zh: 新的「摊位布局」留出了足够空间，让人慢慢看版画。

words.enDefinition: a product available on its own without the rest of an offering

examples.en: After the showcase, our team offered the meal planner as a standalone product for students.
examples.zh: 展示会结束后，小组把餐食计划表作为「独立销售的产品」提供给学生。

examples.en: The notebook started as part of a course pack and later became a standalone product.
examples.zh: 笔记本原本包含在课程套装里，后来成了「独立销售的产品」。

collocations: offer something as a standalone product

words.enDefinition: a written or established procedure describing how to carry out a recurring operation consistently

examples.en: The repair shop wrote a standard operating procedure for receiving equipment from customers at the counter.
examples.zh: 维修店给在柜台接收顾客器材制定了一份「标准操作规程」。

examples.en: We followed the standard operating procedure while checking labelled orders before opening the collection shelf.
examples.zh: 打开自取货架前，我们依照「标准操作规程」核对了贴好标签的订单。

words.enDefinition: a structured, typically time-limited programme that helps startups develop and grow through intensive support

examples.en: Our startup accelerator asked each team to demonstrate progress at the end of the programme.
examples.zh: 我们的「创业加速器」要求各团队在项目结束时展示进展。

examples.en: The founders joined a startup accelerator that offered three months of workshops and mentoring.
examples.zh: 创始人加入了一个「创业加速器」，有为期三个月的工作坊和导师辅导。

words.enDefinition: a short, intensive programme that introduces people to practical aspects of starting a business

examples.en: The startup boot camp included a weekend exercise on interviewing students about everyday problems.
examples.zh: 「创业集训营」安排了一次周末练习，让大家访谈学生，了解日常遇到的问题。

examples.en: I attended a startup boot camp before deciding whether to develop the idea more seriously.
examples.zh: 我参加了一次「创业集训营」，再决定要不要更认真地做下去。

words.enDefinition: a programme or organisation that helps early-stage businesses develop through resources and advice

examples.en: A startup incubator gave us access to meeting rooms and an adviser for our pilot.
examples.zh: 一家「创业孵化器」让我们使用会议室，还给试点安排了一位顾问。

examples.en: My team joined a startup incubator before we had a product ready to sell.
examples.zh: 产品还没准备好上市，我们团队就加入了「创业孵化器」。

words.enDefinition: A document describing the work to be done, including its scope, deliverables, and expectations.

examples.en: The organiser wrote a statement of work for the group making signs for the showcase.
examples.zh: 组织者为给展演制作标牌的小组写了份「工作说明书」。

examples.en: We checked the statement of work to see whether the photographer would also edit the images.
examples.zh: 我们查阅「工作说明书」，看看摄影师是否也负责修图。

words.enDefinition: A group that reviews a project's direction and helps decide what should happen next.

examples.en: The steering group asked which branch could try the new booking form with fewer disruptions.
examples.zh: 「项目指导小组」问，在哪个分点试用新预约表影响会更小。

examples.en: We briefed the steering group after the theatre and museum teams compared their attendance figures.
examples.zh: 剧院组和博物馆组对比到场人数后，我们向「项目指导小组」作了汇报。

words.enDefinition: to become involved and offer help when a person or team needs extra support

examples.en: I offered to step in to help when the queue reached the edge of the courtyard.
examples.zh: 队伍排到庭院边缘时，我主动提出「临时出面帮忙」。

examples.en: The owner asked a worker from the next stall to step in to help briefly.
examples.zh: 店主请隔壁摊位的一名员工「临时出面帮忙」。

collocations: offer to step in to help
ask someone to step in to help
be willing to step in to help

words.enDefinition: A change to the recorded quantity of goods in inventory

examples.en: I made a stock adjustment after we found two damaged sketchbooks in the crate.
examples.zh: 我们在箱子里发现两本破损的素描本后，我做了「库存调整」。

examples.en: The stock adjustment added three bags we had missed in the first count.
examples.zh: 这次「库存调整」补进了第一次盘点漏数的三个包。

words.enDefinition: A reusable container used for carrying or storing goods to sell

examples.en: We labeled each stock bin before loading the folding cart for the market.
examples.zh: 把货装上折叠推车带去市集前，我们给每个「库存周转箱」贴了标签。

examples.en: The second stock bin stayed under the table until the postcard rack was empty.
examples.zh: 明信片架子空掉之前，第二个「库存周转箱」一直放在桌下。

words.enDefinition: A difference between recorded stock and the quantity actually present

examples.en: We noticed a stock discrepancy after counting the clips left in the storage box.
examples.zh: 数完收纳盒里剩下的夹子后，我们发现了一处「库存数量不符」。

examples.en: An unrecorded sample explained the stock discrepancy between our sheet and the shelf.
examples.zh: 一件未登记的样品，正好解释了清单和货架之间的「库存数量不符」。

words.enDefinition: A transfer or quantity change tracked in an inventory system

examples.en: We logged a stock movement for the box we took from the studio to campus.
examples.zh: 我们把从工作室运到学校的那箱货记成了一条「库存变动」。

examples.en: The spreadsheet shows each stock movement between the market stall and our storage cupboard.
examples.zh: 电子表格记着摊位和存货柜之间每一笔「库存变动」。

words.enDefinition: organising stock so items that should be used or sold sooner are taken first, such as older or sooner-expiring items

examples.en: Our stock rotation kept the older rolls of paper at the front of the cupboard.
examples.zh: 我们按「库存轮换」的办法，把较早进的纸卷放在柜子前面。

examples.en: I put dates on the boxes to make stock rotation easier for the next market.
examples.zh: 我在箱子上标日期，方便下次摆摊前进行「库存轮换」。

words.enDefinition: part of a larger company with its own strategic focus

examples.en: The textbook company treated equipment leasing as a strategic business unit with its own goals.
examples.zh: 教材案例公司把设备租赁当成一个有自身目标的「战略业务单元」。

examples.en: Our class debated whether the repair service could become a strategic business unit with distinct competitors.
examples.zh: 我们班讨论了维修服务是否可以成为一个面对不同竞争对手的「战略业务单元」。

words.enDefinition: the extent to which activities support one another and the chosen strategy

examples.en: A restricted menu and a single preparation station showed strategic fit in the student café case.
examples.zh: 菜单项目少，并且只设一个备餐工位，这体现了学生咖啡馆案例中的「战略匹配」。

examples.en: Our class looked for strategic fit between the workshop's mobile service and its portable equipment.
examples.zh: 我们观察工作坊推行上门服务和配备便携器材之间的「战略匹配」。

words.enDefinition: firms within an industry that follow similar competitive approaches

examples.en: The lecturer asked whether the full-service repair shops belonged to a different strategic group from kiosks.
examples.zh: 讲师问，全服务维修店和小修理亭是否属于不同的「战略群组」。

examples.en: Our report placed low-cost textbook sellers in the same strategic group because they offered similar services.
examples.zh: 报告把低价教材卖家放进同一个「战略群组」，因为它们的服务差不多。

words.enDefinition: a long-term result an organisation aims to achieve

examples.en: The main strategic objective was to reach more students living far from the main campus.
examples.zh: 主要「战略目标」是服务更多住在主校区较远处的学生。

examples.en: Our tutor asked us to state a strategic objective before discussing changes to the workshop.
examples.zh: 导师让我们先提出一个「战略目标」，然后再讨论工作坊该怎么调整。

words.enDefinition: choices about how to offer distinct value in a market

examples.en: The case examined strategic positioning through a service focused on repairs that could be done overnight.
examples.zh: 案例通过一项专做隔夜修完业务的服务来讨论「战略定位」。

examples.en: Our lecturer asked how the company's strategic positioning would change if it also served large retailers.
examples.zh: 讲师问，如果这家公司也服务大型零售商，它的「战略定位」会怎样改变。

collocations: strategic positioning in a niche market

words.enDefinition: a choice that delivers one benefit while giving up another

examples.en: The case illustrated a strategic trade-off between quick turnaround and a wide range of repair services.
examples.zh: 案例展示了快速交付和提供多种维修服务之间的「战略取舍」。

examples.en: We discussed the strategic trade-off involved in serving only customers within walking distance of campus.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了只服务校园步行范围内的顾客涉及怎样的「战略取舍」。

words.enDefinition: putting strategic choices into practice across an organisation

examples.en: The lecturer described how strategy execution depended on new training at all three campus outlets.
examples.zh: 讲师介绍了为什么「战略执行」有赖于三个校园门店都开展新的培训。

examples.en: Our group compared the company's announced goals with the actions it took during strategy execution.
examples.zh: 我们小组将公司的公开目标与它在「战略执行」期间采取的行动作了比较。

words.enDefinition: the process of choosing goals and how to pursue them

examples.en: Our tutor used strategy formulation to connect the repair business's goals with its available resources.
examples.zh: 导师通过「战略制定」说明如何把维修企业的目标与可用资源联系起来。

examples.en: The first stage of strategy formulation involved deciding which local markets the case company could serve.
examples.zh: 「战略制定」的第一阶段是决定案例公司能服务哪些本地市场。

words.enDefinition: without a coherent competitive basis after trying incompatible approaches

examples.en: Our lecturer said the fictional cafeteria was stuck in the middle after trying to serve everyone.
examples.zh: 讲师说，虚构的这家食堂想满足所有人，结果「夹在不同战略之间」。

examples.en: The store became stuck in the middle because it offered neither low prices nor a distinctive service.
examples.zh: 这家店价格不低，服务也没有特色，结果「夹在不同战略之间」。

collocations: avoid being stuck in the middle
a company stuck in the middle

words.enDefinition: A student who investigates a question and advises a partner organisation as part of a project.

examples.en: Each student consultant spent a morning at the food cooperative before suggesting any changes.
examples.zh: 每位「学生咨询顾问」都在食品合作社待了一个上午，才提出调整建议。

examples.en: A student consultant explained how our volunteer records had helped the team understand what delayed deliveries.
examples.zh: 一名「学生咨询顾问」解释了志愿者的记录怎样帮团队了解送货拖延的原因。

collocations: assign a student consultant to a project

words.enDefinition: a student who starts or runs a business venture while studying

examples.en: As a student entrepreneur, Maya tested her bicycle service between afternoon lectures each week.
examples.zh: 作为「学生创业者」，玛雅每周利用下午课间测试自己的自行车服务。

examples.en: The student entrepreneur talked about running a small design business while completing her degree.
examples.zh: 那位「学生创业者」讲了自己一边读学位一边经营小型设计公司的经历。

words.enDefinition: a business or social enterprise project led by students

examples.en: The university offered meeting space to a student-led venture selling repaired bicycles near campus.
examples.zh: 学校把会议场地提供给一个卖翻修自行车的「学生主导的创业项目」。

examples.en: Our student-led venture started in a design seminar and continued after the module ended.
examples.zh: 我们的「学生主导的创业项目」始于一门设计研讨课，课程结束后仍在继续。

words.enDefinition: a business owned by one or more students

examples.en: We bought our society's posters from a student-owned business near the main library.
examples.zh: 我们从主图书馆附近的一家「学生所有的企业」订了社团海报。

examples.en: The student-owned business hired two classmates to help with orders during the busy season.
examples.zh: 那家「学生所有的企业」在旺季雇了两名同学帮忙处理订单。

words.enDefinition: Permission or an arrangement allowing someone to enter and use a studio.

examples.en: We arranged studio access for both design teams while they worked on the exhibition signs.
examples.zh: 两支设计团队做展览标牌时，我们给他们安排了「工作室使用权限」。

examples.en: The coordinator checked studio access before asking our group to collect the printed programmes.
examples.zh: 协调员先确认了「工作室使用权限」，再请我们小组去领印好的手册。

words.enDefinition: The hours during which people with permission can use a studio.

examples.en: We checked studio access hours before arranging to work on the signs after our classes.
examples.zh: 安排下课后做标牌之前，我们先查了「工作室可使用时段」。

examples.en: The notice listed studio access hours separately for the exhibition teams and regular members.
examples.zh: 通知分别列出了展览团队与普通会员的「工作室可使用时段」。

words.enDefinition: An arrangement giving members access to a studio and any facilities included with membership.

examples.en: Our studio membership included weekly access to a table large enough for the display maps.
examples.zh: 我们的「工作室会员资格」包含每周使用一张大桌子的权限，那桌子够铺开展示地图。

examples.en: I asked about studio membership because our group needed somewhere to prepare posters each month.
examples.zh: 我们小组每月都需要地方做海报，所以我问了「工作室会员资格」的事。

words.enDefinition: a person with deep knowledge or practical experience in a particular subject

examples.en: We asked a subject matter expert whether the repair estimate included time for inspecting each bicycle.
examples.zh: 我们请教一位「领域专家」，维修用时的估算是否包含逐辆检查自行车的时间。

examples.en: The subject matter expert explained which costs usually changed when a shop extended its hours.
examples.zh: 「领域专家」说明了店铺延长营业时间时哪些成本通常会变。

words.enDefinition: a model where customers pay periodically for continuing access

examples.en: The student design team proposed a subscription model for its library of printable revision cards.
examples.zh: 学生设计团队提出用「订阅模式」提供可打印的复习卡片库。

examples.en: Our subscription model gave residents access to shared tools for as long as they stayed subscribed.
examples.zh: 我们的「订阅模式」让住户在订阅期间都能使用共享工具。

words.enDefinition: income earned from customers' ongoing paid access

examples.en: The music students used subscription revenue from their lesson library to pay for editing software.
examples.zh: 音乐专业的学生用课程库的「订阅收入」支付剪辑软件的费用。

examples.en: The line for subscription revenue grew when several campus clubs switched to yearly plans.
examples.zh: 几个校园社团改用年度方案后，账上的「订阅收入」增加了。

words.enDefinition: Indicators used to judge whether a project has achieved the intended result.

examples.en: We chose success measures that the repair shop could follow without collecting extra customer details.
examples.zh: 我们挑了几项「衡量项目成效的指标」，维修店不用多收客户信息就能跟踪。

examples.en: One of our success measures was how long customers waited before getting a booking confirmation.
examples.zh: 客户等预约确认需要多久，是我们的「衡量项目成效的指标」之一。

words.enDefinition: preparing people in advance to take over important roles

examples.en: Succession planning helped the student enterprise prepare a new manager before the current one graduated.
examples.zh: 「继任规划」帮助学生企业在现任经理毕业前，为下一任经理做好上岗准备。

examples.en: The lecturer asked why succession planning was important for a student cooperative that changed officers annually.
examples.zh: 讲师问，对每年更换负责人的学生合作社来说，「继任规划」为什么重要。

words.enDefinition: the mistake of continuing an activity because resources have already been spent despite weak future prospects

examples.en: The sunk cost fallacy kept the shop using the unpopular stand because it had already bought it.
examples.zh: 店铺因为展台已经买下就继续使用，即使它不受欢迎，这就是「沉没成本谬误」。

examples.en: Our tutor discussed the sunk cost fallacy after a team proposed keeping a machine nobody used.
examples.zh: 有组建议保留没人用的机器，导师接着讨论了「沉没成本谬误」。

collocations: an example of the sunk cost fallacy
fall for the sunk cost fallacy

words.enDefinition: the separate oversight body in a two-tier company governance system

examples.en: In our case, the supervisory board reviewed management's progress and challenged its plans for expansion.
examples.zh: 案例中，「监督委员会」审查了管理层的工作进展，并对扩张计划提出质疑。

examples.en: The fictional company's supervisory board discussed the proposed change with worker representatives before meeting management.
examples.zh: 这家虚构公司的「监督委员会」在会见管理层前，与员工代表讨论了拟议的变更。

words.enDefinition: Used to identify who provided particular goods or materials for an activity or job.

examples.en: The display stands were supplied by the art studio next door for the weekend.
examples.zh: 这些展架在周末「由隔壁艺术工作室供应」。

examples.en: The handout listed which materials were supplied by the campus store for the demonstration.
examples.zh: 讲义列出了演示材料里有哪些「由校园商店供应」。

collocations: refreshments supplied by a local shop

words.enDefinition: Tasks the supplier is expected to perform as part of an arrangement to provide goods or services.

examples.en: The table of supplier responsibilities included wrapping the printed panels before we picked them up.
examples.zh: 「供应方职责」表中包括在我们取件前包好印制的展板。

examples.en: We checked supplier responsibilities to see who would provide the stands for the finished signs.
examples.zh: 我们核对了「供应方职责」，看看由谁为做好的标牌提供支架。

words.enDefinition: Used on event materials to credit a person or organisation that helped fund or provide something.

examples.en: The programme described the exhibition as supported by the local print shop and two student clubs.
examples.zh: 手册写明，展览「由本地印刷店和两家学生社团提供支持」。

examples.en: A sign at reception said the film night was supported by several local businesses.
examples.zh: 接待处的标牌写着，电影之夜「由几家本地商户提供支持」。

words.enDefinition: a labelled lane in a diagram or board used to group work by team, role or category

examples.en: Each swimlane on the flowchart showed which team was responsible for that part of the process.
examples.zh: 流程图里的每条「泳道」都标明了相应流程归哪个团队负责。

examples.en: We added a swimlane for items waiting for customers to collect after their repairs.
examples.zh: 我们加了一条「泳道」，放修好后等顾客领取的物品。

collocations: move a card to another swimlane

words.enDefinition: the expenses or effort involved in moving to another provider

examples.en: The clubs faced switching costs because changing booking tools meant transferring records and training volunteers.
examples.zh: 各社团面临「转换成本」，因为改用其他预约工具意味着要迁移记录并培训志愿者。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which switching costs might matter when the workshop changed suppliers for spare parts.
examples.zh: 导师问，工作坊更换备件供应商时，哪些「转换成本」可能比较重要。

words.enDefinition: A meeting in which team members put evidence or ideas together to form a shared understanding.

examples.en: Our synthesis session combined queue observations with notes from the volunteer interviews we had completed.
examples.zh: 我们开了次「综合整理讨论会」，把排队观察情况和已完成的志愿者访谈记录合在一起分析。

examples.en: We booked a synthesis session after the last branch sent its figures for the semester.
examples.zh: 最后一个分点发来本学期的数据后，我们安排了「综合整理讨论会」。

collocations: bring evidence to a synthesis session

words.enDefinition: To combine information from several interviews to find shared themes and important differences.

examples.en: Our team met to synthesise interviews with volunteers from both locations in the booking study.
examples.zh: 团队开会「综合整理访谈信息」，受访的是预约研究涉及的两个场点的志愿者。

examples.en: We decided to synthesise interviews before comparing staff accounts with the weekly booking figures.
examples.zh: 我们决定先「综合整理访谈信息」，再把员工的说法和每周预约数据作对照。

words.enDefinition: A small stand used to raise items above table level

examples.en: I put the enamel pins on a table riser behind the postcards.
examples.zh: 我把珐琅徽章放在明信片后面的「桌面陈列增高架」上。

examples.en: The little table riser made our bowls easier to see from the aisle.
examples.zh: 小小的「桌面陈列增高架」让人从过道就能看到我们的碗。

collocations: place a product on a table riser

words.enDefinition: Fabric hanging around the sides of a display table

examples.en: We used a table skirt to keep the spare boxes out of sight.
examples.zh: 我们用「摊桌围布」把备用箱挡住了。

examples.en: I clipped the table skirt to the display table before arranging the cards.
examples.zh: 摆卡片之前，我先把「摊桌围布」夹在陈列桌上。

collocations: hide boxes behind a table skirt

words.enDefinition: A small stand that supports a sign on a flat surface

examples.en: We used a tabletop sign holder for the notice about collecting custom orders.
examples.zh: 我们用「桌面标牌架」摆放领取定制订单的告示。

examples.en: The tabletop sign holder tipped over when I moved the box next to it.
examples.zh: 我挪动旁边的箱子时，「桌面标牌架」倒了。

collocations: set out a tabletop sign holder

words.enDefinition: the proportion of the value transacted through a platform that it earns as revenue, such as through commissions or fees

examples.en: We used the take rate to estimate what the marketplace earned from each completed booking.
examples.zh: 我们用「平台抽佣率」估算交易平台从每笔完成的预约中获得多少收入。

examples.en: The student team lowered the take rate after local makers asked to keep more of each sale.
examples.zh: 本地创作者希望每笔销售能多留一点钱，学生团队因此降低了「平台抽佣率」。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement with many successive levels of management

examples.en: The case showed a tall structure in which a request passed through several management levels.
examples.zh: 案例中的「多层级组织结构」使一项请求要经过好几级管理人员。

examples.en: We used a tall structure for the simulation and compared how quickly each team made decisions.
examples.zh: 我们在模拟中采用了「多层级组织结构」，比较各小组的决策速度。

collocations: a tall structure with several management layers
move away from a tall structure

words.enDefinition: A sheet for keeping a count by making a mark per occurrence

examples.en: I used a tally sheet to count how many bookmarks we sold each hour.
examples.zh: 我用「划记统计表」记每小时卖了多少书签。

examples.en: There was a mark on the tally sheet for every mug we took out.
examples.zh: 每拿出一个马克杯，「划记统计表」上就添一道。

collocations: keep a tally sheet by the counter

words.enDefinition: A tool that holds tape and helps cut off lengths

examples.en: The tape dispenser made it faster to seal boxes at the end of term.
examples.zh: 学期末，「胶带切割器」让我们封箱更快了。

examples.en: Could you leave the tape dispenser by the labels after you close that box?
examples.zh: 你封好那只箱子后，能把「胶带切割器」放在标签旁边吗？

words.enDefinition: the percentage of revenue a venture aims to retain as profit

examples.en: Our team checked the target margin before asking the printer for another notebook sample.
examples.zh: 小组请印刷商再打一本样之前，先核对了「目标利润率」。

examples.en: The lecturer asked what selling price would meet our target margin in the campus café exercise.
examples.zh: 在校园咖啡馆练习中，讲师问怎样的售价才能达到我们的「目标利润率」。

words.enDefinition: the act of assigning work or the particular task allocated to a person

examples.en: The task assignment gave me responsibility for checking delivery times during the student market.
examples.zh: 「任务指派」让我负责在学生集市期间核对送货时间。

examples.en: We reviewed the task assignment after noticing that two people were checking the same boxes.
examples.zh: 发现两个人在检查同一批箱子后，我们重新查看了「任务指派」。

words.enDefinition: an explanation that shows a worker or trainee how to carry out a particular task

examples.en: The task demonstration showed new staff how to compare each label with the order form.
examples.zh: 「工作任务示范」给新员工展示了怎么把每张标签和订单表核对。

examples.en: I repeated the task demonstration because the workers on the later shift had missed it.
examples.zh: 晚班的人没看到，我又做了一次「工作任务示范」。

words.enDefinition: the person responsible for ensuring that a specific task is completed

examples.en: The task owner checked with both shifts before changing the collection shelf labels that afternoon.
examples.zh: 当天下午，「任务负责人」先和两班人确认，再换自取货架的标签。

examples.en: Each card listed the task owner and the time when the work was due.
examples.zh: 每张卡片列出了「任务负责人」和任务的截止时间。

words.enDefinition: regularly moving workers between tasks so they share different duties

examples.en: The supervisor introduced task rotation so everyone could practise both packing and helping at the counter.
examples.zh: 主管引入了「任务轮换」，让每个人都能练习打包和柜台服务。

examples.en: We used task rotation during the market instead of leaving one worker on labels all day.
examples.zh: 集市期间我们实行「任务轮换」，没有让一名员工整天贴标签。

words.enDefinition: the current stage of a task, such as waiting, in progress or complete

examples.en: I updated the task status once the customer had collected the last repaired item.
examples.zh: 顾客取走最后一件修好的物品后，我更新了「任务状态」。

examples.en: The afternoon shift checked each task status before deciding whether to open another station.
examples.zh: 下午班在决定要不要多开一个工位之前，检查了每个「任务状态」。

words.enDefinition: a written or recorded account of a situation created for learners to analyse and discuss

examples.en: The teaching case described a bicycle shop trying to serve two different groups of customers.
examples.zh: 这个「教学案例」讲了一家试图服务两类顾客的自行车店。

examples.en: Our tutor shortened the teaching case so everyone could read it before the afternoon seminar.
examples.zh: 导师缩短了「教学案例」，让大家在下午研讨课前都能读完。

words.enDefinition: a guide for instructors on how to teach a case, often with questions and possible analysis

examples.en: The course team used a teaching note to organise discussion around the moment of decision.
examples.zh: 课程团队依据「教学指导说明」，围绕需要决策的时刻组织讨论。

examples.en: I helped my supervisor review a teaching note for a new business school case.
examples.zh: 我协助导师审阅了一份商学院新案例的「教学指导说明」。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement that carries out much of its work through teams

examples.en: The course case described a team-based structure where each group handled repairs from booking to collection.
examples.zh: 课程案例中的「团队制结构」让每组都负责从预约到取件的整个维修流程。

examples.en: Under the team-based structure, employees from different specialisms planned each exhibition together from the beginning.
examples.zh: 在「团队制结构」下，不同专业的员工从一开始就共同筹划每场展览。

words.enDefinition: A strip on packaging designed to be pulled to open it

examples.en: We chose an envelope with a tear strip so customers could open it easily.
examples.zh: 我们选了带「易撕封条」的信封，顾客拆起来方便。

examples.en: The tear strip on the sample box came off too easily during transport.
examples.zh: 样品盒的「易撕封条」在运输途中太容易脱落。

collocations: a box with a tear strip

words.enDefinition: a business co-founder who leads or contributes substantially to technical development

examples.en: The technical co-founder built the first working version while her partner organised the interviews.
examples.zh: 「技术联合创始人」做出了首个能运行的版本，她的搭档则组织访谈。

examples.en: We met a technical co-founder who had designed an app for campus bicycle repairs.
examples.zh: 我们见到一位「技术联合创始人」，他设计过一个校园自行车维修应用。

words.enDefinition: a short-term arrangement in which someone takes over work while the usual worker is unavailable

examples.en: The shop arranged temporary cover while the regular supervisor attended a conference off campus.
examples.zh: 常驻主管去校外开会时，店里做了「临时替岗安排」。

examples.en: We found temporary cover for the equipment desk during the busy part of the afternoon.
examples.zh: 下午最忙的那个时段，我们给器材服务台做了「临时替岗安排」。

collocations: find temporary cover for a shift

words.enDefinition: the endpoint of a path through a decision tree, showing the resulting outcome or payoff

examples.en: We wrote the final profit beside each terminal node at the end of the tree.
examples.zh: 我们在决策树末端的每个「终端节点」旁写了最终利润。

examples.en: Each branch led to a different terminal node because the repair costs were different.
examples.zh: 各条分支通向不同的「终端节点」，因为维修成本不同。

collocations: calculate the value at a terminal node

words.enDefinition: a written statement defining a group's purpose, scope, and responsibilities

examples.en: We drafted terms of reference for the committee before giving it responsibility for the pilot.
examples.zh: 我们先为委员会拟定「职责范围说明」，再让它负责试点。

examples.en: The terms of reference stated which decisions the working group could make without going back to the board.
examples.zh: 「职责范围说明」明确了哪些决定工作小组可以自行作出，无需再次提请董事会。

words.enDefinition: a person who takes part in a test, such as a trial of a design

examples.en: Each test participant was asked to borrow a sample kit using only the printed instructions.
examples.zh: 我们请每位「测试参与者」只看纸质说明，借一份样品套件。

examples.en: One test participant found the return button without seeing the sign at the entrance.
examples.zh: 一位「测试参与者」没看到入口的指示牌，也找到了归还按钮。

words.enDefinition: to check whether the action recommended would still make sense or work under relevant conditions

examples.en: We decided to test the recommendation against records from a busier week before submitting it.
examples.zh: 我们决定在提交前依据一周较忙时的记录「检验建议方案」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to test the recommendation assuming the owner could hire only one person.
examples.zh: 导师请我们在店主只能雇一人的条件下「检验建议方案」。

collocations: test the recommendation under different conditions
find a way to test the recommendation

words.zhGloss: 请利益相关方参与测试
words.enDefinition: To try an idea, process, or design with people who will be affected and listen to their responses.
acceptedZhAnswers: 请利益相关方参与测试

examples.en: We needed something simple to test with stakeholders before changing the cooperative's entire collection process.
examples.zh: 更改合作社的整个领取流程之前，我们需要一个简单方案来「请利益相关方参与测试」。

examples.en: Our team drafted a reminder card to test with stakeholders who ran evening theatre sessions.
examples.zh: 团队草拟了提醒卡，打算「请负责晚间剧院活动的相关人员参与测试」。

collocations: choose what to test with stakeholders
prepare a draft to test with stakeholders
decide when to test with stakeholders

words.enDefinition: a belief stated clearly enough that data or observation could support or challenge it

examples.en: We turned our broad claim into a testable assumption about Saturday afternoon orders from students.
examples.zh: 我们把宽泛的说法具体化，变成一个关于学生周六下午订单的「可验证的假设」。

examples.en: The project worksheet asked each team to put one testable assumption at the top of the page.
examples.zh: 项目练习表要求每支团队在页首写一个「可验证的假设」。

words.enDefinition: someone who pays for an offering used by another person

examples.en: The department acted as a third-party payer for equipment that its students borrowed by the hour.
examples.zh: 学生按小时借用设备，系里作为「第三方付款方」。

examples.en: Our pitch identified the alumni fund as a third-party payer for the student's first workshop pass.
examples.zh: 我们的推介说明，校友基金是学生第一张工作坊通行证的「第三方付款方」。

words.enDefinition: the pressure created by firms that might enter an industry

examples.en: The threat of new entrants increased once cheaper equipment made local badge printing easier.
examples.zh: 设备变便宜，本地印制徽章更容易，「新进入者威胁」也随之增大。

examples.en: The class considered the threat of new entrants even though the repair shop had few rivals.
examples.zh: 尽管维修店的竞争对手不多，班上仍考虑了「新进入者威胁」。

collocations: assess the threat of new entrants
a low threat of new entrants
reduce the threat of new entrants

words.enDefinition: the pressure from alternatives that meet the same need differently

examples.en: The threat of substitutes rose when campus clubs switched from printed notices to electronic screens.
examples.zh: 校园社团把纸质通知改成电子屏之后，「替代品威胁」加大了。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to consider the threat of substitutes for the paid bicycle storage service.
examples.zh: 导师让我们考虑付费自行车寄存服务可能面临的「替代品威胁」。

collocations: respond to the threat of substitutes

words.enDefinition: the amount of work or number of units a process completes during a given time

examples.en: The stall's throughput increased after two workers began packing orders at separate tables.
examples.zh: 两名员工分桌打包后，摊位的「单位时间处理量」提高了。

examples.en: We measured throughput in repaired items per hour during the first afternoon of the fair.
examples.zh: 展会第一个下午，我们按每小时修好的物品数衡量「单位时间处理量」。

words.enDefinition: An arrangement of products on several levels to improve visibility

examples.en: A tiered display made the small ceramic cups visible behind the taller mugs.
examples.zh: 用「阶梯式陈列」摆放，高马克杯后面的小陶瓷杯也能看见。

examples.en: We built a tiered display from three sturdy boxes and a piece of fabric.
examples.zh: 我们用三个结实的箱子和一块布做了个「阶梯式陈列」。

collocations: use a tiered display for small items

words.enDefinition: setting different prices for different levels of access or quantity

examples.en: Our club booking app used tiered pricing based on the number of events a society ran.
examples.zh: 我们的社团预订应用根据社团举办的活动数量采用「分档定价」。

examples.en: The studio introduced tiered pricing so regular users could choose a plan with more workshop hours.
examples.zh: 工作室推出「分档定价」，让常来的用户可以选工作坊时长更多的方案。

words.enDefinition: a device or application used to record when employees begin and end work

examples.en: I used the time clock near the counter before putting on my work apron.
examples.zh: 我用柜台旁的「工时打卡系统」打完卡，才穿上工作围裙。

examples.en: The time clock showed a confirmation after I logged the end of my shift.
examples.zh: 我记录下班时间后，「工时打卡系统」显示了确认信息。

collocations: clock in at the time clock

words.enDefinition: work that must be completed promptly because a delay would cause significant problems

examples.en: Printing the last labels was a time-critical task before the boxes could leave on Friday.
examples.zh: 周五箱子发走前，印好最后一批标签是个「时限紧迫的任务」。

examples.en: The supervisor moved a second worker onto the time-critical task just before the afternoon break.
examples.zh: 下午休息前，主管又加了一人去做「时限紧迫的任务」。

words.enDefinition: how long it takes for cumulative revenue to cover cumulative costs

examples.en: We estimated the time to break even for a campus photo booth with an upfront equipment cost.
examples.zh: 我们为需要预付设备成本的校园自拍亭估算了「盈亏平衡所需时间」。

examples.en: Our time to break even increased when the team delayed the first set of public workshops.
examples.zh: 团队推迟首批公开工作坊后，我们达到「盈亏平衡所需的时间」变长了。

collocations: shorten the time to break even

words.enDefinition: confirmation that an employee's recorded hours have been reviewed and accepted

examples.en: The manager finished timesheet approval for the weekend team before the office closed on Monday.
examples.zh: 周一办公室关闭以前，经理完成了周末班组的「工时表审批」。

examples.en: I checked who was responsible for timesheet approval while our usual supervisor was away.
examples.zh: 平时的主管不在，我问了现在谁负责「工时表审批」。

words.enDefinition: the latest time at which workers are expected to send their timesheets for processing

examples.en: The coordinator moved the timesheet deadline ahead of the university's public holiday this month.
examples.zh: 协调员把「工时表提交截止时间」提前到学校本月的公休日前。

examples.en: I set a reminder for the timesheet deadline after missing the previous Friday's submission.
examples.zh: 上周五没交上之后，我给「工时表提交截止时间」设了提醒。

collocations: send a reminder about the timesheet deadline

words.enDefinition: A service or collection that lends tools for people to use and return.

examples.en: The campus tool library lent our workshop clamps for assembling the display boards on Friday.
examples.zh: 周五我们要组装展板，校园「工具借用处」借了些夹具给我们工场。

examples.en: We used the tool library before deciding which equipment our group actually needed to buy.
examples.zh: 我们先用「工具借用处」的服务，再决定小组到底需要购置哪些设备。

words.enDefinition: a slide showing measurable signs that a venture is gaining users, sales or other engagement

examples.en: The traction slide showed how many clubs had booked equipment more than once that semester.
examples.zh: 「进展和市场验证页」显示，当学期有多少社团预约器材超过一次。

examples.en: We updated the traction slide after the second library began accepting bookings from our tool.
examples.zh: 第二家图书馆开始通过我们的工具接收预约后，我们更新了「进展和市场验证页」。

collocations: add evidence to the traction slide

words.zhGloss: 培养内部培训人员的活动
words.enDefinition: A session that prepares participants to teach a new process or skill to other people.
acceptedZhAnswers: 培养内部培训人员的活动

examples.en: The team ran a train-the-trainer session so supervisors could teach the new process to volunteers.
examples.zh: 团队举办了一次「培养内部培训人员的活动」，让主管能教志愿者使用新流程。

examples.en: At the train-the-trainer session, staff practised explaining what to do when a booking changed.
examples.zh: 在「培养内部培训人员的活动」中，员工练习讲解预约变更时该怎么做。

words.enDefinition: a colleague paired with a new worker to help them learn tasks and settle in

examples.en: My training buddy showed me where to record orders that needed to be collected later.
examples.zh: 「培训搭档」给我指了该在哪里记录稍后来取的订单。

examples.en: We assigned every new volunteer a training buddy for the first two shifts that month.
examples.zh: 我们给当月每位新志愿者在头两个班次安排了「培训搭档」。

words.enDefinition: a list of topics or tasks that should be covered or verified during training

examples.en: I used the training checklist to make sure we had practised each step twice together.
examples.zh: 我用「培训检查清单」确认我们每个步骤都一起练过两次。

examples.en: The coordinator added a new returns task to the training checklist for student volunteers.
examples.zh: 协调员在学生志愿者的「培训检查清单」上加了一项新的归还任务。

words.enDefinition: to pass responsibility for an unfinished task to someone else who will continue it

examples.en: I needed to transfer an open task before leaving for my afternoon class downtown.
examples.zh: 去市区上下午的课前，我得「交接未完成的任务」。

examples.en: The coordinator asked how to transfer an open task without losing the notes attached to it.
examples.zh: 协调员问，怎样「交接未完成的任务」，同时保留附在任务里的记录。

collocations: transfer an open task to the next shift
choose to transfer an open task
transfer an open task to another worker

words.enDefinition: an initial attempt made to see whether a process or arrangement works in practice

examples.en: Our trial run showed that one volunteer was not enough to check all the reservations.
examples.zh: 「试运行」表明，一名志愿者来不及核对所有预约。

examples.en: We carried out a trial run with borrowed display stands before paying for our own.
examples.zh: 自己花钱买之前，我们先借来展示架做了「试运行」。

words.enDefinition: an approach considering social, environmental, and financial performance together

examples.en: The class used the triple bottom line to compare two plans for refurbishing campus furniture.
examples.zh: 同学们用「三重底线」比较了两项校园家具翻新方案。

examples.en: The team presented its triple bottom line results using figures on waste, access, and costs.
examples.zh: 团队用废弃物数量、服务可及性和成本的数据汇报了「三重底线」成果。

words.enDefinition: to earn more than the total cost of doing business

examples.en: The student repair stall began to turn a profit after it moved into a shared workspace.
examples.zh: 学生维修摊搬进共享工作空间后，开始「实现盈利」。

examples.en: Our theatre group hoped to turn a profit after paying for the venue and printed programmes.
examples.zh: 剧团希望付完场地费和节目单印刷费后仍能「实现盈利」。

words.enDefinition: a plan to restore a poorly performing business to viability

examples.en: The case company's turnaround strategy began with reducing losses at the two least busy branches.
examples.zh: 案例公司的「扭转经营困境的战略」从减少两家最清闲分店的亏损做起。

examples.en: Our group proposed a turnaround strategy for a fictional repair chain with declining sales and rising costs.
examples.zh: 我们为一家销量下滑、成本上升的虚构连锁维修企业提出了「扭转经营困境的战略」。

words.enDefinition: verification in which two people check something, often to catch a mistake one person might miss

examples.en: We did a two-person check on the order total before giving the boxes to the customer.
examples.zh: 把箱子交给顾客之前，我们对订单总计做了「双人核查」。

examples.en: The checklist required a two-person check whenever the spare keys changed hands during a busy shift.
examples.zh: 清单规定，繁忙班次内每次交接备用钥匙都要「双人核查」。

words.enDefinition: a marketplace that brings two distinct participant groups together

examples.en: The class project imagined a two-sided marketplace that connected students needing repairs with local tailors.
examples.zh: 课程项目设想了一个「双边交易平台」，把需要修补衣物的学生和本地裁缝联系起来。

examples.en: Our tutor drew a two-sided marketplace with private tutors on one side and learners on the other.
examples.zh: 导师画出一个「双边交易平台」，一边是私人辅导老师，另一边是学习者。

collocations: both sides of a two-sided marketplace

words.enDefinition: days on which a person cannot work or take an assignment
