examples.en: I shared my unavailable dates as soon as the university confirmed the exam timetable.
examples.zh: 学校一确认考试时间表，我就提交了自己「不能排班的日期」。

examples.en: The form asked us to list unavailable dates for the six weeks before the market.
examples.zh: 表格请我们列出集市开始前六周内「不能排班的日期」。

words.enDefinition: Space beneath a table used to store equipment or extra goods

examples.en: We left the under-table storage clear for bags and boxes already sold.
examples.zh: 我们把「桌下储物空间」空出来，放已卖出的袋子和盒子。

examples.en: The longer table gave us enough under-table storage for the extra stock.
examples.zh: 长桌给我们留出了足够的「桌下储物空间」来存放额外的货。

words.enDefinition: to set a price lower than is appropriate

examples.en: The tutor asked whether we might underprice the service by leaving preparation out of the calculation.
examples.zh: 导师问，不把准备工作算进去，会不会让我们「把服务价格定得过低」。

examples.en: Our team learned how easy it was to underprice handmade notebooks when counting materials alone.
examples.zh: 我们团队了解到，只算材料，很容易「把手工笔记本的价格定得过低」。

words.enDefinition: selling price per unit minus its variable cost

examples.en: Our unit contribution margin fell after we began including a printed guide with every kit.
examples.zh: 每套工具都附送纸质指南后，我们的「单位边际贡献」下降了。

examples.en: The class compared unit contribution margin for a plain notebook and one with a custom cover.
examples.zh: 同学们比较了普通笔记本和定制封面笔记本的「单位边际贡献」。

words.enDefinition: the revenues and costs associated with one business unit such as a sale or customer

examples.en: Our advisor asked about unit economics before agreeing to discuss opening a second campus repair stall.
examples.zh: 导师先问清「单位经济性」，才同意讨论开第二个校园维修摊。

examples.en: The unit economics of the delivery project changed when we included each driver's waiting time.
examples.zh: 把每位司机的等待时间算进去后，配送项目的「单位经济性」发生了变化。

words.enDefinition: the quantity or package sold as one item

examples.en: For our pantry project, the unit of sale was a bag containing six apples.
examples.zh: 在我们的食品小店项目里，「销售计量单位」是一袋六个苹果。

examples.en: The instructor asked whether the unit of sale should be one notebook or a pack of three.
examples.zh: 老师问，「销售计量单位」应该是一本笔记本，还是三本一组。

words.enDefinition: one governing board that may include executive and non-executive members

examples.en: The lecturer drew a unitary board with executives and outside directors sitting on the same body.
examples.zh: 讲师画了一个「单层董事会」，高管和外部董事同属一个机构。

examples.en: Our case used a unitary board to review management's plans for expanding the equipment service.
examples.zh: 在案例中，由「单层董事会」审查管理层扩大器材服务的计划。

words.enDefinition: the principle that each worker takes orders from one supervisor

examples.en: The case used unity of command so each technician received instructions from one direct supervisor.
examples.zh: 案例采用「统一指挥原则」，每名技术员只听一位直属主管安排。

examples.en: We discussed how unity of command would work when two departments shared the workshop staff.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了两个部门共用工作坊人员时，该怎样落实「统一指挥原则」。

collocations: the principle of unity of command

words.enDefinition: a company formed to develop or sell a technology or discovery originating at a university

examples.en: A university spinout demonstrated its new water sensor at the careers fair last week.
examples.zh: 上周招聘会上，一家「大学成果衍生企业」演示了新研发的水质传感器。

examples.en: The research team formed a university spinout to develop the software beyond the grant period.
examples.zh: 研究团队组建了「大学成果衍生企业」，以便在资助期结束后继续开发软件。

words.enDefinition: a need that existing products, services or arrangements do not adequately address

examples.en: Our interviews revealed an unmet need for equipment bookings outside the library's usual hours.
examples.zh: 访谈发现，在图书馆平时开放时间之外预约设备，是一项「未被满足的需求」。

examples.en: The team looked for an unmet need before committing to any particular design that term.
examples.zh: 当学期团队先找「未被满足的需求」，再决定要做哪种具体设计。

words.enDefinition: Open arriving packages and take the goods out of them

examples.en: I stayed to unpack a shipment of blank tote bags after everyone else left.
examples.zh: 其他人离开后，我留下来「拆了一批到货」，里面是空白托特包。

examples.en: Can you help unpack a shipment before we arrange the merchandise on the table?
examples.zh: 把货摆上桌之前，你能帮忙「拆开这批刚到的货」吗？

words.enDefinition: expansion into businesses with little connection to current operations

examples.en: The case showed unrelated diversification when the repair company bought a small music tutoring service.
examples.zh: 案例中，维修公司收购了一家小型音乐辅导机构，体现了「非相关多元化」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why a publisher might choose unrelated diversification by entering the storage business.
examples.zh: 导师问，一家出版社为什么可能进入仓储业务，走上「非相关多元化」道路。

words.enDefinition: an estimate intended to show the high end of what a quantity could plausibly be

examples.en: Our upper-bound estimate assumed that every participating society would request the largest equipment kit.
examples.zh: 我们的「上界估计」假设，每个参与社团都会申请最大的设备套件。

examples.en: We used the upper-bound estimate to see whether even the largest storeroom would be adequate.
examples.zh: 我们通过「上界估计」检查，即使最大的储藏室是否也够用。

words.enDefinition: a plausible outcome better than the main forecast

examples.en: In the upside scenario, the campus shop stocked our bags and ordered a second batch.
examples.zh: 在「有利情景」中，校园商店上架了我们的包，还订了第二批。

examples.en: Our upside scenario assumed that schools would book more group sessions than the original estimate.
examples.zh: 我们的「有利情景」假设各学校预订的团体课会比原先估计的多。

collocations: run the numbers for an upside scenario

words.enDefinition: charging according to how much a customer actually uses

examples.en: The student team chose usage-based pricing for lockers and measured the time each locker was occupied.
examples.zh: 学生团队为储物柜采用「按用量定价」的方式，并记录每个柜子的占用时长。

examples.en: In our project, usage-based pricing meant small societies paid only for the storage they used.
examples.zh: 在我们的项目中，「按用量定价」意味着小型社团只为实际使用的存储空间付费。

words.enDefinition: an account of how a person or system uses a product to achieve a particular goal

examples.en: We wrote a use case about a volunteer lending equipment when the regular desk was closed.
examples.zh: 我们写了一个「使用场景」，描述常规服务台关闭后志愿者如何出借器材。

examples.en: The mentor asked whether the prototype addressed the most common use case during the semester.
examples.zh: 导师问，原型能不能应付学期中最常见的「使用场景」。

words.enDefinition: the sequence of steps and experiences someone goes through while trying to achieve a goal with a service

examples.en: We mapped the user journey from finding the repair stand to collecting the finished bicycle.
examples.zh: 我们画出了从找到维修摊到取回修好自行车的「用户历程」。

examples.en: The user journey revealed that many students had to ask twice about the pickup time.
examples.zh: 「用户历程」显示，很多学生得问两遍才能确定取件时间。

words.enDefinition: a planned session in which participants try using a product so the team can observe difficulties

examples.en: During the user testing session, students tried to find a pickup time without asking for help.
examples.zh: 那次「用户测试」中，同学们试着自己找到一个取件时间。

examples.en: The team recorded which step caused confusion in the user testing session on Tuesday afternoon.
examples.zh: 团队记下了周二下午那次「用户测试」中让人看不懂的步骤。

words.enDefinition: To check that an observation or conclusion is supported by reliable information or further testing.

examples.en: We tried to validate a finding about late arrivals by checking the museum's group booking records.
examples.zh: 我们核对博物馆的团体预约记录，试着「核实一项发现」，它和迟到有关。

examples.en: The students returned on Saturday to validate a finding from their weekday observation of the queue.
examples.zh: 学生们周六再次到访，去「核实他们在工作日观察排队时的一项发现」。

collocations: validate a finding with additional data

words.enDefinition: To check that the proposed steps are practical and achieve the intended result in relevant cases.

examples.en: We used a recent booking to validate the proposed workflow before asking volunteers to try it.
examples.zh: 请志愿者试用之前，我们用近期一笔预约「验证了拟议的工作流程」。

examples.en: The client helped us validate the proposed workflow using a request that involved two rehearsal rooms.
examples.zh: 客户帮我们用一项涉及两间排练室的申请「验证拟议的工作流程」。

collocations: use examples to validate the proposed workflow
validate the proposed workflow with staff
ask someone to validate the proposed workflow

words.enDefinition: setting prices around the benefit customers perceive

examples.en: The student team discussed value-based pricing after club leaders described how much time the scheduling tool saved.
examples.zh: 社团负责人讲了日程工具能省多少时间后，学生团队讨论了「价值导向定价」。

examples.en: For the photo service, value-based pricing considered what same-day delivery was worth to graduating students.
examples.zh: 摄影服务用「价值导向定价」考虑当天交付对毕业生有多大的价值。

words.enDefinition: how a venture retains some benefit from what it creates

examples.en: Our group discussed value capture after deciding that local businesses could sponsor the free map.
examples.zh: 小组决定让本地商家赞助免费地图后，讨论了如何实现「价值获取」。

examples.en: The lecturer explained value capture using a refill service that charged for each jar filled.
examples.zh: 讲师以按灌装瓶数收费的补充装服务为例，解释了什么是「价值获取」。

words.enDefinition: connected activities through which a company creates and delivers value

examples.en: We mapped the value chain from ordering raw materials to handling repairs after each sale.
examples.zh: 我们画出了从订购原料到售后维修的「价值链」。

examples.en: The case described how a faster packing step changed the value chain for a small publisher.
examples.zh: 案例介绍了更快的打包环节如何改变一家小出版社的「价值链」。

words.enDefinition: making an offering useful or beneficial to someone

examples.en: For our team, value creation meant getting borrowed equipment into students' hands between classes.
examples.zh: 对我们组而言，「价值创造」就是让学生在两节课之间就能拿到借用的器材。

examples.en: In class, we discussed how saving students a trip across campus could count as value creation.
examples.zh: 我们在课上讨论，替同学省下一趟横穿校园的路为什么也算「价值创造」。

words.enDefinition: getting the benefits of an offering to the customer

examples.en: We planned value delivery around locker pickup because many students finished class after our stall closed.
examples.zh: 很多学生下课时摊位已经收了，所以我们计划用取物柜自提来实现「价值交付」。

examples.en: The business tutor asked how home visits changed value delivery for the sewing repair project.
examples.zh: 商业课导师问，上门服务会怎样改变缝补项目的「价值交付」。

words.enDefinition: a model centered on delivering distinctive customer benefits

examples.en: The team explained its value-driven business model to judges using an example of custom fittings.
examples.zh: 团队用一对一试穿调整的例子向评委说明了「价值驱动型商业模式」。

examples.en: Our value-driven business model relied on hand-bound portfolios and offered students a choice of paper.
examples.zh: 我们的「价值驱动型商业模式」以手工装订作品集为主，并允许学生自选纸张。

collocations: a value-driven business model for custom work

words.enDefinition: the benefit an offering promises to people considering it

examples.en: Our value proposition is convenient laptop repairs while students are already on campus for class.
examples.zh: 我们的「价值主张」是同学们来学校上课时，就能顺便修电脑。

examples.en: The judges asked why evening pickup mattered enough to be part of our value proposition.
examples.zh: 评委问我们，为什么晚间自提重要到足以成为「价值主张」的一部分。

words.enDefinition: A tag identifying a specific version of a product

examples.en: I checked the variant label before putting the small tote into its bag.
examples.zh: 把小号手提包放进袋子前，我核对了「商品规格标签」。

examples.en: The variant label on the box told me which fabric the customer had picked.
examples.zh: 盒子上的「商品规格标签」让我知道顾客选了哪种面料。

words.enDefinition: A seller's request for permission to trade at an event

examples.en: The ceramics club sent in a vendor application for the spring market.
examples.zh: 陶艺社递交了春季市集的「摊商报名申请」。

examples.en: We mentioned the size of our table in the vendor application this year.
examples.zh: 我们在今年的「摊商报名申请」里写了桌子的尺寸。

words.enDefinition: The process of confirming a seller's arrival at an event

examples.en: Our team completed vendor check-in before carrying the boxes into the hall.
examples.zh: 我们组先办了「摊商签到」，再把箱子搬进大厅。

examples.en: I asked where the power outlets were during vendor check-in while my friend unloaded.
examples.zh: 朋友在卸货，我趁「摊商签到」问了插座的位置。

words.enDefinition: The period or process of bringing sellers' goods into an event venue

examples.en: The organiser sent a map showing which door to use for vendor load-in.
examples.zh: 主办方发了一张地图，标明「摊商进场卸货」走哪个门。

examples.en: We had fifteen minutes for vendor load-in before the next van arrived.
examples.zh: 下一辆货车到来前，有十五分钟供「摊商进场卸货」。

words.enDefinition: A set of instructions and information prepared for event sellers

examples.en: The vendor packet shows where we can unload our boxes on Saturday.
examples.zh: 「摊商资料包」里标了周六可以在哪里卸下箱子。

examples.en: I checked the vendor packet for the size of tables available for rent.
examples.zh: 我查了「摊商资料包」，看看能租到多大的桌子。

collocations: the vendor packet includes a map

words.enDefinition: a session where early-stage founders bring specific problems to advisers for practical guidance

examples.en: We brought questions about the launch schedule to a venture clinic after our morning lecture.
examples.zh: 上午上完课，我们带着发布日程的问题去了「创业项目咨询活动」。

examples.en: During the venture clinic, an adviser helped us narrow our interviews to one student group.
examples.zh: 在「创业项目咨询活动」中，一位顾问帮我们把访谈范围缩小到一类学生。

collocations: bring questions to a venture clinic

words.enDefinition: a short document that outlines a proposed venture and what it aims to achieve

examples.en: We submitted a venture concept note before the incubator asked us to prepare a full application.
examples.zh: 孵化器要求准备完整申请前，我们先递交了一份「创业构想简报」。

examples.en: The venture concept note explained who might use the repair service and why it was needed.
examples.zh: 「创业构想简报」说明了谁可能会用维修服务，以及为什么需要。

words.enDefinition: an experienced person who advises a team starting or developing a venture

examples.en: The venture mentor asked whether we had spoken to students outside our immediate friendship group.
examples.zh: 「创业导师」问我们，是否找过平时关系不那么近的学生聊过。

examples.en: I met my venture mentor on Friday to discuss how to recruit pilot users.
examples.zh: 周五我见了「创业导师」，讨论怎么招募试点用户。

collocations: receive advice from a venture mentor
match a team with a venture mentor

words.enDefinition: significant points used to track a new venture's progress

examples.en: The tutor asked each team to list venture milestones it could reach before the end of term.
examples.zh: 导师请各团队列出学期结束前可以达到的「创业发展里程碑」。

examples.en: Signups from two universities counted among our venture milestones during the first year of testing.
examples.zh: 测试第一年，两所大学报名加入，算是我们的「创业发展里程碑」。

words.enDefinition: a plan showing the main stages and milestones in developing a venture over time

examples.en: The venture roadmap put testing ahead of expansion to the other side of the campus.
examples.zh: 「创业项目路线图」把测试排在了扩展到校园另一头之前。

examples.en: We revised the venture roadmap when another team offered to share its workshop space.
examples.zh: 另一支团队提出共享工作坊场地后，我们修改了「创业项目路线图」。

words.enDefinition: an organisation that actively builds new ventures by bringing together ideas, teams and shared resources

examples.en: The venture studio assigned two designers to help the team prepare its first prototype.
examples.zh: 「创业工作室」安排两名设计师帮助团队做出首个原型。

examples.en: Our tutor compared a venture studio that starts projects with an incubator that supports them.
examples.zh: 导师比较了自己发起项目的「创业工作室」和为项目提供支持的孵化器。

words.enDefinition: bringing more stages of the same supply chain under common control

examples.en: In our case, the publisher moved toward vertical integration by bringing previously outsourced printing in-house.
examples.zh: 在案例中，出版社把原先外包的印刷业务收回内部，逐步走向「纵向一体化」。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether vertical integration could make paper deliveries less dependent on an outside company.
examples.zh: 导师问，「纵向一体化」能否让纸张配送减少对外部公司的依赖。

words.enDefinition: a way of addressing a problem that can realistically work under the available conditions

examples.en: Our group found a viable solution once the library agreed to handle evening collection.
examples.zh: 图书馆同意负责晚间领取后，我们小组找到了一个「切实可行的解决方案」。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether this was a viable solution for a society with only two volunteers.
examples.zh: 导师问，对于只有两名志愿者的社团来说，这算不算「切实可行的解决方案」。

words.enDefinition: a statement describing the future an organisation hopes to create

examples.en: The group's vision statement imagined a campus where every student could borrow basic tools.
examples.zh: 小组的「愿景宣言」描绘了一个每个学生都能借到基本工具的校园。

examples.en: Our tutor asked us to shorten the vision statement so people could remember it easily.
examples.zh: 导师请我们缩短「愿景宣言」，让大家更容易记住。

words.enDefinition: Material inserted to fill empty space around goods inside a package

examples.en: We added paper void fill so the small bowl wouldn't move in transit.
examples.zh: 我们加了纸质「包装空隙填料」，小碗在运输时就不会晃动。

examples.en: The larger boxes needed more void fill around the mugs before we sealed them.
examples.zh: 大盒子封口前，马克杯周围得多加一些「包装空隙填料」。

words.enDefinition: setting prices according to the quantity purchased, often with lower unit prices for larger orders

examples.en: The student printer offered volume pricing to societies that ordered several hundred leaflets at once.
examples.zh: 学生打印店为一次订购几百张传单的社团采用「按采购量定价」。

examples.en: We used volume pricing for the badges, so larger orders qualified for a lower unit price.
examples.zh: 我们的徽章采用「按采购量定价」，采购数量达到更高档时，单价会更低。

words.enDefinition: a level of activity that triggers a change in terms or costs

examples.en: The supplier set a volume threshold of one hundred bags before offering the lower price.
examples.zh: 供应商把「数量门槛」定为一百个袋子，达到才给较低价格。

examples.en: We reached the volume threshold and had to move production into a bigger campus workshop.
examples.zh: 我们达到了「数量门槛」，不得不把生产搬到校园里更大的工作坊。

words.enDefinition: a framework for evaluating whether resources are valuable, rare, costly to imitate and supported by the firm's organisation

examples.en: The tutor used the VRIO framework to assess a repair team's unusually deep knowledge of equipment.
examples.zh: 导师用「VRIO 分析框架」评估维修团队对器材掌握的丰富知识。

examples.en: We applied the VRIO framework to assess whether our booking service could give us a lasting advantage.
examples.zh: 我们运用「VRIO 分析框架」评估预约服务能否带来持久优势。

collocations: an assessment using the VRIO framework

words.enDefinition: a prediction of how long someone or something will wait before being served or processed

examples.en: The desk displayed a wait time estimate after the number of people needing repairs doubled.
examples.zh: 需要维修的人翻了一倍后，服务台显示了「预计等候时长」。

examples.en: The coordinator updated the wait time estimate when the second worker returned from the break.
examples.zh: 第二名员工休息回来后，协调员更新了「预计等候时长」。

words.enDefinition: An appointment arranged after a customer arrives without booking ahead

examples.en: We could offer a walk-in appointment for a quick consultation at the repair table.
examples.zh: 我们在维修台可以让人「现场登记预约」，做个简短咨询。

examples.en: The poster explains when students can get a walk-in appointment for a mending lesson.
examples.zh: 海报说明了同学们什么时候可以「现场登记预约」学衣物缝补。

words.enDefinition: To explain something to the client in order, pointing out the key parts as you go.

examples.en: We used a diagram to walk the client through the way staff verified group bookings.
examples.zh: 我们用一张图「向客户逐步讲解」员工怎么核实团体预约。

examples.en: The students offered to walk the client through their figures before sharing the full report.
examples.zh: 学生们提出在分享整份报告前，先「逐步向客户讲解」这些数字。

collocations: walk the client through the draft
walk the client through the model
walk the client through each step

words.enDefinition: a customer who comes directly to a stall, desk or counter without booking or ordering first

examples.en: I kept two blue bags for any walk-up customer who asked about them.
examples.zh: 我留了两个蓝色包，免得有「未预约的现场顾客」来问却没货。

examples.en: A walk-up customer bought the last print while we were checking our reservations.
examples.zh: 我们核对预订时，一位「未预约的现场顾客」买走了最后一幅版画。

collocations: a sale to a walk-up customer

words.enDefinition: A sign designed to withstand exposure to outdoor weather

examples.en: Our weatherproof sign stayed legible through the brief rain at the outdoor market.
examples.zh: 室外市集上下了阵雨，我们的「耐风雨招牌」还是看得清。

examples.en: We put a weatherproof sign by the gate so customers could find the stall.
examples.zh: 我们在大门旁立了块「耐风雨招牌」，让顾客能找到摊位。

words.enDefinition: the workers or arrangements needed to keep an operation working over the weekend

examples.en: We arranged weekend coverage because the art market was staying open until Sunday afternoon.
examples.zh: 艺术集市会开到周日下午，我们安排了「周末值班安排」。

examples.en: The team added a second worker for weekend coverage when Saturday orders began increasing.
examples.zh: 周六订单开始增加后，团队给「周末值班安排」多加了一人。

words.enDefinition: A call held each week so the team and client can discuss the project's progress.

examples.en: We brought an example of a delayed booking to the weekly client call on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 周二的「每周客户通话」上，我们举了一个预约拖延的例子。

examples.en: The weekly client call gave the theatre manager a chance to ask about our initial findings.
examples.zh: 「每周客户通话」给了剧院经理一个机会，可以问问我们有哪些初步发现。

collocations: prepare for a weekly client call
bring a question to the weekly client call

words.enDefinition: evaluation criteria to which weights have been assigned to reflect their relative importance

examples.en: We used weighted criteria so that location counted more than the colour of the fixtures.
examples.zh: 我们采用「带权重的评估标准」，让地段比固定装置的颜色占更大比重。

examples.en: The team adjusted the weighted criteria after learning how important afternoon access was to customers.
examples.zh: 团队得知下午能进店对顾客很重要，调整了「带权重的评估标准」。

words.enDefinition: how much someone is prepared to pay for a product or service

examples.en: We asked about willingness to pay after hearing that several societies already borrowed equipment for free.
examples.zh: 得知好几个社团已经能免费借器材，我们接着询问了「支付意愿」。

examples.en: The pilot compared completed purchases at several prices to estimate students' willingness to pay.
examples.zh: 试点比较了几个价位的实际购买情况，以估计学生的「支付意愿」。

words.enDefinition: A message informing the client that the agreed work has been finished.

examples.en: Our organiser received a work completion notice before going to collect the new board covers.
examples.zh: 我们的组织者去领新展板封面之前，收到了「完工通知」。

examples.en: The studio sent a work completion notice to the gallery after finishing the printed labels.
examples.zh: 工场做完印制标签后，给画廊发了「完工通知」。

words.enDefinition: a maximum number of items that may be actively worked on at one time

examples.en: Our work-in-progress limit meant we could start another repair only after finishing an existing one.
examples.zh: 根据「在办事项数量上限」，我们得先完成一项正在做的维修，才能开下一项。

examples.en: The team lowered its work-in-progress limit to stop too many orders reaching the counter together.
examples.zh: 团队调低了「在办事项数量上限」，免得太多订单同时送到柜台。

words.enDefinition: a document or set of directions explaining how to perform a specific work task

examples.en: The work instruction showed which label went on each kind of returned item in the shop.
examples.zh: 「作业指导书」说明了店里不同种类的退回品该贴哪种标签。

examples.en: We added a photograph to the work instruction for setting up the second display shelf.
examples.zh: 我们在搭建第二个展示架的「作业指导书」中加了一张照片。

words.enDefinition: a list of jobs awaiting processing, often in an order that determines what is done next

examples.en: My work queue contained three label requests and a repair form when I started the shift.
examples.zh: 我开始上班时，「待处理工作队列」里有三项标签请求和一张维修单。

examples.en: The team moved rush orders to the front of the work queue before the post office closed.
examples.zh: 邮局关门前，团队把加急订单调到了「待处理工作队列」最前面。

collocations: add a job to the work queue

words.enDefinition: to operate the cash register and handle transactions during a period of work

examples.en: I learned to work the register at the market before helping with the afternoon shift.
examples.zh: 去下午班帮忙之前，我先学了怎么在集市上「负责收银」。

examples.en: The supervisor asked who could work the register while the usual cashier took a break.
examples.zh: 主管问，平时的收银员休息时谁能「负责收银」。

collocations: train someone to work the register

words.enDefinition: a cooperative owned and democratically controlled by its workers

examples.en: A worker cooperative took over the repair business in the case after the founder retired.
examples.zh: 案例中，创始人退休后，一家「工人合作社」接手了维修业务。

examples.en: The students discussed how a worker cooperative might let staff share responsibility for new equipment purchases.
examples.zh: 学生讨论了「工人合作社」怎样让员工共同承担采购新设备的责任。

words.enDefinition: Ideas accepted for planning or analysis until the team can check whether they are true.

examples.en: Our working assumptions included the idea that each centre recorded cancellations in the same way.
examples.zh: 我们的「工作中的暂定假设」之一，是各中心用同一种方式记录取消预约。

examples.en: We revisited our working assumptions after the charity gave us attendance data for two more months.
examples.zh: 慈善机构多给了两个月的到场数据后，我们重新审视了「工作中的暂定假设」。

words.enDefinition: The way two people or organisations relate to each other when they work together.

examples.en: The student studio built a working relationship with the local theatre by making signs together.
examples.zh: 学生工作室通过和当地剧院一起制作标牌，建立了「工作合作关系」。

examples.en: Clear handover notes helped us keep a good working relationship with the people using the space next.
examples.zh: 清楚的交接记录让我们和下一批使用场地的人保持了良好的「工作合作关系」。

words.enDefinition: an estimate of the amount of work expected during a future period

examples.en: We based the workload forecast on how many orders had arrived before each previous event.
examples.zh: 我们用之前每场活动前收到的订单数来做「工作量预测」。

examples.en: The workload forecast showed that Thursday would be busier than the rest of the week.
examples.zh: 「工作量预测」显示，周四会比这周其他日子忙。

words.enDefinition: a situation in which some people or stations have substantially more work than others

examples.en: The supervisor noticed a workload imbalance when all the afternoon orders went to one bench.
examples.zh: 下午订单全都去了同一张工作台，主管发现「工作量分配不均」。

examples.en: We changed the labels to reduce a workload imbalance between the two service desks.
examples.zh: 我们调整了标签，以缓解两处服务台之间的「工作量分配不均」。

words.enDefinition: the amount of work a particular station can complete in a set time under given conditions

examples.en: We compared workstation capacity at the two benches before assigning the afternoon repair orders.
examples.zh: 分派下午的维修订单前，我们比较了两张工作台的「工位处理能力」。

examples.en: The supervisor checked workstation capacity when the team added another printer to the label desk.
examples.zh: 团队为标签台增添一台打印机时，主管查看了「工位处理能力」。

words.enDefinition: The person coordinating one defined area of work within a larger project.

examples.en: The workstream lead for field research organised visits to compare the two museum entrances.
examples.zh: 实地调研的「分项工作负责人」安排了参访，比较博物馆的两个入口。

examples.en: Each workstream lead reported one finding and one question for the rest of the group.
examples.zh: 每位「分项工作负责人」报告了一项发现，并给小组其他成员提了一个问题。

collocations: ask the workstream lead to report

words.enDefinition: the least favourable plausible set of events or conditions considered in a plan

examples.en: The worst-case scenario combined a late delivery with the loss of our second collection desk.
examples.zh: 「最坏的情景」是送货延迟，同时失去第二处自取台。

examples.en: We discussed the worst-case scenario before deciding how much spare time to put in the schedule.
examples.zh: 我们先讨论了「最坏的情景」，再决定在日程里预留多少时间。
